Šarić leads the work package on signal compression and transmission standards, contributing ECG and PPG codec implementations compliant with the SCP-ECG data standard. The work package also produces interoperability guidelines for compressed signal exchange between different hospital information systems used on the two sides of the border. Deliverables include a compression middleware component integrated into the project's shared telemedicine platform and a joint training session for clinical IT staff at both partner sites.

SYN-PRJ-0271.title: Cross-Institutional Learning Trace Data Harmonisation for Comparative Analytics
SYN-PRJ-0271.text:
CROSSLEARN: Cross-Institutional Learning Trace Data Harmonisation for Comparative Analytics (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R1006 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen, Hungary; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Subotica Tech – College of Applied Sciences, Subotica.
CROSSLEARN addresses the lack of interoperability between learning management system log formats at universities on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border, which prevents comparative analytics research. The project is producing a shared data schema and an open-source transformation pipeline covering Moodle, Canvas, and one proprietary system used by a Hungarian partner. Mitrović leads the work package on statistical harmonisation, which develops procedures for aligning feature distributions across institutions before joint model training. An ongoing longitudinal study tracks 2,600 students across four partner universities from enrolment through first degree, with annual data extracts. Outputs include a harmonised benchmark dataset and two cross-border student mobility analytics pilots.

SYN-PRJ-0297.title: Conducted Disturbance Characterisation and Unified Time-domain Simulation for Low-Voltage Smart Grids
SYN-PRJ-0297.text:
CONDUCTS: Conducted Disturbance Characterisation and Unified Time-domain Simulation for Low-Voltage Smart Grids (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0611 principal investigator; R0637 team member; R0028 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Elektrotehnički fakultet, University of Belgrade; Elektrodistribucija Srbije d.o.o. – Regional Centre Novi Sad.
The project builds a validated simulation and measurement infrastructure for analysing conducted disturbances in low-voltage distribution networks with high penetration of power electronic loads. Key activities include: extended characterisation of emission sources (EV chargers, PV inverters, smart meters, LED drivers) using LISN measurements and Norton equivalent extraction; development of a time-domain feeder simulation library in MATLAB/Simulink with open-licence distribution; a 12-month field monitoring campaign on two suburban feeders; and a probabilistic compliance assessment tool. Results feed into a position paper on Serbian national transposition of IEC 61000-3 limits for aggregated loads.

SYN-PRJ-0334.title: Reliability-Centred Operation of Biomass Densification Systems under Variable Feedstock Quality
SYN-PRJ-0334.text:
RELIODENSE: Reliability-Centred Operation of Biomass Densification Systems under Variable Feedstock Quality (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0135 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad; Bioenergo d.o.o., Vrbas, Serbia.
RELIODENSE addresses the gap between laboratory degradation models and field-deployable maintenance decision tools for biomass densification equipment. The project integrates on-line NIR feedstock sensing, low-cost MEMS vibration loggers, and Bayesian degradation models into a prototype decision support system tested at two commercial pellet facilities in Vojvodina. Research tasks include calibration of NIR regression models for mixed agricultural residues, development of the particle-filtering RUL estimator, discrete-event simulation of full production lines, and a field validation campaign. The project supports one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher. The primary output is a validated software prototype and an open dataset of bearing vibration and feedstock quality records from the two field sites.

SYN-PRJ-0340.title: Self-Diagnosing Sensor Networks for Autonomous Precision Agriculture in the Pannonian Region
SYN-PRJ-0340.text:
SENSORNET-AP: Self-Diagnosing Sensor Networks for Autonomous Precision Agriculture in the Pannonian Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2023).
Participants: R0754 work package leader.
Partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, University of Pécs, Hungary; Provincial Institute for Agriculture Novi Sad; AgroData Solutions Kft., Pécs, Hungary.
The project deployed and evaluated a cross-border agricultural sensor network spanning eight farm sites in Hungary and Serbia. Žarko Jakovljević led the work package responsible for node-level fault detection firmware and gateway-side data quality validation. The work package produced a reference firmware architecture supporting three diagnostic modules (drift detection, connectivity health scoring, and battery state estimation) and a validation protocol used to certify sensor data before ingestion into partner farm management systems. Field trials covered approximately 1,100 hectares of maize, sunflower, and wheat. The project produced two open datasets published through the Pannonian Environmental Data Repository and contributed results to two of the journal publications listed in this profile.

SYN-PRJ-0341.title: Distributed In-situ Data Quality Assurance for Low-Power Environmental Monitoring Networks
SYN-PRJ-0341.text:
DIAQUAL: Distributed In-situ Data Quality Assurance for Low-Power Environmental Monitoring Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2026).
Participants: R0754 principal investigator.
Partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
DIAQUAL addresses the absence of standardised data quality assurance methods for resource-constrained IoT nodes used in environmental monitoring. The project is developing a layered diagnostic framework in which lightweight statistical tests execute at node level, aggregation logic runs at gateway level, and a calibration traceability module operates at the cloud backend. The framework targets NB-IoT and LTE-M deployments and is being validated on soil, water-level, and air-quality sensor networks operated by project partners. The project employs two research assistants based at BioSense Institute and includes a measurement campaign at ten instrumented sites across the Fruška Gora protected area. A hardware reference design and open-source firmware library are planned deliverables.

SYN-PRJ-0350.title: Low-Power Wide-Area Connectivity for Smart Greenhouse Monitoring in the Pannonian Region
SYN-PRJ-0350.text:
AGRILINK: Low-Power Wide-Area Connectivity for Smart Greenhouse Monitoring in the Pannonian Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0800 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; University of Szeged, Faculty of Engineering, Hungary; Agro-Innovation Centre Palić (fictional); Greentech Pannonia d.o.o. (fictional).
AGRILINK develops and validates a LoRaWAN-based sensor network architecture for monitoring temperature, humidity, CO₂, and soil moisture in greenhouse clusters across northern Serbia and southern Hungary. The University of Novi Sad component is responsible for radio propagation characterisation of greenhouse structures, network planning methodology, and gateway placement optimisation. Tihomir Urošević leads the work package on propagation modelling and link-budget validation, coordinating measurement campaigns at partner greenhouse sites. The project also produces an open-access planning guide for small agricultural producers considering IoT adoption, and delivers a pilot deployment covering approximately 3 hectares of greenhouse area near Subotica.

SYN-PRJ-0351.title: Propagation-Aware Indoor Localisation for Industrial IoT Asset Tracking
SYN-PRJ-0351.text:
INDORLOC: Propagation-Aware Indoor Localisation for Industrial IoT Asset Tracking (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2023).
Participants: R0800 team member; R0905 team member; R1018 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Mihajlo Pupin Institute, Belgrade (fictional division).
INDORLOC investigated the relationship between multipath propagation structure and the accuracy of fingerprint-based and geometry-based localisation algorithms in industrial halls. The project combined channel sounding campaigns in three factory environments near Novi Sad with ray-launching simulations calibrated to measured data. Tihomir Urošević contributed antenna design for the measurement platform and conducted the 868 MHz wideband measurement campaigns. The project produced a calibrated propagation dataset made publicly available, and demonstrated that localisation error below 2 m is achievable with a four-gateway LoRa infrastructure when gateway positions are chosen to minimise delay-spread variance across the coverage area.

SYN-PRJ-0378.title: Sub-Surface LoRaWAN Sensing for Urban Infrastructure Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0378.text:
SUBSENSE: Sub-Surface LoRaWAN Sensing for Urban Infrastructure Monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0811 principal investigator; R0660 team member; R0989 team member.
Partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences; Public Utility Company Novi Sad Waters – fictional; Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania – fictional.
SUBSENSE addressed the absence of standardised propagation models and deployment guidelines for LoRaWAN sensor networks in below-grade urban infrastructure, including utility tunnels, underground car parks, and building basements. The project combined controlled laboratory measurements of material-specific signal attenuation with large-scale field campaigns in Novi Sad. A parametric link budget toolkit was developed that accepts building material properties, structure geometry, and gateway position as inputs and outputs coverage probability maps. The toolkit was validated in three pilot environments provided by municipal partners. Results were disseminated in four journal papers and three conference contributions. A freely downloadable software package was released under an open-source licence at the end of the project.

SYN-PRJ-0379.title: LoRaWAN Gateway Optimisation and Adaptive Rate Control for Smart City Applications in the Pannonian Region
SYN-PRJ-0379.text:
LOROPT: LoRaWAN Gateway Optimisation and Adaptive Rate Control for Smart City Applications in the Pannonian Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0811 work package leader; R0446 team member.
Partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences; University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary – fictional; City of Subotica, Department of Environmental Protection – fictional.
LOROPT brought together partners from Novi Sad and Pécs to develop jointly validated tools for LoRaWAN network planning in mid-size Pannonian cities, which share similar low-rise building stock, flat terrain, and continental vegetation patterns. Branislava Janković led the work package on propagation model calibration and gateway placement optimisation. The project produced a shared measurement dataset of approximately 30 000 RSSI records across both cities, a calibrated ray-tracing model, and a genetic-algorithm-based placement tool. Two pilot networks were commissioned, one monitoring air quality sensors in Subotica and one monitoring soil moisture in an agricultural periurban zone near Pécs. The project trained six early-stage researchers across the two institutions.

SYN-PRJ-0380.title: Integrated Quality Assurance Methodology for Pre-Weld Surface Preparation in Automated Thin-Sheet Joining Lines
SYN-PRJ-0380.text:
PREWELD-QA: Integrated Quality Assurance Methodology for Pre-Weld Surface Preparation in Automated Thin-Sheet Joining Lines (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0593 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Metalform d.o.o., Novi Sad; Presing Komponente d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project develops a structured quality assurance methodology covering measurement methods, acceptance criteria, and control chart templates for pre-weld surface cleanliness on cold-rolled mild-steel blanks in automated MIG/MAG joining lines. Work includes characterisation of residual contamination types (lubricants, rust-preventive oils, press shop dust) by FTIR-ATR and TOC analysis, quantification of their influence on arc stability and weld quality, and translation of laboratory findings into practical process capability targets. Two partner companies from the Vojvodina automotive supply sector provide industrial test cases. The final deliverable is a guidance document and training module targeting quality engineers at small and medium-sized fabricators.

SYN-PRJ-0381.title: Process Monitoring and Control Tools for Small-Scale Electrostatic Powder Coating Pre-Treatment Lines
SYN-PRJ-0381.text:
COATLINE: Process Monitoring and Control Tools for Small-Scale Electrostatic Powder Coating Pre-Treatment Lines (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2020–2021).
Participants: R0593 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Vojvodina Coating Contractors Association.
This project addressed the lack of structured process monitoring in small powder coating operations in Vojvodina. Activities included a baseline survey of bath chemistry management practices at seven local contractors, instrument calibration audits, and a pilot SPC deployment at two volunteer companies. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian/English) SPC implementation guide for pre-treatment lines, freely distributed to members of the Vojvodina Coating Contractors Association. Results from the pilot companies were subsequently published in peer-reviewed form. Total funding was 1.2 million RSD.

SYN-PRJ-0383.title: Methodology and Tool Support for Safe Migration of Legacy Embedded C Code to MISRA-C:2012
SYN-PRJ-0383.text:
SAFE-MIGRATE: Methodology and Tool Support for Safe Migration of Legacy Embedded C Code to MISRA-C:2012 (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2018–2020).
Participants: R1022 principal investigator.
Partners: NTP Novi Sad — tenant company Embeddium d.o.o.; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
SAFE-MIGRATE developed practical methods and tool support to assist small and medium embedded-systems companies in the Vojvodina region in migrating legacy C firmware to MISRA-C:2012 compliance. The project produced the initial version of the MisraFix rewriting tool, a catalogue of refactoring patterns for safety-relevant firmware, and a training programme delivered to engineers at two local companies working on automotive and industrial control products. The project included a pilot application in which the methodology was applied to a 47 kB motor-controller firmware under an industry collaboration agreement. A total of four peer-reviewed publications resulted from the project.

SYN-PRJ-0391.title: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software
SYN-PRJ-0391.text:
SAFEPLL: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2024).
Participants: R0995 work package leader; R0749 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary; Automatika-Pro d.o.o., Novi Sad; RoboSystems Kft., Pécs, Hungary.
SAFEPLL addressed the integration of functional safety requirements into model-driven PLC product-line workflows, targeting IEC 62061 SIL 1 and SIL 2 certified applications. The project brought together researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest with two SME automation integrators. Veljko Pantelić led the work package on traceability from HAZOP artefacts to generated code, contributing the SysML parametric diagram transformation described in the 2021 conference paper. The project produced a methodology document adopted by both industrial partners as an internal development guideline, and delivered training workshops for engineering staff at both companies.

SYN-PRJ-0393.title: Harmonic and EMC Interaction in Multi-Drive Industrial Power Systems
SYN-PRJ-0393.text:
HARMONIA: Harmonic and EMC Interaction in Multi-Drive Industrial Power Systems (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2018–2020).
Participants: R0283 coordinator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina.
HARMONIA examined harmonic and conducted EMI interactions arising when multiple variable-speed drives share a common AC supply or DC bus in manufacturing plant environments. The project combined controlled laboratory experiments on two- and three-drive configurations with simulation studies using measured drive models. Key findings concerned the conditions under which inter-drive harmonic coupling can cause individual drives to fail IEC 61800-3 limits even when each drive passes in isolation, and the degree to which switching frequency offset reduces this risk. Practical installation guidelines were produced for plant electrical engineers. The project funded one master's thesis and supported the development of the Faculty's multi-drive test bench.

SYN-PRJ-0415.title: Formal Methods Training and Tool Integration for Small Embedded Software Teams in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0415.text:
FORMBASE: Formal Methods Training and Tool Integration for Small Embedded Software Teams in the Western Balkans (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2024).
Participants: R0375 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics; Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad; Pécs Engineering and Innovation Centre, Hungary.
FORMBASE aimed to lower the barrier to formal methods adoption in small software teams developing embedded control systems in Hungary and Serbia. Stefan Kostić led the work package responsible for curriculum development and tool-integration workshops. The project produced a three-day training course covering CBMC, Frama-C, and UPPAAL, delivered to 68 engineers from 11 companies across the two countries. A companion open-access textbook of 180 pages was written in Serbian and Hungarian. The project also ran a tool evaluation study comparing six open-source formal verification tools on a shared benchmark of embedded firmware, with results published as a technical report. Two pilot adoptions in participating companies were documented as case studies.

SYN-PRJ-0514.title: Cross-Border Deployment of Secure LPWAN Telemetry Infrastructure for Environmental and Industrial Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0514.text:
TRANS-LPWAN: Cross-Border Deployment of Secure LPWAN Telemetry Infrastructure for Environmental and Industrial Monitoring (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0286 work package leader.
Partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary; ЈВП Воде Војводине, Нови Сад; Tiszamenti Vízügyi Igazgatóság, Szolnok, Hungary.
TRANS-LPWAN је прекогранични пројекат који развија заједничку инфраструктуру за телеметријски мониторинг животне средине и индустријских постројења у пограничном подручју Србије и Мађарске. Главни технички допринос тима са Факултета техничких наука односи се на безбедносни слој: дефинисање протокола за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера на уређајима расположеним дуж прекограничних руских обала Тисе, управљање кључевима у административно хетерогеном окружењу са два различита национална оператора мреже, и успостављање процедуре за безбедну даљинску надоградњу уређаја без физичког приступа. Пројекат подразумева пилот-инсталацију на 35 теренских чворова.

SYN-PRJ-0517.title: Formal Regression Methods for Testing Embedded Control Firmware
SYN-PRJ-0517.text:
FRMTEST: Formal Regression Methods for Testing Embedded Control Firmware (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0233 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš.
The project developed a coherent toolchain for specification-driven regression testing of embedded firmware, covering model authoring in a constrained EFA dialect, automated test case generation, hardware-in-the-loop execution adapters for STM32 and NXP platforms, and mutation-based suite adequacy assessment. Research activities included empirical studies on maintenance cost across firmware release histories and the development of the SpecMutate framework. The project funded two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher and resulted in six peer-reviewed publications. Dissemination included a publicly released open-source toolchain prototype and a two-day industrial workshop held in Novi Sad attended by engineers from three regional firms.

SYN-PRJ-0543.title: Text-Based Automated Compliance Monitoring for SMEs in the Energy and Finance Sectors
SYN-PRJ-0543.text:
COMPLYTEX: Text-Based Automated Compliance Monitoring for SMEs in the Energy and Finance Sectors (Innovation Fund of Serbia, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0552 principal investigator; R0109 team member.
Partners: NTP Novi Sad – portfolio kompanija RegTech Solutions d.o.o. (fiktivna); Energodata Consulting d.o.o., Novi Sad (fiktivna); Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu.
Projekat razvija prototip SaaS alata koji malim i srednjim preduzećima u energetskom i finansijskom sektoru omogućuje automatsku provjeru usklađenosti internih dokumenata sa relevantnim zakonskim propisima. Tehničko jezgro čini model semantičke sličnosti treniran kontrastivnim učenjem, nadopunjen modulom za detekciju out-of-distribution dokumenata. Sistem je integrisan sa pretragom pravnih baza podataka putem API-ja i prezentuje rezultate kroz veb interfejs sa objašnjenjima na nivou rečenice. U projektu učestvuju dva privredna partnera koji obezbeđuju realne testne dokumente i učestvuju u evaluaciji prototipa u produkcijskim uslovima.

SYN-PRJ-0554.title: Legal Text Classification for Under-Resourced Balkan Languages
SYN-PRJ-0554.text:
LEXICO: Legal Text Classification for Under-Resourced Balkan Languages (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2023).
Participants: R0484 principal investigator; R0039 team member; R1030 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad; School of Computing, Union University, Belgrade.
LEXICO addressed the absence of annotated legal corpora and pretrained language models tailored to Balkan languages with limited digital legal resources. The project assembled a multilingual corpus covering Serbian, Macedonian, and Bosnian court decisions (approximately 18,000 documents in total), established annotation guidelines for outcome and procedural-stage labels, and trained lightweight transformer models suitable for deployment on modest hardware. Deliverables included two publicly released datasets, three peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype web interface for case outcome screening used in a demonstration with a Belgrade-based legal aid organisation. The project was carried out entirely within Serbian institutions, with informal advisory input from collaborators at Masaryk University.

SYN-PRJ-0555.title: Data Augmentation Methods for Judicial Decision Support in Small-Data Regimes
SYN-PRJ-0555.text:
DAJURIS: Data Augmentation Methods for Judicial Decision Support in Small-Data Regimes (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0484 principal investigator; R0749 team member; R0979 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad.
DAJURIS investigates the boundary conditions under which synthetic data generation improves downstream legal classification, focusing on corpora with fewer than 1,000 labelled instances. The project compares rule-based paraphrasing, conditional generative models, and diffusion-based text augmentation on four task types drawn from Serbian administrative and civil law. A secondary objective is the development of an evaluation protocol that incorporates domain expert judgment alongside automatic metrics, addressing the gap between perplexity-based assessment and legal coherence. Results feed into practical guidelines for legal informatics practitioners. The project involves two PhD students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and a collaboration with the Faculty of Law for expert annotation.

SYN-PRJ-0556.title: Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains
SYN-PRJ-0556.text:
VERIFAI-RS: Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0127 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade; Department of Computer Science, University of Pécs; Regional Legal Information Centre Novi Sad (observer partner).
The project investigated automated fact verification and explanation methods for AI-generated text with a focus on legal, medical, and financial documents in Serbian and English. The team built annotated corpora for hallucination detection, developed lightweight NLI models fine-tuned on domain-specific data, and designed a modular verification pipeline applicable to retrieval-augmented generation architectures. The project funded two PhD students and supported collaboration with the Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade, and the University of Pécs. Outputs include three datasets released under open licences, seven peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype verification module tested with a regional legal information provider.

SYN-PRJ-0558.title: Efficient Vector Search Infrastructures for Multilingual Document Repositories
SYN-PRJ-0558.text:
VECSEARCH: Efficient Vector Search Infrastructures for Multilingual Document Repositories (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0741 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia; Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad.
The project investigates the co-design of approximate nearest-neighbour index structures and multilingual text encoders for document retrieval in public-sector repositories. Work packages cover: (1) encoder fine-tuning for South Slavic languages with limited supervision, (2) quantisation-aware index construction balancing recall and storage, and (3) a prototype retrieval service validated on a 10-million-document legal and administrative corpus provided by a partner institution. The project funds two PhD students and covers compute costs on the PARADOX-IV HPC cluster. An open benchmark dataset covering Serbian and Croatian legal documents is a planned deliverable.

SYN-PRJ-0559.title: Cross-Lingual Document Discovery in Regional Public Administration Archives
SYN-PRJ-0559.text:
CROSSDOC: Cross-Lingual Document Discovery in Regional Public Administration Archives (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0741 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; University of Debrecen, Faculty of Informatics, Hungary; City Archive of Subotica; Municipal Document Centre of Pécs, Hungary.
CROSSDOC aims to improve access to administrative documents held by Hungarian and Serbian public bodies by building a shared cross-lingual retrieval layer. The Serbian technical team, led by Todorović, is responsible for the index infrastructure work package, including the design of a federated index architecture that allows each national partner to retain custody of its documents while exposing a unified query interface. The system will be piloted with two municipal archives containing approximately 400,000 documents each. Hungarian-language tokenisation and transliteration components are contributed by the University of Debrecen partner.

SYN-PRJ-0661.title: Scalable On-Premises Storage and Query Engine for Industrial Sensor Networks
SYN-PRJ-0661.text:
SENSORDB: Scalable On-Premises Storage and Query Engine for Industrial Sensor Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0019 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics; Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia.
The project addressed the gap between general-purpose columnar databases and the specific write and query patterns of high-frequency industrial sensor deployments. Work packages covered codec selection heuristics, mixed-rate schema design, and cost-model-guided query planning. A prototype engine extension was developed and tested against live data streams from two partner facilities in Vojvodina. The project funded two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. Hardware acquired includes a four-node NVMe cluster used for reproducible benchmarks. Collaboration with the Budapest University of Technology and Economics provided access to complementary datasets from Hungarian utility-monitoring infrastructure.

SYN-PRJ-0662.title: Low-Cost Data Infrastructure for Precision Agriculture Sensor Networks in the Cross-Border Region
SYN-PRJ-0662.text:
AGRISENSE: Low-Cost Data Infrastructure for Precision Agriculture Sensor Networks in the Cross-Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2024).
Participants: R0019 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad; Csongrád-Csanád County Agricultural Advisory Centre (invented); NTP Agro Solutions d.o.o. Novi Sad (invented).
AGRISENSE deployed a network of 180 low-cost soil and microclimate sensors across agricultural land in Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád County. Hadžić led the data management work package, responsible for the on-premises storage layer, compression pipeline, and a web-based dashboard for agronomists. The irregular-timestamp columnar layout work published in 2024 emerged directly from this project. The storage system runs on a single rack-mounted server provided by the Serbian partner and has been operational since mid-2023, ingesting approximately 2 million records per day.

SYN-PRJ-0849.title: Performance Measurement Frameworks for ISO-Transitioning SMEs in the Danube Region
SYN-PRJ-0849.text:
PERFMAP: Performance Measurement Frameworks for ISO-Transitioning SMEs in the Danube Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2023).
Participants: R0104 coordinator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Engineering, University of Miskolc; Regional Development Agency Vojvodina Nord, Subotica; Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Bács-Kiskun County, Kecskemét.
PERFMAP aimed to develop and disseminate practical performance measurement toolkits tailored to manufacturing SMEs in cross-border regions of Hungary and Serbia undergoing ISO 9001 transitions. The project combined empirical survey research across 140 companies, participatory tool development workshops in Novi Sad and Subotica, and a 12-month pilot in 18 volunteer companies. Outputs included a validated short-form BSC instrument, a pre-certification readiness checklist, and a freely accessible web-based self-assessment platform developed by the Hungarian partner. The project also supported four joint training events attended by approximately 200 quality managers and consultants. Two peer-reviewed journal publications and five conference papers were produced during the project period.

SYN-PRJ-0850.title: Evaluating Long-Term Effectiveness of Quality Management System Implementations in Serbian Manufacturing
SYN-PRJ-0850.text:
QMSEVAL: Evaluating Long-Term Effectiveness of Quality Management System Implementations in Serbian Manufacturing (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0104 principal investigator; R0035 team member; R0988 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade; Serbian Chamber of Commerce – Association of Manufacturers.
QMSEVAL is a longitudinal study tracking operational and financial performance outcomes in 60 Serbian manufacturing SMEs across three years following ISO 9001 certification or recertification. The project applies a repeated-measures design with annual data collection combining company records, structured manager interviews, and external audit documentation. Analysis focuses on identifying factors that sustain post-certification performance gains versus those associated with performance drift. Secondary objectives include the development of a predictive model for post-certification performance and the validation of a composite performance index against independent financial audit data. The project supports one doctoral student and collaborates with the Faculty of Organizational Sciences, Belgrade, on survey design and data analysis.

SYN-PRJ-0992.title: Legibility Standards for Age-Inclusive Hospital Signage in Cross-Border Healthcare Facilities
SYN-PRJ-0992.text:
SIGN-AGE: Legibility Standards for Age-Inclusive Hospital Signage in Cross-Border Healthcare Facilities (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2023).
Participants: R0041 coordinator.
Partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia; County Hospital Bács-Kiskun, Kecskemét, Hungary; University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary.
The project addressed the lack of harmonised age-inclusive wayfinding standards in cross-border healthcare contexts between Serbia and Hungary. Activities included legibility testing of symbol–text combinations with older adult participants at partner hospitals on both sides of the border, development of a shared design specification document, and production of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) signage template package. The project also delivered training workshops for facilities managers at four hospitals. The University of Novi Sad team led the perceptual testing work package and coordinated production of the final guideline document. The project resulted in a tested and piloted sign system implemented in one hospital facility in each country.

SYN-PRJ-0993.title: Towards a National Guideline for Wayfinding Sign Systems in Serbian Public Healthcare Facilities
SYN-PRJ-0993.text:
WAYFIND-RS: Towards a National Guideline for Wayfinding Sign Systems in Serbian Public Healthcare Facilities (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0041 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Oncology of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica; Institute for Standardisation of Serbia, Belgrade.
This project compiles empirical legibility data across a range of target user groups, lighting conditions, and sign configurations encountered in Serbian public hospitals, with the goal of generating evidence-based minimum requirements for a national guideline. The research programme includes field audits of 20 hospital facilities, controlled laboratory experiments on type size, symbol design, colour contrast, and material reflectance, and an extended consultation process with the Serbian Chamber of Engineers and the Ministry of Health. A draft guideline document is under preparation for submission to the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia as a basis for a national pre-standard.

SYN-PRJ-1392.title: Rational Solid-Form Selection for Poorly Soluble APIs: Integrated Screening and Scale-Up Workflows
SYN-PRJ-1392.text:
SOLIDFORM: Rational Solid-Form Selection for Poorly Soluble APIs: Integrated Screening and Scale-Up Workflows (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0151 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Belgrade; Farmaceutski Zavod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner).
The project established a tiered screening workflow integrating computational co-former selection (hydrogen-bond propensity and complementary functionality scoring) with experimental LAG, solution, and spray-drying screening for five poorly soluble APIs provided by a local formulation company. Characterisation relied on in-house PXRD, DSC-TGA, and Raman mapping, supplemented by access to solid-state NMR at a partner facility. Successful co-crystals were scaled to 50–100 g by twin-screw extrusion and assessed for dissolution improvement and physical stability under ICH storage conditions. The project trained two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed papers and three conference contributions.

SYN-PRJ-1710.title: Weld Condition Monitoring in Industrial Steel Structures Using Low-Cost Sensor Networks
SYN-PRJ-1710.text:
WELDMON: Weld Condition Monitoring in Industrial Steel Structures Using Low-Cost Sensor Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0666 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade; Kovinarstvo Petrović d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project aimed to develop and field-test a practical SHM system specifically targeting weld fatigue damage in industrial steel structures. Activities included laboratory fatigue testing of representative weld joint geometries, development of automated OMA routines for edge-computing hardware, and 18-month deployments on two real industrial structures (a crane girder and a mezzanine frame) in Vojvodina. The project produced sensor placement guidelines, an open-source data processing pipeline, and a damage detection threshold framework accounting for temperature and operational load variability. Four journal papers, one conference paper, and a technical guideline document were produced. Two MSc students completed their theses within the project.

SYN-PUB-00215.title: Delta-of-Delta Encoding for Monotonic Sensor Counters in Relational Column Stores
SYN-PUB-00215.text:
Delta-of-Delta Encoding for Monotonic Sensor Counters in Relational Column Stores (2013, journal, Novi Sad Journal of Computing and Information Science).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Miroslav Topalović (outside co-author).
Keywords: delta encoding; monotonic counters; columnar storage; compression ratio.
Monotonic counter sequences produced by industrial pulse sensors exhibit strong first-order and second-order differences that standard LZ-family compressors exploit poorly when applied at the row level. This paper evaluates a purely arithmetic delta-of-delta scheme applied within a columnar storage engine on sequences of 32-bit unsigned integers sampled at 1 kHz. Experiments use 14 days of vibration counter data from a water-treatment facility logging 48 sensor channels, yielding roughly 58 billion raw values. The scheme is compared against Snappy, LZ4, and a Gorilla-style float codec adapted for integers. Delta-of-delta achieves a compression ratio of 18.3:1 against raw binary, outperforming LZ4 (11.1:1) with 40 % lower decompression CPU time. Encoding throughput on a single core reaches 920 MB/s. The paper also derives a closed-form bound on the representable range for a fixed bit-width delta register and proposes a lightweight overflow-detection branch that adds under 2 % latency overhead.

SYN-PUB-00216.title: Bitmap Index Compression Trade-offs for Low-Cardinality Attributes in Time-Series Tables
SYN-PUB-00216.text:
Bitmap Index Compression Trade-offs for Low-Cardinality Attributes in Time-Series Tables (2015, conference, Central European Workshop on Databases and Information Systems (CEWDIS)).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Miroslav Topalović (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author); Ondřej Blaha (outside co-author).
Keywords: bitmap index; Roaring Bitmaps; low-cardinality; time-series tables.
Bitmap indexes over low-cardinality categorical attributes are common in data-warehouse workloads, but their behaviour on append-only time-series tables with frequent partial scans has received less attention. We compare uncompressed bitmaps, WAH (Word-Aligned Hybrid), CONCISE, and Roaring Bitmaps on synthetic and real sensor-classification workloads where cardinality ranges from 4 to 256 distinct values and table sizes range from 10 million to 2 billion rows. Real data come from a Serbian environmental monitoring network logging air-quality sensor states at 10-second intervals over 18 months across 31 stations. Roaring Bitmaps reduce index size by 55–72 % relative to WAH while maintaining AND/OR operation throughput within 8 % of uncompressed bitmaps for selective queries. We identify a crossover point at cardinality 64 above which WAH outperforms Roaring in sequential full-scan aggregation. Query plans that choose index type adaptively based on observed cardinality at load time reduce total query time by 23 % in the mixed workload benchmark.

SYN-PUB-00217.title: Columnar Storage Layout for Mixed-Rate Sensor Streams: Alignment, Padding, and Scan Cost
SYN-PUB-00217.text:
Columnar Storage Layout for Mixed-Rate Sensor Streams: Alignment, Padding, and Scan Cost (2016, book chapter, Advances in Industrial Data Engineering, Springer Series on Data Management (invented)).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Katarina Jovanović (outside co-author); Sven Lindqvist (outside co-author).
Keywords: mixed-rate sensors; columnar layout; scan cost; schema design.
Industrial sensor networks rarely emit all channels at a uniform rate. A pressure transducer may log at 100 Hz while a thermal sensor logs at 1 Hz, creating mixed-rate column groups within a single logical schema. Storing such streams in a uniform columnar layout either wastes space through padding or requires indirection structures that slow scans. This chapter surveys three physical layout strategies—uniform-stride padding, epoch-grouped variable-stride, and separate per-rate column families—and analyses their scan cost analytically and experimentally. Experiments use a 90-day dataset of 112 sensor channels from a pilot manufacturing line at 14 distinct sampling rates, totalling 430 GB uncompressed. Epoch-grouped variable-stride achieves the best compromise: 31 % less storage than uniform-stride padding with scan overhead under 6 % compared to single-rate baselines. Practical guidelines for schema designers are derived, including a heuristic for grouping channels into rate classes.

SYN-PUB-00218.title: Efficient SUM and AVG Aggregation Over Compressed Integer Columns Without Full Decompression
SYN-PUB-00218.text:
Efficient SUM and AVG Aggregation Over Compressed Integer Columns Without Full Decompression (2018, conference, International Symposium on Data Engineering and Management (ISDEM)).
Authors: Katarina Jovanović (outside co-author); Tibor Fekete (outside co-author); Petar Hadžić (R0019).
Keywords: in-database aggregation; partial decompression; delta coding; SUM aggregation; cache pressure.
Computing SUM and AVG over delta-compressed integer columns typically requires full decompression before the arithmetic pass. We present a method that accumulates partial sums directly over delta-coded blocks by exploiting the algebraic structure of prefix-sum reconstruction, reducing decompression to the final carry-propagation step. The technique is implemented inside a fork of an open-source columnar engine (DuckDB-compatible file format) and evaluated on six months of electricity sub-metering data at 1-second resolution across 200 household circuits, approximately 31 billion rows. End-to-end SUM throughput increases by 1.8× on a single core and 2.1× on four cores compared to decompress-then-aggregate. The method generalises to COUNT DISTINCT with HyperLogLog sketches embedded in compressed blocks, yielding a 1.4× speedup there. Memory bandwidth measurements confirm that savings come primarily from reduced cache pressure rather than reduced arithmetic.

SYN-PUB-00219.title: Adaptive Bit-Packing Width Selection for High-Frequency Accelerometer Streams
SYN-PUB-00219.text:
Adaptive Bit-Packing Width Selection for High-Frequency Accelerometer Streams (2019, journal, Novi Sad Journal of Computing and Information Science).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Nemanja Dragić (outside co-author).
Keywords: bit-packing; accelerometer; adaptive compression; SIMD; vibration data.
Fixed-width bit-packing assigns the same bit-width to every value in a block, wasting bits when the dynamic range is temporarily narrow. We propose a lightweight adaptive scheme that re-estimates the required bit-width every 512 values using a running maximum register and encodes the width in a 6-bit block header. The scheme targets 16-bit signed accelerometer samples recorded at 4 kHz. A corpus of 22 hours of vibration data from rotating machinery in a Serbian food-processing plant (seven machine types, 63 sensors) is used for evaluation. Adaptive bit-packing reduces storage by 19–34 % relative to fixed 16-bit packing and by 9–17 % relative to fixed optimal-width packing computed offline. Decompression speed on SSE4.2 SIMD instructions remains within 4 % of fixed-width scalar decompression. We also report failure modes when the running maximum underestimates abrupt transients and propose a saturating-rollback mechanism.

SYN-PUB-00220.title: Zone Maps vs. Min-Max Indexes in Columnar Engines: Behaviour Under Skewed Sensor Value Distributions
SYN-PUB-00220.text:
Zone Maps vs. Min-Max Indexes in Columnar Engines: Behaviour Under Skewed Sensor Value Distributions (2021, conference, Balkan Conference on Data Management and Analytics (BCDMA)).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author); Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: zone maps; min-max index; block pruning; skewed distributions; columnar engines.
Zone maps (per-block min-max metadata) are a standard pruning mechanism in columnar databases, but their effectiveness degrades when value distributions within blocks are highly skewed or multi-modal, which is common in sensor streams that include fault and alarm states. We characterise the pruning rate of zone maps analytically as a function of block size and intra-block value variance and validate the model on four real sensor datasets: river-level gauges, photovoltaic panel voltage logs, industrial pressure manifolds, and HVAC temperature arrays. Block sizes of 512 to 65536 values are tested. For multi-modal distributions the pruning rate drops below 30 % even at block size 512. We evaluate two lightweight alternatives—quantile sketches and learned min-max predictors trained on preceding blocks—and find that a 7-quantile sketch stored in 28 bytes per block restores pruning rates to above 70 % at a metadata overhead of 0.03 % of raw data size. Implementation notes for integration into an open-source columnar engine are provided.

SYN-PUB-00221.title: Compression-Aware Query Planning for Time-Bounded Window Aggregations
SYN-PUB-00221.text:
Compression-Aware Query Planning for Time-Bounded Window Aggregations (2022, journal, Journal of Data and Storage Engineering (invented)).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Nemanja Dragić (outside co-author); Tibor Fekete (outside co-author); Sven Lindqvist (outside co-author).
Keywords: window aggregation; query planning; cost model; columnar storage; time-series.
Time-bounded window aggregations (e.g., SUM over the last 15 minutes) on append-only sensor tables require accessing a suffix of one or more compressed blocks. The query planner must decide whether to decompress an entire boundary block or to seek within it, a choice that depends on block size, compression codec, and selectivity. We formalise this as a cost model parameterised by measured decompression throughput, seek latency, and block fill factor, and integrate it into a rule-based planner for a columnar storage engine. Evaluation uses six months of power-grid sensor data at 500 Hz from a regional substation, with window widths ranging from 1 second to 24 hours. The cost-model-guided planner reduces query latency by 28–41 % over a baseline that always decompresses full boundary blocks, and by 12–18 % over a simpler heuristic that always seeks. The model's calibration requires a 90-second profiling pass run once at database initialisation.

SYN-PUB-00222.title: On-Disk Representation of Irregular-Timestamp Sensor Logs: Separating Time and Value Columns
SYN-PUB-00222.text:
On-Disk Representation of Irregular-Timestamp Sensor Logs: Separating Time and Value Columns (2024, journal, Novi Sad Journal of Computing and Information Science).
Authors: Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Petar Hadžić (R0019).
Keywords: irregular timestamps; columnar layout; Gorilla encoding; IoT sensors; Vojvodina.
Most time-series storage literature assumes uniform sampling intervals, so timestamp columns are stored implicitly as a start time plus stride. Environmental and IoT sensors with event-driven reporting produce irregular timestamps that must be stored explicitly. We study the compression and scan-performance implications of separating timestamp columns from value columns on disk versus interleaving them. Three physical layouts are compared on a 14-month dataset of soil-moisture readings from 180 field sensors distributed across Vojvodina, Serbia, with inter-arrival times varying from 30 seconds to 45 minutes. Separating columns allows timestamp and value codecs to be chosen independently; Gorilla-style XOR encoding for floating-point values combined with FOR (Frame of Reference) encoding for microsecond-resolution timestamps reduces combined storage by 26 % relative to interleaved LZ4. Random-access latency increases by 11 % due to two separate seeks, which is acceptable for analytical workloads but warrants consideration for point-lookup-heavy use cases.

SYN-PUB-00223.title: Benchmarking In-Database Compression Codecs for Sub-Second Rollup Queries on a Single-Node Commodity Server
SYN-PUB-00223.text:
Benchmarking In-Database Compression Codecs for Sub-Second Rollup Queries on a Single-Node Commodity Server (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Data Engineering Practices (EWDEP)).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Nemanja Dragić (outside co-author); Ondřej Blaha (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: codec benchmark; rollup queries; commodity server; PFOR; Zstandard.
Sub-second rollup latency over billion-row sensor tables is achievable on a single commodity server if the codec, block size, and aggregation strategy are matched to the query workload. We construct a reproducible benchmark using publicly available hardware (AMD EPYC 7003, 128 GB DDR4, NVMe SSD) and four synthetic workloads derived from real sensor patterns: smooth analogue signals, step-change switching signals, random noise, and mixed. Eight codecs are tested: LZ4, Zstandard-3, Zstandard-9, Gorilla float, delta-varint, bit-packing, PFOR, and a cascade of delta followed by bit-packing. Rollup query latency, compression ratio, and encode/decode throughput are reported for block sizes of 256, 1024, and 4096 values. Delta+bit-packing on smooth signals achieves 0.38-second rollup over 2 billion rows with a 21:1 ratio. No single codec dominates across all workloads; a decision table mapping signal type to codec is provided. All benchmark code and datasets are released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-00224.title: Predicting Compressibility of Sensor Blocks from Lightweight Signal Statistics
SYN-PUB-00224.text:
Predicting Compressibility of Sensor Blocks from Lightweight Signal Statistics (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint (cs.DB)).
Authors: Petar Hadžić (R0019); Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Slađana Paunović (R0253); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author); Dimitrije Kosanović (R0635).
Keywords: compressibility prediction; codec selection; autocorrelation; signal statistics; write-time optimisation.
Choosing a compression codec at write time without compressing the data first requires a proxy metric that correlates with compression ratio. We evaluate seven lightweight statistics—range, variance, zero-crossing rate, run-length entropy estimate, lag-1 autocorrelation, approximate quantile spread, and bit-reversal entropy—as predictors of final compression ratio for LZ4, Zstandard, delta+PFOR, and Gorilla across a corpus of 4.1 million 1024-value blocks drawn from 11 sensor deployments spanning energy, agriculture, and manufacturing domains. Lag-1 autocorrelation alone achieves a Spearman rank correlation of 0.81 with the delta+PFOR ratio and can be computed in a single pass over a block in under 0.2 µs on the target hardware. A two-feature classifier (autocorrelation + range) correctly routes blocks to the best codec in 73 % of cases, reducing mean storage size by 14 % compared to a fixed-codec policy with no runtime overhead above 1.1 %.

SYN-PUB-00225.title: Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata
SYN-PUB-00225.text:
Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata (2013, journal, Infoteka: Časopis za informatiku i bibliotekarstvo).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Petar Hadžić (R0019).
Keywords: morfološka analiza; stemovanje; višeskriptni tekst; srpski jezik; rangiranje.
Srpski jezik je morfološki bogat, što znači da ista leksema može imati nekoliko desetina flektivnih oblika. U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa. Koristimo tri stemera dostupna za srpski jezik — dva pravilo-zasnovana i jedan statistički — i kombinujemo ih s fonemskim kanonizacionim korakom opisanim u prethodnim radovima. Evaluacija je sprovedena na podskupu CLEF 2012 kolekcije koji sadrži dokumente u oba pisma. Rezultati pokazuju da redosled operacija (stemovanje pre ili posle normalizacije skripte) utiče na odziv, pri čemu stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije (poboljšanje od 4 do 9 procentnih poena u MAP). Rad daje i analizu grešaka za 50 ručno pregledanih upita.

SYN-PUB-00335.title: Signal Attenuation Through Reinforced Concrete Walls at Sub-GHz Frequencies: A Controlled Laboratory Study
SYN-PUB-00335.text:
Signal Attenuation Through Reinforced Concrete Walls at Sub-GHz Frequencies: A Controlled Laboratory Study (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Regional Symposium on Telecommunications and Signal Processing (RSTSP), Belgrade).
Authors: Zorica Milanović (outside co-author); Olivera Kuzmanović (R0028); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: penetration loss; concrete; sub-GHz; link budget; indoor propagation.
Penetration loss through reinforced concrete walls is a critical parameter for indoor and sub-surface LoRa deployments but is rarely characterised under controlled conditions. This study measured insertion loss at 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz through six concrete slab samples with varying aggregate composition and rebar density, obtained from a demolition site in Novi Sad. A vector network analyser with calibrated horn antennas was used in a shielded measurement cell. Median penetration loss at 868 MHz ranged from 14.3 dB for a 15 cm unreinforced slab to 31.7 dB for a 30 cm slab with 12 mm rebar at 10 cm spacing. Frequency dependence followed an approximately linear relationship with slab thickness in the 868–915 MHz band. The results provide material-specific correction factors for use in link budget tools targeting basement and underground infrastructure sensor deployments.

SYN-PUB-00478.title: Co-crystal formation between furosemide and three pyridine derivatives: structural inference from PXRD and Raman spectroscopy in the absence of single-crystal data
SYN-PUB-00478.text:
Co-crystal formation between furosemide and three pyridine derivatives: structural inference from PXRD and Raman spectroscopy in the absence of single-crystal data (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 6th Central European Symposium on Pharmaceutical Technology).
Authors: Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Vasilije Ivković (R0038); Vesna Ilić (outside co-author); Lidija Radić (R0151).
Keywords: furosemide; co-crystal; Raman spectroscopy; PXRD indexing; FaSSIF.
Three co-crystals of furosemide (a poorly soluble loop diuretic) with 2-aminopyridine, 3-hydroxypyridine, and 4,4′-bipyridine were prepared by LAG with acetonitrile and characterised entirely in polycrystalline form. Single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction could not be grown from any of the nine solvent systems attempted. Structural inference relied on indexing of PXRD patterns (DICVOL06 and TREOR90 algorithms), lattice parameter comparison with Cambridge Structural Database entries, and Raman band shifts. The carbonyl stretch of furosemide at 1678 cm⁻¹ shifted to 1663 cm⁻¹ in the 2-aminopyridine co-crystal, consistent with N–H···O hydrogen bonding. Quantitative phase analysis of DSC data confirmed 1:1 stoichiometry for all three co-crystals by molar enthalpy comparison. Dissolution experiments in simulated intestinal fluid (FaSSIF) at 37 °C showed 1.5-, 1.9-, and 1.3-fold increases in maximum dissolved concentration for the three co-crystals, respectively. The 3-hydroxypyridine co-crystal showed a spring-and-parachute effect with maximum concentration maintained for 120 minutes.

SYN-PUB-00488.title: Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbour Retrieval for Embedding-Based Recommenders: A Benchmark on Commodity Hardware
SYN-PUB-00488.text:
Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbour Retrieval for Embedding-Based Recommenders: A Benchmark on Commodity Hardware (2024, journal, Information Retrieval Journal).
Authors: Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Anita Bošnjak (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: approximate nearest neighbour; HNSW; embedding retrieval; two-stage recommendation; scalability.
Two-stage recommenders use approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search to retrieve candidate items from a learned embedding space before a more expensive ranking model re-scores them. We benchmark five ANN index structures—HNSW, IVF-Flat, IVF-PQ, ScaNN, and a flat exact baseline—on three embedding spaces of different dimensionalities (64, 128, 256) and catalogue sizes (50K, 500K, 5M items) using recall@100 and query latency at fixed memory budgets on a single server with 64 GB RAM and no GPU. HNSW achieves the best recall–latency trade-off for catalogues up to 500K items; IVF-PQ becomes competitive at 5M items under 16 GB memory constraints. We also measure how ANN retrieval recall translates to end-to-end NDCG@10 degradation and find that recall@100 above 0.92 causes less than 1% NDCG loss relative to exact retrieval. A practical configuration guide is included.

SYN-PUB-00492.title: Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams
SYN-PUB-00492.text:
Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams (2018, journal, Control Engineering Practice).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: incremental learning; Gaussian mixture model; online detection; concept drift; district heating.
This paper proposes an incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining. The algorithm maintains a fixed number of Gaussian components (K = 5 to 20 evaluated) and uses a Bayesian update rule to adjust component means, covariances, and weights with each arriving window of observations. Feature vectors are 32-dimensional, derived from 10-second traffic windows. The method was evaluated on a 180-day Modbus/TCP capture from a district heating control network and compared with a static GMM retrained every 24 hours. The iGMM maintained an F1 score within 0.03 of the periodically retrained model while reducing retraining compute cost by 94%. Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested. Memory footprint per detector instance was under 120 KB.

SYN-PUB-00493.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection for Legal Document Classifiers: A Study on Serbian Administrative Text
SYN-PUB-00493.text:
Out-of-Distribution Detection for Legal Document Classifiers: A Study on Serbian Administrative Text (2024, journal, Expert Systems with Applications).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Jelena Đurić (outside co-author); Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Kristina Ilić (R0960); Claudia Neumann (outside co-author).
Keywords: out-of-distribution detection; legal NLP; classifier calibration; energy score; administrative text.
Classifiers deployed in production legal systems regularly encounter documents that belong to no category in the training taxonomy—newly enacted law types, atypical procedural forms, or documents from adjacent domains. This paper studies out-of-distribution (OOD) detection as a complement to standard closed-set classification in the context of Serbian administrative law. Seven OOD detection methods are evaluated: maximum softmax probability, ODIN, Mahalanobis distance, energy-based scoring, a Monte Carlo dropout ensemble, a deep ensemble, and a one-class neural baseline. Evaluation uses an in-distribution set of 6,400 administrative decisions across 16 categories and four OOD sets of increasing distance from the in-distribution. At a 95% true-positive rate threshold, energy-based scoring and the Mahalanobis method perform best, achieving AUROC values of 0.91 and 0.89 respectively. The paper discusses calibration of classifier confidence scores as a prerequisite for reliable OOD thresholding in production deployments.

SYN-PUB-00509.title: Legibility thresholds of directional arrows in hospital corridor signage: a controlled viewing-distance study
SYN-PUB-00509.text:
Legibility thresholds of directional arrows in hospital corridor signage: a controlled viewing-distance study (2010, journal, Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design).
Authors: Milena Vranić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Milica Ostojić (R0290).
Keywords: directional arrows; legibility distance; stroke width; illuminance; hospital signage.
This study measured the critical viewing distance at which 42 adult participants could correctly identify seven directional arrow variants used in Serbian public hospital signage. Stimuli were printed on matte substrates and presented under three illuminance levels (50 lx, 150 lx, and 500 lx) in a light-tight chamber. Arrow width-to-height ratio, stroke width, and arrowhead angle were varied systematically across 21 design conditions. Participants identified the direction of travel indicated by each arrow from distances ranging from 1 m to 18 m in 0.5 m increments. Results showed that reducing stroke width below 12% of symbol height caused identification accuracy to drop below 90% at distances exceeding 8 m even at 500 lx. Arrowhead angles between 40° and 55° yielded the highest identification rates across all illuminance levels. Recommendations for minimum stroke width and arrowhead geometry are proposed for standardisation within hospital wayfinding guidelines in Serbia.

SYN-PUB-00510.title: Pictogram comprehension across age groups in a tertiary care hospital in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-00510.text:
Pictogram comprehension across age groups in a tertiary care hospital in Vojvodina (2012, journal, Applied Ergonomics and Design).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Marija Čolić (R0325); Katalin Fehér (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: pictogram comprehension; age groups; ISO 7001; healthcare pictograms; text–symbol pairing.
The study assessed comprehension rates of 30 ISO 7001 transport and healthcare-related pictograms among three age groups (18–35, 36–59, 60–79 years; n = 180 total, 60 per group) recruited in the waiting areas of a large regional hospital. Participants were shown each pictogram individually on a calibrated tablet display at a standardised ambient luminance of 200 cd/m² and asked to state its meaning without any contextual cues. A second session introduced a bilingual Serbian–Hungarian text label beneath the symbol. Comprehension scores without labels averaged 58% for the 60–79 age group compared to 79% for the 18–35 group. Adding text labels raised overall comprehension to 91% but reduced the benefit specifically for pictograms with ambiguous spatial relationships. Sixteen pictograms fell below the ISO-recommended 67% comprehension threshold when tested without labels in the oldest group. The findings support mandatory text pairing in wayfinding applications targeting mixed-age hospital populations.

SYN-PUB-00512.title: Contrast sensitivity and sign character recognition in adults aged 65 and older: implications for minimum type size in healthcare wayfinding
SYN-PUB-00512.text:
Contrast sensitivity and sign character recognition in adults aged 65 and older: implications for minimum type size in healthcare wayfinding (2015, journal, Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design).
Authors: Vesna Petrović (outside co-author); Maja Grubić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Marina Stevanović (R0862).
Keywords: contrast sensitivity; type size; mesopic conditions; older adults; sans-serif legibility.
Contrast sensitivity functions (CSFs) were measured for 68 adults aged 65–84 using a sinusoidal grating test under photopic (300 lx) and mesopic (5 lx) conditions. The same participants then completed a character recognition task with uppercase sans-serif text (Helvetica Neue LT Pro 55 Roman and 75 Bold weights) at sizes ranging from 12 mm to 80 mm cap height, presented on matte white signage-grade substrate at contrast ratios of 4.5:1 and 8:1. CSF peak sensitivity at mesopic luminance was on average 0.41 log units lower than at photopic luminance across the group. A type size of 40 mm cap height at 8:1 contrast achieved 95% correct identification at a 5 m viewing distance under mesopic conditions. Below 25 mm at 4.5:1 contrast, accuracy dropped below 80% even at 3 m. Recommendations are formulated for minimum type sizes in hospital corridor and lift-lobby signage where night-time lighting is reduced.

SYN-PUB-00514.title: Symbol–text spatial arrangement and reading order in bilingual hospital signage: Serbian and Hungarian side-by-side layouts
SYN-PUB-00514.text:
Symbol–text spatial arrangement and reading order in bilingual hospital signage: Serbian and Hungarian side-by-side layouts (2017, journal, Information Design Journal).
Authors: Annamária Szűcs (outside co-author); Milena Vranić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: bilingual signage; symbol placement; eye tracking; Serbian; Hungarian; reading order.
Healthcare facilities in the Vojvodina region of Serbia are legally required to provide bilingual signage in Serbian and Hungarian in municipalities where the Hungarian community exceeds 15% of the population. This study examined how the spatial arrangement of a pictogram relative to bilingual text blocks affects reading speed and comprehension. Forty subjects with Serbian as their first language and 40 with Hungarian as their first language completed timed reading tasks for six layout configurations varying the symbol position (left, right, above text) and the ordering of the two language text blocks. Eye-tracking data were collected using a remote eye tracker at 60 Hz. Symbol-left placement with Serbian text on top produced the fastest mean fixation-to-decision time (1.8 s) for Serbian-dominant readers, while Hungarian-dominant readers showed no statistically significant preference for language ordering. Results inform a bilingual signage template for healthcare facilities in the region.

SYN-PUB-00515.title: Retroreflective materials for emergency egress signage: luminance uniformity measurements in reduced-power lighting scenarios
SYN-PUB-00515.text:
Retroreflective materials for emergency egress signage: luminance uniformity measurements in reduced-power lighting scenarios (2018, journal, Lighting Research and Building Science).
Authors: Đorđe Milovanović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: retroreflective materials; emergency signage; luminance uniformity; egress signs; low illuminance.
Emergency egress signs in hospitals are required to remain readable during power failures when only battery-backed emergency lighting operates, typically reducing corridor illuminance to 1–5 lx. This study evaluated four commercially available retroreflective substrate materials (two glass-bead and two microprismatic types) as potential replacements for internally illuminated plastic sign panels. Luminance uniformity and minimum–maximum luminance ratios were measured across each substrate at five incidence angles (0°, 10°, 20°, 30°, 45°) under a 2 lx emergency lighting simulation using a standardised LED emergency luminaire. Microprismatic materials maintained luminance uniformity ratios above 0.65 at incidence angles up to 20°, while glass-bead materials dropped below 0.40 beyond 10°. A practical assessment protocol using portable luminance meters is described, enabling facilities managers to evaluate installed retroreflective signs without laboratory equipment. Limitations related to specular reflections from polished floor surfaces are discussed.

SYN-PUB-00516.title: Information hierarchy and sign density at decision points in hospital wayfinding: a subjective workload study
SYN-PUB-00516.text:
Information hierarchy and sign density at decision points in hospital wayfinding: a subjective workload study (2019, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Information Design, Novi Sad).
Authors: Branislav Jović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Maja Grubić (outside co-author); Petra Hanáková (outside co-author).
Keywords: information hierarchy; sign density; decision points; NASA-TLX; virtual environment simulation.
Excessive sign density at navigational decision points has been identified anecdotally as a source of confusion, but empirical data on information load thresholds remain sparse. Sixty participants navigated a hospital corridor simulation rendered in a 3-D virtual environment displayed on a large-format monitor. Sign panels at simulated T-junctions contained between 2 and 10 destination entries, with sub-experiments varying font size, colour-coding, and arrow orientation. NASA-TLX subscale scores for mental demand and frustration increased significantly when entry count exceeded six (p < 0.01) regardless of colour-coding condition. Response time to select the correct destination increased by an average of 0.32 s per additional entry beyond six. A hierarchical categorisation of destinations into three display tiers (immediate clinical areas, support services, building exits) is proposed as a practical method for managing information density within the six-entry threshold.

SYN-PUB-00517.title: A field evaluation of redesigned wayfinding signs in an oncology centre: before-and-after navigation performance and user satisfaction
SYN-PUB-00517.text:
A field evaluation of redesigned wayfinding signs in an oncology centre: before-and-after navigation performance and user satisfaction (2020, journal, Health Environments Research and Design).
Authors: Ivana Zdravković (outside co-author); Nataša Todorović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: field evaluation; sign system redesign; oncology centre; navigation performance; user satisfaction.
A complete wayfinding sign system was redesigned and installed in a 380-bed oncology centre following a structured design process that incorporated legibility testing and staff consultation. Pre-installation data were collected over three weeks (n = 94 unassisted navigation observations) and post-installation data over three weeks six months after installation (n = 98 observations). The primary outcome was successful unassisted navigation, defined as reaching the stated destination without asking staff for directions or making more than one corrective backtrack. Successful navigation increased from 61% pre-installation to 84% post-installation. Staff reported a 43% reduction in wayfinding-related questions from patients and visitors based on a structured log kept by reception personnel. Patient satisfaction survey scores related to ease of finding one's way increased by 1.4 points on a 7-point Likert scale. The study describes the design process, testing methodology, and implementation logistics.

SYN-PUB-00518.title: Floor-level and ceiling-level wayfinding cues: visibility from wheelchair and walking-frame user eye heights
SYN-PUB-00518.text:
Floor-level and ceiling-level wayfinding cues: visibility from wheelchair and walking-frame user eye heights (2021, journal, Universal Access in the Built Environment).
Authors: Tatjana Spasojević Brkić (outside co-author); Ana Todorović (R0760); Ildikó Papp (R0626); Jelena Korać (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: wheelchair users; sign installation height; universal access; detection distance; mobility aids.
Standard-height wall-mounted signage is designed for standing adult eye heights (approximately 1.55–1.70 m) and may be partially or fully outside the useful visual field of wheelchair users (eye height approximately 1.20 m) and walking-frame users who adopt a forward-inclined posture (functional eye height approximately 0.95–1.10 m). This study measured detection and identification distances for wall-mounted signs at three installation heights (1.0 m, 1.5 m, 2.1 m) for 22 wheelchair users and 18 walking-frame users recruited at rehabilitation and geriatric wards. Detection distance for signs at 1.0 m was significantly greater for wheelchair users than for walking-frame users (p = 0.008). Floor-applied vinyl wayfinding strips were also tested; identification of the destination label was not possible beyond 2.5 m for any participant group due to perspective distortion. Dual-height mounting at 1.0 m and 1.5 m is recommended for facilities serving high proportions of mobility-impaired users.

SYN-PUB-00519.title: Typeface weight and stroke modulation effects on character recognition under simulated cataract contrast reduction
SYN-PUB-00519.text:
Typeface weight and stroke modulation effects on character recognition under simulated cataract contrast reduction (2022, journal, Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design).
Authors: Maja Grubić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Laura Bennetti (outside co-author).
Keywords: typeface selection; stroke modulation; cataract simulation; contrast sensitivity loss; character recognition.
Cataract-related vision impairment reduces contrast sensitivity rather than acuity, making it a useful model for testing signage under age-related conditions. Using a cataract simulation filter (Neuro-Vision CatSim 2 goggles, calibrated to approximately 0.3 log unit loss at 3 cycles/degree), 55 participants aged 22–40 with normal acuity completed character identification tasks for eight typefaces varying in stroke weight (thin, regular, medium, bold, extrabold) and modulation (low-modulation grotesks versus high-modulation humanist sans-serifs). Text was presented at a fixed cap height of 35 mm at 5 m on matte-white signage substrate at 180 lx. Bold and extrabold weight variants of low-modulation grotesks achieved identification accuracy above 93% under the cataract filter; thin and regular weights of high-modulation humanist faces fell below 75%. The results suggest that stroke modulation is a more critical parameter than weight alone for users with contrast sensitivity deficits.

SYN-PUB-00520.title: Standardisation gaps in hospital wayfinding sign systems in the Western Balkans: a comparative policy review
SYN-PUB-00520.text:
Standardisation gaps in hospital wayfinding sign systems in the Western Balkans: a comparative policy review (2023, journal, Design Policy and Regulation Studies).
Authors: Emina Hadžimuratović (outside co-author); Branislav Jović (outside co-author); Vesna Petrović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: wayfinding standards; Western Balkans; healthcare regulation; ISO 7001; policy comparison.
This paper reviews existing technical standards, building regulations, and national guidelines governing hospital wayfinding signage in six Western Balkan countries (Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania). Regulatory documents were collected through national standards institutes and ministry of health websites; interviews were conducted with eight hospital facility managers across the region. No country in the survey has a dedicated national standard for healthcare wayfinding; applicable requirements are scattered across fire safety codes, accessibility legislation, and voluntary quality frameworks. The ISO 7001 pictogram standard has been formally adopted in Serbia and Croatia but not in the remaining four countries. Significant variation exists in minimum contrast, type size, and symbol size requirements across the jurisdictions that do specify such values. The paper identifies the most consequential gaps and discusses pathways toward a regional harmonised guideline, drawing on comparisons with German DIN and UK NHS wayfinding standards.

SYN-PUB-00521.title: Dynamic digital wayfinding displays in hospital entrance lobbies: update frequency and motion effects on older adult legibility
SYN-PUB-00521.text:
Dynamic digital wayfinding displays in hospital entrance lobbies: update frequency and motion effects on older adult legibility (2024, journal, Applied Ergonomics and Design).
Authors: Jelena Korać (outside co-author); Ralf Schindler (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: digital displays; dynamic content; older adults; legibility; dwell time; hospital lobby.
Digital display panels are increasingly used as directory boards in hospital lobbies, with content cycling through multiple screens or using scrolling text. This study examined how content update frequency (static, 5 s cycle, 3 s cycle, continuous scroll at 40 px/s) affected legibility and task completion for 44 adults aged 65–80 and 44 adults aged 25–40. Participants were asked to locate a named destination on a digital directory panel at a standardised distance of 3.5 m.
