Task completion rate for older adults fell from 91% on static displays to 54% on 3-second cycled displays and to 29% on continuously scrolled content. Younger adults showed no significant difference across cycle frequencies but performed below 80% on continuous scroll. Fixation duration data from remote eye tracking showed that older adults required at least 4.2 s of stable display time to complete a single read. Recommendations for minimum dwell times and motion-free zones in digital hospital directory design are proposed.

SYN-PUB-00522.title: Colour-zone coding systems in hospital wayfinding: memorability and navigation efficiency in a multi-storey building simulation
SYN-PUB-00522.text:
Colour-zone coding systems in hospital wayfinding: memorability and navigation efficiency in a multi-storey building simulation (2025, conference, Proceedings of the 15th European Symposium on Wayfinding Research, Ljubljana).
Authors: Ivana Zdravković (outside co-author); Annamária Szűcs (outside co-author); Đorđe Milovanović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: colour-zone coding; wayfinding; multi-storey hospital; colour vision deficiency; redundant coding.
Colour-zone coding assigns a distinct colour to each functional zone or floor of a hospital, aiming to reduce cognitive load during navigation. This study tested whether participants could correctly associate six colour codes with their corresponding zones after a single briefing exposure, and whether this association aided navigation in a multi-storey virtual building simulation. Seventy-two participants were divided into a colour-coded sign condition and a text-only sign condition. In the virtual building, navigation to six targets was timed and error-counted over three consecutive trials. After three trials, colour-coded condition participants committed fewer wrong-floor errors (mean 0.8 vs. 2.1 per participant) and showed steeper learning curves. However, 18 participants reported colour vision deficiency or difficulty; post-hoc analysis showed their error rates were equivalent across conditions, indicating that colour coding without secondary coding (shape or pattern) provides no benefit for this group. Revised guidelines integrating redundant coding are discussed.

SYN-PUB-00722.title: Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles
SYN-PUB-00722.text:
Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Nina Dimitrijević (R0054).
Keywords: stealthy attacks; autoencoder ensemble; coil-write injection; Modbus; temporal features.
Stealthy coil-write injection attacks modify a small number of PLC output coils at irregular intervals designed to evade detectors sensitive only to rate or volume changes. This paper evaluates temporal autoencoder ensembles—ten autoencoders trained on temporally shuffled subsets of a 60-day Modbus/TCP capture—for detecting such attacks. Each autoencoder receives a 30-dimensional feature vector derived from 5-second windows including coil change frequency, write-to-read ratio per coil address, and inter-write interval statistics. Anomaly scores from ensemble members are aggregated by the maximum rule. Against 240 injected stealthy attack episodes of varying intensity (1 to 8 modified coils per window), the ensemble achieved recall of 0.89 at a false positive rate of 0.8 per hour, compared with 0.64 for a single autoencoder and 0.58 for a static threshold detector. Computational cost of the ensemble was 2.3× that of a single autoencoder, remaining feasible on edge hardware.

SYN-PUB-00754.title: Piecewise-Linear Approximation of ECG Signals Using Adaptive Breakpoint Selection
SYN-PUB-00754.text:
Piecewise-Linear Approximation of ECG Signals Using Adaptive Breakpoint Selection (2013, journal, Journal of Biomedical Signal Analysis).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Pavol Struhár (R0261); Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Dragan Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: ECG compression; piecewise-linear approximation; dynamic programming; wearable.
This paper examines piecewise-linear approximation as a preprocessing stage for ECG compression. A dynamic-programming algorithm selects breakpoints by minimising the sum of squared residuals subject to a maximum reconstruction error bound of 10 µV. Experiments were conducted on 30 records from the PhysioNet MIT-BIH arrhythmia database resampled to 360 Hz. The method achieves an average compression ratio of 4.1:1 at a per-sample root-mean-square error below 8 µV, outperforming fixed-window linear interpolation by approximately 18% in bit rate under identical distortion constraints. Computational cost is O(N log N) per record, making the approach suitable for microcontroller deployment in wearable monitors. The study also evaluates how premature ventricular contractions, which deviate from normal quasi-periodic morphology, affect the breakpoint density and proposes a beat-classification pre-filter that reduces the density penalty for irregular beats by 23%.

SYN-PUB-00755.title: Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings
SYN-PUB-00755.text:
Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings (2015, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Biomedical Engineering and Medical Informatics (SBEMI)).
Authors: Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Ana Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Holter ECG; DCT; beat segmentation; compression ratio; PRD.
Long-term (Holter) ECG recordings present compression challenges because gradual heart-rate drift shifts beat boundaries relative to fixed analysis windows. This work proposes a beat-synchronous discrete cosine transform (DCT) coder in which each beat is individually segmented using a Pan-Tompkins R-peak detector, zero-padded or truncated to a uniform 512-sample frame, and transformed to the DCT domain. Coefficient quantisation thresholds are derived per lead from a short training segment of the same recording, adapting to inter-patient variability. Tested on 18 two-lead 24-hour recordings at 250 Hz sampled at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, the coder achieves a mean compression ratio of 9.3:1 at a percentage root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 1.8%, with diagnostic quality preserved as assessed by two cardiologists. The encoding latency per beat averages 0.4 ms on a standard laptop CPU, confirming real-time feasibility.

SYN-PUB-00756.title: Wavelet Packet Decomposition for Compression of Neonatal EEG with Burst-Suppression Patterns
SYN-PUB-00756.text:
Wavelet Packet Decomposition for Compression of Neonatal EEG with Burst-Suppression Patterns (2016, journal, Signal, Image and Data Compression Letters).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Jelena Graovac (outside co-author); Klaus Binder (outside co-author).
Keywords: EEG compression; burst-suppression; wavelet packet; best-basis; neonatal.
Neonatal EEG with burst-suppression (BS) patterns has highly non-stationary quasi-periodicity that challenges standard EEG compressors tuned to adult signals. This study applies wavelet packet decomposition with adaptive basis selection via the best-basis algorithm, followed by run-length and Huffman coding of thresholded coefficients. The degree of non-stationarity is quantified by a burst-ratio metric computed over 10-second epochs, and the decomposition depth is adjusted accordingly. A dataset of 22 neonatal eight-channel recordings (duration 2–4 hours each, sampled at 256 Hz) was provided by the Institute for Child and Youth Health Care of Vojvodina. At a reconstruction SNR of 30 dB, the adaptive scheme achieves a compression ratio of 6.8:1 compared to 4.9:1 for a fixed-depth packet transform, a gain attributed primarily to more efficient representation of suppression epochs. No statistically significant difference in burst detection sensitivity was found between original and reconstructed signals using an automated BS detector.

SYN-PUB-00757.title: Exploiting Inter-Beat Redundancy in ECG Compression via Differential Pulse-Code Modulation of DCT Coefficients
SYN-PUB-00757.text:
Exploiting Inter-Beat Redundancy in ECG Compression via Differential Pulse-Code Modulation of DCT Coefficients (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Coding and Compression).
Authors: Klaus Binder (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Dragan Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: inter-beat redundancy; DPCM; DCT; arithmetic coding; atrial fibrillation.
Consecutive cardiac beats in sinus rhythm show high morphological similarity, so their DCT coefficient sequences are strongly correlated across time. This paper models each lead's DCT coefficient track as a first-order autoregressive process and applies differential pulse-code modulation (DPCM) along the beat index rather than within a single beat. A predictor is trained on the first 30 seconds of each record and updated every 60 seconds to track slow morphological drift. Arithmetic coding is applied to the residual with a Laplacian model for the dominant low-frequency coefficients and a Cauchy model for higher-frequency ones. On a corpus of 48 single-lead records at 500 Hz, mean PRD is 1.4% at a compression ratio of 12.7:1, compared to 9.3:1 for independent per-beat DCT coding at matched PRD. The improvement degrades gracefully to 10.1:1 in the presence of atrial fibrillation, where inter-beat morphology is less predictable.

SYN-PUB-00758.title: Sparse Coding of PPG Signals Using a Learned Overcomplete Dictionary
SYN-PUB-00758.text:
Sparse Coding of PPG Signals Using a Learned Overcomplete Dictionary (2019, conference, Biomedical Compression and Coding Workshop (BCCW), Ljubljana).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Marek Kowalski (outside co-author); Milena Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: PPG; sparse coding; K-SVD; overcomplete dictionary; matching pursuit.
Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals share quasi-periodic pulse structure but exhibit waveform variation due to respiratory modulation and motion artefact. This work trains a 256-atom overcomplete dictionary on a 10,000-pulse corpus using the K-SVD algorithm, then encodes each 200-sample pulse segment as a sparse combination of at most eight atoms, with atom indices and coefficients quantised to 8 and 16 bits respectively. A greedy matching pursuit selects atoms sequentially. On a held-out test set of 3,200 pulses from 16 subjects collected with a finger oximeter at 100 Hz, the method achieves a mean reconstruction error of 0.6% PRD at 3.2 bits per sample, compared to 4.1 bits per sample for a 12-coefficient per-pulse DCT coder at the same PRD. Dictionary generalisation across subjects is evaluated; inter-subject PRD increase is 0.3 percentage points on average, suggesting moderate portability without per-subject retraining.

SYN-PUB-00759.title: Compression of Multi-Lead ECG Using Joint Sparsity Across Leads
SYN-PUB-00759.text:
Compression of Multi-Lead ECG Using Joint Sparsity Across Leads (2020, journal, Journal of Biomedical Signal Analysis).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Jelena Graovac (outside co-author); Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: 12-lead ECG; joint sparsity; multi-lead compression; dictionary learning.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-00760.title: Rate-Distortion Analysis of Beat-Aligned Versus Free-Running Frames for ECG Entropy Coding
SYN-PUB-00760.text:
Rate-Distortion Analysis of Beat-Aligned Versus Free-Running Frames for ECG Entropy Coding (2021, journal, Signal Processing: Biomedical Applications).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Dragan Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: rate-distortion; ECG framing; entropy coding; context-adaptive arithmetic coding.
A systematic rate-distortion (R-D) comparison is made between two framing strategies for ECG entropy coding: beat-aligned frames that follow R-peak detection and free-running fixed-length frames of equivalent average duration. For each strategy, DCT coefficients are entropy coded with a context-adaptive arithmetic coder using three coefficient-magnitude context classes. R-D curves are computed at PRD values of 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, and 8% across 60 single-lead records spanning normal sinus rhythm, sinus tachycardia, and first-degree AV block. Beat-aligned framing provides lower bit rates at PRD below 2%—a mean advantage of 0.4 bits per sample—while free-running framing is competitive at higher distortion where the frame-synchronisation overhead of beat detection is not amortised. The crossover PRD and its dependence on heart rate are characterised analytically. The results inform codec design choices in constrained implantable device scenarios.

SYN-PUB-00761.title: Learned Entropy Models for ECG Compression Using Recurrent Context Prediction
SYN-PUB-00761.text:
Learned Entropy Models for ECG Compression Using Recurrent Context Prediction (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Signal and Image Processing (ECSIP), Vienna).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Valentina Risso (outside co-author); Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: learned compression; entropy model; GRU; ECG; neural codec.
Recent learned image compression methods use neural networks to model the entropy of quantised latent representations. This paper adapts that paradigm to single-lead ECG by replacing the standard spatial entropy model with a small gated recurrent unit (GRU) that predicts the probability distribution of each DCT coefficient from the previous 16 coefficients in the same beat and from the corresponding coefficient in the preceding beat, capturing both intra-beat spectral structure and inter-beat temporal redundancy. The GRU has 64 hidden units and is trained jointly with a scalar quantiser on 120 hours of ECG drawn from publicly available databases. At a target PRD of 1.5%, the learned model uses 1.6 bits per sample compared to 2.1 bits per sample for a hand-designed Laplacian arithmetic coder, a 24% reduction. Model size is 48 kB, and decoding runs at 180× real time on a laptop CPU. The paper also analyses failure modes on arrhythmic beats.

SYN-PUB-00762.title: Embedded Coding of Physiological Signals: A Survey of Transform, Sparse, and Learned Approaches
SYN-PUB-00762.text:
Embedded Coding of Physiological Signals: A Survey of Transform, Sparse, and Learned Approaches (2024, book chapter, Advances in Biomedical Data Processing, Vol. 4 (Springer)).
Authors: Klaus Binder (outside co-author); Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Jelena Graovac (outside co-author).
Keywords: survey; ECG; EEG; PPG; transform coding; sparse representation; learned compression.
This chapter surveys compression techniques for ECG, EEG, and PPG signals with emphasis on methods that exploit quasi-periodic structure. The first part covers classical transform-based approaches—DCT, wavelet, and wavelet packet—and their adaptation to beat-aligned or epoch-aligned frames. The second part reviews sparse representation methods, including structured dictionaries and joint multi-channel sparsity. The third part covers learned approaches: variational autoencoders, recurrent entropy models, and hybrid transform-neural architectures published up to early 2024. For each family, representative methods are compared on standardised datasets where available, and compression ratio, PRD, and encoder complexity are tabulated. The chapter also discusses application constraints: energy budgets in implantable devices, latency in real-time telemetry, and regulatory considerations for diagnostic-grade reconstruction. Open problems, including compression under non-stationary arrhythmic conditions and the lack of unified evaluation benchmarks, are identified.

SYN-PUB-00763.title: Variable-Rate Learned ECG Compression with a Single Model via Conditional Quantisation Noise
SYN-PUB-00763.text:
Variable-Rate Learned ECG Compression with a Single Model via Conditional Quantisation Noise (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Valentina Risso (outside co-author).
Keywords: variable-rate compression; conditional quantisation; learned codec; ECG; single model.
Most learned compression models are trained at a fixed rate-distortion tradeoff, requiring separate models per operating point. This preprint proposes a single-model variable-rate ECG codec in which the quantisation noise level is fed as a scalar condition to both the GRU entropy model and a lightweight convolutional synthesis network. The condition scalar is drawn from a uniform grid of 16 values covering PRD targets from 0.5% to 8%. Training uses a weighted sum of rate and distortion losses with the condition scalar randomised each mini-batch. On a held-out test set of 48 single-lead records, the single conditioned model matches or slightly exceeds per-target trained models at all 16 operating points, with a maximum PRD deviation of 0.12 percentage points. Total model footprint is 61 kB, only 27% larger than a single fixed-rate model. Ablations confirm that conditioning the synthesis network is necessary; conditioning only the entropy model reduces the gain by roughly half.

SYN-PUB-00779.title: Benchmarking Balanced Scorecard Adoption Rates and Practices Among Manufacturing SMEs in the Western Balkans: A Survey of 210 Companies
SYN-PUB-00779.text:
Benchmarking Balanced Scorecard Adoption Rates and Practices Among Manufacturing SMEs in the Western Balkans: A Survey of 210 Companies (2023, journal, South-East European Journal of Industrial Management).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Nenad Jakovljević (R0058); Ivana Savić (outside co-author); Sanja Knežević (outside co-author); Bojan Trajkovski (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmarking; balanced scorecard adoption; Western Balkans; SME survey; ISO 9001.
Large-scale survey data on balanced scorecard adoption in the Western Balkans have been absent from the literature, limiting comparative analysis and policy relevance. This paper reports findings from a structured survey of 210 manufacturing SMEs (50–499 employees) across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, conducted in 2021–2022. The questionnaire covered BSC adoption status, number of KPIs monitored, review frequency, software tools used, and the relationship between BSC use and ISO certification status. Adoption rates were 34% in Serbia, 21% in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and 17% in North Macedonia. Among adopters, the average number of tracked KPIs was 18 (SD = 7.4), and financial perspective indicators dominated. Only 38% of adopters reviewed their BSC on a monthly or more frequent basis. Chi-square tests confirm a significant association between BSC adoption and ISO 9001 certification across all three countries. The dataset is publicly available through the Faculty of Technical Sciences repository.

SYN-PUB-00803.title: Kalman-filter-based plausibility checking for soil temperature sensor arrays with heterogeneous failure modes
SYN-PUB-00803.text:
Kalman-filter-based plausibility checking for soil temperature sensor arrays with heterogeneous failure modes (2024, journal, Measurement Science and Sensor Diagnostics).
Authors: Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author); Jana Novotná (outside co-author); Vladan Nedić (R0060); Žarko Ivanović (R0630); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754).
Keywords: Kalman filter; soil temperature; sensor fault isolation; heat diffusion model; edge computation.
Soil temperature arrays deployed at multiple depths are subject to at least four distinct failure modes: complete open-circuit failure, partial short inducing constant-low readings, slow drift from burial-induced mechanical stress on thermistor leads, and intermittent noise injection from nearby electric fence controllers. This paper applies an ensemble Kalman filter to a seven-sensor vertical array, using a one-dimensional heat diffusion model as the process model parameterised with local soil thermal diffusivity estimates. The filter's innovation sequence is monitored with a chi-squared test to isolate faulty sensors without discarding the ensemble. In a 14-month field deployment at two sites in the Banat region, the method identified all 9 sensor faults confirmed by physical inspection, correctly attributed failure mode in 7 of those cases, and continued providing usable profile estimates from the remaining functional sensors throughout each fault episode. The paper also examines computational feasibility on a Cortex-M4 at 80 MHz, where the 7-state filter update completes in 3.8 ms, making edge execution practical with 30-minute sampling.

SYN-PUB-00821.title: Fatigue Life Estimation of Thin-Web Flexure Hinges Under Variable-Amplitude Cyclic Bending
SYN-PUB-00821.text:
Fatigue Life Estimation of Thin-Web Flexure Hinges Under Variable-Amplitude Cyclic Bending (2021, journal, Journal of Fatigue and Fracture of Engineering Materials).
Authors: Jelena Filipović (R0373); Ljiljana Puzović (R0061); Bojan Erić (R0365); Nemanja Zorić (outside co-author); Petra Novak (outside co-author); Bojan Rašković (outside co-author).
Keywords: fatigue life estimation; flexure hinge; rainflow counting; Miner's rule; variable-amplitude loading; spring steel.
Flexure hinges in precision mechanisms are routinely subjected to cyclic loading over millions of cycles, yet most published life estimates rely on constant-amplitude S–N data without accounting for variable-amplitude spectra. This paper applies the rainflow cycle-counting method together with Miner's linear damage rule to estimate the fatigue life of thin-web circular flexure hinges made from two spring steels (X10CrNi18-8 and 42CrMo4) under three representative variable-amplitude bending spectra derived from experimental measurements on a laboratory micro-positioning stage. Finite-element-based stress analysis provides local stress amplitudes at the hinge throat for each counted cycle. Predicted lives ranged from 1.2 × 10⁶ to 8.7 × 10⁷ cycles depending on material and spectrum, with 42CrMo4 outperforming X10CrNi18-8 under the high-mean-stress spectrum by a factor of approximately 3.4. Experimental fatigue tests were conducted on twelve specimens; predicted lives agreed with measured lives within a factor of 2.1 in all cases, consistent with standard engineering fatigue scatter. The study provides a practical workflow for life estimation in the early design stage without requiring dedicated component-level fatigue testing.

SYN-PUB-00958.title: Threshold Selection Strategies for Binary Classifiers Trained on Severely Imbalanced Sensor Data
SYN-PUB-00958.text:
Threshold Selection Strategies for Binary Classifiers Trained on Severely Imbalanced Sensor Data (2013, journal, Journal of Applied Signal Processing and Machine Intelligence).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Dunja Erić (R0890); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: class imbalance; threshold selection; fault detection; sensor data; classification.
Operational sensor logs from industrial machinery frequently exhibit class imbalance ratios exceeding 1:500 between fault and normal states. Standard classifiers trained on such data learn to minimise overall loss by almost entirely ignoring the minority class. This paper evaluates seven threshold-moving strategies—including cost-sensitive calibration, F-beta optimisation, and precision-recall break-even—on four publicly available and two proprietary vibration datasets with imbalance ratios between 1:200 and 1:1200. Experiments use three base classifiers: logistic regression, a gradient-boosted tree, and a one-dimensional convolutional network. Results show that threshold strategies interacting with the base classifier type produce large performance variation: no single strategy dominates across all settings. For the convolutional model, precision-recall break-even consistently achieves the best G-mean scores, while cost-sensitive calibration favours recall at an unacceptable precision cost on the most extreme imbalance cases. Recommendations are given as a decision guide indexed by imbalance ratio and acceptable false-positive rate.

SYN-PUB-00959.title: Comparative Evaluation of Oversampling Techniques for Multivariate Time-Series Fault Classification
SYN-PUB-00959.text:
Comparative Evaluation of Oversampling Techniques for Multivariate Time-Series Fault Classification (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Intelligent Systems (BCIS)).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: oversampling; SMOTE; multivariate time-series; fault classification; AUPRC.
Synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) and its variants were originally designed for tabular data and do not respect temporal dependencies present in multivariate sensor streams. This paper compares six oversampling methods—SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, TimeGAN-based synthesis, DTW-barycentric averaging, and a simple window-jitter baseline—on three industrial datasets: hydraulic pump telemetry, CNC spindle vibration, and electrical substation load measurements. Each dataset is split chronologically to avoid leakage, and ten-fold cross-validation is applied within the training segment. Evaluation uses area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) and macro F1. DTW-barycentric averaging achieves the highest AUPRC on the two vibration datasets (0.84 and 0.79 respectively) but underperforms TimeGAN on the load dataset. Window jitter, despite its simplicity, ranks third overall and substantially outperforms standard SMOTE in all tested settings, suggesting that temporal coherence is more important than interpolation sophistication for most fault types.

SYN-PUB-00960.title: A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information
SYN-PUB-00960.text:
A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information (2018, journal, Pattern Recognition and Data Analysis).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author).
Keywords: one-class SVM; semi-supervised learning; anomaly detection; partial labels; constraint optimisation.
In many industrial monitoring scenarios, operators can label a small fraction of anomalous events while the majority of the data stream remains unlabelled. Standard one-class SVM (OC-SVM) ignores partial labels entirely; this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation. The method is evaluated on four datasets: bearing degradation signals, network intrusion logs, medical ECG records with annotated arrhythmia bursts, and a synthetic benchmark with controlled sparsity of positive labels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). At 5% label density, the constrained OC-SVM reduces false-negative rate by 18 percentage points relative to the unconstrained baseline without statistically significant change in false-positive rate. The framework adds a single hyperparameter controlling constraint weight and remains tractable for datasets up to 500,000 samples with an RBF kernel. Ablation studies confirm that gains diminish beyond 15% label density, at which point a supervised SVM becomes preferable.

SYN-PUB-00961.title: Detecting Concept Drift in Streaming Fault Data Using Adaptive Windowing and Classifier Ensemble Voting
SYN-PUB-00961.text:
Detecting Concept Drift in Streaming Fault Data Using Adaptive Windowing and Classifier Ensemble Voting (2019, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Data Streams).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071); Katarina Jovanović (outside co-author); Lukas Bauer (outside co-author).
Keywords: concept drift; ADWIN; ensemble learning; streaming data; gas compressor monitoring.
Industrial processes evolve over time due to wear, seasonal variation, and deliberate operational changes, causing the statistical properties of sensor streams to shift. Classifiers trained on historical data degrade silently when such drift occurs. This work applies ADWIN-based adaptive windowing to trigger retraining of a rotating ensemble of gradient-boosted classifiers on a gas compressor monitoring stream collected over 26 months. Three types of artificial concept drift—sudden, gradual, and recurrent—are injected into a held-out test segment and detection latency is measured. ADWIN combined with ensemble voting detects sudden drift with a median latency of 47 samples and gradual drift with a latency of 190 samples, compared to 620 samples for a non-adaptive baseline. Memory overhead is bounded by retaining at most five ensemble members. The study also documents four naturally occurring drifts identified in the real 26-month log, correlating two of them with documented maintenance events.

SYN-PUB-00962.title: Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data
SYN-PUB-00962.text:
Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data (2021, journal, Expert Systems with Applications and Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Sanja Kovačević (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071).
Keywords: self-training; pseudo-labelling; Monte Carlo dropout; uncertainty estimation; semi-supervised learning.
Self-training iteratively assigns pseudo-labels to unlabelled samples and retrains a classifier, but in highly imbalanced settings pseudo-label noise disproportionately corrupts the minority class. This paper introduces an uncertainty filter based on prediction entropy estimated through Monte Carlo dropout: only samples whose entropy falls below a calibrated threshold enter the pseudo-labelled pool. The method is tested on three high-dimensional datasets (128 to 512 features) derived from chemical reactor sensors, semiconductor fabrication metrology, and server performance counters, all with imbalance ratios above 1:300. Starting from 2% labelled data, the filtered self-training approach reaches 91% of fully supervised F1 performance on the chemical reactor dataset, compared to 74% for standard self-training. Runtime scales linearly in dataset size and does not require architectural changes beyond enabling dropout at inference time. A sensitivity analysis over the entropy threshold is provided.

SYN-PUB-00963.title: Benchmarking Real-Time Anomaly Detection Pipelines on Edge Hardware Under Memory and Latency Constraints
SYN-PUB-00963.text:
Benchmarking Real-Time Anomaly Detection Pipelines on Edge Hardware Under Memory and Latency Constraints (2022, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Embedded Machine Learning (EWEML)).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Nikola Đurić (outside co-author); María Ortega Blanco (outside co-author); Petar Stevanović (R0833).
Keywords: edge inference; real-time anomaly detection; model quantisation; FPGA; SCADA.
Deploying anomaly detection at the network edge requires balancing model accuracy against strict memory budgets and latency targets. This paper profiles eight detection pipelines—including isolation forest, lightweight autoencoder, quantised convolutional network, and random forest with feature hashing—on three edge boards (an ARM Cortex-A72 single-board computer, a microcontroller-class device with 256 KB RAM, and an FPGA soft-processor). Workloads are drawn from wind turbine SCADA signals and smart meter load profiles sampled at 10 Hz and 1 Hz respectively. The quantised convolutional network fits within 200 KB and achieves 97% of its full-precision AUPRC while meeting a 5 ms per-window latency budget on the ARM board. On the microcontroller, only isolation forest and feature-hashed random forest are deployable; the latter achieves the better AUPRC (0.71 vs. 0.63). All profiling code and configuration files are released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-00964.title: Imbalanced Learning for Industrial Time-Series: A Structured Review of Methods and Evaluation Practices
SYN-PUB-00964.text:
Imbalanced Learning for Industrial Time-Series: A Structured Review of Methods and Evaluation Practices (2023, book chapter, Advances in Machine Learning for Industrial Applications (Springer series)).
Authors: Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071); Sonja Bošković (R0923); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: survey; imbalanced learning; industrial time-series; evaluation metrics; concept drift.
This chapter surveys the literature on learning from imbalanced industrial time-series data published between 2010 and 2022, covering approximately 160 papers. The chapter is organised around five methodological families: resampling, cost-sensitive training, anomaly-detection-based approaches, threshold adjustment, and ensemble methods. For each family, representative algorithms are described, and reported evaluation metrics are tabulated. A recurring finding is that many papers report only accuracy or AUC-ROC despite these being insensitive to minority-class performance at high imbalance ratios; the chapter argues for systematic reporting of AUPRC and G-mean alongside domain-relevant cost measures. A taxonomy of evaluation pitfalls specific to temporal data—including label leakage across temporal folds and inappropriate use of stratified k-fold on non-stationary streams—is presented. The chapter concludes with a structured list of open problems, including the combination of concept drift adaptation with imbalanced learning and the lack of standardised public benchmarks for industrial fault streams.

SYN-PUB-00965.title: Active Learning with Query-by-Committee for Labelling Efficiency in Imbalanced Fault Streams
SYN-PUB-00965.text:
Active Learning with Query-by-Committee for Labelling Efficiency in Imbalanced Fault Streams (2024, journal, Machine Learning for Industrial Systems).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Sanja Kovačević (outside co-author); Lukas Bauer (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: active learning; query by committee; labelling cost; minority class; fault streams.
Obtaining labelled fault examples is expensive in industrial settings because it requires expert inspection. Active learning selects the most informative unlabelled samples for expert annotation, potentially reducing labelling cost. This paper applies query-by-committee (QBC) using a committee of five classifiers—two gradient-boosted trees, two SVMs with different kernels, and a shallow neural network—to three simulated fault streams with imbalance ratios of 1:100, 1:500, and 1:2000. A disagreement-weighted sampling strategy biased toward minority-class candidates is introduced to counteract the tendency of standard QBC to query near the decision boundary in the majority class region. The biased strategy reaches 90% of fully labelled F1 using only 12% of available labels at 1:500 imbalance, compared to 21% for unbiased QBC and 31% for random sampling. Latency until the first useful model (F1 > 0.5) is reduced from 840 queries to 310 queries under the biased strategy.

SYN-PUB-00966.title: Evaluating Distribution Shift Between Training and Deployment Windows in Predictive Maintenance Models
SYN-PUB-00966.text:
Evaluating Distribution Shift Between Training and Deployment Windows in Predictive Maintenance Models (2026, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Data-Driven Engineering (ICDDE)).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Nikola Đurić (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Marija Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: distribution shift; predictive maintenance; temporal validation; maximum mean discrepancy; retraining.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-00967.title: Embedded Predictive Coding for Inertial Measurement Unit Streams in Vehicle Telematics
SYN-PUB-00967.text:
Embedded Predictive Coding for Inertial Measurement Unit Streams in Vehicle Telematics (2020, journal, Vehicular Communications).
Authors: Uroš Filipović (outside co-author); Jovanka Đorđević (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Ksenija Mitrović (R0552).
Keywords: predictive coding; IMU; vehicle telematics; recursive least squares; Cortex-M7; event retention.
Fleet telematics units generate high-volume 6-axis IMU data at 100 Hz used for driver behaviour scoring and road surface classification. This paper describes a predictive coder for IMU streams that uses second-order linear prediction with coefficients updated per frame via a recursive least-squares routine fitting within 2 kB of working memory on a Cortex-M7 at 216 MHz. Residuals are quantised with a non-uniform scalar quantiser whose levels are adapted to a Laplacian residual distribution. Across 480 km of mixed urban, motorway, and rural driving logged with an instrumented vehicle, the coder achieves a mean compression ratio of 5.2:1 at 3.1% root-mean-square normalised distortion. Hard braking and pothole events, identified by a reference classifier, were preserved with 96.4% event retention versus 78.1% for a non-adaptive arithmetic coder at the same bit rate. Computational load was 1.4% of CPU capacity, leaving ample headroom for concurrent GNSS and CAN processing.

SYN-PUB-00990.title: Characterising packet loss patterns in NB-IoT deployments across mixed urban and agricultural terrain in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-00990.text:
Characterising packet loss patterns in NB-IoT deployments across mixed urban and agricultural terrain in Vojvodina (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Wireless Sensor Networks Workshop (CEWSNW)).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Lidija Arsić (R0073); Anita Fekete (outside co-author); Siniša Ranković (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT; packet loss; link characterisation; Vojvodina; Markov chain.
This paper reports an empirical measurement campaign assessing NB-IoT link behaviour at 29 fixed sites across a 2,400 km² area in the Vojvodina region, covering densely built township centres, sparse rural roads, and open crop fields. Uplink and downlink packets were transmitted at 5-minute intervals over 60 consecutive days using commercial SIM7020 modules attached to custom data loggers. The dataset comprises approximately 1.2 million transmission attempts per direction. Results show that packet loss rate is strongly bimodal: median loss of 1.3 percent at sites within 4 km of a base station versus 18.7 percent at sites beyond 12 km. Burst loss episodes lasting more than 30 minutes were observed predominantly between 05:00 and 08:00 local time, correlated with agricultural machinery interference signatures identified via received signal strength indicators. A Markov chain model fitted to the burst statistics achieves a Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of 0.04 against the measured distribution. The characterisation informs retransmission and local buffering policies discussed in a companion study.

SYN-PUB-01007.title: Cross-cultural measurement invariance of a digital cognitive flexibility task across Serbian, Romanian, and Hungarian adolescent samples
SYN-PUB-01007.text:
Cross-cultural measurement invariance of a digital cognitive flexibility task across Serbian, Romanian, and Hungarian adolescent samples (2020, journal, European Journal of Psychological Assessment).
Authors: Luminiţa Coman (outside co-author); Katarina Radić (R0665); Eszter Fekete (outside co-author); Katarina Vukić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322); Emilija Jokić (R0074).
Keywords: measurement invariance; cognitive flexibility; cross-cultural; bifactor model; adolescents.
A computer-administered task battery measuring cognitive flexibility via task-switching and set-shifting paradigms was administered to adolescent samples in Serbia (n = 487), Romania (n = 413), and Hungary (n = 398), ages 15–17. Confirmatory factor analyses with a bifactor structure distinguished a general cognitive flexibility factor and two specific factors (rule updating, interference suppression). Multi-group confirmatory factor analysis tested configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Full metric invariance held across all three groups (ΔCFI = 0.007); scalar invariance was partial, with two intercepts non-invariant in the Hungarian sample, attributable to differential familiarity with the task interface. Latent mean comparisons adjusting for partial invariance showed no significant group differences on the general factor (p = 0.17), but the Romanian group scored lower on interference suppression (d = 0.29). Response-time parameters were more variable across groups than accuracy parameters.

SYN-PUB-01334.title: Conditional tail expectation for bivariate environmental risk under asymmetric dependence
SYN-PUB-01334.text:
Conditional tail expectation for bivariate environmental risk under asymmetric dependence (2019, journal, Annals of the Faculty of Sciences — Series Mathematics and Informatics).
Authors: Vesna Stanković (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Aleksa Popović (R0099).
Keywords: conditional tail expectation; coherent risk measures; Archimedean copulas; Tisza basin; tail asymmetry.
The conditional tail expectation (CTE), also known as expected shortfall, is a coherent risk measure widely used in financial risk management but less frequently applied to environmental hazard quantification. This paper derives analytical expressions for the bivariate CTE when the dependence structure belongs to the class of Archimedean copulas with completely monotone generators, covering the Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard and Joe families. The expressions are used to compute the expected discharge at one gauging station given that discharge at a second station simultaneously exceeds its empirical 95th, 99th and 99.9th percentiles, using records from eleven paired stations in the Tisza basin. Clayton copula fits indicate substantial asymmetry in lower and upper tail dependence, and the resulting CTEs are 12 to 38 percent higher than those implied by the bivariate Gaussian model with matched Kendall τ. Simulation experiments confirm the accuracy of the analytical results for sample sizes as small as n = 200.

SYN-PUB-01377.title: Polymorphic screening of sulfamethoxazole by slurry conversion and solvent-drop grinding: identification of two previously unreported forms
SYN-PUB-01377.text:
Polymorphic screening of sulfamethoxazole by slurry conversion and solvent-drop grinding: identification of two previously unreported forms (2010, journal, Journal of Pharmaceutical Solid-State Research).
Authors: Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author); Lidija Radić (R0151); Marija Uzelac (R0103).
Keywords: polymorphism; sulfamethoxazole; slurry conversion; PXRD; DSC.
Sulfamethoxazole is a widely used sulfonamide antibiotic whose polymorphic landscape has been incompletely characterised. Slurry conversion experiments in twelve solvents at 25 °C and 40 °C, combined with solvent-drop grinding using seven solvent systems, were carried out and the resulting solid phases were analysed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Two previously unreported crystalline forms, designated Form IV and Form V, were identified. Form IV, obtained reproducibly from acetonitrile slurries at 40 °C, showed a characteristic PXRD peak at 2θ = 8.3° absent from all known forms. DSC showed a sharp endotherm at 164 °C for Form IV, compared with 170 °C for the stable Form I. Form V appeared transiently during solvent-drop grinding with dimethyl sulfoxide and converted to Form I within 48 hours at ambient conditions. Variable-temperature PXRD confirmed an irreversible solid–solid transition of Form IV to Form I at 152 °C. The results extend the known polymorph space of this compound and provide reproducible preparation protocols for both new forms.

SYN-PUB-01379.title: Constructing a Composite Performance Index for Small and Medium-Sized Manufacturers: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region
SYN-PUB-01379.text:
Constructing a Composite Performance Index for Small and Medium-Sized Manufacturers: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region (2012, journal, Journal of Industrial Engineering and Management Research).
Authors: Branislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Miroslava Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: composite index; AHP; KPI; SME; Vojvodina.
This paper addresses the challenge of aggregating heterogeneous key performance indicators into a single composite index for manufacturing SMEs that lack dedicated measurement infrastructure. Using data collected from 34 enterprises in Vojvodina in 2010–2011, the study applies a weighted linear aggregation method where weights are derived through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with input from twelve senior managers across the sample companies. Four performance dimensions — financial, customer, internal processes, and learning and growth — were operationalised through 22 individual KPIs. Cronbach's alpha was used to verify internal consistency within each dimension (ranging from 0.71 to 0.84). The resulting composite index was validated against external audit scores and profit margin data. Results indicate that process-related KPIs carry disproportionate weight when managers with ISO 9001 experience are included as raters. The paper concludes with a simplified instrument suitable for quarterly self-assessment, reducing measurement burden to six core indicators without significant loss of discriminant validity. Limitations related to sample size and regional specificity are discussed.

SYN-PUB-01380.title: Adapting the Balanced Scorecard to ISO 9001 Transition Contexts: Conceptual Alignment and Practical Constraints
SYN-PUB-01380.text:
Adapting the Balanced Scorecard to ISO 9001 Transition Contexts: Conceptual Alignment and Practical Constraints (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Quality, Reliability and Maintenance in Manufacturing (QRMM 2013), Ljubljana).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Vuk Todić (R0246); Tamara Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: balanced scorecard; ISO 9001; alignment; quality management; conceptual mapping.
The balanced scorecard (BSC) and ISO 9001 quality management standard share process-oriented thinking but differ substantially in measurement philosophy, documentation requirements, and management commitment expectations. This conceptual paper maps the structural overlap between the four BSC perspectives and the ten clauses of ISO 9001:2015, identifying 14 areas of direct alignment and eight areas of potential conflict. The analysis draws on a review of 61 published implementation case studies from European manufacturing companies published between 2000 and 2012, supplemented by interviews with five quality managers in Serbian companies undergoing ISO 9001 certification at the time of the study. The paper argues that the BSC customer perspective is most easily absorbed into the ISO framework, while the learning and growth perspective requires the greatest adaptation due to ISO's weak treatment of human capital metrics. A mapping matrix is proposed as a practical tool for consultants guiding simultaneous BSC and ISO implementations. The paper does not present empirical validation but sets the foundation for subsequent quantitative research.

SYN-PUB-01381.title: Measurement Invariance of Balanced Scorecard Scales Across Manufacturing Subsectors: Evidence from Serbia and Slovenia
SYN-PUB-01381.text:
Measurement Invariance of Balanced Scorecard Scales Across Manufacturing Subsectors: Evidence from Serbia and Slovenia (2015, journal, International Journal of Production and Quality Management).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Nejc Vidmar (outside co-author); Ivana Savić (outside co-author); Miroslava Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: measurement invariance; balanced scorecard; SEM; manufacturing; cross-sector.
Balanced scorecard instruments are frequently adapted informally when moved between industry contexts, raising questions about whether scale items retain the same meaning across manufacturing subsectors. This study tests measurement invariance of a 28-item BSC survey instrument across three subsectors — metal processing, food manufacturing, and textile production — using data from 187 respondents in Serbian and Slovenian companies with 50–500 employees. Confirmatory factor analysis and multigroup structural equation modelling (SEM) were conducted in R using the lavaan package. Configural and metric invariance were confirmed across all three groups; scalar invariance held for the financial and internal processes perspectives but failed for two items in the customer perspective, suggesting that customer satisfaction is conceptualised differently in food manufacturing relative to the other subsectors. Practical implications for cross-sector benchmarking are discussed. The validated instrument is included as an appendix and is made available for replication studies.

SYN-PUB-01382.title: ISO 9001 Certification and Post-Certification Performance Drift in Serbian SMEs: A Longitudinal Analysis
SYN-PUB-01382.text:
ISO 9001 Certification and Post-Certification Performance Drift in Serbian SMEs: A Longitudinal Analysis (2016, journal, Total Quality and Business Excellence Review).
Authors: Dragan Ćirić (outside co-author); Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Katalin Takács (R0584).
Keywords: ISO 9001; performance drift; longitudinal; SME; Serbia.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-01383.title: Weighting Methods for Balanced Scorecard KPIs: A Comparative Study of AHP, Entropy Weighting, and Equal Weighting in the Context of Medium-Sized Enterprises
SYN-PUB-01383.text:
Weighting Methods for Balanced Scorecard KPIs: A Comparative Study of AHP, Entropy Weighting, and Equal Weighting in the Context of Medium-Sized Enterprises (2017, journal, Central European Journal of Operations Research and Decision Sciences).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Gábor Molnár (outside co-author); Siniša Kovač (R0834); Tamara Vuković (outside co-author); Radovan Janković (R0775).
Keywords: AHP; entropy weighting; balanced scorecard; KPI ranking; SME.
The choice of KPI weighting method in balanced scorecard implementations is rarely subjected to empirical scrutiny. This study compares three weighting approaches — pairwise AHP, entropy-based objective weighting, and simple equal weighting — applied to the same dataset of 41 medium-sized manufacturing companies in Serbia and Hungary. For each company, a composite performance score was calculated using all three methods, and the resulting rankings were compared using Spearman rank correlation and Kendall's W. Entropy weighting and AHP produce highly correlated rankings (ρ = 0.91), while equal weighting diverges substantially when KPI variance is uneven across dimensions. Sensitivity analysis shows that AHP rankings are more stable under data perturbation than entropy rankings. Survey data from 163 managers indicate a strong preference for AHP outputs when presented alongside the rationale, despite higher procedural complexity. The paper recommends a hybrid approach combining AHP for strategic KPIs with entropy weighting for operational indicators. Data and R scripts are available in the supplementary materials.

SYN-PUB-01384.title: Performance Measurement Maturity and ISO 9001 Readiness: Developing a Pre-Certification Assessment Tool
SYN-PUB-01384.text:
Performance Measurement Maturity and ISO 9001 Readiness: Developing a Pre-Certification Assessment Tool (2018, journal, Quality Engineering and Management Practice).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Ivana Savić (outside co-author); Sanja Knežević (outside co-author); Nejc Vidmar (outside co-author).
Keywords: maturity model; ISO 9001 readiness; performance measurement; assessment tool; SME.
Companies approaching ISO 9001 certification for the first time vary considerably in the sophistication of their existing performance measurement practices. This paper presents the development and validation of a 20-item Performance Measurement Maturity Assessment (PMMA) tool designed to estimate ISO 9001 transition readiness. Item generation drew on a review of maturity model literature and on semi-structured interviews with 18 quality consultants active in the Western Balkans region. Content validity was assessed by a panel of seven experts. Pilot testing was conducted with 62 manufacturing SMEs; exploratory factor analysis in SPSS yielded four factors explaining 67% of variance: data collection infrastructure, managerial engagement, process documentation, and corrective action routines. Confirmatory factor analysis on a second sample of 88 companies confirmed the factor structure (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.058). PMMA scores correlate significantly with time-to-certification outcomes tracked over 18 months (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). The tool is intended for use by consultants and internal quality managers as a structured diagnostic prior to ISO implementation.

SYN-PUB-01385.title: Integrating Risk-Based Thinking from ISO 9001:2015 into Balanced Scorecard Design: A Framework for Manufacturing SMEs
SYN-PUB-01385.text:
Integrating Risk-Based Thinking from ISO 9001:2015 into Balanced Scorecard Design: A Framework for Manufacturing SMEs (2019, book chapter, Advances in Quality and Production Management (edited volume, TU Wien Press)).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Dragan Ćirić (outside co-author); Walter Hofmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: risk-based thinking; ISO 9001:2015; balanced scorecard; risk KPI; integrated management.
The 2015 revision of ISO 9001 introduced an explicit requirement for risk-based thinking, replacing the earlier concept of preventive action. This requirement has no direct counterpart in classical balanced scorecard design, creating a gap in integrated management systems. This book chapter proposes a framework for embedding risk indicators into each of the four BSC perspectives, drawing on ISO 31000 risk management terminology and on data from ten case companies that participated in a structured implementation pilot in 2017–2018. For each perspective, the chapter identifies two to four candidate risk KPIs, specifies data sources, and illustrates aggregation logic using the companies' own figures. A worked numerical example demonstrates how a composite risk-adjusted BSC score differs from an unadjusted score in companies with high process variability. The chapter also discusses barriers encountered during the pilot, including resistance from finance managers unfamiliar with non-financial risk quantification and inconsistency in how risk registers were maintained across companies.

SYN-PUB-01387.title: Aggregation Bias in Multi-Perspective Performance Indices: Simulation Evidence and Practical Corrections
SYN-PUB-01387.text:
Aggregation Bias in Multi-Perspective Performance Indices: Simulation Evidence and Practical Corrections (2022, journal, Operations Research and Management Science Letters).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Gábor Molnár (outside co-author); Tamara Vuković (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: aggregation bias; composite index; Monte Carlo; balanced scorecard; KPI.
Composite performance indices that aggregate KPIs across multiple perspectives are susceptible to aggregation bias when individual indicators are correlated within perspectives or when perspectives differ in the number of constituent indicators. This paper quantifies aggregation bias through a Monte Carlo simulation study calibrated on empirical correlation structures estimated from a panel dataset of 74 Serbian and Croatian manufacturing companies observed over three years. Simulation results show that standard weighted arithmetic aggregation systematically overstates overall performance when within-perspective correlations exceed 0.5, with bias increasing with the number of indicators per perspective. Three correction procedures are compared: principal component score substitution, geometric aggregation, and within-perspective decorrelation prior to aggregation. Geometric aggregation provides the best bias-correction at minimal computational cost and is recommended as the default for practitioners. The paper provides worked examples and an Excel template implementing all three methods. Findings have direct implications for balanced scorecard implementations where perspectives contain redundant indicators.

SYN-PUB-01388.title: Short-Form Balanced Scorecard Instruments for Operational Monitoring: Validity and Reliability in High-Turnover Manufacturing Environments
SYN-PUB-01388.text:
Short-Form Balanced Scorecard Instruments for Operational Monitoring: Validity and Reliability in High-Turnover Manufacturing Environments (2024, journal, Measurement in Industrial and Quality Management).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Dragan Ćirić (outside co-author).
Keywords: short-form instrument; balanced scorecard; item-response theory; operational monitoring; manufacturing.
Full-length balanced scorecard instruments are burdensome to administer in manufacturing environments with high staff turnover and limited administrative capacity. This paper develops and validates a 10-item short-form BSC instrument designed for monthly operational monitoring. Items were selected from a longer 32-item pool using a three-stage procedure: item-response theory analysis, expert rating for practical measurability, and empirical validation across 56 Serbian manufacturing SMEs followed over six months. The short form retains adequate coverage of all four perspectives with two to three items each. Reliability coefficients (McDonald's ω) range from 0.72 to 0.79 per perspective. Convergent validity with the full instrument is confirmed (r = 0.87 for composite scores). Sensitivity to change was tested by comparing short-form scores before and after documented process improvement interventions in 14 of the 56 companies; the instrument detected improvement in 11 of 14 cases. The short-form instrument and scoring guide are provided as supplementary materials.

SYN-PUB-01389.title: Linking Employee Competence Development Metrics to ISO 9001 Clause 7.2 Requirements: A Practical Measurement Approach for Mid-Sized Manufacturers
SYN-PUB-01389.text:
Linking Employee Competence Development Metrics to ISO 9001 Clause 7.2 Requirements: A Practical Measurement Approach for Mid-Sized Manufacturers (2026, journal, European Journal of Quality and Industrial Practice).
Authors: Aleksandra Matić (R0104); Walter Hofmann (outside co-author); Ivana Savić (outside co-author).
Keywords: competence measurement; ISO 9001 Clause 7.2; learning and growth; balanced scorecard; training effectiveness.
ISO 9001:2015 Clause 7.2 requires organisations to determine and maintain employee competence, yet offers no guidance on measurement. This creates a gap when companies attempt to incorporate competence development into the learning and growth perspective of a balanced scorecard. Drawing on data from 22 mid-sized Serbian manufacturers that had held ISO 9001 certification for at least five years, this study documents the measurement practices actually used, identifies the most common operationalisations of competence KPIs, and tests which measures predict training effectiveness as assessed by follow-up operational audits. A total of 31 distinct competence metrics were identified across the sample. Regression analysis on a subsample with sufficient longitudinal data (n = 15) shows that metrics combining task completion rates with a structured competence gap assessment score are stronger predictors of audit outcomes than training hours alone. The paper proposes a four-item measurement mini-framework that aligns with both Clause 7.2 and standard learning and growth BSC indicators.

SYN-PUB-01476.title: A Surrogate-Assisted MOEA/D Approach to Cell-Level Neural Architecture Search with Latency Constraints
SYN-PUB-01476.text:
A Surrogate-Assisted MOEA/D Approach to Cell-Level Neural Architecture Search with Latency Constraints (2024, journal, Applied Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems).
Authors: Vukica Vasić (R0112); Vukica Grujić (R0305); Dragan Miletić (outside co-author); Petar Stevanović (R0833); Ágnes Fülöp (outside co-author); Nikola Stojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: neural architecture search; MOEA/D; Gaussian process surrogate; latency constraint; DARTS.
Neural architecture search at the cell level involves evaluating thousands of candidate graphs, each requiring full training to estimate accuracy. This work proposes embedding a Gaussian process surrogate model inside MOEA/D to predict validation accuracy and inference latency jointly, allowing expensive true evaluations to be reserved for the most promising decomposition subproblems. The search space follows the DARTS cell formulation with eight candidate operations and a fixed stack of six cells. Surrogate updates use a batch of ten true evaluations per generation, selected by expected hypervolume improvement. Experiments run on CIFAR-100 and a 10-class subset of a publicly available remote-sensing scene dataset, with a hard latency constraint of 15 ms on an ARM Cortex-A55 core measured with ONNX Runtime. Across 20 independent runs, the surrogate-assisted variant reaches equivalent hypervolume to a fully evaluated MOEA/D baseline using 38 percent fewer true evaluations. Discovered architectures with skip connections eliminated outperform hand-designed baselines by 1.2–2.4 percentage points in top-1 accuracy at matched latency. The approach is reproducible; all code and architecture logs are released publicly.

SYN-PUB-01514.title: Interaction between grid-following inverter current control bandwidth and conducted emission levels: a parametric study
SYN-PUB-01514.text:
Interaction between grid-following inverter current control bandwidth and conducted emission levels: a parametric study (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Dragana Pekez (R0115); Ana Mamužić (R0283).
Keywords: grid-following inverter; current control; LCL filter; conducted emissions; CISPR 11.
The relationship between the current control loop bandwidth of grid-following single-phase inverters and their conducted emission characteristics in the 150 kHz to 2 MHz range is examined through a parametric simulation study validated by laboratory measurements. A full-cycle time-domain inverter model is implemented in PLECS and exercised across current controller bandwidths from 500 Hz to 8 kHz, LCL filter corner frequencies from 4 kHz to 20 kHz, and DC bus voltages of 200 V, 350 V and 600 V. Conducted emission spectra at the AC terminals are extracted via an embedded LISN model and compared with CISPR 11 Class B limits. Increasing controller bandwidth from 1 kHz to 5 kHz reduces low-frequency distortion but increases emissions in the 200 kHz to 600 kHz band by 3 to 11 dB depending on LCL corner frequency. A low-pass post-filter of 47 µH/10 nF placed after the LCL filter reduces peak emission levels by 8 dB with less than 0.3% increase in fundamental voltage drop. Laboratory validation on a 2 kW prototype confirms simulation trends with deviations below 4 dB across 90% of the measured frequency range.

SYN-PUB-01675.title: Natural Language Inference as a Proxy for Factual Consistency Checking in Generated Text
SYN-PUB-01675.text:
Natural Language Inference as a Proxy for Factual Consistency Checking in Generated Text (2019, journal, Journal of Language Technology and Computational Linguistics).
Authors: Renáta Somogyi (outside co-author); Petra Kováčová (outside co-author); Luka Radovanović (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: natural language inference; factual consistency; text generation; encoder attention; adversarial evaluation.
Factual consistency checking in automatically generated text is often framed as a natural language inference (NLI) task, treating the source document as premise and each generated sentence as hypothesis. This paper investigates how well off-the-shelf NLI models serve this purpose. We evaluate five multilingual NLI checkpoints on four existing faithfulness benchmarks and find that entailment scores correlate with human faithfulness ratings at Spearman ρ = 0.49–0.67, varying substantially across domains. Performance drops markedly on long source documents (over 800 tokens), where models tend to produce neutral labels even for clearly hallucinated sentences. We trace this degradation to attention saturation in the encoder and show that chunking the premise into paragraphs and aggregating with min-pooling raises ρ by 0.09 on average. We also construct a controlled adversarial subset by swapping named entities and reversing numerical values, finding that NLI models detect fewer than half of these manipulations. The analysis suggests NLI-based consistency checking is a useful but incomplete signal, and that domain-specific fine-tuning and length-handling strategies are necessary for reliable deployment.

SYN-PUB-01676.title: Probing Intermediate Representations of Pre-Trained Language Models for Factual Knowledge
SYN-PUB-01676.text:
Probing Intermediate Representations of Pre-Trained Language Models for Factual Knowledge (2020, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Engineering).
Authors: Emilija Tešić (R0127); Luka Radovanović (outside co-author); Tobias Brendel (outside co-author).
Keywords: probing classifiers; knowledge encoding; language model layers; factual recall; hallucination.
Pre-trained language models (PLMs) are known to encode factual knowledge in their parameters, but the distribution of this knowledge across layers is not well understood. This paper applies a probing classifier methodology to six PLMs of varying sizes, testing for subject–relation–object triples from a manually constructed knowledge base of 4 800 facts in four domains: geography, institutional history, scientific authorship, and legal norms. For each fact, linear probes are trained on the hidden states of every transformer layer. Probing accuracy peaks at middle layers for relational facts (mean 71 percent) and at upper layers for entity-centric facts (mean 68 percent). Larger models do not consistently outperform smaller ones on low-frequency facts. We further investigate whether facts that are poorly encoded by the probe are also more susceptible to hallucination at inference time, finding a moderate but consistent correlation (r = 0.44 across domains). The results have implications for strategies that selectively freeze or update layers during fine-tuning to reduce hallucination.

SYN-PUB-01677.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Transformer Outputs Using Monte Carlo Dropout: A Study on Question Answering
SYN-PUB-01677.text:
Uncertainty Quantification in Transformer Outputs Using Monte Carlo Dropout: A Study on Question Answering (2021, journal, Journal of Intelligent Information Systems and Applications).
Authors: Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Mladen Ivković (R0134); Dragoslav Milenković (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: MC dropout; uncertainty quantification; question answering; calibration; hallucination detection.
This paper investigates whether Monte Carlo (MC) dropout can serve as a practical uncertainty estimate for transformer-based question answering (QA) models, and whether high uncertainty correlates with hallucinated or incorrect answers. Experiments use three QA datasets: one in English, one in Serbian, and one bilingual domain-specific dataset covering regulatory documents. MC dropout is applied at inference time with 30 forward passes; variance across answer span predictions is used as an uncertainty proxy. Models with high predictive variance are shown to produce incorrect answers at a rate 2.3 times higher than low-variance instances (p < 0.001). Calibration curves indicate that raw MC dropout variance is poorly calibrated (expected calibration error 0.18) but becomes usable after temperature scaling (ECE 0.07). For open-domain questions, uncertainty correlates more strongly with answer correctness than for closed-domain regulatory QA, where models tend to be overconfident. We discuss practical thresholds for triggering human review based on uncertainty estimates and the trade-off between coverage and abstention rate.

SYN-PUB-01678.title: Towards Automatic Citation Grounding: Linking Sentences in Generated Reports to Source Passages
SYN-PUB-01678.text:
Towards Automatic Citation Grounding: Linking Sentences in Generated Reports to Source Passages (2022, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Information Retrieval and Natural Language Generation).
Authors: Luka Radovanović (outside co-author); Sofija Đorđević (outside co-author); Renáta Somogyi (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: citation grounding; retrieval-augmented generation; bi-encoder; cross-encoder; attribution.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems retrieve source passages before generating text, but they do not reliably attribute each generated sentence to the passages that support it. This paper addresses citation grounding: the automatic identification of which retrieved passage, if any, provides evidence for a generated sentence. We formulate the task as a bi-encoder retrieval problem followed by a cross-encoder re-ranking step, and train on a newly constructed dataset of 9 400 (generated sentence, passage, label) triples drawn from generated financial and medical reports. Labels were produced by a two-stage annotation protocol combining automatic NLI pre-filtering with human adjudication. The bi-encoder alone achieves recall@3 of 0.79; adding the cross-encoder re-ranker raises it to 0.86. Grounding precision at rank 1 is 0.71. We find that sentences containing numerical claims are the most difficult to ground (precision 0.58), while definitional sentences are easiest (precision 0.83). The paper also introduces a simple attribution confidence score and shows it correlates with human judgements of citation quality (ρ = 0.61).

SYN-PUB-01679.title: Detecting Hallucinations in Long-Form Language Model Outputs Using Decomposition and Atomic Claim Verification
SYN-PUB-01679.text:
Detecting Hallucinations in Long-Form Language Model Outputs Using Decomposition and Atomic Claim Verification (2023, journal, Transactions on Computational Linguistics and Text Analysis).
Authors: Jovana Bjelić (outside co-author); Tobias Brendel (outside co-author); Marija Vukelić (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: atomic claim verification; hallucination detection; long-form generation; NLI; decomposition.
Long-form text generated by large language models may contain a mixture of supported and unsupported claims within a single paragraph, making sentence-level faithfulness evaluation insufficient. This paper proposes a pipeline that decomposes generated paragraphs into atomic claims using a fine-tuned decomposition model, retrieves relevant evidence passages for each claim from a linked corpus, and classifies each claim as supported, contradicted, or unverifiable using a fine-tuned NLI model. The pipeline is evaluated on three long-form generation tasks: biographies, medical treatment summaries, and legal case descriptions. On a human-annotated test set of 480 generated documents, the pipeline achieves claim-level detection F1 of 0.74, compared with 0.61 for a sentence-level baseline. Error analysis shows that implicit presuppositions and vague quantifiers are the main sources of remaining false negatives. We further report that the fraction of unverifiable claims—those where no retrieved passage addresses the claim—is a useful document-level hallucination risk signal, correlating with human overall quality ratings at ρ = 0.58.

SYN-PUB-01680.title: Retrieval Quality and Its Effect on Downstream Hallucination Rates in RAG Systems
SYN-PUB-01680.text:
Retrieval Quality and Its Effect on Downstream Hallucination Rates in RAG Systems (2024, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Engineering).
Authors: Luka Radovanović (outside co-author); Sofija Đorđević (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; retrieval quality; hallucination rate; dense retrieval; BM25.
In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the quality of retrieved context directly affects the faithfulness of generated outputs, yet the relationship is rarely studied in controlled settings. This paper designs a factorial experiment varying retrieval precision (high, medium, low, and adversarial) across three RAG configurations (BM25 only, dense retrieval only, and hybrid) and two generator sizes. Retrieval precision is operationalised by injecting passages with controlled relevance degradation into the retrieval pool. Hallucination rates are measured using the atomic claim verification pipeline from prior work. Moving from high to medium retrieval precision increases hallucination rate by an average of 11 percentage points; adversarial passages (containing plausible but incorrect facts) increase it by 28 percentage points relative to the high-precision baseline. Dense retrieval generators are more susceptible to adversarial passages than BM25 generators. Generator size moderates adversarial sensitivity: larger models (7B parameters) show smaller increases than smaller models (1.3B) under adversarial conditions. The results provide empirical grounding for retrieval quality requirements in production RAG deployments.

SYN-PUB-01681.title: Post-Hoc Explanation Consistency Under Distribution Shift: An Empirical Study
SYN-PUB-01681.text:
Post-Hoc Explanation Consistency Under Distribution Shift: An Empirical Study (2024, journal, Journal of Machine Learning Research and Applications).
Authors: Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Petra Kováčová (outside co-author); Marija Vukelić (outside co-author); Slađana Paunović (R0253); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: distribution shift; explanation consistency; SHAP; LIME; integrated gradients.
Post-hoc explanation methods are typically evaluated on held-out data from the same distribution as the training set. This paper examines how LIME, SHAP, and integrated gradients behave when the test distribution shifts relative to training. We induce controlled distribution shifts in four classification tasks (text, tabular, image, and time-series) by progressively modifying covariate distributions. Explanation consistency is measured as the rank correlation between feature importance scores produced on original and shifted instances matched by prediction confidence. All three methods degrade under shift, but the rate and nature of degradation differ: SHAP explanations lose consistency faster on tabular data (rank correlation drops from 0.81 to 0.47 at moderate shift), while integrated gradients are relatively stable for text and image tasks. We also show that explanation inconsistency is a detectable signal for distribution shift itself, providing a potential monitoring use case. The study uses no proprietary data; all datasets and shift protocols are described in sufficient detail for replication.

SYN-PUB-01682.title: GroundCheck: A Framework for Real-Time Citation Verification in RAG-Powered Document Assistants
SYN-PUB-01682.text:
GroundCheck: A Framework for Real-Time Citation Verification in RAG-Powered Document Assistants (2025, conference, Proceedings of the Annual Symposium on Applied Natural Language Processing).
Authors: Jovana Bjelić (outside co-author); Nikola Jovanović (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: citation verification; RAG; real-time; document assistant; claim verification.
Production document assistant systems built on retrieval-augmented generation need to verify that claims in their outputs are traceable to specific source passages before responses are shown to users. This paper describes GroundCheck, a modular verification framework that intercepts generation outputs, decomposes them into atomic claims, and runs lightweight verification against the retrieved context within a latency budget of 400 milliseconds per response on commodity hardware. The framework uses a distilled cross-encoder for claim–passage entailment checking (73M parameters) and a rule-based post-processing step to attach inline citation markers to verified claims. In an offline evaluation against manually annotated outputs from a legal document assistant, GroundCheck achieves precision 0.80 and recall 0.76 for correctly identified unsupported claims. A qualitative deployment study with 24 legal professionals found that citation markers increased perceived trustworthiness of the system on a seven-point scale by 1.4 points on average. Failure analysis highlights remaining difficulties with multi-hop reasoning chains and implicitly contradictory evidence.

SYN-PUB-01683.title: Evaluating Explanation Fidelity Under Prompt Variation in Instruction-Tuned Language Models
SYN-PUB-01683.text:
Evaluating Explanation Fidelity Under Prompt Variation in Instruction-Tuned Language Models (2026, journal, Transactions on Computational Linguistics and Text Analysis).
Authors: Luka Radovanović (outside co-author); Tobias Brendel (outside co-author); Pavol Struhár (R0261); Dragana Kovačević (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127).
Keywords: self-explanation; instruction tuning; fidelity; prompt engineering; saliency.
Instruction-tuned language models can produce natural-language explanations for their own outputs on request, but it is unclear whether these self-explanations reflect the model's actual inference path or are generated independently of it. This paper measures explanation fidelity by comparing self-generated explanations to three external explanation methods (saliency, attention rollout, and a perturbation-based method) across 600 prompted classification and extraction tasks. Agreement between self-explanations and external methods, measured by normalised token-level overlap, averages 0.41 and varies substantially with prompt wording. Systematically varying the explanation prompt reveals that adding the phrase 'cite the exact words from the input that determined your answer' raises agreement to 0.55 without affecting task performance. We also find that self-explanations are more likely to be faithful when the model's output confidence is high and when the task is extractive rather than abstractive. The results have practical implications for the design of explanation prompts in deployed systems and suggest that external verification of self-explanations is necessary for high-stakes applications.

SYN-PUB-01686.title: Character-Level Neural Transliteration for Serbian: Training Data, Architecture Choices, and Error Analysis
SYN-PUB-01686.text:
Character-Level Neural Transliteration for Serbian: Training Data, Architecture Choices, and Error Analysis (2019, journal, Natural Language Engineering).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127); Miroslav Ćirić (outside co-author); Jana Zahorecová (R0931).
Keywords: neural transliteration; sequence-to-sequence; character-level model; Serbian; error analysis.
