Deterministic rule-based transliteration between Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts handles the majority of tokens correctly, but fails on foreign loanwords, abbreviations, and alphanumeric strings. This paper investigates whether a character-level sequence-to-sequence neural model can handle these exceptions while remaining accurate on regular tokens. We trained models on a corpus of 2.3 million aligned Cyrillic–Latin token pairs extracted from parallel editions of official gazettes, experimenting with LSTM encoder-decoder architectures with attention, as well as a character-level transformer. The transformer model achieved a character error rate of 0.4% on regular tokens and 3.1% on the exception classes, compared with 0.1% and 19.4% respectively for the deterministic baseline. We performed a detailed error analysis categorising 800 mistransliterated tokens by type. The paper concludes that a cascaded system — deterministic rules followed by the neural model for detected exceptions — outperforms either component alone, reaching a token error rate of 0.6% overall.

SYN-PUB-01738.title: Harmonic Spectrum Interaction Between Multiple Variable-Speed Drives Sharing a Common DC Bus
SYN-PUB-01738.text:
Harmonic Spectrum Interaction Between Multiple Variable-Speed Drives Sharing a Common DC Bus (2020, journal, IET Power Electronics).
Authors: Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Predrag Stanojević (outside co-author); Жељко Узелац (R0131); Ana Mamužić (R0283); Marco Trentini (outside co-author).
Keywords: common DC bus; multi-drive system; harmonic interaction; intermodulation; switching frequency offset.
Industrial plants often connect multiple drives to a shared DC bus, creating conditions for harmonic coupling not addressed by single-drive EMC standards. This paper examines the conducted emission spectra at the AC supply terminals of a two-drive, common DC-bus arrangement with drive ratings of 4 kW and 11 kW, operated with identical and deliberately offset switching frequencies. When both drives are switched at 8 kHz, intermodulation products appear at frequencies predicted by Δfsw·n (n = 1, 2, 3) and reach amplitudes 3–8 dB above the single-drive case in the 1–5 MHz range. Offsetting switching frequencies by 500 Hz suppressed the most prominent intermodulation clusters by 6–12 dB. A discrete-frequency superposition model, assuming uncorrelated switching instants, underestimates the coupled peaks by 4 dB on average, indicating partial phase coherence. Results inform both filter specification and switching-frequency assignment strategies for multi-drive installations.

SYN-PUB-01784.title: Weibull-based failure rate estimation for flat-die pellet presses processing mixed agricultural residues
SYN-PUB-01784.text:
Weibull-based failure rate estimation for flat-die pellet presses processing mixed agricultural residues (2011, journal, Journal of Agricultural Machinery and Biosystems Engineering).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: Weibull distribution; pellet press; bearing failure; agricultural residues; maintenance interval.
This study applies two- and three-parameter Weibull distributions to time-to-failure data collected from eight flat-die pellet presses operating in cooperative-scale biomass facilities in Vojvodina over a 36-month observation window. A total of 214 failure events were logged across drive-shaft bearings, die-roller assemblies, and gearbox seals. Feedstock composition—straw, sunflower husk, and corn stover blends—was recorded at each batch. Shape and scale parameters were estimated by maximum likelihood with 95% confidence intervals. Results indicate that die-roller bearing shape parameters cluster between 1.8 and 2.4 for straw-dominant batches, shifting to 1.2–1.6 for high-ash sunflower husk feeds, consistent with accelerated abrasive wear. Mean time between failures for roller assemblies was 312 hours under optimal moisture (12–14%) versus 187 hours at moisture above 18%. The findings suggest that feedstock moisture is the strongest single predictor of bearing service life, with silica content a secondary but significant factor. A maintenance interval nomogram is proposed as a practical planning aid for facility managers.

SYN-PUB-01785.title: Effect of feedstock moisture variation on ring-die wear progression in a continuous pelletisation line
SYN-PUB-01785.text:
Effect of feedstock moisture variation on ring-die wear progression in a continuous pelletisation line (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on Biomass Processing and Conversion, Novi Sad).
Authors: Veljko Savić (R0135); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: ring-die wear; pelletisation; moisture; profilometry; wear modelling.
Ring-die geometry measurements were taken at 250-hour intervals on a pilot-scale pelletisation line fed with willow chip feedstock at controlled moisture levels of 10%, 14%, 18%, and 22%. Die hole diameter and surface roughness were measured at nine radial positions using a contact profilometer after each interval over a total of 1,500 operating hours. At 22% moisture, mean die-hole diameter growth reached 0.31 mm by 1,000 hours, compared with 0.14 mm at 14% moisture. Surface roughness Ra increased roughly linearly under dry conditions but exhibited a step change at approximately 600 hours under wet conditions, attributed to localised corrosion pitting. A semi-empirical wear rate model incorporating feedstock moisture as a multiplicative factor on the Preston wear coefficient is calibrated against the measured data. The model predicts die replacement intervals within ±8% of observed intervals in a hold-out validation set of three commercial-scale presses. Practical guidance on moisture management to extend die service life is provided.

SYN-PUB-01786.title: Condition monitoring of pellet press roller bearings using vibration envelope analysis under variable load conditions
SYN-PUB-01786.text:
Condition monitoring of pellet press roller bearings using vibration envelope analysis under variable load conditions (2015, journal, Maintenance and Reliability – Eksploatacja i Niezawodność).
Authors: Nemanja Vučković (outside co-author); Goran Tadić (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135).
Keywords: vibration monitoring; envelope analysis; roller bearing; variable load; condition monitoring.
Vibration signals were acquired from the roller bearing housings of two flat-die presses at a 20 kHz sampling rate over 480 hours of mixed-feedstock operation. Envelope spectrum analysis was applied after bandpass filtering in the 2–10 kHz range to isolate bearing fault frequencies associated with outer-race and inner-race defects. A comparative baseline was established during a 48-hour run on uniform dried straw. Load fluctuations caused by variable feedstock bulk density were characterised simultaneously via motor current measurements. Results show that bearing defect frequency amplitudes are suppressed during high-density feedstock runs due to increased radial loading dampening high-frequency resonance. A simple normalisation procedure using instantaneous motor current as a proxy for radial load is proposed to decouple this effect. The corrected envelope spectra show fault indicator sensitivity improvements of 15–23 dB relative to uncorrected spectra. The method is validated against two known incipient outer-race defects introduced deliberately on test bearings.

SYN-PUB-01787.title: Stochastic degradation modelling for briquetting press toggle mechanisms subject to cyclically varying compaction forces
SYN-PUB-01787.text:
Stochastic degradation modelling for briquetting press toggle mechanisms subject to cyclically varying compaction forces (2017, journal, Reliability Engineering and System Safety).
Authors: Péter Kovács (outside co-author); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135); Slobodan Đorđević (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308).
Keywords: gamma process; crack growth; briquetting press; covariate degradation model; replacement optimisation.
A gamma process model is fitted to crack growth measurements on toggle-link pins sampled from seven briquetting presses in southern Hungary and northern Serbia over 24 months. Crack length was measured by dye-penetrant inspection at each scheduled maintenance visit, yielding 94 data points across 31 individual pins. The compaction force cycle, which varies with feedstock chip geometry and flow rate, was instrumented on two presses using strain-gauged tie rods. A covariate extension of the gamma process model incorporates mean compaction force as a time-varying covariate, estimated from a moving average of the tie-rod signal. Model fitting used an expectation-maximisation algorithm; goodness-of-fit was assessed with the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic. The covariate model reduced residual variance by 34% relative to a baseline gamma process without covariates. Replacement timing optimisation under a cost-per-unit-time criterion suggests that condition-triggered replacement at 60–70% of critical crack length minimises long-run maintenance cost for the studied fleet.

SYN-PUB-01788.title: Reliability block diagram modelling of a mobile biomass briquetting unit with redundant screw feed subsystems
SYN-PUB-01788.text:
Reliability block diagram modelling of a mobile biomass briquetting unit with redundant screw feed subsystems (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Maintenance and Industrial Engineering, Zagreb).
Authors: Veljko Savić (R0135); Nemanja Vučković (outside co-author).
Keywords: reliability block diagram; mobile briquetting unit; system availability; Monte Carlo simulation; agricultural machinery.
A reliability block diagram was constructed for a trailer-mounted briquetting unit used in field-collection scenarios in the Pannonian Plain. The unit incorporates two parallel screw feed paths, a single-stage roller press, and a hydraulic baling conveyor. Failure data for 18 months of seasonal operation were collected from maintenance logs of six identical units owned by two agricultural cooperatives. Component-level failure rates were estimated from 47 documented failures and fitted to exponential and Weibull distributions depending on component type. System availability was computed analytically for the RBD and compared with Monte Carlo simulation results (10,000 runs). Simulation-based availability was 0.883 (90% CI: 0.871–0.895), versus 0.891 from the analytical model; the 0.9% deviation is attributed to load-sharing effects between the parallel screws not captured in the analytical model. A sensitivity analysis identifies the hydraulic pump seals and the press roller drive chain as the subsystems most limiting to system availability, together accounting for 38% of total downtime.

SYN-PUB-01789.title: Influence of sunflower husk ash content on abrasive wear rate of pellet die steel: a laboratory pin-on-disc study
SYN-PUB-01789.text:
Influence of sunflower husk ash content on abrasive wear rate of pellet die steel: a laboratory pin-on-disc study (2019, journal, Tribology in Industry).
Authors: Marija Stanković (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135); Zoltán Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: abrasive wear; pellet die steel; sunflower husk; ash content; pin-on-disc.
Pin-on-disc wear tests were conducted on coupons of X46Cr13 die steel—the most common die material in Vojvodina pellet facilities—using abrasive slurries prepared from sunflower husk ash at five mass fractions: 0%, 2%, 5%, 10%, and 15%. Tests were run at a sliding speed of 0.3 m/s and a normal load of 20 N for 3,600 seconds each, with three replicates per condition. Mass loss was recorded gravimetrically at 600-second intervals. Specific wear rate increased from 1.4 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 0% ash to 6.1 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 15% ash. SEM micrographs of worn surfaces confirm a transition from ploughing-dominated to micro-cutting-dominated wear mechanisms above 5% ash content, correlated with an increase in angular silica particles in that fraction. The results provide quantitative input for updating the wear coefficient in maintenance scheduling models for pellet lines processing high-ash feedstocks. An empirical correction factor as a function of ash mass fraction is tabulated.

SYN-PUB-01790.title: Maintenance optimisation under uncertain feedstock quality: a Markov decision process approach for pellet mill scheduling
SYN-PUB-01790.text:
Maintenance optimisation under uncertain feedstock quality: a Markov decision process approach for pellet mill scheduling (2020, journal, European Journal of Industrial Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Savić (R0135); Aleksandar Lazić (outside co-author); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Radovan Petrušić (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: Markov decision process; maintenance scheduling; feedstock quality; pellet mill; stochastic optimisation.
A discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) is formulated for scheduling preventive maintenance of pellet mill roller assemblies when feedstock quality—represented as moisture content and ash fraction—follows a stochastic switching process between three quality states: optimal, moderate, and poor. Transition probabilities between quality states were estimated from 24 months of feedstock sampling records from a Vojvodina energy cooperative. Degradation of roller surface hardness was modelled as a function of quality state using field hardness measurements taken at 200-hour intervals. The state space encompasses roller degradation level (five discrete levels) combined with current quality state; the action space covers continue, inspect, and replace. Optimal policies were found by value iteration. The resulting policy recommends accelerating inspection to every 150 hours when the quality state shifts to poor, and this triggered policy reduces expected long-run cost per operating hour by 11.4% relative to a fixed 200-hour schedule in a simulation over 10,000 hours. Sensitivity of the optimal policy to transition probability estimation error is analysed.

SYN-PUB-01792.title: On-line acoustic emission monitoring for early detection of die cracking in flat-die pellet presses
SYN-PUB-01792.text:
On-line acoustic emission monitoring for early detection of die cracking in flat-die pellet presses (2022, journal, Measurement – Journal of the International Measurement Confederation).
Authors: Veljko Savić (R0135); Marija Stanković (outside co-author); Nemanja Vučković (outside co-author).
Keywords: acoustic emission; die cracking; pellet press; change-point detection; early warning.
Four resonant acoustic emission (AE) sensors were mounted on the die flange of a flat-die pellet press instrumented at a pilot facility in Novi Sad. The press was operated continuously for 720 hours processing corn stover pellets while die condition was assessed by periodic dye-penetrant inspection. An initial micro-crack network was confirmed by inspection at hour 480. AE hit rate, cumulative energy, and frequency centroid were computed in rolling 10-minute windows. A change-point detection algorithm (PELT with BIC criterion) applied to cumulative AE energy identified a statistically significant change point at hour 462 ± 6 hours, 18 hours before the first visual confirmation of cracking. The false alarm rate over the pre-cracking period was 0.7 alarms per 100 hours, using a threshold calibrated on a 120-hour noise baseline. The study demonstrates that AE monitoring can provide approximately 18–24 hours of advance warning for this failure mode under the tested operating conditions, sufficient for orderly production scheduling of a planned die replacement.

SYN-PUB-01793.title: Feedstock particle size distribution as a predictor of roller bearing vibration signature in a ring-die pellet mill: an experimental investigation
SYN-PUB-01793.text:
Feedstock particle size distribution as a predictor of roller bearing vibration signature in a ring-die pellet mill: an experimental investigation (2023, journal, Biosystems Engineering).
Authors: Nemanja Vučković (outside co-author); Claudia Ferenczi (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135).
Keywords: particle size; ring-die mill; vibration features; linear discriminant analysis; process monitoring.
Roller bearing vibration was measured on a ring-die mill fed with poplar wood chips sieved to four particle size classes: <2 mm, 2–4 mm, 4–6 mm, and 6–8 mm, and three mixture compositions. Vibration was captured at 25.6 kHz using tri-axial accelerometers mounted on both roller bearing housings. Statistical features—RMS, kurtosis, crest factor, and spectral power in the 1–3 kHz and 5–10 kHz bands—were computed per 30-second window. A one-way ANOVA confirmed significant differences in RMS (p < 0.001) and 5–10 kHz spectral power (p < 0.001) across particle size classes; kurtosis showed no significant sensitivity (p = 0.14). The coarse 6–8 mm class produced the highest bearing RMS values and was associated with intermittent slip events visible as amplitude modulations in the time-domain signal. A linear discriminant classifier trained on six vibration features achieved 84.1% correct classification of particle size regime in a leave-one-out cross-validation. The results suggest vibration features can serve as proxies for feedstock particle size in real-time process monitoring.

SYN-PUB-01794.title: Remaining useful life estimation for pellet mill rollers integrating feedstock quality forecasts from near-infrared spectroscopy
SYN-PUB-01794.text:
Remaining useful life estimation for pellet mill rollers integrating feedstock quality forecasts from near-infrared spectroscopy (2024, journal, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture).
Authors: Aleksandar Lazić (outside co-author); Veljko Savić (R0135); Filip Urošević (R0920); Marija Stanković (outside co-author); Ladislav Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: remaining useful life; particle filtering; NIR spectroscopy; feedstock quality; Bayesian degradation model.
This paper proposes a remaining useful life (RUL) estimation framework for pellet mill press rollers in which the degradation model is fed with short-horizon feedstock quality forecasts derived from on-line near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. A Bayesian linear Gaussian state-space degradation model tracks roller surface wear depth, estimated from periodic laser displacement measurements. NIR spectra collected from the feedstock hopper are reduced to moisture and ash fraction estimates using a partial least squares regression calibrated on 210 reference samples. A one-step-ahead quality forecast is generated from an autoregressive model fitted to 8 weeks of historical quality records at a pellet production site in Bačka. RUL distributions are propagated forward using particle filtering. On a holdout test period of 12 weeks, the 80% credible interval of the RUL distribution captured the actual roller replacement event in 9 of 11 trials. The framework reduced average excess roller service time beyond a safe replacement threshold from 68 hours to 22 hours compared with fixed-interval scheduling.

SYN-PUB-01795.title: Comparative evaluation of fixed-interval, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies for biomass pellet lines: a simulation study based on field failure data
SYN-PUB-01795.text:
Comparative evaluation of fixed-interval, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies for biomass pellet lines: a simulation study based on field failure data (2026, journal, International Journal of Production Research).
Authors: Veljko Savić (R0135); István Lukács (R0750); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Nemanja Vučković (outside co-author); Radovan Petrušić (outside co-author).
Keywords: discrete-event simulation; maintenance strategy comparison; pellet production line; availability; cost analysis.
A discrete-event simulation model of a full pellet production line—feed preparation, ring-die press, cooler, sieving, and bagging—was parameterised using failure and repair time distributions derived from 36 months of maintenance records from three commercial facilities in Vojvodina. Three maintenance strategies were compared: time-based fixed-interval (TBM), condition-based using a single vibration threshold (CBM), and predictive using the NIR-integrated RUL model developed in an earlier study (PM). Each strategy was evaluated over 10,000 simulated hours using 500 replications. Key performance indicators were line availability, number of unplanned stops, and total maintenance cost per tonne of product. CBM increased mean availability from 88.2% (TBM) to 91.6% while reducing unplanned stops by 31%. PM achieved 93.1% availability and reduced unplanned stops by 47% relative to TBM, at a modelled sensor and software cost premium of approximately 14,000 EUR per line per year. A break-even analysis shows PM becomes economically preferred over CBM at production volumes above approximately 4,200 tonnes per year for the cost structure prevailing in the studied facilities.

SYN-PUB-01950.title: Thermal analysis and PXRD characterisation of carbamazepine–nicotinamide co-crystals prepared by three mechanochemical routes
SYN-PUB-01950.text:
Thermal analysis and PXRD characterisation of carbamazepine–nicotinamide co-crystals prepared by three mechanochemical routes (2012, journal, Central European Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences).
Authors: Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Lidija Radić (R0151); Sanja Kovačević (outside co-author); Ivan Palijan (outside co-author).
Keywords: co-crystal; carbamazepine; mechanochemistry; Rietveld refinement; dissolution.
Carbamazepine–nicotinamide (1:1) co-crystals were prepared by neat grinding, liquid-assisted grinding (LAG) with three solvents, and twin-screw extrusion, and the products were compared by PXRD, DSC, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Neat grinding at ambient temperature yielded a mixture containing approximately 30% residual Form III carbamazepine after 60 minutes, whereas LAG with ethanol and water produced phase-pure co-crystal within 20 minutes based on Rietveld refinement of PXRD patterns (Rwp < 4.2%). Twin-screw extrusion at 70 °C and 100 rpm gave phase-pure product with a mean crystallite size of 112 nm estimated by the Scherrer equation, substantially smaller than LAG product (340 nm). DSC showed a single melting endotherm at 158 °C for the co-crystal versus 174 °C for Form III carbamazepine. Intrinsic dissolution rate measured in phosphate buffer pH 6.8 was 1.4-fold higher for the co-crystal than for Form III. The work provides a quantitative comparison of three scalable preparation routes relevant to pharmaceutical manufacturing.

SYN-PUB-01951.title: Confocal Raman mapping of co-crystal distribution in binary tablet matrices
SYN-PUB-01951.text:
Confocal Raman mapping of co-crystal distribution in binary tablet matrices (2014, journal, Pharmaceutical Characterisation and Technology).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Tijana Đorđević (outside co-author); Nikola Savić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Raman mapping; tablet characterisation; co-crystal; compaction; amorphisation.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-01952.title: Solid-state screening of ibuprofen co-formers selected by hydrogen-bond propensity calculations
SYN-PUB-01952.text:
Solid-state screening of ibuprofen co-formers selected by hydrogen-bond propensity calculations (2015, journal, Crystal Engineering and Materials Chemistry).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Adrián Fülöp (outside co-author).
Keywords: ibuprofen; co-crystal screening; hydrogen-bond propensity; dissolution rate; CSD.
Fourteen co-former candidates for ibuprofen were ranked using hydrogen-bond propensity (HBP) scores calculated from a Cambridge Structural Database subset of 1 200 entries containing carboxylic acid donors. The six highest-scoring candidates—nicotinamide, isonicotinamide, caffeine, l-proline, saccharin, and urea—were subjected to solution crystallisation, LAG, and spray-drying. PXRD, DSC, and solution-state ¹H NMR (DMSO-d₆) were used to confirm co-crystal formation. Three new co-crystalline phases were obtained: ibuprofen–isonicotinamide (2:1), ibuprofen–saccharin (1:1), and ibuprofen–l-proline (1:1). The ibuprofen–isonicotinamide co-crystal showed a 2.1-fold increase in intrinsic dissolution rate in pH 7.4 phosphate buffer and a powder flowability improvement (Carr index decreased from 28 to 19) relative to racemic ibuprofen. The HBP ranking correctly predicted three of four successful outcomes, supporting its utility as a pre-screening filter to reduce experimental effort. The ibuprofen–urea and ibuprofen–caffeine combinations gave only physical mixtures under all conditions tested.

SYN-PUB-01953.title: Variable-temperature PXRD study of a solvate–anhydrate transformation in a fluoroquinolone antibiotic
SYN-PUB-01953.text:
Variable-temperature PXRD study of a solvate–anhydrate transformation in a fluoroquinolone antibiotic (2016, journal, Journal of Pharmaceutical Solid-State Research).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author); Katarzyna Wiśniewska (outside co-author).
Keywords: solvate; anhydrate; variable-temperature PXRD; fluoroquinolone; dynamic vapour sorption.
A monohydrate and a dimethylformamide (DMF) solvate of a fluoroquinolone compound (coded FQ-7, a developmental compound) were characterised by variable-temperature PXRD in the range 25–200 °C at 2 °C min⁻¹ using a Cu Kα source equipped with an Anton Paar TTK 450 chamber. The monohydrate lost water over 60–90 °C yielding an anhydrous Form A (confirmed by TGA mass loss of 5.4 wt%, theoretical 5.6 wt%), while the DMF solvate desolvated at 130–150 °C yielding anhydrous Form B. Form A and Form B show distinct PXRD patterns and do not interconvert below 180 °C. Form A dissolved 1.8× faster than Form B in 0.1 M HCl at 37 °C in a rotating disc experiment. Dynamic vapour sorption (DVS) showed that Form A re-hydrates reversibly above 55% relative humidity, while Form B does not sorb water below 80% RH. These results have implications for storage condition specification and manufacturing decisions for FQ-7.

SYN-PUB-01954.title: Quantification of amorphous content in milled cefuroxime axetil by chemometric analysis of PXRD patterns
SYN-PUB-01954.text:
Quantification of amorphous content in milled cefuroxime axetil by chemometric analysis of PXRD patterns (2017, journal, Pharmaceutical Analytical Techniques).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Jelena Marinković (outside co-author); Tamás Kővári (outside co-author); Željko Zarić (R0391).
Keywords: amorphous content; PXRD; PLS regression; cefuroxime axetil; ball milling.
Ball milling of cefuroxime axetil (CA) at 400 rpm in a planetary mill introduced amorphous content that was quantified using two approaches: (i) a calibration curve based on physical mixtures of crystalline and spray-dried amorphous CA, and (ii) partial least squares (PLS) regression on the full 5–40° 2θ PXRD pattern. The PLS model, trained on 24 mixtures at 0–100% amorphous fraction (five replicates each), gave an RMSECV of 1.8% and RMSEP of 2.3% on an independent test set of 15 samples. The calibration curve method gave RMSEP of 4.1% under the same conditions. After 30 minutes of milling, amorphous content reached a plateau of approximately 42% ± 3%, as confirmed by independent DSC (measured by enthalpy of crystallisation on heating). Dissolution testing in pH 6.8 buffer at 37 °C showed that partially amorphous CA lots (≥ 35% amorphous) dissolved 1.6× faster than crystalline CA, but also showed greater variability across three production batches. The PLS-PXRD method is proposed as an in-line quantification tool.

SYN-PUB-01955.title: Raman mapping of spatial co-former distribution in spray-dried co-crystal intermediates as a function of drying inlet temperature
SYN-PUB-01955.text:
Raman mapping of spatial co-former distribution in spray-dried co-crystal intermediates as a function of drying inlet temperature (2019, journal, Journal of Pharmaceutical Solid-State Research).
Authors: Adrián Fülöp (outside co-author); Tijana Đorđević (outside co-author); Lidija Radić (R0151); Vesna Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: spray drying; Raman mapping; co-crystal; naproxen; inlet temperature.
Spray drying is increasingly considered for continuous manufacturing of pharmaceutical co-crystals, yet the effect of inlet temperature on intra-particle co-former distribution remains poorly understood. Naproxen–picolinamide co-crystal solutions in ethanol (5 wt% total solids, 1:1 molar ratio) were spray-dried at four inlet temperatures (80, 110, 140, and 170 °C) with a fixed outlet temperature range of 58–65 °C. Particles collected on filters were embedded in epoxy resin, sectioned to approximately 1 μm thickness, and mapped by confocal Raman microscopy (256 × 256 pixels, step 0.5 μm). At 80 °C, 94% of map pixels showed co-crystal phase; at 170 °C, this dropped to 71%, with naproxen-rich segregated domains appearing at the particle surface. PXRD quantification confirmed partial amorphisation (up to 18%) at 170 °C. Residual ethanol content measured by headspace GC decreased monotonically from 0.43 wt% at 80 °C to below the ICH Q3C limit at 140 °C. The findings indicate that an inlet temperature of 110–130 °C provides acceptable phase purity and solvent removal simultaneously.

SYN-PUB-01956.title: Solid-state characterisation of a ternary co-crystal: indomethacin, saccharin, and l-tartaric acid
SYN-PUB-01956.text:
Solid-state characterisation of a ternary co-crystal: indomethacin, saccharin, and l-tartaric acid (2021, journal, European Journal of Solid-State Pharmaceutical Chemistry).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Katarzyna Wiśniewska (outside co-author); Bojan Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: ternary co-crystal; indomethacin; solid-state NMR; dissolution; physical stability.
Ternary pharmaceutical co-crystals remain rare and their preparation is empirically guided. An indomethacin–saccharin–l-tartaric acid (1:1:1) ternary phase was obtained by LAG with acetonitrile and confirmed by PXRD (new diffraction peaks at 6.2°, 11.8°, and 17.4° 2θ not present in any binary sub-system), DSC (single eutectic-like endotherm at 148 °C), TGA, and solid-state ¹³C CP-MAS NMR collected at a national facility. Raman mapping of tablet cross-sections confirmed homogeneous co-crystal distribution. The ternary co-crystal dissolved 2.3× faster than crystalline γ-indomethacin in pH 6.8 phosphate buffer (USP Apparatus II, 37 °C, 75 rpm, n = 6), compared with 1.9× for the binary indomethacin–saccharin co-crystal prepared and tested under identical conditions. Physical stability testing at 40 °C / 75% RH for 12 weeks showed no detectable phase change by PXRD. The work demonstrates that controlled introduction of a third co-former can measurably improve dissolution performance beyond the binary co-crystal.

SYN-PUB-01957.title: Crystal engineering of aceclofenac co-crystals for improved aqueous solubility: systematic co-former selection and scale-up by twin-screw extrusion
SYN-PUB-01957.text:
Crystal engineering of aceclofenac co-crystals for improved aqueous solubility: systematic co-former selection and scale-up by twin-screw extrusion (2022, journal, Crystal Engineering and Materials Chemistry).
Authors: Vesna Ilić (outside co-author); Sanja Lukić (R0504); Lidija Radić (R0151); Marija Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: aceclofenac; co-crystal; twin-screw extrusion; solubility; stability.
Aceclofenac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with low aqueous solubility (0.011 mg mL⁻¹ at 25 °C). Twenty-two co-formers listed on the GRAS list were screened by LAG; five yielded new crystalline phases by PXRD. The three most stable candidates—nicotinamide, caffeine, and theophylline—were selected for full characterisation. DSC, TGA, PXRD, and Raman mapping confirmed co-crystal identity and purity. Aqueous solubility measured by the miniaturised shake-flask method (n = 3) increased to 0.034, 0.029, and 0.021 mg mL⁻¹ respectively for the three co-crystals. All three were prepared at 50 g scale by twin-screw extrusion (temperature 65 °C, screw speed 80 rpm, feed ratio adjusted to 1:1 molar), yielding phase-pure product as confirmed by PXRD with Rwp < 5.0%. Flowability (Hausner ratio) improved from 1.41 for pure aceclofenac to 1.22, 1.18, and 1.25 for the three co-crystals. A 24-month open-dish stability study at 25 °C / 60% RH showed no polymorphic conversion for nicotinamide and caffeine co-crystals; the theophylline co-crystal showed partial conversion to theophylline monohydrate after 6 months.

SYN-PUB-01958.title: Crystal engineering approaches to active pharmaceutical ingredients: from polymorph screening to co-crystal scale-up
SYN-PUB-01958.text:
Crystal engineering approaches to active pharmaceutical ingredients: from polymorph screening to co-crystal scale-up (2023, book chapter, Advances in Pharmaceutical Solid-State Science, Vol. 4 (edited volume, Springer Verlag–adjacent academic publisher)).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author).
Keywords: co-crystal; polymorph screening; PXRD; DSC; pharmaceutical development.
This book chapter provides a methodological overview of solid-state screening workflows for active pharmaceutical ingredients, intended for graduate students and early-career researchers entering the field. The chapter covers the logical sequence from initial polymorph screening through co-former selection, crystallisation method optimisation, and scale-up considerations. Specific sections address PXRD data collection and interpretation, DSC experimental design (mass, scan rate, atmosphere), Raman mapping data acquisition parameters and chemometric processing, and the use of crystallographic databases in co-former selection. Case studies drawn from the authors' own laboratory data on ibuprofen, carbamazepine, and aceclofenac co-crystals are used throughout. Quantitative benchmarks are provided for typical experimental outcomes: for example, the success rate of LAG screening from a random 20-member co-former set is reported from several published studies as 15–30%. The chapter concludes with a discussion of regulatory expectations for co-crystal characterisation, referencing the EMA reflection paper and FDA guidance.

SYN-PUB-01959.title: Fast-dissolving co-crystal pellets of piroxicam–malonic acid prepared by hot-melt extrusion: effect of polymer matrix on phase purity and in vitro release
SYN-PUB-01959.text:
Fast-dissolving co-crystal pellets of piroxicam–malonic acid prepared by hot-melt extrusion: effect of polymer matrix on phase purity and in vitro release (2025, journal, European Journal of Solid-State Pharmaceutical Chemistry).
Authors: Lidija Radić (R0151); Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Adrián Fülöp (outside co-author); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Katarzyna Wiśniewska (outside co-author).
Keywords: piroxicam; hot-melt extrusion; co-crystal; HPMCAS; supersaturation.
Piroxicam–malonic acid co-crystal (PMC, 1:1) was incorporated into pellets by hot-melt extrusion (HME) using three hydrophilic polymers: polyvinyl caprolactam–polyvinyl acetate–polyethylene glycol graft copolymer (Soluplus equivalent), hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS-MF grade), and polyvinylpyrrolidone–vinyl acetate 64 (PVP-VA64) at 20 wt% drug loading. Extrusion was carried out at 100–130 °C depending on polymer; torque and melt temperature were logged for all runs. Post-extrusion PXRD analysis showed that the PVP-VA64 matrix caused complete co-crystal-to-amorphous conversion, while HPMCAS-MF and Soluplus matrices retained 88% and 79% crystalline co-crystal, respectively (Rietveld quantification). Raman mapping of pellet cross-sections (64 × 64 pixels, step 3 μm) confirmed the co-crystal distribution correlated with PXRD results. In vitro dissolution in FaSSIF-V2 at pH 6.5 showed that all three pellet formulations exceeded the intrinsic dissolution rate of crystalline piroxicam by at least 2.1×, with the HPMCAS-MF pellets showing the most sustained supersaturation profile over 240 minutes. Six-month stability testing at 25 °C / 60% RH showed no further amorphisation in HPMCAS-MF pellets.

SYN-PUB-02130.title: Modelling conducted emissions from LED drivers: comparison of behavioural and circuit-level approaches
SYN-PUB-02130.text:
Modelling conducted emissions from LED drivers: comparison of behavioural and circuit-level approaches (2016, conference, EMC Europe 2016 – Proceedings of the European Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Wrocław).
Authors: Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Andrija Šarić (R0163); Petra Sedláček (outside co-author); Đorđe Petrović (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Veljko Bulatović (R0306).
Keywords: LED driver; conducted emissions; behavioural model; circuit-level model; aggregation.
Two modelling strategies for predicting conducted emissions from LED retrofit lamp drivers are compared: a behavioural model based on measured Thevenin equivalent source impedance and voltage, and a circuit-level model derived from the reverse-engineered schematic of three driver types with rated power of 7 W, 12 W and 18 W. Both models are embedded in a low-voltage network simulation and evaluated against LISN measurements over 150 kHz to 30 MHz. The behavioural approach reproduces measured emission profiles with an average RMS error of 3.1 dB but requires individual characterisation of each unit. The circuit-level model achieves 4.7 dB average error without unit-specific measurement but is sensitive to uncertainty in parasitic component values. A hybrid procedure combining measured impedance data with a simplified circuit skeleton reduces average error to 2.6 dB. The study covers 15 driver samples from four unnamed market sources. Implications for aggregated emission prediction when large numbers of LED luminaires are installed on a single feeder are discussed, with a Monte Carlo analysis of 50 to 500 simultaneous loads.

SYN-PUB-02145.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Judgment Outcomes: A Feasibility Study on Serbian Case Law
SYN-PUB-02145.text:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Judgment Outcomes: A Feasibility Study on Serbian Case Law (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Tibor Takács (R0251); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Sofija Mirković (R0164); Gregor Vidmar (outside co-author).
Keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; RAG; outcome prediction; dense retrieval; civil case law.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems combine a retrieval component with a generative model and have been applied to question answering in several legal jurisdictions, but their use for outcome prediction on small corpora remains unexplored. This preprint describes a feasibility study in which a dense retrieval index is built from 1,840 Serbian civil court decisions and used to condition a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence model on retrieved precedents at inference time. Three retrieval configurations—BM25, dense passage retrieval with a multilingual encoder, and a hybrid combination—are compared on a 200-instance test set. The hybrid configuration achieves the highest accuracy (0.71) and macro F1 (0.63), compared to 0.65 and 0.57 for the no-retrieval baseline. Analysis of retrieved documents shows that recency and jurisdictional tier of retrieved cases are positively associated with prediction correctness. The study flags limitations arising from incomplete metadata and inconsistent anonymisation in the source corpus.

SYN-PUB-02526.title: Extending the standard knowledge-tracing model with slip and guess priors estimated from population response distributions
SYN-PUB-02526.text:
Extending the standard knowledge-tracing model with slip and guess priors estimated from population response distributions (2014, journal, International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Nevena Simić (R0755); Anita Schulze (outside co-author); Bogdan Kapor (R0196); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: Bayesian knowledge tracing; slip and guess; EM algorithm; algebra tutoring.
The standard Bayesian knowledge-tracing (BKT) model assumes fixed, hand-tuned slip and guess parameters, which often leads to local optima and poor generalisation across learner populations. This paper proposes a population-informed BKT variant in which slip and guess priors are estimated from aggregate response distributions of a held-out calibration cohort before individual-level EM updating. The approach was tested on interaction logs from a secondary-school algebra tutoring system used by 2,104 students over one academic year, comprising 1.3 million item-response events. Compared to standard BKT, the population-prior model reduced mean absolute error in next-item predictions by 11.4 % and improved AUC from 0.71 to 0.76. Cross-validation over five disjoint school cohorts confirmed stability. The paper also provides identifiability conditions under which the prior-informed model is distinguishable from the standard formulation.

SYN-PUB-02565.title: Adaptive Spreading Factor Selection Using RSSI History and a Lightweight Decision Tree for Battery-Constrained LoRa Nodes
SYN-PUB-02565.text:
Adaptive Spreading Factor Selection Using RSSI History and a Lightweight Decision Tree for Battery-Constrained LoRa Nodes (2022, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan IoT and Embedded Systems Conference (BIESC), Novi Sad).
Authors: Branislava Janković (R0811); Marija Vučković (outside co-author); Ivan Radosavljević (outside co-author); Ivan Vlaisavljević (R0199).
Keywords: adaptive data rate; decision tree; energy efficiency; on-device inference; LoRa.
The standard ADR algorithm in LoRaWAN relies on the network server receiving at least 20 consecutive uplinks before adjusting the spreading factor, which is impractical for sensors transmitting infrequently. This paper describes an on-device decision tree trained on RSSI history from a 45-node deployment in Novi Sad collected over six months. The tree uses five features: last RSSI, RSSI variance over the last four frames, time of day, estimated battery voltage, and current SF. It was trained offline and compressed to a 2 kB lookup table deployable on Cortex-M0 class microcontrollers. In a six-week field evaluation, the algorithm reduced mean airtime per node by 23% compared with static SF10 and by 11% compared with standard ADR, while maintaining a packet delivery ratio above 96%. Mean current consumption per node decreased from 4.1 mA to 3.2 mA averaged over the evaluation period.

SYN-PUB-02612.title: Adapting formative quiz feedback for learners with attention difficulties: format, immediacy, and length
SYN-PUB-02612.text:
Adapting formative quiz feedback for learners with attention difficulties: format, immediacy, and length (2018, journal, Journal of Educational Multimedia and Hypermedia).
Authors: Gordana Stanković (outside co-author); Snežana Crnković (R0203); Renata Šobot (outside co-author); Klaus Mühlberger (outside co-author); Danijela Fejsa (R0207).
Keywords: formative feedback; attention difficulties; feedback format; UDL self-regulation; LMS.
Students with attention-related learning differences often disengage from formative feedback when it is presented in lengthy prose form after a delay. This study compared three feedback formats—extended prose, bulleted key-point summaries, and audio-recorded summaries—delivered either immediately or 24 hours after quiz completion, in a 3 × 2 factorial design with 96 upper-secondary students with documented attention difficulties. Immediate bulleted feedback produced the highest revision accuracy on a follow-up task (M = 71.4 %, SD = 9.2), outperforming delayed prose feedback by 18.6 percentage points. Audio summaries showed intermediate effects and were rated highest for perceived usefulness in a post-study questionnaire. Format and immediacy interacted significantly (F(2,90) = 6.14, p = .003). The results support the UDL guideline on providing options for self-regulation and suggest practical trade-offs for learning management system designers configuring automated feedback pipelines.

SYN-PUB-02651.title: Colour contrast and background complexity in digital worksheets: effects on reading speed for students with visual processing difficulties
SYN-PUB-02651.text:
Colour contrast and background complexity in digital worksheets: effects on reading speed for students with visual processing difficulties (2020, journal, European Journal of Special Needs Education).
Authors: Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Danijela Fejsa (R0207).
Keywords: colour contrast; WCAG; visual processing; digital worksheets; reading speed.
Poorly chosen colour combinations and busy background patterns are common in digitised worksheets circulated in Serbian primary schools, yet their effect on students with visual processing difficulties has not been studied locally. This study recruited 36 students (ages 9–11) with identified visual processing difficulties and 36 age-matched peers. Participants read 16 short passages presented in a 4 × 2 design crossing contrast ratio (WCAG AA compliant vs non-compliant) and background complexity (plain vs textured). Reading speed was measured in words per minute; comprehension was assessed with four forced-choice questions per passage. For students with visual processing difficulties, WCAG AA-compliant contrast combined with plain backgrounds produced a mean reading speed 23 % higher than the non-compliant textured condition (p < .001). The control group showed smaller but statistically significant differences in the same direction. The study provides empirical grounding for existing accessibility guidelines in a population that is underrepresented in the evidence base.

SYN-PUB-02652.title: A framework for rapid UDL auditing of existing LMS course structures in higher education
SYN-PUB-02652.text:
A framework for rapid UDL auditing of existing LMS course structures in higher education (2021, journal, Journal of Open, Flexible and Distance Learning).
Authors: Tamara Nikolić (outside co-author); Marta Vukić (outside co-author); Danijela Fejsa (R0207).
Keywords: LMS audit; accessibility; UDL in higher education; course design; remediation.
Learning management systems accumulate course materials over years without systematic accessibility review. This paper proposes a five-phase rapid auditing framework—inventory, automated check, manual check, learner-feedback probe, and remediation prioritisation—applicable within a single semester by a small institutional team. The framework was piloted at two Serbian universities, covering 47 active courses across four faculties. Automated checks using an open-source accessibility linter detected issues in 89 % of courses; manual checks revealed an additional 34 % of courses with problems invisible to automated tools, primarily in PDF attachments and embedded video without captions. Learner-feedback probes (n = 203 students) corroborated technical findings and added perceived barriers not captured by checklist approaches. The paper reports estimated remediation time per course type and discusses how remediation effort can be distributed between instructors and central e-learning support units without requiring large resource commitments.

SYN-PUB-02653.title: Automated readability adjustment of instructional texts: comparing three algorithms against teacher-expert benchmarks
SYN-PUB-02653.text:
Automated readability adjustment of instructional texts: comparing three algorithms against teacher-expert benchmarks (2023, journal, International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education).
Authors: Danijela Fejsa (R0207); Vladimir Ćosić (outside co-author); Dragana Glušac (outside co-author).
Keywords: text simplification; readability algorithms; NLP; instructional text; UDL representation.
Automated text simplification tools are increasingly offered within e-learning platforms as a means of scaling UDL-consistent representation options. This study evaluated three publicly available readability-adjustment algorithms—two rule-based and one based on statistical language modelling—against a benchmark set of 60 instructional paragraphs that had been manually simplified by eight experienced special-education teachers. Texts covered science and social studies content for grades 4–6. Algorithm output was rated by five independent expert raters on vocabulary appropriateness, retention of meaning, and grammatical acceptability, each on a 1–5 scale. The statistical model outperformed both rule-based tools on vocabulary appropriateness (M = 3.81 vs 2.94 and 3.02, F(2,177) = 18.6, p < .001) but scored lower than teacher benchmarks on meaning retention (M = 3.62 vs 4.41). All automated outputs showed grammatical issues specific to Serbian morphology. Findings caution against unsupervised deployment of automated simplification and recommend human editorial review as a minimum quality gate.

SYN-PUB-02654.title: Designing accessible video lectures: caption accuracy, speaker notes, and dual-coding effects for students with auditory processing difficulties
SYN-PUB-02654.text:
Designing accessible video lectures: caption accuracy, speaker notes, and dual-coding effects for students with auditory processing difficulties (2024, journal, Computers & Education).
Authors: Jelena Vasiljević (outside co-author); Nataša Milanović (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Danijela Fejsa (R0207); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: video lectures; captions; auditory processing; dual coding; higher education accessibility.
Video lectures have become a primary instructional format in higher education, yet their accessibility for students with auditory processing difficulties depends on caption quality and the availability of supplementary text. This study recruited 44 undergraduate students with documented auditory processing difficulties and 44 without, at two Serbian universities. Participants viewed six 8-minute video lectures presented in three conditions: no captions, auto-generated captions (mean word error rate 14.3 %), and manually corrected captions paired with downloadable speaker notes. A post-viewing retention test and a transfer application task measured learning outcomes. For students with auditory processing difficulties, the corrected-captions-plus-notes condition produced retention scores 21.7 percentage points higher than the no-caption condition (p < .001) and 9.4 points higher than auto-captions alone (p = .014). The no-caption vs auto-caption difference was not significant for this group. Control-group differences between conditions were smaller and only the corrected-plus-notes vs no-caption comparison reached significance. The study quantifies the cost of caption errors and supports the case for institutional captioning quality standards.

SYN-PUB-02655.title: Student self-monitoring tools in UDL-aligned digital environments: a mixed-methods study across three schools
SYN-PUB-02655.text:
Student self-monitoring tools in UDL-aligned digital environments: a mixed-methods study across three schools (2025, journal, Journal of Learning Analytics).
Authors: Renata Šobot (outside co-author); Marko Đurišić (outside co-author); Danijela Fejsa (R0207).
Keywords: self-monitoring; UDL engagement; learning analytics; specific learning differences; LMS.
Self-monitoring is a key element of the UDL engagement principle, yet digital tools supporting it are rarely evaluated with students who have specific learning differences in South-Eastern European contexts. This mixed-methods study followed 87 primary students (grades 6–8) across three inclusive schools in Vojvodina over one academic year. Students used a purpose-built self-monitoring module embedded in the school's existing LMS: they set weekly reading goals, logged completion, and received graphic progress displays. Quantitative analysis of log data showed that students with specific learning differences used the tool less frequently than peers (mean 2.1 vs 3.6 check-ins per week, p = .002) but showed a steeper improvement in goal-attainment rates over the year (interaction F(3,249) = 5.22, p = .002). Focus groups with 24 students identified low initial self-efficacy and interface complexity as barriers. Teachers reported that the tool improved their ability to identify students needing additional support early in a unit. Revised interface recommendations are derived from student and teacher feedback.

SYN-PUB-02656.title: Cross-disciplinary teacher collaboration in UDL material adaptation: lessons from a two-year professional development programme in Vojvodina schools
SYN-PUB-02656.text:
Cross-disciplinary teacher collaboration in UDL material adaptation: lessons from a two-year professional development programme in Vojvodina schools (2026, journal, Teaching and Teacher Education).
Authors: Emilija Šarić (outside co-author); Andrea Fehér (outside co-author); Gordana Stanković (outside co-author); Danijela Fejsa (R0207).
Keywords: professional development; teacher collaboration; UDL implementation; Vojvodina; material adaptation.
Sustainable implementation of UDL in schools depends on cross-disciplinary teacher collaboration, yet most professional development programmes focus on individual skill acquisition. This paper reports a process evaluation of a two-year professional development programme delivered across nine primary and secondary schools in Vojvodina (2023–2025), in which 74 teachers from different subject areas worked in mixed-discipline teams to adapt digital materials for students with specific learning differences. The programme comprised four full-day workshops, monthly peer-review sessions, and individual coaching. Pre/post questionnaires measuring UDL knowledge, collaborative self-efficacy, and adaptation self-efficacy were administered at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Significant improvements were observed on all three scales at 24 months (d = 0.71, 0.58, 0.84 respectively). Qualitative coding of workshop artefacts and field notes identified sustained cross-disciplinary collaboration as the mechanism most frequently credited by teachers for improvements in material quality. Barriers included timetable constraints and inconsistent school leadership support.

SYN-PUB-02734.title: Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom
SYN-PUB-02734.text:
Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom (2022, journal, Informatika i sistemi: Časopis za informacione tehnologije i računarstvo).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Dejan Vuković (outside co-author); Željko Đurić (R0213); Mónika Papp (R0524).
Keywords: pretraga u realnom vremenu; tok vesti; inkrementalni indeks; skalabilnost.
Sistemi za pretragu u realnom vremenu nad tokovima vesti zahtevaju inkrementalno ažuriranje indeksa s niskim kašnjenjem. Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu sistema koji obrađuje do 1 200 novinskih članaka u minuti, sa prosečnim kašnjenjem indeksiranja od 340 ms na jednom serverskom čvoru s 16 jezgara. Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije. Evaluacija preciznosti pretrage sprovedena je na simuliranom toku od 2,1 miliona članaka prikupljenih tokom 30 dana. Sistem je prilagodljiv i može se horizontalno skalirati dodavanjem čvorova za normalizaciju nezavisno od čvorova za indeksiranje.

SYN-PUB-02735.title: Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval
SYN-PUB-02735.text:
Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval (2023, journal, Information Processing and Management).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Éva Gyöngyössy (outside co-author); Željko Đurić (R0213); Miroslav Ćirić (outside co-author).
Keywords: multilingual embeddings; transformer; dense retrieval; mixed-script; fine-tuning.
Pretrained multilingual transformer models encode text at the subword level and might be expected to handle script variation implicitly, since their vocabularies cover both Serbian scripts. This paper measures to what extent this expectation holds in practice. We fine-tuned three publicly available multilingual models of different sizes on SrMIR-1, the mixed-script Serbian retrieval benchmark, and compared their nDCG@10 scores against a script-normalizing BM25 baseline and a hybrid model. Without fine-tuning, the multilingual models rank below the BM25 baseline on mixed-script queries. After fine-tuning on 12 000 query–passage pairs, the best model reaches nDCG@10 of 0.601, above the hybrid BM25 baseline of 0.587. However, for queries and documents that mix scripts within a single sentence, fine-tuned models underperform by up to 9 percentage points relative to their performance on single-script inputs, indicating that subword tokenization does not fully resolve the alignment problem. We release the fine-tuning splits and evaluation scripts.

SYN-PUB-02944.title: Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software
SYN-PUB-02944.text:
Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software (2011, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Software Engineering and Testing (CEWSET)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: mutation testing; finite state machines; embedded software; test adequacy; mutation operators.
This paper defines a catalogue of 18 mutation operators tailored to finite state machine (FSM) specifications commonly used in embedded control firmware. Operators cover state deletion, transition guard modification, action substitution, and reset-condition negation. An experiment was conducted on four open-source microcontroller firmware projects totalling approximately 14,000 lines of C code. Mutants were seeded automatically using a custom Python tool, and an existing hand-written test suite was used as the baseline oracle. Mutation scores ranged from 41% to 67% across the four subjects, revealing systematic gaps in transition coverage. The paper reports the proportion of equivalent mutants identified through static analysis (approximately 12% of all seeded mutants) and discusses the effort required for manual equivalence classification. The results motivate the need for specification-driven test generation rather than ad hoc test suite growth.

SYN-PUB-02945.title: Deriving Test Suites from UML Statecharts: A Comparison of Three Path-Selection Strategies
SYN-PUB-02945.text:
Deriving Test Suites from UML Statecharts: A Comparison of Three Path-Selection Strategies (2013, journal, Software Testing and Verification Journal).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Anita Kovačević (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Pavol Čáni (R0371).
Keywords: UML statecharts; model-based testing; path selection; test generation; embedded systems.
Model-based test generation from UML statecharts can follow different path-selection criteria, each yielding test suites of different size and fault-detection capability. This study compares all-transitions, all-transition-pairs, and boundary-interior path selection applied to a set of seven industrial-scale statechart models provided by a regional automotive supplier. Models ranged from 12 to 89 states and 18 to 204 transitions. Test cases were generated automatically and executed against seeded mutation faults. All-transition-pairs coverage detected 14% more mutants on average compared with all-transitions, while increasing test suite size by a factor of 3.1. Boundary-interior selection offered a middle ground but showed inconsistent results across subjects. Execution times on target hardware were measured to assess whether suite sizes remain feasible under real-time constraints. The paper recommends a hybrid strategy that applies all-transition-pairs only to safety-critical subsystems and all-transitions elsewhere.

SYN-PUB-02946.title: Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes
SYN-PUB-02946.text:
Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes (2015, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Control).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Elena Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: regression test selection; change-impact analysis; binary instrumentation; firmware; continuous integration.
Regression testing of embedded firmware is expensive because full test suite execution on hardware targets can take hours. This paper presents a lightweight change-impact analysis technique that identifies which tests in an existing suite are affected by a given firmware patch without requiring full re-execution. The method instruments the firmware binary at basic-block granularity to record coverage during an initial full run, then uses static call-graph differencing to predict which blocks are reachable from changed functions. On a dataset of 120 patches drawn from the version history of three open-source firmware projects, the technique retained on average 31% of the original test suite while missing 2.1% of fault-detecting tests. False negative rates are characterised per patch type. The implementation is released as a set of scripts wrapping GCC and a custom binary instrumentation tool. Practical integration into a continuous integration pipeline is described.

SYN-PUB-02947.title: Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation
SYN-PUB-02947.text:
Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation (2016, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Formal Techniques for Embedded Systems (FTES)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Anita Kovačević (outside co-author); Marco Ferreira (outside co-author).
Keywords: contract-based specification; interrupt-driven firmware; ISR testing; model-based test generation; ARM Cortex-M.
Interrupt-driven firmware presents challenges for model-based testing because interleaving of interrupt service routines (ISRs) with the main execution thread produces combinatorial state spaces. This paper proposes a contract language, IFContract, that allows engineers to annotate ISR entry and exit conditions, shared-variable invariants, and timing constraints using a syntax embedded in C comments. A parser translates annotations into an extended FSM representation. Test cases covering pairwise ISR–main-thread interactions are generated from this model. The approach was evaluated on firmware for a battery management unit implemented on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The generated suite comprised 147 test cases and detected all 38 manually seeded interface faults. Compared with a randomly generated suite of the same size, the model-based suite found 23% more faults. Annotation effort was measured at 2.3 lines of contract per 10 lines of ISR code on average.

SYN-PUB-02948.title: Weak Mutation vs. Strong Mutation for Assessing Test Suite Quality in Resource-Constrained Environments
SYN-PUB-02948.text:
Weak Mutation vs. Strong Mutation for Assessing Test Suite Quality in Resource-Constrained Environments (2017, journal, Software Testing and Verification Journal).
Authors: Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: weak mutation; strong mutation; mutation score; embedded testing; test quality.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-02949.title: Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems
SYN-PUB-02949.text:
Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Software Testing Methods for Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems, Springer).
Authors: Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Katarina Knežević (R0982); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; embedded systems; test generation; timed automata; coverage criteria.
This book chapter surveys the state of practice in model-based testing (MBT) as applied to embedded and cyber-physical systems. It covers modelling notations including UML statecharts, extended finite automata, and timed automata, and maps them to corresponding test generation algorithms. Coverage criteria are categorised into structural, fault-based, and requirements-based families. A discussion of toolchain integration addresses challenges specific to embedded targets: cross-compilation, hardware-in-the-loop execution, and limited observability. Two worked examples illustrate applying MBT to an automotive body control module and an industrial motor controller. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems including scalability to large state spaces, handling of real-time constraints, and the lack of standardised interfaces between modelling and test execution tools.

SYN-PUB-02951.title: Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic
SYN-PUB-02951.text:
Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic (2021, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Marco Ferreira (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Srđan Popović (outside co-author).
Keywords: test oracle; signal temporal logic; hardware-in-the-loop; automated testing; firmware verification.
Specifying correct output behaviour for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) firmware tests is labour intensive because engineers must manually define acceptable signal ranges and timing windows for each scenario. This paper investigates the use of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formulas as automatically checkable test oracles in HIL test environments. STL formulas are mined from a set of passing execution traces using a template-guided parameter synthesis procedure. The synthesised formulas are then used as oracles for new test runs. The approach was evaluated on a DC motor control firmware and a temperature regulation firmware, each executed on physical target hardware. Oracle construction time dropped from a median of 47 minutes per scenario (manual) to under 4 minutes (automated). False positive and false negative rates of synthesised oracles were 3.1% and 1.8% respectively across 310 test scenarios. Limitations related to non-deterministic hardware timing are discussed.

SYN-PUB-02952.title: Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm
SYN-PUB-02952.text:
Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm (2022, journal, Information and Software Technology).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Igor Starčević (R0738); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: formal specification; industrial case study; firmware development; communicating automata; defect reduction.
Adopting formal specification practices in industry requires integrating review steps into existing development workflows without excessive overhead. This paper reports a two-year action research study conducted with a Serbian firm that develops programmable logic controllers. The study introduced a lightweight formalism based on communicating extended finite automata (CEFA) for specifying firmware modules, along with a peer-review checklist and a set of automated consistency checks. Defect data were collected for 34 firmware modules developed before and after adoption. Post-adoption modules showed a 29% reduction in defects found during system integration testing. Developer survey data indicate that engineers found the notation acceptable after a two-day training course. Barriers including tool fragmentation and version control of model artefacts are documented. The paper provides a replication package containing the checklist, consistency check scripts, and anonymised defect logs.

SYN-PUB-02953.title: SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models
SYN-PUB-02953.text:
SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Testing and Analysis (ECSTA)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Luca Bianchi (outside co-author); Emilija Vranješ (R0749).
Keywords: mutation testing; extended finite automata; specification-level faults; model fidelity; test generation framework.
Most mutation testing tools operate at the source code level, but for model-based testing workflows it is useful to seed faults into the formal model rather than the implementation. SpecMutate is a framework that applies 23 mutation operators directly to extended finite automata (EFA) models serialised in an XML interchange format. Operators include guard weakening, output-action swapping, state-merge, and variable initialisation faults. The framework integrates with an open-source model-based test generator and reports the model mutation score alongside the implementation mutation score. An experiment on six firmware EFA models with a combined 312 states found that model mutation scores and code mutation scores diverged significantly for three of the subjects, indicating that the model had lower fidelity than assumed. Runtime for model mutation analysis was under two minutes per model on a standard workstation, making it suitable for pre-commit checks.

SYN-PUB-02954.title: Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data
SYN-PUB-02954.text:
Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering).
Authors: Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Elena Varga (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Luca Bianchi (outside co-author).
Keywords: test prioritisation; regression testing; fault localisation; APFD; history-based testing.
Test prioritisation orders a regression suite so that fault-detecting tests execute earlier, reducing feedback latency. This paper proposes a history-based prioritisation strategy that weights tests by the fault-localisation entropy of the code regions they cover across previous test campaigns. Coverage and fault data from nine firmware projects with histories spanning 12 to 31 releases were used to train and evaluate the strategy. The proposed approach achieved an average percentage of faults detected (APFD) of 0.78, compared with 0.61 for random ordering and 0.71 for a coverage-based baseline. Computational overhead of computing prioritisation order was below 90 seconds for all subjects. The paper also analyses how quickly the historical model degrades after a major refactoring event and proposes a simple reset heuristic triggered by structural change thresholds.

SYN-PUB-02955.title: Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios
SYN-PUB-02955.text:
Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios (2025, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.XXXXX).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; large language models; specification gaps; firmware testing; test scenario generation.
Model-based test generation is constrained by the completeness of the formal model: scenarios not captured in the specification are not tested. This preprint explores a workflow where an LLM is prompted with natural-language firmware documentation and existing EFA models to suggest additional test scenarios that may correspond to specification gaps. Suggested scenarios are reviewed by engineers and, if accepted, formalised as model extensions. The approach was piloted on three firmware modules from an industrial PLC project. Engineers accepted 41% of LLM suggestions after review; of those, 17 were formalised and added to the model. Subsequent mutation analysis showed an increase in model mutation score of 6.3 percentage points on average. The paper does not claim that LLM suggestions are reliable in general but characterises conditions under which they are useful as a complement to structured specification review.

SYN-PUB-02956.title: Automated Generation of Compatibility Test Cases from Android Permission Change Logs
SYN-PUB-02956.text:
Automated Generation of Compatibility Test Cases from Android Permission Change Logs (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Software Engineering (CECSE)).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author); Olivera Tomić (R0327).
Keywords: permission model; test case generation; Android; JUnit; automated testing.
Android's permission model underwent significant restructuring between API levels 22 and 23 with the introduction of runtime permissions, causing widespread behavioural incompatibilities in deployed applications. This paper presents PermGen, a tool that parses Android SDK change logs and permission usage declarations in application manifests to automatically generate JUnit-based test cases targeting permission-related execution paths. The tool was evaluated on 45 applications from the Google Play Store's productivity category, generating on average 17.3 test cases per application. Execution of generated suites on a physical device pool covering API levels 21 through 27 revealed 83 previously undocumented permission-handling defects across 31 applications. Compared to manually authored test suites covering the same permission scenarios, PermGen achieved 78% of the fault detection rate at 12% of the authoring effort, measured in developer-hours. Limitations regarding obfuscated code and dynamically requested permissions are discussed.

SYN-PUB-02958.title: Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration
SYN-PUB-02958.text:
Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration (2022, journal, Journal of Automation Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233).
Keywords: incremental generation; model-to-text; Xtend; PLC; software product lines; model differencing.
Full regeneration of PLC source code from a configuration model is straightforward but can be impractical in projects where manually authored customisation sections exist alongside generated code. This paper presents an incremental generation strategy that identifies which model elements have changed between two configuration revisions and regenerates only the affected Structured Text compilation units, preserving protected regions in unaffected units. Change detection is implemented as a model differencing step operating on XMI serialisations of feature model configurations, producing a delta structure that drives selective Xtend template invocation. The strategy was evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 50 configuration pairs derived from a packaging-machine product line model with 41 features. Regeneration time was reduced by a mean of 74% compared to full regeneration, with no instances of incorrect code produced across 1,200 generated file revisions as verified by a regression test suite. The paper formalises the notion of generation dependency to characterise when incremental regeneration is sound.

SYN-PUB-03013.title: Uticaj kvaliteta anotacije na performanse klasifikatora pravnih dokumenata: studija slučaja sa srpskim korpusom
SYN-PUB-03013.text:
Uticaj kvaliteta anotacije na performanse klasifikatora pravnih dokumenata: studija slučaja sa srpskim korpusom (2019, journal, Informatica – An International Journal of Computing and Informatics).
Authors: Nemanja Ćosić (outside co-author); Pavol Čáni (R0371); Ana Filipović (outside co-author); Radomir Janković (R0237); Ksenija Mitrović (R0552).
Keywords: annotation quality; inter-annotator agreement; BERT; legal classification; crowdsourcing.
Istraživanje analizira kako različiti nivoi neslaganja između anotatora utiču na performanse klasifikacionih modela u srpskom pravnom domenu. Eksperiment koristi tri različito anotatovane verzije istog korpusa od 3.600 dokumenata: prvu anotiranu od strane pravnih eksperata (visoka konzistentnost, kapa = 0,82), drugu od strane studenata prava (srednja konzistentnost, kapa = 0,67) i treću od strane opštih korisnika putem platforme sličnoj crowdsourcing modelu (niska konzistentnost, kapa = 0,54). Na svakoj verziji trenirani su logistička regresija, Random Forest i BERT-baziran model. Rezultati pokazuju da razlika u F1 meri između ekspertske i crowdsourced anotacije iznosi između 3,1 i 7,8 procentnih poena, zavisno od modela i pravne kategorije. BERT model pokazuje veću robustnost na bučne oznake od klasičnih modela. Diskutovane su implikacije za praktičnu organizaciju anotacionih projekata u pravnom domenu.

SYN-PUB-03207.title: Spatial copula modelling of extreme precipitation fields over the Carpathian–Pannonian region using max-stable processes
SYN-PUB-03207.text:
Spatial copula modelling of extreme precipitation fields over the Carpathian–Pannonian region using max-stable processes (2018, journal, Journal of Hydrometeorology).
Authors: Éva Molnár (outside co-author); Slađana Paunović (R0253); Radu Cojocaru (outside co-author); Nevena Kecman (R0408); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: max-stable processes; Brown–Resnick model; spatial extremes; composite likelihood; areal reduction factor.
Spatial risk assessment of extreme precipitation requires models that capture both the marginal behaviour at individual sites and the spatial dependence structure across the region. Max-stable processes provide a coherent framework for this task. Daily precipitation records from 62 stations in Hungary, Romania, Croatia and Serbia for the period 1971–2015 were obtained from national meteorological services. Marginal generalised extreme value parameters were estimated at each station, and three max-stable models — Smith, Schlather and Brown–Resnick — were fitted by pairwise composite likelihood. The Brown–Resnick model with an empirically estimated variogram was selected by the composite likelihood information criterion. Extremal coefficients between station pairs indicate that stations separated by more than 180 km are effectively independent for annual maximum daily precipitation. Areal reduction factors derived from the fitted model differ by up to 25 percent from those currently used in regional design guidelines.

SYN-PUB-03497.title: Frequency-Selective Impedance Measurement as an Indirect Indicator of Partial Discharge Onset Voltage in Oil-Paper Insulation
SYN-PUB-03497.text:
