Frequency-Selective Impedance Measurement as an Indirect Indicator of Partial Discharge Onset Voltage in Oil-Paper Insulation (2020, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation).
Authors: Ivana Novaković (R0280); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Katarzyna Walczak (outside co-author).
Keywords: impedance spectroscopy; oil-paper insulation; partial discharge inception; thermal ageing; dielectric diagnostics.
This study investigates whether changes in the complex impedance spectrum of oil-paper insulation at frequencies between 1 Hz and 1 MHz can serve as a precursor to partial discharge inception, measured by conventional IEC 60270 methods. Flat test cells consisting of three layers of thermally aged kraft paper impregnated with mineral oil were subjected to a step-ramp voltage protocol while simultaneous impedance spectra were recorded with a four-terminal impedance analyser at 50 V signal amplitude. For cells aged at 110 °C for periods of 0, 250, 500, and 1000 hours, the partial discharge inception voltage decreased from 12.1 kV to 7.4 kV while the loss tangent at 1 kHz increased from 0.0031 to 0.019. A peak in the derivative of the imaginary impedance component with respect to voltage, observable at frequencies above 10 kHz, consistently preceded electrical PD inception by 3–8% of the inception voltage in all 27 tested specimens. The method is proposed as a non-disruptive complement to acoustic PD monitoring during field transformer inspections.

SYN-PUB-03505.title: Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations
SYN-PUB-03505.text:
Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations (2026, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Ivana Novaković (R0280); Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Nándor Takács (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEC 62443; firmware update; industrial security standards; security level; OTA compliance.
IEC 62443 defines security levels and component requirements for industrial automation and control systems but provides limited normative guidance on firmware update mechanisms. This paper analyses firmware update security requirements implied by IEC 62443-3-3 and IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Levels 1 through 3, identifying 23 specific requirements that a compliant OTA firmware update subsystem must satisfy. For each requirement, the paper maps existing technical mechanisms — from HMAC-based integrity checking to certificate-based authentication and monotonic rollback counters — and identifies three areas where current practice does not clearly satisfy the standard's intent: cryptographic agility, update transaction atomicity across power loss events, and audit logging on Class 1 devices. A reference architecture for a compliant firmware update service is outlined, and the paper estimates implementation effort in person-months for each architectural component at three device capability tiers. The analysis is illustrated using data from two anonymised industrial deployments reviewed during the study.

SYN-PUB-03533.title: Conducted EMI Characterisation of a 2.2 kW IGBT Inverter Drive Under Variable Switching Frequency
SYN-PUB-03533.text:
Conducted EMI Characterisation of a 2.2 kW IGBT Inverter Drive Under Variable Switching Frequency (2013, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Miroslav Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: IGBT inverter; switching frequency; LISN; common-mode; CISPR 11.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-03535.title: A Lumped-Parameter EMI Source Model for Three-Phase PWM Drives: Parameter Extraction and Frequency-Range Validation
SYN-PUB-03535.text:
A Lumped-Parameter EMI Source Model for Three-Phase PWM Drives: Parameter Extraction and Frequency-Range Validation (2016, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Miroslav Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: EMI model; parameter extraction; vector network analyser; CM/DM separation; three-phase drive.
Accurate EMI source models are needed to reduce reliance on full-system measurements during filter development. This work describes a parameter extraction procedure for a lumped CM and DM source model of a three-phase 7.5 kW drive. Impedance parameters were extracted from open- and short-circuit measurements at the drive AC terminals using a vector network analyser across 100 kHz–30 MHz. The resulting model comprises eight passive elements representing the inverter module, gate-drive supply, motor cable, and chassis coupling capacitances. Model predictions of conducted emission spectra were compared against LISN measurements at three load points (25%, 50%, and 100% rated torque), yielding a root-mean-square spectral error of 2.1 dB for CM and 2.8 dB for DM components. The extraction procedure is repeatable and requires less than two hours of bench time, making it practical for production-variant characterisation in industrial settings.

SYN-PUB-03536.title: Passive EMC Filter Sizing for IEC 61800-3 Category C2 Compliance: A Design Procedure Based on Attenuation Margin Analysis
SYN-PUB-03536.text:
Passive EMC Filter Sizing for IEC 61800-3 Category C2 Compliance: A Design Procedure Based on Attenuation Margin Analysis (2017, journal, European Transactions on Electrical Power Systems).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Predrag Stanojević (outside co-author).
Keywords: EMC filter design; IEC 61800-3; attenuation margin; nanocrystalline core; insertion loss.
This paper presents a structured procedure for dimensioning passive EMC input filters for variable-speed drives to meet IEC 61800-3 Category C2 quasi-peak limits. The procedure uses measured CM and DM source impedances and a target attenuation profile derived from the gap between unfiltered emission spectra and the regulatory limit line, with a 6 dB safety margin applied throughout. Filter topologies (LC, LCL, and CL stages) are compared for a 15 kW test drive, and component values are selected to avoid resonances within the 150 kHz–2 MHz band that could cause limit exceedances at intermediate frequencies. Prototype filters were wound on nanocrystalline toroidal cores and verified by insertion-loss measurement per IEC 60939-3 before integration. Final compliance measurements confirmed that all quasi-peak and average readings were at least 5 dB below the Category C2 limit across the full 150 kHz–30 MHz range. Total filter volume was 0.38 litres and mass 0.61 kg for the 15 kW case.

SYN-PUB-03537.title: Effect of Motor Cable Length on Common-Mode Conducted Emissions in Variable-Speed Drive Systems
SYN-PUB-03537.text:
Effect of Motor Cable Length on Common-Mode Conducted Emissions in Variable-Speed Drive Systems (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD-CEE)).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283); Thomas Berger (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: motor cable; cable capacitance; cable shielding; CM emissions; transmission-line model.
Long motor cables are common in industrial installations and amplify common-mode conducted disturbances by adding distributed capacitance to ground. This experimental study quantifies the effect for shielded and unshielded cables of lengths 5 m, 20 m, and 50 m connected to a 5.5 kW drive. CM conducted emission levels at the drive input were measured for each combination. Unshielded 50 m cables increased broadband CM noise by 10–14 dB relative to the 5 m reference below 1 MHz, primarily due to cable-to-ground capacitance estimated at 3.4 nF for the 50 m case. Shield grounding at both ends reduced CM emissions by 5–9 dB across 150 kHz–5 MHz for the 20 m cable. A transmission-line model incorporating per-unit-length parameters measured by time-domain reflectometry reproduced the resonant structure of the emission spectrum within ±3 dB. Practical wiring recommendations derived from the data are summarised for installation engineers.

SYN-PUB-03538.title: Thermal Derating of EMC Filter Components Under Continuous Duty in Enclosed Drive Cabinets
SYN-PUB-03538.text:
Thermal Derating of EMC Filter Components Under Continuous Duty in Enclosed Drive Cabinets (2019, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Zoran Todić (R0660).
Keywords: thermal derating; film capacitors; nanocrystalline choke; insertion loss; cabinet temperature.
EMC input filters for variable-speed drives are frequently mounted inside closed industrial cabinets where ambient temperatures can reach 55–65 °C, yet most component datasheets specify capacitance and ESR at 25 °C. This study characterises the thermal behaviour of X2 and Y2 film capacitors and nanocrystalline common-mode chokes under continuous 100% rated current at cabinet temperatures up to 70 °C. Capacitance drift in Y2 components reached −12% at 65 °C, shifting insertion-loss notch frequencies by 4–7% and potentially reducing CM attenuation by up to 4 dB near design-critical frequencies. Core loss in nanocrystalline chokes increased surface temperature by 18 K above ambient at rated current, consistent with manufacturer core-loss curves. Updated derating guidelines are proposed that increase capacitor values by 15% and choke inductance by 10% relative to room-temperature designs to maintain compliant insertion loss across the operating temperature range.

SYN-PUB-03539.title: EMC Filter Design for SiC MOSFET-Based Motor Drives: Comparison with IGBT Baseline at 150 kHz–30 MHz
SYN-PUB-03539.text:
EMC Filter Design for SiC MOSFET-Based Motor Drives: Comparison with IGBT Baseline at 150 kHz–30 MHz (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 22nd European Conference on Power Electronics and Applications (EPE-ECCE Europe)).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Thomas Berger (outside co-author).
Keywords: SiC MOSFET; IGBT comparison; rise time; high-frequency EMI; four-stage filter.
Silicon carbide MOSFET inverters switch at voltages and currents with rise times below 50 ns, generating significantly higher high-frequency conducted emissions than conventional IGBT-based drives of equivalent power rating. This work compares the conducted emission spectra of a 7.5 kW SiC MOSFET drive (switching at 50 kHz) and an IGBT baseline (switching at 8 kHz) under the same load, and documents the additional filter attenuation required to achieve IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance for the SiC case. The SiC drive exceeded the Category C2 quasi-peak limit by up to 22 dB in the 5–30 MHz band compared to 9 dB for the IGBT. An optimised four-stage LC filter reduced the worst-case exceedance to within the 6 dB safety margin, at the cost of a 40% increase in filter volume relative to the IGBT design. Measured and simulated spectra agree within ±3 dB across the full range.

SYN-PUB-03540.title: Measurement Uncertainty in Conducted EMI Testing of Variable-Speed Drives: Contributions from LISN, Cable Routing, and Receiver Settings
SYN-PUB-03540.text:
Measurement Uncertainty in Conducted EMI Testing of Variable-Speed Drives: Contributions from LISN, Cable Routing, and Receiver Settings (2022, journal, Metrology and Measurement Systems).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283); Vera Knežević (R0320); Zoran Mihajlović (outside co-author); Radomir Bogdanović (R0344).
Keywords: measurement uncertainty; GUM; LISN; cable routing; CISPR 16.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-03541.title: EMC Considerations for Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Automation
SYN-PUB-03541.text:
EMC Considerations for Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Automation (2023, book chapter, Industrial Power Electronics: Systems, Devices and Applications (Springer, edited volume)).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Nataša Milošević (R0530); Tihomir Urošević (R0800).
Keywords: IEC 61800-3; PWM inverter; filter design; installation practice; industrial automation.
This book chapter provides a self-contained treatment of EMC requirements and mitigation strategies for variable-speed drive systems in industrial automation contexts. It covers the regulatory framework (IEC 61800-3, IEC 61000-6-2, and IEC 61000-6-4), the physical origins of conducted and radiated disturbances in PWM inverter drives, and practical filter and shielding design methods. Worked examples are based on measurement data from 2.2 kW to 55 kW drive systems. The chapter addresses installation variables including motor cable routing, grounding topology, and proximity to sensitive signal cables, with quantitative guidance on separation distances and screen termination. A section on SiC-based drives discusses how faster switching transitions alter both emission profiles and filter requirements relative to IGBT designs. The chapter is intended for practising engineers and postgraduate students with a background in power electronics.

SYN-PUB-03542.title: Frequency-Domain Characterisation of Ground Impedance Effects on Common-Mode Filter Performance in Drive Systems
SYN-PUB-03542.text:
Frequency-Domain Characterisation of Ground Impedance Effects on Common-Mode Filter Performance in Drive Systems (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Marco Trentini (outside co-author); Predrag Stanojević (outside co-author); Dimitrije Puzović (R0343).
Keywords: protective earth impedance; CM filter; Y-capacitor; field installation; insertion loss variability.
The attenuation provided by Y-capacitors in common-mode EMC filters depends on the impedance of the protective earth (PE) connection, which varies substantially between industrial installations. This paper characterises PE impedance at 47 industrial sites across northern Serbia using a vector network analyser, finding that impedance magnitude at 1 MHz ranges from 0.4 Ω to 18 Ω and exhibits significant inductive character above 500 kHz. The measured impedance profiles are used as input to a circuit simulation of a 15 kW drive with a three-stage CM filter, evaluating worst-case degradation in CM insertion loss. CM attenuation at 1 MHz degraded by up to 9 dB between the best and worst PE cases, rendering a filter that passed IEC 61800-3 Category C2 under laboratory conditions non-compliant in 14% of simulated field conditions. A modified filter topology using a split CM choke with partial differential-mode rejection reduces this variability to within ±2 dB.

SYN-PUB-03543.title: Active Common-Mode Voltage Reduction in SiC Inverter Drives Using Predictive PWM with Reduced Switching Vectors
SYN-PUB-03543.text:
Active Common-Mode Voltage Reduction in SiC Inverter Drives Using Predictive PWM with Reduced Switching Vectors (2026, preprint, arXiv (eess.SP)).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Thomas Berger (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283).
Keywords: common-mode voltage; SiC inverter; PWM strategy; zero vector elimination; bearing currents.
Common-mode voltage (CMV) generated by three-phase two-level inverters reaches peak values of Vdc/2 per switching event and is the primary driver of CM conducted emissions and bearing current damage in motor drives. This preprint evaluates a PWM strategy that restricts the active switching vector set to eliminate zero vectors, thereby reducing the peak CMV from Vdc/2 to Vdc/6 with no additional hardware. Implemented on a 7.5 kW SiC inverter drive, the strategy reduced CM conducted emission peaks in the 150–500 kHz band by 8–14 dB compared to standard space-vector PWM at equal fundamental output quality. Total harmonic distortion of the output phase voltage increased from 2.1% to 3.8%, remaining within acceptable limits. CM choke size in a co-designed filter was reduced by 35% for equivalent IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance. Thermal measurements confirm no significant change in switch loss distribution.

SYN-PUB-03544.title: Comparison of Deterministic and Empirical Propagation Models for Gateway Coverage Estimation in a European City Centre
SYN-PUB-03544.text:
Comparison of Deterministic and Empirical Propagation Models for Gateway Coverage Estimation in a European City Centre (2014, journal, European Wireless Communications Letters).
Authors: Tamás Varga (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Jasmina Jokić (R0769); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: ray tracing; Okumura-Hata; COST 231; gateway placement; city centre.
Gateway placement in LoRaWAN deployments is commonly guided by empirical models calibrated for generic urban environments, yet their accuracy in dense historic city centres with irregular street patterns is poorly documented. This paper compares predictions from the Okumura–Hata, COST 231 Walfisch–Ikegami, and a 3-D ray-tracing tool (implemented in-house) against 6 200 measurement points collected in the old town area of Pécs, Hungary. Building geometry was derived from a municipal GIS dataset at 1:500 scale. The ray-tracing model achieved a mean absolute error of 3.1 dB, compared with 6.4 dB and 8.9 dB for the two empirical models. Computational time for ray tracing was approximately 40 minutes per gateway location on a standard workstation; a reduced-order version using only two-bounce reflections reduced this to 9 minutes with a 0.8 dB increase in error. Practical implications for rapid deployment planning are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03561.title: A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments
SYN-PUB-03561.text:
A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments (2010, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286); Dragan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: authenticated bootloader; HMAC; IEEE 802.15.4; SCADA; firmware delivery.
This paper describes the design and evaluation of an authenticated bootloader protocol intended for 8-bit microcontroller-based sensor nodes communicating over IEEE 802.15.4 radio links in industrial SCADA deployments. The protocol uses HMAC-SHA256 for image authentication and a two-phase commit scheme to prevent partial writes during interrupted transmissions. Experimental evaluation was conducted on a testbed of 24 nodes deployed across a simulated substation environment, with artificial packet-loss rates ranging from 5% to 40%. Mean firmware delivery time for a 64 KB image increased from 38 seconds under ideal conditions to 147 seconds at 40% packet loss, while no corrupted images were accepted across 2 400 delivery trials. Code size overhead on the target MCU was 3.2 KB of flash. The paper also discusses replay-attack resistance and the limitations of symmetric key management at scale, proposing a zone-based key hierarchy as a practical mitigation for deployments with up to 500 nodes.

SYN-PUB-03562.title: Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links
SYN-PUB-03562.text:
Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Embedded Systems and Industrial Networks (WESIN)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: delta patching; bsdiff; VCDIFF; firmware update; constrained devices.
Firmware images for constrained devices rarely change more than a few percent between successive releases, yet most over-the-air update mechanisms transmit full images. This paper evaluates three binary delta algorithms — bsdiff, VCDIFF, and a purpose-built block-aligned differencer — applied to firmware images from four representative industrial sensor product lines. Patch sizes across 38 consecutive release pairs averaged 11.4% of full image size for bsdiff and 14.7% for the block-aligned approach, with the latter requiring 40% less RAM during reconstruction. Transmission time over a simulated 1.2 kbit/s channel, representative of 868 MHz narrowband industrial radio, was reduced from an average of 4.1 minutes to 28 seconds. Reconstruction failure rates under 10% artificial bit-error conditions were below 0.3% for all schemes when combined with a 16-bit CRC per block. The paper includes a complexity analysis and discusses applicability to devices with less than 8 KB of available RAM.

SYN-PUB-03563.title: Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела
SYN-PUB-03563.text:
Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела (2013, conference, Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР).
Authors: Нeнад Ћирић (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: формална верификација; SPIN; Promelamodel checking; firmware protocol; LTL.
У овом раду примењен је алат за проверу модела SPIN на протокол за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера у бежичним телеметријским мрежама. Протокол је моделован у Прометеловом језику, а верификација је обухватила 14 безбедносних и животних особина формулисаних у линеарној темпоралној логици. Пронађена су три услова у којима поновна репродукција старе поруке може да доведе до инсталације претходне верзије фирмвера ако је монотони бројач секвенце нулиран након ресетовања уређаја. Предложено је проширење протокола са тrajnim бројачем у заштићеном нелетљивом меморијском простору. Исправљени протокол је верификован без кршења постављених особина у простору стања са до 2,1 × 10⁸ стања. Рад такође дискутује ограничења апстракције криптографских примитива у SPIN моделу и предлаже методологију за раздвојено моделовање протоколне логике и криптографских претпоставки.

SYN-PUB-03564.title: Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study
SYN-PUB-03564.text:
Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study (2015, journal, International Journal of Industrial Communication and Control Systems).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Momčilo Nedeljković (R0441); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Tijana Marković (outside co-author); Dragan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: key distribution; wireless sensor networks; industrial security; Blom scheme; 6LoWPAN.
Managing cryptographic keys across hundreds of constrained field devices is a practical bottleneck in industrial wireless deployments. This paper systematically compares five key distribution schemes — pre-shared master key, pairwise key pre-distribution, a Blom matrix scheme, a hierarchical certificate authority approach adapted for 6LoWPAN, and an elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman bootstrapping protocol — across three criteria: memory footprint on a Cortex-M0 class device, time to complete key establishment after node power-on, and resilience to node capture. Measurements were taken on a physical testbed of 60 nodes. The Blom scheme achieved the best balance for networks under 200 nodes, requiring 1.8 KB RAM and completing key establishment in under 400 ms. The ECC bootstrapping protocol was the only scheme providing forward secrecy but demanded 14 KB RAM and 2.3 seconds for key exchange, making it unsuitable for the lowest-tier devices. Practical recommendations are derived for three deployment tiers based on device capability.

SYN-PUB-03565.title: Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site
SYN-PUB-03565.text:
Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site (2017, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (ISIEA-EU)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author); Tibor Pásztor (R0590).
Keywords: LoRa; LoRaWAN; firmware OTA; spreading factor; industrial site measurement.
LoRa physical layer spreading factors SF7 through SF12 offer data rates from roughly 250 bit/s to 5.5 kbit/s at the expense of airtime, a constraint with direct implications for over-the-air firmware update feasibility. This paper reports on measurements conducted at a chemical plant in Novi Sad over six weeks using a network of 18 end-devices at distances between 80 m and 1.4 km from a single gateway. Packet delivery ratio at SF12 averaged 91.3% under normal plant operation but dropped to 73.8% during periods of heavy crane and conveyor activity. A store-and-forward segmentation protocol with per-segment HMAC authentication was deployed, and mean time to complete a 32 KB firmware update was measured at 22 minutes at SF12. The paper proposes an adaptive spreading-factor selection policy that reduced average update time to 9.4 minutes while maintaining delivery success above 97% across all trials.

SYN-PUB-03566.title: Replay Attack Taxonomy and Countermeasure Classification for Over-the-Air Firmware Update Protocols
SYN-PUB-03566.text:
Replay Attack Taxonomy and Countermeasure Classification for Over-the-Air Firmware Update Protocols (2018, book chapter, Security Protocols for Embedded and Industrial Systems, Springer).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author).
Keywords: replay attack; firmware update; countermeasures; taxonomy; constrained devices.
Replay attacks against firmware update protocols can result in downgrade to vulnerable firmware versions, denial of service, or unnecessary device reboots in safety-critical industrial settings. This book chapter surveys replay attack vectors specific to constrained wireless devices, classifying them along four axes: attacker capability (passive monitor, active injector, insider), network topology (star, mesh, multi-hop), device state (idle, update-in-progress, post-install reboot), and available countermeasure class (nonce-based, timestamp-based, monotonic counter, challenge–response). For each combination, the chapter provides an analysis of effectiveness and implementation cost in terms of RAM, non-volatile write cycles, and required time synchronization infrastructure. Fourteen representative firmware update protocols from research literature and three from open-source embedded projects are mapped onto the taxonomy. The chapter concludes with a decision framework that assists protocol designers in selecting countermeasure combinations appropriate to their threat model and device constraints.

SYN-PUB-03567.title: Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-03567.text:
Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers (2019, journal, Microprocessors and Microsystems: Embedded Hardware Design).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author).
Keywords: Merkle tree; firmware patch; ECDSA; integrity verification; Cortex-M.
Applying binary patches to firmware in the field requires verification mechanisms that can detect partial or corrupted patch delivery without storing the complete expected image. This paper proposes a Merkle hash tree construction adapted for delta patches, where leaf nodes correspond to fixed-size patch chunks and the root hash is authenticated by an ECDSA signature over NIST P-256. The scheme was implemented on an STM32L4 series microcontroller with 64 KB RAM. Hash tree construction over a 16 KB patch (32 leaves) required 210 ms and consumed a peak of 4.1 KB stack space. Verification of a partial delivery — detecting one corrupted chunk among 32 — required fewer than 50 ms. The paper compares this approach against full-image HMAC and rolling-hash alternatives in terms of detection granularity, storage requirements, and recovery strategy. A discussion of the tradeoffs in choosing tree depth is included, with measurements at depths 3, 4, and 5.

SYN-PUB-03568.title: Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model
SYN-PUB-03568.text:
Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model (2020, journal, Transactions on Industrial Wireless Communications and Networking).
Authors: Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: duty cycle; 868 MHz ISM; LoRaWAN; firmware update latency; queuing model.
Regulatory duty-cycle limits in the European 868 MHz ISM band constrain transmission time to 1% in sub-band 1, directly affecting over-the-air firmware update completion times for LPWAN devices. This paper develops a queuing-theory-based analytical model for firmware delivery latency under duty-cycle constraints, accounting for segmentation overhead, retransmission probability, and concurrent traffic from non-update messages. The model is parameterised using empirical measurements from a 30-node LoRaWAN testbed. Analytical predictions of mean delivery time matched measurements within 8% across all tested configurations. The model predicts that for a 64 KB image at SF10, mean delivery time under 1% duty cycle is 4.7 hours in a lightly loaded network and rises to over 18 hours under moderate concurrent telemetry load. A scheduling strategy that prioritises update segments during predicted low-traffic windows is described and shown analytically to reduce mean delivery time by 31%.

SYN-PUB-03569.title: Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee
SYN-PUB-03569.text:
Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee (2021, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Wireless Sensor Systems and IoT Security (ECWSSIS)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author).
Keywords: Zigbee; multicast firmware; AES-CCM; industrial IoT; group key management.
When many co-located devices require the same firmware update simultaneously, unicast delivery multiplies airtime linearly with node count. This paper describes a secure multicast delivery scheme for Zigbee-based industrial sensor clusters, using AES-128 CCM* group encryption with individual per-device session key wrapping to prevent one node from decrypting another's update confirmation. The protocol was implemented on CC2530-based nodes and evaluated in a testbed of 8 and 16 node clusters. For a 48 KB image, multicast delivery to a 16-node cluster completed in 6.8 minutes versus 41.3 minutes for sequential unicast, a factor of 6.1 improvement. Delivery success rate was 98.7% at 16 nodes under representative packet loss of 8%. The paper analyses the key management overhead introduced by per-device key wrapping and discusses the session key refresh interval as a function of assumed node compromise rate.

SYN-PUB-03570.title: Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity
SYN-PUB-03570.text:
Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity (2022, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing).
Authors: Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: X.509; offline certificate validation; firmware authentication; constrained devices; public key infrastructure.
Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. The paper analyses the security implications of the short-lived certificate approach under various attacker models, including the case where the attacker can delay delivery to extend a certificate's apparent validity.

SYN-PUB-03572.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices
SYN-PUB-03572.text:
Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices (2024, journal, Journal of Cryptographic Engineering).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Nándor Takács (outside co-author).
Keywords: post-quantum cryptography; Dilithium; Falcon; SPHINCS+; firmware authentication; IoT benchmarking.
Anticipated deployment lifetimes of industrial sensor nodes of 10–20 years motivate evaluation of post-quantum signature algorithms for firmware authentication on severely constrained hardware. This paper benchmarks four NIST post-quantum signature candidates — CRYSTALS-Dilithium2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and a lattice-based scheme submitted to the ongoing standardisation process — on two representative Class 1 IoT platforms: an ARM Cortex-M0+ at 48 MHz with 32 KB RAM and a Cortex-M4 at 120 MHz with 256 KB RAM. Metrics collected include signature verification time, public key and signature sizes, and peak RAM consumption. On the Cortex-M0+ platform, Falcon-512 verification completed in 480 ms consuming 28 KB RAM peak, which exceeds available memory, while SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s verified in 1 140 ms with 6.2 KB peak RAM, making it the only scheme feasible on the lower-end device. Dilithium2 was feasible on the Cortex-M4 at 94 ms. The paper discusses the practical tradeoffs for protocol designers choosing between these schemes given device capability distribution in a deployment.

SYN-PUB-03573.title: Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments
SYN-PUB-03573.text:
Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments (2025, journal, Transactions on Industrial Wireless Communications and Networking).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT; adaptive segmentation; firmware delivery; deep indoor; CQI.
NB-IoT deployment in basement-level and shielded industrial environments produces highly variable signal conditions, with RSRP measurements in one monitored processing facility ranging from −85 dBm to −138 dBm across 22 fixed sensor positions. This paper describes an adaptive firmware delivery protocol that adjusts segment size and retransmission window based on real-time channel quality indicator reports available in the NB-IoT stack. Segment sizes were varied between 64 and 512 bytes; the adaptive scheme selected optimal sizes per device per update session. In a 22-device testbed deployment over four months, the adaptive protocol reduced total update time by 38% compared to a fixed 128-byte segment baseline and reduced the number of incomplete update sessions from 11.4% to 2.1%. Energy consumption per completed update was also measured on battery-powered nodes, with the adaptive scheme consuming 12% less energy due to fewer retransmissions. A lightweight predictor using a 5-point CQI moving average was sufficient to achieve near-optimal segment sizing.

SYN-PUB-03632.title: Sensitivity of deep-knowledge-tracing variants to hyperparameter choices: a systematic benchmarking on three open educational datasets
SYN-PUB-03632.text:
Sensitivity of deep-knowledge-tracing variants to hyperparameter choices: a systematic benchmarking on three open educational datasets (2023, journal, Transactions on Learning Technologies).
Authors: Nikola Stanković (outside co-author); Anita Schulze (outside co-author); Zlata Ristić (R0291); Emilija Zec (R0322); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: deep knowledge tracing; benchmarking; hyperparameter sensitivity; hidden Markov; educational data mining.
Deep knowledge tracing (DKT) and two extensions—DKT+ with forgetting regularisation and DKVMN with memory-augmented networks—were systematically benchmarked across three publicly released educational interaction datasets representing algebra tutoring (N ≈ 300,000 events), geometry tutoring (N ≈ 70,000 events), and a reading skills platform (N ≈ 45,000 events). A grid search over 216 hyperparameter combinations per model variant examined hidden-unit counts (32–256), dropout rates (0–0.5), learning-rate schedules, and sequence-length truncation thresholds. AUC for next-item prediction ranged from 0.71 to 0.79 across conditions; variance attributable to hyperparameter choice exceeded variance attributable to model variant for two of three datasets. A comparison with a well-tuned four-state hidden Markov baseline showed that HMM matched DKT AUC within 0.02 on the reading dataset while requiring 40-fold less computation. Recommendations for reproducible DKT evaluation are provided.

SYN-PUB-03793.title: Detecting Concept Drift in Imbalanced Behavioural Streams: A Comparison of Window-Based and Statistical Drift Detectors
SYN-PUB-03793.text:
Detecting Concept Drift in Imbalanced Behavioural Streams: A Comparison of Window-Based and Statistical Drift Detectors (2024, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Intelligent Data Analysis (ISIDA)).
Authors: Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Gregor Peterlin (outside co-author); Carla Marchetti (outside co-author); Petar Stevanović (R0833); Vukica Grujić (R0305).
Keywords: concept drift; data streams; ADWIN; imbalanced streams; online learning.
Operational anomaly detection systems face distribution shift over time as both normal and anomalous behaviour patterns evolve. This paper evaluates eight drift detection methods—ADWIN, Page-Hinkley, DDM, EDDM, STEPD, HDDM-A, HDDM-W, and a windowed Kolmogorov–Smirnov test applied to feature marginals—in the context of imbalanced data streams with minority class rates between 0.5% and 3%. Synthetic streams are constructed from three real tabular datasets by injecting controlled gradual and abrupt drifts at known positions. Drift detectors are combined with a random forest base model retrained on detection. ADWIN achieves the best trade-off between true-detection rate (0.82) and false-alarm rate (0.09) for gradual drift, while HDDM-W performs best for abrupt drift (detection rate 0.91). All methods show degraded performance when minority class density changes independently of the majority class, a scenario that standard drift benchmarks do not cover.

SYN-PUB-03829.title: Quantitative XRD phase analysis of PVD coating cross-sections after high-temperature oxidation and machining exposure
SYN-PUB-03829.text:
Quantitative XRD phase analysis of PVD coating cross-sections after high-temperature oxidation and machining exposure (2020, journal, Surface and Coatings Technology).
Authors: Jana Beranová (outside co-author); Danilo Grujić (R0377); Tamara Vukić (outside co-author); Marko Đurđević (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920); Jovan Bogićević (R0308).
Keywords: Rietveld refinement; XRD; TiAlN oxidation; CrAlN; phase analysis.
TiAlN, CrAlN and TiSiN coatings were subjected to two degradation routes: isothermal furnace oxidation (700 °C, 2 h in air) and actual turning exposure (AISI 4140, 45 HRC, 200 m/min, until VB = 0.3 mm). XRD patterns collected from coating cross-sections prepared by FIB milling were refined by the Rietveld method. After furnace oxidation, TiAlN showed 18 vol% rutile TiO₂ and 9 vol% α-Al₂O₃; CrAlN showed 6 vol% Cr₂O₃ and no alumina phase; TiSiN showed 3 vol% TiO₂. After machining exposure, oxide fractions were systematically lower for all coatings, suggesting that mechanical wear removes oxidised surface layers faster than they form. The retained face-centred cubic phase fraction correlated positively with residual hardness measured by nanoindentation (R² = 0.84). Results provide a quantitative basis for linking XRD phase changes to tribological performance degradation in used cutting inserts.

SYN-PUB-03940.title: Comparing SMOTE and ADASYN on Short Legal Texts with Fewer Than 500 Training Instances
SYN-PUB-03940.text:
Comparing SMOTE and ADASYN on Short Legal Texts with Fewer Than 500 Training Instances (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information and Intelligent Systems).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Aleksa Lazić (R0318).
Keywords: SMOTE; ADASYN; text resampling; TF-IDF; misdemeanour rulings.
Resampling techniques designed for tabular data are often applied to text feature vectors without assessing whether interpolation in high-dimensional TF-IDF space produces semantically coherent synthetic documents. This paper applies SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and ADASYN to a dataset of 487 Serbian misdemeanour rulings represented as 2,000-dimensional TF-IDF vectors, with minority classes containing as few as 31 samples. Classification performance is assessed using stratified five-fold cross-validation with SVM and gradient boosting classifiers. ADASYN yields the highest macro F1 improvement (from 0.34 to 0.51 for SVM), but manual inspection of 50 synthetic vectors shows that 38% contain feature combinations absent in any real document. The paper proposes a nearest-neighbour coherence filter that removes synthetic points deviating beyond two standard deviations from their class centroid, recovering coherence while retaining 81% of generated samples. This filtered variant outperforms unfiltered ADASYN on two of three evaluation metrics.

SYN-PUB-03969.title: Coordinated Reactive Power Dispatch in Low-Voltage Networks Using a Two-Stage Optimisation Framework
SYN-PUB-03969.text:
Coordinated Reactive Power Dispatch in Low-Voltage Networks Using a Two-Stage Optimisation Framework (2022, journal, Energies – Special Issue on Distribution Network Optimisation).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Luka Petrović (outside co-author); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Vera Knežević (R0320); Cristina Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: reactive power dispatch; two-stage optimisation; voltage control; on-load tap changer; distribution system operator.
This paper proposes a two-stage optimisation framework for coordinating reactive power resources in low-voltage distribution networks, combining a day-ahead scheduling stage based on forecast generation and load profiles with a real-time correction stage executed at 15-minute intervals. Reactive power resources considered include smart photovoltaic inverters, a single on-load tap changer at the MV/LV transformer, and a switched capacitor bank at the feeder midpoint. The day-ahead stage minimises total reactive power losses subject to voltage band constraints using a linear programming relaxation of the power flow equations. The correction stage applies a rule-based droop adjustment using local voltage measurements only, requiring no communication infrastructure. The framework is tested on a 52-node low-voltage benchmark network and validated on a real feeder topology from Novi Sad obtained from the distribution system operator. Simulation over a 30-day period shows average voltage deviation reduction of 34 % and reactive energy import reduction of 41 % relative to a no-control baseline. Computational time for the day-ahead stage is under 8 seconds on standard hardware.

SYN-PUB-03983.title: Latent class recovery of arithmetic skill states in primary-school learners: a simulation and empirical study
SYN-PUB-03983.text:
Latent class recovery of arithmetic skill states in primary-school learners: a simulation and empirical study (2010, journal, Journal of Educational Measurement and Assessment).
Authors: Miroslav Kovač (outside co-author); Tanja Horvat (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: latent class analysis; arithmetic skill; primary education; simulation study.
This study evaluated the accuracy of latent class analysis (LCA) for recovering discrete skill states in a sample of 412 third-grade pupils completing a computer-administered arithmetic battery. Three-, four-, and five-class solutions were compared using BIC, AIC, and entropy indices. Simulation conditions varied sample size (100–800), class separation (low, medium, high), and item discrimination. Results showed that four-class solutions with medium-to-high separation were recovered reliably at sample sizes above 250. Applied to the empirical data, a four-class model distinguished non-starters, counting-based solvers, partial-fact retrievers, and fluent retrievers, with class membership predicting end-of-year teacher grades (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Response latency added incremental classification accuracy beyond accuracy scores alone (ΔBIC = −38). Implications for adaptive routing in primary mathematics software are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03985.title: Response time as a diagnostic signal in adaptive vocabulary tests: evidence from an IRT-based speed–accuracy model
SYN-PUB-03985.text:
Response time as a diagnostic signal in adaptive vocabulary tests: evidence from an IRT-based speed–accuracy model (2015, journal, Language Testing and Assessment Quarterly).
Authors: Vera Petrović (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: response time; speed-accuracy model; adaptive testing; vocabulary assessment.
This study applied a joint speed–accuracy IRT model—specifically a hierarchical version of the van der Linden (2007) framework—to data from an adaptive English vocabulary test taken by 934 university students in Serbia. The test consisted of 60 items drawn from a calibrated bank and was delivered via a browser-based platform that logged response times at millisecond resolution. Separate latent dimensions for ability and speed were estimated; the correlation between person speed and ability was −0.22, indicating that faster responders were not reliably more accurate. Item-level analyses showed that high-frequency vocabulary items elicited shorter and less variable response times, while low-frequency items produced bimodal response-time distributions consistent with dual-process retrieval. A subscore derived from response-time residuals predicted self-reported study habits independently of accuracy-based scores. Implications for adaptive test termination rules are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03986.title: Hidden Markov models for tracking conceptual change in secondary-school physics: a comparison of transition structures
SYN-PUB-03986.text:
Hidden Markov models for tracking conceptual change in secondary-school physics: a comparison of transition structures (2016, journal, Computers & Education Research).
Authors: Ivan Radovanović (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author); Miroslav Kovač (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: hidden Markov model; conceptual change; physics simulation; knowledge states.
Conceptual change in Newtonian mechanics was modelled as a latent Markov process using interaction logs from a physics simulation environment used by 318 high-school students across eight weeks. Four hidden states—misconception-dominant, transitional, partial-correct, and expert—were hypothesised based on prior qualitative research. Three transition structures (unconstrained, left-to-right, and partially ordered) were compared by marginal likelihood. The partially ordered model, which permitted regression from partial-correct to transitional but not to misconception-dominant, provided the best fit (ΔBIC = 112 versus unconstrained). State residence times averaged 3.1 instructional sessions for the transitional state. Instructional scaffolding events logged by the system were associated with a 2.3-fold increase in forward transition probability. The study provides a template for embedding hidden Markov diagnostics in simulation-based science learning environments.

SYN-PUB-03988.title: Detecting disengaged response patterns in large-scale online assessments using mixture IRT with a non-effortful responder class
SYN-PUB-03988.text:
Detecting disengaged response patterns in large-scale online assessments using mixture IRT with a non-effortful responder class (2018, journal, Educational and Psychological Measurement).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Katarina Vukić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: mixture IRT; disengagement; response time; large-scale assessment; non-effortful responding.
A mixture IRT model was developed to jointly estimate item parameters and classify respondents as effortful or non-effortful, using both accuracy and response-time features. The model was applied to data from a national diagnostic assessment of mathematics delivered online to 11,342 eighth-grade students in Serbia in 2018. The non-effortful class, characterised by near-chance accuracy and response times below 4 seconds, comprised 8.7 % of the sample. Excluding non-effortful respondents shifted item difficulty estimates by up to 0.42 logits for cognitively demanding items and narrowed ability-distribution standard deviation from 1.21 to 1.09. A sensitivity analysis using three alternative time thresholds confirmed stability of class membership above 82 % agreement. The study quantifies the impact of disengagement on population ability estimates and provides a mixture-model framework that can be integrated into operational assessment pipelines.

SYN-PUB-03989.title: Clickstream feature engineering for early prediction of learning outcomes in a university-level statistics MOOC
SYN-PUB-03989.text:
Clickstream feature engineering for early prediction of learning outcomes in a university-level statistics MOOC (2019, journal, Journal of Learning Analytics).
Authors: Nikola Stanković (outside co-author); Anita Schulze (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: clickstream analysis; MOOC; dropout prediction; learning analytics; IRT.
Forty-seven clickstream features—covering session frequency, video replay rates, quiz attempt sequences, forum post counts, and time-of-day patterns—were extracted from the activity logs of 2,891 enrolees in a university-level introductory statistics MOOC run over 12 weeks. Feature importance was assessed via gradient-boosted trees and logistic regression; a parsimonious nine-feature model achieved AUC = 0.81 for dropout prediction at week four, compared to AUC = 0.68 for a baseline demographic model. Psychometric analysis using a two-parameter IRT model applied to weekly quiz items showed that estimated ability trajectories up to week three predicted final certificate attainment with r = 0.74. Combining ability trajectories with clickstream features in a stacked model improved AUC to 0.84. The study identifies a minimal feature set suitable for deployment in low-resource learning management systems.

SYN-PUB-03990.title: Estimating knowledge-state transitions without ground-truth labels: an expectation-maximisation approach for unstructured course logs
SYN-PUB-03990.text:
Estimating knowledge-state transitions without ground-truth labels: an expectation-maximisation approach for unstructured course logs (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Educational Data Mining (EDM 2021)).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Ferretti (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322); Nevena Simić (R0755).
Keywords: knowledge tracing; EM algorithm; unstructured logs; corporate learning; label-free estimation.
Most knowledge-tracing studies rely on structured item banks with known correct answers; many real-world e-learning platforms produce unstructured logs where correctness labels are absent or unreliable. This paper develops an EM-based procedure that infers binary correctness proxies from response-time distributions, item co-occurrence patterns, and sequential consistency, without requiring manual item annotation. The procedure was validated on two datasets: a synthetic log generated from a known BKT model (parameter recovery RMSE ≤ 0.06) and an anonymised log of 7,200 learners using a corporate onboarding platform where ground-truth performance ratings were available for a 15 % subsample. On the subsample, inferred correctness correlated r = 0.68 with human ratings. Knowledge-state trajectories estimated from the inferred labels predicted six-month retention test scores (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) after controlling for time on platform. The procedure requires only event-timestamp and item-identifier fields.

SYN-PUB-03991.title: Psychometric calibration of an eye-tracking-based reading fluency diagnostic for early primary grades
SYN-PUB-03991.text:
Psychometric calibration of an eye-tracking-based reading fluency diagnostic for early primary grades (2022, journal, Reading and Writing: An Interdisciplinary Journal).
Authors: Sonja Babić (outside co-author); Ivan Radovanović (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: eye tracking; reading fluency; Rasch model; early literacy; primary education.
An eye-tracking-based reading fluency assessment was developed and calibrated for first- and second-grade children (N = 344, ages 6–8) using a Rasch model applied to fixation-derived accuracy scores and a log-normal response-time model for reading rate. Stimuli consisted of 36 short passages graded by lexical frequency and syntactic complexity. Item calibration indicated good fit (infit MNSQ range: 0.83–1.17) for 31 of 36 passages; five passages were revised after think-aloud protocols revealed ambiguous illustrations. Test information peaked at θ = −0.8, appropriate for the target population. A concurrent validity study against an established teacher-administered oral reading fluency probe yielded r = 0.73. Differential item functioning by gender was absent for 34 of 36 items. The diagnostic was subsequently embedded in a tablet-based assessment application deployed in 12 primary schools in Vojvodina.

SYN-PUB-03992.title: Alignment between formative diagnostic inferences and summative grades: an IRT-based audit across six secondary-school subjects in Serbia
SYN-PUB-03992.text:
Alignment between formative diagnostic inferences and summative grades: an IRT-based audit across six secondary-school subjects in Serbia (2024, journal, Assessment in Education: Principles, Policy & Practice).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Katarina Vukić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: formative assessment; summative grades; multidimensional IRT; grade inflation; secondary education.
Data from six secondary-school subjects—mathematics, Serbian language, biology, history, physics, and English—were collected from a digital learning management platform used by 3,412 students in 22 schools across Serbia during one academic year. For each subject, a multidimensional IRT model was estimated from platform quiz responses, and inferred diagnostic ability scores were compared to end-of-year teacher grades using Pearson and Spearman correlations, classification accuracy matrices, and Bland–Altman agreement plots. Correlations ranged from 0.51 (history) to 0.74 (mathematics). Systematic grade inflation relative to diagnostic scores was found in 14 of 22 schools, with a mean offset of 0.4 grade points on a five-point scale. Schools with higher diagnostic–grade alignment also showed lower within-school grade variance. The findings suggest that diagnostic platform scores and teacher grades measure partially overlapping but non-redundant constructs.

SYN-PUB-03993.title: Inferring prerequisite structures among skills from observational response data: a constraint-based graphical modelling approach
SYN-PUB-03993.text:
Inferring prerequisite structures among skills from observational response data: a constraint-based graphical modelling approach (2026, journal, Journal of Educational Data Science).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Ferretti (outside co-author); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Sonja Babić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322); Luka Nedić (R0911).
Keywords: prerequisite structures; causal discovery; skill graphs; adaptive learning; mathematics.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-04013.title: Evaluation of PERSIANN-CDR Satellite Precipitation Estimates Against Ground Observations Over the Middle Danube Basin, 2003–2013
SYN-PUB-04013.text:
Evaluation of PERSIANN-CDR Satellite Precipitation Estimates Against Ground Observations Over the Middle Danube Basin, 2003–2013 (2015, journal, International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Remote Sensing Research).
Authors: Žarko Pejić (R0364); Tamás Kovács (outside co-author); Isidora Vranješ (R0981); Danijela Đorđević (R0324); Miroslava Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Halász (outside co-author).
Keywords: PERSIANN-CDR; bias evaluation; Middle Danube Basin; daily precipitation; satellite validation.
Satellite-derived precipitation products are increasingly used in data-sparse regions, but their accuracy must be assessed against independent ground observations before application in agronomic or hydrological models. This study evaluated PERSIANN-CDR daily and monthly precipitation estimates over the Middle Danube Basin covering Serbia, northern Croatia, and southwestern Hungary, comparing them with records from 47 synoptic stations for the period 2003–2013. Statistical metrics including bias ratio, correlation coefficient, probability of detection, and false alarm ratio were computed at both temporal aggregations. At the monthly scale, PERSIANN-CDR showed a mean wet bias of 8.4% over the study area, with overestimation concentrated in the Fruška Gora foothill zone and underestimation over the flat Vojvodina plain. Daily performance was markedly lower, with a probability of detection of 0.61 and a false alarm ratio of 0.34 for events exceeding 10 mm. Systematic biases identified here were used as inputs for a multiplicative bias correction scheme applied in follow-up downscaling work.

SYN-PUB-04014.title: Constructing a 25-Year Field-Scale Rainfall Archive for Vojvodina and Its Application to Historical Burn Analysis of Parametric Crop Insurance
SYN-PUB-04014.text:
Constructing a 25-Year Field-Scale Rainfall Archive for Vojvodina and Its Application to Historical Burn Analysis of Parametric Crop Insurance (2026, journal, Climate Services).
Authors: Ljubica Ristić (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364); Marco Ceriani (outside co-author); Danijela Đorđević (R0324); Stevan Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: rainfall archive; burn analysis; parametric insurance; ERA5; TMPA; maize; sunflower.
Actuarially sound index insurance products require long historical records at the spatial resolution at which policies will be written. This paper describes the construction of a daily, 1 km resolution rainfall archive for Vojvodina spanning 1999–2023, produced by applying the KED downscaling framework to a blended ERA5–IMERG covariate and using all available station records (29–48 stations per year depending on network completeness). Archive consistency across the pre-IMERG era was maintained by substituting TMPA 3B42 for years before 2014 after demonstrating statistically equivalent covariate performance. A burn analysis was performed for three parametric products—sowing-period deficit, flowering-period excess, and grain-filling deficit—for maize and sunflower across 1,214 cadastral municipalities. Mean annual payout frequencies under tested trigger calibrations ranged from 14% to 27% depending on product and crop. The archive and analysis scripts are made publicly available. These outputs are intended to support insurers and reinsurers operating in the Pannonian agricultural zone in setting actuarially fair premiums.

SYN-PUB-04278.title: Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija
SYN-PUB-04278.text:
Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija (2010, conference, Zbornik radova Konferencije o primeni računara i interneta u Srbiji (PRIS 2010)).
Authors: Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349).
Keywords: invertovani indeks; mešovito pismo; normalizacija; srpski jezik.
U radu se opisuje metodologija izgradnje invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo. Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji, a zatim se fonemski ključevi koriste kao primarni identifikatori u indeksu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na korpusu od 120 000 novinskih članaka preuzetih iz tri srpska dnevna lista u periodu 2000–2008. Mere preciznosti i odziva upoređene su s dva bazična sistema koji koriste isključivo ćirilični, odnosno isključivo latinični indeks. Predloženi sistem postiže F1 vrednost od 0,81 u zadatku ad-hoc pretrage, što je povećanje od 14 procentnih poena u odnosu na bolji od dva bazična sistema. Rad takođe razmatra pitanje memorijskog otiska hibridnog indeksa i predlaže strategiju kompresije rečnika.

SYN-PUB-04279.title: Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification
SYN-PUB-04279.text:
Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification (2011, journal, Journal of Language Technology and Computational Linguistics).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Radovan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: phoneme canonicalization; Serbian; script unification; legal text retrieval.
Serbian is officially written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts, and documents frequently contain tokens in both scripts within a single sentence or paragraph. This paper presents a token canonicalization procedure in which each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions, and the resulting phoneme string serves as the canonical form for retrieval purposes. We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions. The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline and from 11.7% to 2.4% compared with a Cyrillic-only baseline. Precision at rank 10 improved by 8 percentage points over both baselines. Edge cases involving foreign loanwords and proper nouns are discussed, and a set of override rules is proposed for the 230 most frequent exceptions identified in the corpus.

SYN-PUB-04280.title: Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search
SYN-PUB-04280.text:
Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search (2014, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Information Retrieval Symposium (CEIRS 2014)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Tomislav Blažević (outside co-author); Milena Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: query expansion; transliteration; web search; Serbian; named entity.
Users searching Serbian-language web content often type queries in one script while relevant documents are stored in the other. This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index. We constructed a test collection of 1 800 queries and 210 000 web pages crawled from .rs domains, with relevance judgments pooled from four assessors. Three expansion strategies were compared: (1) appending the full transliteration variant, (2) appending only tokens whose transliteration differs from the original by more than two characters, and (3) expanding only named entities detected by a rule-based tagger. Strategy 3 achieved the best mean average precision of 0.497, versus 0.431 for no expansion, while reducing index bloat to 6% over the baseline index size. We also report retrieval latency measurements on a commodity server, showing that the overhead introduced by expansion remains under 12 ms at the 95th percentile for queries up to eight tokens.

SYN-PUB-04281.title: Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima
SYN-PUB-04281.text:
Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima (2015, conference, Zbornik radova 23. Telekomunikacionog foruma TELFOR).
Authors: Bojan Marković (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Ana Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: detekcija nedoslednosti pisma; klasifikacija; digitalni arhivi; srpski jezik.
Digitalni arhivi srpskih novina i institucionalnih dokumenata često sadrže nedoslednosti gde je isti dokument delom u ćirilici, a delom u latinici, ponekad zbog grešaka pri skeniranju ili uredničkih intervencija. Ovaj rad predlaže metod automatske detekcije takvih nedoslednosti na nivou rečenice, korišćenjem klasifikatora koji kao atribute uzima raspodelu skriptnih blokova, učestalosti bigrama i morfosintaksičke signale. Klasifikator je treniran na 9 400 ručno označenih rečenica iz arhive jednog novosadskog lista i testiran na 2 100 rečenica iz arhive beogradskog lista. Postiže preciznost od 0,91 i odziv od 0,88 u klasi nedoslednih rečenica. Korak korekcije primenjuje fonemsku transliteraciju na detektovane nedosledne tokene. Eksperiment na donstremu (pretragom dokumenta) pokazuje da korigovana verzija arhive daje veću tačnost od nekorigovane za 7 procentnih poena u prosečnoj preciznosti.

SYN-PUB-04282.title: A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval
SYN-PUB-04282.text:
A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval (2017, conference, Language Resources and Evaluation Conference Proceedings (LREC-SE 2017)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark corpus; evaluation; mixed-script; BM25; retrieval models.
Reproducible evaluation of retrieval systems for Serbian requires a shared test collection that explicitly accounts for mixed-script documents. This paper describes the construction of SrMIR-1, a benchmark corpus comprising 95 000 documents from four genres — news, law, literature, and social media — with 600 topics and graded relevance judgments produced by 12 trained assessors following TREC-style pooling at depth 30. Approximately 41% of documents contain tokens in both scripts. Inter-assessor agreement, measured by Cohen's kappa, was 0.73 across all topics. The paper reports baseline results for five retrieval models: BM25, language modelling with Dirichlet smoothing, a transliteration-aware BM25 variant, a neural dense retrieval model fine-tuned on Serbian, and a hybrid sparse–dense model. The transliteration-aware BM25 variant achieves the highest nDCG@10 of 0.531 among sparse models, while the hybrid model reaches 0.587. The corpus is publicly available under a Creative Commons licence.

SYN-PUB-04284.title: Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering
SYN-PUB-04284.text:
Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Workshop on Slavic Natural Language Processing (SlavicNLP 2021)).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: passage retrieval; question answering; BM25; script normalization; Serbian.
Open-domain question answering over Serbian-language document collections requires a passage retrieval component that is robust to the script in which both the question and the passage are written. This paper describes an adaptation of a BM25-based passage retrieval pipeline in which the tokenizer applies script normalization before indexing and at query time. We built an evaluation set of 340 factoid questions with 1 to 4 correct passages each, drawn from a mixed-script encyclopedia-style corpus of 180 000 passages. We compared four configurations: BM25 with no normalization, BM25 with script normalization, a dense bi-encoder model trained on Serbian data, and a hybrid of the latter two. The script-normalized BM25 retrieves at least one correct passage in the top 20 for 72% of questions, a gain of 17 percentage points over unnormalized BM25. The hybrid model reaches 81%. Failure analysis highlights questions containing transliterated foreign proper nouns as the main remaining challenge.

SYN-PUB-04285.title: Normalizacija skripte u kontekstu pretraživača internih dokumenata za mala i srednja preduzeća: iskustva iz prakse
SYN-PUB-04285.text:
Normalizacija skripte u kontekstu pretraživača internih dokumenata za mala i srednja preduzeća: iskustva iz prakse (2024, conference, Zbornik radova SYmposium on Informatics and Applied Mathematics (SIAM-Serbia 2024)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Bojan Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: interna pretraga; MSP; normalizacija pisma; implementacija; evaluacija.
Mala i srednja preduzeća u Srbiji čuvaju interne dokumente — ugovore, zapisnike, izveštaje — u mešovitom pismu bez konzistentne politike. Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma razvijenim u okviru naše istraživačke grupe. Pilot kompanije imale su kolekcije između 8 000 i 45 000 dokumenata. Merili smo preciznost pretrage pre i posle uvođenja normalizacije, korisnički odaziv i troškove uvođenja. U svim slučajevima normalizacija je poboljšala preciznost za najmanje 11 procentnih poena. Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema. Rad identifikuje i ograničenja: module treba ažurirati kada kompanija uvede novu terminologiju u jednom pismu, jer inicijalni rečnik sinonima nije potpun.

SYN-PUB-04286.title: SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers
SYN-PUB-04286.text:
SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers (2025, journal, ACM Transactions on Information Systems).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author); Éva Gyöngyössy (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark; social media; administrative text; script mixing; evaluation.
SrMIR-1, released in 2017, covered news, law, literature, and general web content. Since then, social media posts and administrative e-government documents have become important retrieval targets, both exhibiting pronounced script mixing and informal orthography. This paper describes SrMIR-2, which adds two new document registers to the benchmark: 60 000 posts from a Serbian microblogging platform and 28 000 administrative forms and decisions from three municipal e-government portals. We created 280 new topics for these registers with relevance judgments from six trained assessors (kappa = 0.69). Baseline experiments show that script-normalizing BM25 outperforms unnormalized BM25 by a larger margin on social media (22 percentage points in nDCG@10) than on administrative documents (9 points), attributable to the higher rate of informal transliteration in social media. The benchmark is released with code for reproducible evaluation. We also report an ablation study isolating the contribution of named-entity handling in the normalization pipeline.

SYN-PUB-04287.title: Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load
SYN-PUB-04287.text:
Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load (2026, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Information Retrieval (ECIR 2026)).
Authors: Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Dejan Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: production retrieval; latency; accuracy; cascaded pipeline; query log analysis.
Deploying script-normalizing retrieval in production requires careful attention to latency, especially when normalization involves neural components. This paper presents a systematic study of trade-offs along the latency–accuracy spectrum for five pipeline configurations ranging from a purely deterministic rule-based normalizer to a full transformer-based normalizer, tested on a simulated production workload derived from query logs of a Serbian news aggregator with peak loads of 340 queries per second. We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes. The deterministic normalizer adds 3 ms median latency with MRR of 0.61. The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile. A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms. Detailed profiling data and configuration files are provided.

SYN-PUB-04331.title: Effect of Wire Feed Speed and Arc Voltage on Spatter Generation in Short-Arc MIG Welding of 1.5 mm Mild-Steel Sheet
SYN-PUB-04331.text:
Effect of Wire Feed Speed and Arc Voltage on Spatter Generation in Short-Arc MIG Welding of 1.5 mm Mild-Steel Sheet (2013, journal, Welding and Joining Technology — Journal of the Serbian Welding Society).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Bojana Mijatović (R0352); Miroslav Tešanović (outside co-author); Branislav Krstić (outside co-author).
Keywords: MIG welding; spatter; arc voltage; wire feed speed; factorial design.
This study examines the combined influence of wire feed speed (3.5–7.0 m/min) and arc voltage (16–22 V) on spatter mass loss and bead geometry in short-arc MIG welding of 1.5 mm S235JR sheet. A 3² full-factorial design with three replicates was used, yielding 27 weld runs on 150 × 80 mm coupons in flat position. Spatter was collected on adhesive-coated collector plates and weighed on a 0.1 mg resolution balance. Bead cross-sections were metallographically prepared and measured for width, penetration depth, and reinforcement height. Results show that arc voltage has the dominant effect on spatter mass, accounting for 61 % of total variance in the ANOVA model, while wire feed speed primarily governs penetration. A voltage window of 17.5–18.5 V at 5.5 m/min feed rate reduced spatter by 38 % relative to the supplier-recommended default settings without compromising joint tensile strength, verified by cross-weld tensile tests at 415 ± 12 MPa.

SYN-PUB-04455.title: Test Flakiness in Machine Learning Pipelines: Characteristics and Preliminary Detection Heuristics
SYN-PUB-04455.text:
Test Flakiness in Machine Learning Pipelines: Characteristics and Preliminary Detection Heuristics (2023, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Testing and Debugging Machine Learning Systems (TDML)).
Authors: Petar Stevanović (R0833); Olivera Sredojević (R0363); Renata Marković (outside co-author); Petra Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: flaky tests; machine learning pipelines; non-determinism; static analysis; Python.
Machine learning (ML) training pipelines introduce sources of non-determinism—random weight initialisation, data shuffling, hardware-level floating-point variability—that make conventional flakiness detection approaches ill-suited. This paper characterises flakiness in 8 Python ML projects that use pytest for unit and integration testing, identifying 94 flaky tests through repeated reruns (each test executed 50 times per configuration) across three hardware environments. Findings show that 61 % of flakiness in this corpus is attributable to unseeded random operations and 22 % to floating-point tolerance mismatches in assertion statements. A set of lightweight static heuristics based on AST patterns—detecting torch.manual_seed absence, numpy.random calls, and hard-coded floating-point thresholds in assertions—detects 68 % of flaky tests at a false positive rate of 11 %. The paper positions ML pipeline flakiness as a distinct sub-problem requiring dedicated tooling, and outlines a research agenda.

SYN-PUB-04458.title: Automating MISRA-C:2012 Violation Repair Using Syntax-Directed Rewriting
SYN-PUB-04458.text:
Automating MISRA-C:2012 Violation Repair Using Syntax-Directed Rewriting (2019, journal, Software: Practice and Experience).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Nataša Kovačević (outside co-author); Sonja Lukić (outside co-author); Olivera Sredojević (R0363); Renata Pflüger (outside co-author).
Keywords: MISRA-C; automated refactoring; Clang LibTooling; embedded C; compliance.
Achieving compliance with MISRA-C:2012 in a legacy codebase typically involves many hundreds of manual edits. This paper describes a tool, MisraFix, that uses Clang's LibTooling infrastructure to implement syntax-directed rewriting rules for 34 of the 143 MISRA-C:2012 rules classified as decidable and automatable by the authors. The tool is evaluated on a corpus of five embedded firmware codebases totalling 312 kB of C source. Before applying MisraFix, a commercial MISRA-C checker reported 2,847 violations across the five projects; after automated repair, 1,654 violations were resolved (58.1%). All repaired versions compile and pass their existing test suites without modification. The paper categorises the remaining violations by reason for non-automation: semantic ambiguity, required developer intent, or interaction with platform-specific extensions. Runtime of the tool ranges from 3 to 41 seconds per project. Source code and the rewriting rule descriptions are published under a permissive open-source licence.

SYN-PUB-04460.title: Comparison of IDW and Ordinary Kriging for Monthly Rainfall Interpolation in the Vojvodina Lowlands Using a Sparse Station Network
SYN-PUB-04460.text:
Comparison of IDW and Ordinary Kriging for Monthly Rainfall Interpolation in the Vojvodina Lowlands Using a Sparse Station Network (2013, journal, Journal of Spatial Hydrology and Geoinformatics).
Authors: Žarko Pejić (R0364); Miroslava Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: ordinary kriging; IDW; monthly rainfall; Vojvodina; cross-validation.
Accurate spatial representations of monthly rainfall in flat agricultural regions are difficult to achieve when ground station density is low. This study compared inverse distance weighting (IDW) and ordinary kriging (OK) for interpolating monthly precipitation totals across Vojvodina using data from 24 meteorological stations maintained by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia for the period 2001–2010. Cross-validation was performed by withholding one station at a time; root mean square errors were 18.3 mm for IDW and 14.7 mm for OK at the monthly scale, with the largest discrepancies occurring during convective summer months.
