Semivariogram analysis revealed a mean range of approximately 62 km for summer months and 110 km for winter months, indicating substantial seasonal changes in spatial autocorrelation structure. The results suggest that ordinary kriging outperforms IDW in this region but that both methods underestimate peak rainfall cells associated with localised convective events. These findings informed subsequent work on integrating satellite data as auxiliary covariates.

SYN-PUB-04461.title: Kriging with External Drift Using IMERG Precipitation as a Covariate for Sub-Monthly Rainfall Mapping at 1 km Resolution in Northern Serbia
SYN-PUB-04461.text:
Kriging with External Drift Using IMERG Precipitation as a Covariate for Sub-Monthly Rainfall Mapping at 1 km Resolution in Northern Serbia (2018, journal, Agricultural and Forest Meteorology Letters).
Authors: Žarko Pejić (R0364); Stevan Marković (outside co-author); Nataša Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: kriging with external drift; GPM IMERG; 1 km downscaling; growing season; northern Serbia.
This study applied kriging with external drift (KED) to downscale 10-day accumulated rainfall to a 1 km grid over northern Serbia, using GPM IMERG Late Run estimates as the external drift variable and data from 31 ground stations as primary observations. The analysis covered the 2014–2018 growing seasons (April–September). IMERG values were resampled from their native 0.1° resolution to 1 km using bilinear interpolation before entering the KED framework. Leave-one-out cross-validation showed that KED reduced RMSE by 21% relative to ordinary kriging and by 34% relative to IDW, averaged across the study period. Performance gains were most pronounced during spatially heterogeneous convective periods in June and July. The resulting 1 km grids captured within-field rainfall gradients of up to 15 mm per 10-day period across large agricultural parcels, which ordinary kriging had smoothed over. Maps produced in this study were subsequently used as candidate index layers for parametric crop insurance pilot design.

SYN-PUB-04462.title: Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of Input Precipitation Grids
SYN-PUB-04462.text:
Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of Input Precipitation Grids (2020, journal, Journal of Agricultural Risk and Finance).
Authors: Ljubica Ristić (outside co-author); Nataša Filipović (outside co-author); Marco Ceriani (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: rainfall deficit index; basis risk; maize insurance; CHIRPS; ERA5; DSSAT.
Index insurance products that trigger payouts based on area-average rainfall can suffer from basis risk when the spatial resolution of the underlying precipitation data does not capture field-level variability. This study quantified how the choice of precipitation grid resolution (0.25°, 0.05°, and 1 km downscaled) affects the properties of a 30-day rainfall deficit index (RDI) designed for rainfed maize in Vojvodina. Historical RDI series were reconstructed for 1995–2018 using ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25°, CHIRPS at 0.05°, and a KED-downscaled product at 1 km. Basis risk was approximated by computing the correlation between field-scale simulated crop water deficits from a DSSAT maize model and each RDI series for 120 sample parcels. Pearson correlation with the 1 km RDI was 0.71, versus 0.58 for CHIRPS and 0.49 for ERA5. Trigger and exit thresholds calibrated on the 1 km product changed payout frequency by up to 18 percentage points compared with coarser inputs. The findings support the use of downscaled grids in parametric product design where field-level basis risk reduction is a priority.

SYN-PUB-04465.title: Field-Level Validation of Downscaled Precipitation Grids Using Dense Micro-Station Networks in Two Vojvodina Municipalities
SYN-PUB-04465.text:
Field-Level Validation of Downscaled Precipitation Grids Using Dense Micro-Station Networks in Two Vojvodina Municipalities (2024, journal, Journal of Hydrometeorology).
Authors: Žarko Pejić (R0364); Ana Vučković (outside co-author); Nataša Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: micro-station network; field-level validation; tipping-bucket gauge; convective events; downscaling accuracy.
Validating precipitation downscaling products at the field level requires ground truth at sub-kilometre spacing, which standard meteorological networks cannot provide. This study deployed a temporary network of 18 tipping-bucket rain gauges at 300–600 m spacing across two municipalities in Vojvodina—Bačka Palanka and Zrenjanin—during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons, collecting data at 15-minute resolution. These measurements were withheld from the downscaling model and used exclusively for validation. The KED-downscaled product at 1 km showed mean absolute errors of 3.1 mm per 10-day period, compared with 5.8 mm for bilinearly resampled IMERG and 4.4 mm for CHIRPS. The micro-station data also revealed that within-field gradients exceeding 8 mm per 10-day period occurred in approximately 12% of observed convective events, confirming that field-level insurance products cannot rely on grid spacings coarser than 1–2 km in this region. Equipment deployment and data management protocols developed here are available as a supplementary technical guide.

SYN-PUB-04466.title: Assessing sub-kilometre spatial coherence of convective rainfall using a dense disdrometer transect across the Fruška Gora ridge
SYN-PUB-04466.text:
Assessing sub-kilometre spatial coherence of convective rainfall using a dense disdrometer transect across the Fruška Gora ridge (2024, journal, Quarterly Journal of Hydrometeorology).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Тамара Јовановић (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Srđan Ognjanov (R0388); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: spatial coherence; disdrometer transect; Fruška Gora; convective rainfall; decorrelation length.
A transect of 22 optical disdrometers spaced 800 m apart along a 17.5 km line perpendicular to the Fruška Gora mountain ridge was operated during May–September 2022 to characterise the spatial decorrelation of convective rainfall intensity at sub-kilometre scales. During 38 convective events, inter-instrument correlation coefficients for 5-minute intensities were computed as a function of separation distance and storm advection direction. The correlation length for 5-minute intensities exceeded 8 km for stratiform rainfall but dropped to 2.1 km for intense convective cells (R > 20 mm h⁻¹). An anisotropy ratio of 1.6 was identified between the ridge-parallel and ridge-perpendicular directions, attributable to orographic forcing of cell alignment. These results impose quantitative limits on the validity of spatial interpolation at spacings used by most national rain-gauge networks. Implications for the accuracy of kriging-merged products at sub-hourly time steps are discussed with reference to the error budgets reported in our earlier Pannonian Plain merging study.

SYN-PUB-04467.title: Atmospheric correction of Landsat-5 TM imagery over lowland agricultural areas using MODIS-derived aerosol optical depth
SYN-PUB-04467.text:
Atmospheric correction of Landsat-5 TM imagery over lowland agricultural areas using MODIS-derived aerosol optical depth (2011, journal, Journal of Applied Remote Sensing and Cartography).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364); Bojana Petrović (outside co-author); Vukica Čolić (R1014).
Keywords: Landsat-5; 6S atmospheric correction; MODIS AOD; surface reflectance; Vojvodina.
Accurate atmospheric correction is a prerequisite for quantitative surface reflectance retrieval in flat, spectrally homogeneous landscapes. This study evaluates the MODTRAN-based Second Simulation of a Satellite Signal in the Solar Spectrum (6S) code applied to a 2008–2010 Landsat-5 TM archive covering the Vojvodina plain, using collocated AERONET and MODIS MOD04 aerosol optical depth (AOD) at 550 nm as input. Twenty-seven cloud-free scenes were processed. Substituting MODIS-derived AOD for the standard rural aerosol model reduced the root-mean-square error of surface reflectance in the red band from 0.031 to 0.018 when validated against 14 in-situ spectroradiometer measurements collected on concurrent ground-truth campaigns. Corrections were smallest in the blue band (residual RMSE 0.025) owing to remaining uncertainty in the fine-mode fraction. Results confirm that MODIS MOD04 provides a practical, spatially continuous AOD input suitable for retrospective archive processing in the region, avoiding the dependence on sparse sunphotometer networks.

SYN-PUB-04468.title: Object-based classification of informal housing clusters in post-socialist peri-urban zones: a case study of Novi Sad
SYN-PUB-04468.text:
Object-based classification of informal housing clusters in post-socialist peri-urban zones: a case study of Novi Sad (2011, journal, Journal of Applied Remote Sensing and Spatial Analysis).
Authors: Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Jelena Ostojić (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364); Marina Malešević (R0730).
Keywords: OBIA; QuickBird; informal housing; random forest; Novi Sad.
This study applied object-based image analysis (OBIA) to a 2009 QuickBird-2 mosaic (0.6 m pan-sharpened) covering 48 km² on the southern and eastern fringes of Novi Sad to delineate informal residential clusters. Segmentation was performed with a multiresolution algorithm at scale parameters 40–80. Seventeen spectral, textural and geometric features were derived per segment, and a random forest classifier trained on 620 manually labelled reference objects achieved an overall accuracy of 87.3 % (kappa 0.83). The method distinguished informal structures from formal low-density housing and agricultural storage buildings with a producer accuracy of 84 % and user accuracy of 89 % for the informal class. Results documented approximately 340 ha of informally constructed residential fabric predating the 2009 imagery, concentrating along the Danube floodplain margins and two main arterial corridors. The paper discusses the sensitivity of results to segmentation scale choice and the transferability of the feature set to adjacent municipalities.

SYN-PUB-04469.title: Temporal comparison of peri-urban expansion in three Vojvodina towns using Ikonos and WorldView-1 imagery, 2003–2010
SYN-PUB-04469.text:
Temporal comparison of peri-urban expansion in three Vojvodina towns using Ikonos and WorldView-1 imagery, 2003–2010 (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 8th International Symposium on Remote Sensing of Urban Areas (URS 2013), Bucharest).
Authors: Miroslav Ćuk (outside co-author); Marina Malešević (R0730); Дарко Тошић (R0700); Anita Florescu (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: Ikonos; WorldView-1; change detection; Vojvodina; building permits.
Change between 2003 Ikonos (4 m multispectral) and 2010 WorldView-1 (0.5 m panchromatic) imagery was assessed for peri-urban zones of Subotica, Zrenjanin and Sombor to quantify the rate and spatial pattern of new construction at urban fringes. Pre-processing included sensor-specific radiometric normalisation, histogram matching, and co-registration to sub-pixel accuracy (RMSE < 0.4 m). Binary change maps derived from post-classification comparison were validated against municipal building permit records and field survey points. Across the three towns, a combined 178 ha of new built-up area was detected, of which 41 % lacked corresponding building permit records, indicating informal construction activity. Growth was markedly asymmetric: southern peripheral zones showed the highest expansion rates, coinciding with proximity to road infrastructure and lower agricultural land values. Seasonal spectral variability between acquisition dates introduced a false-alarm rate of approximately 7 %, which was reduced to 3 % after applying a minimum mapping unit of 100 m².

SYN-PUB-04470.title: Automated extraction of road network encroachment by informal construction from multi-temporal VHR imagery
SYN-PUB-04470.text:
Automated extraction of road network encroachment by informal construction from multi-temporal VHR imagery (2024, journal, Applied Geomatics).
Authors: Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364); Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Anna Turčanová (R0480); Marina Malešević (R0730).
Keywords: road reserve; encroachment; Pléiades; WorldView-2; Vojvodina road network.
Informal buildings constructed within legal road reserve setbacks reduce effective carriageway width and complicate future road improvement projects. A workflow was developed to detect such encroachments automatically by overlaying multi-temporal change maps (2012–2023, derived from Pléiades and WorldView-2) with cadastrally defined road reserve polygons for 85 km of peri-urban road network in four Vojvodina municipalities. Encroachment detection used a 3 m buffer inward from the road reserve boundary to account for co-registration uncertainty. Over the period, 138 discrete new structures were detected within road reserves, totalling 2,940 m² of footprint. The approach was validated against a municipal road authority field inventory conducted in 2022, achieving 83 % concordance at the segment level. Processing time for the 85 km network was approximately 4 hours on a single GPU workstation. The workflow is designed to run within Google Earth Engine with minor adaptation.

SYN-PUB-04471.title: Seasonal variation in voxel-based canopy structure metrics derived from repeated UAV LiDAR acquisitions in a temperate mixed forest
SYN-PUB-04471.text:
Seasonal variation in voxel-based canopy structure metrics derived from repeated UAV LiDAR acquisitions in a temperate mixed forest (2025, journal, Remote Sensing Letters).
Authors: Darko Mirković (R0877); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Maja Popović (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: UAV LiDAR; seasonal phenology; canopy structure; voxel metrics; temperate forest monitoring.
The sensitivity of voxel-based structural metrics to seasonal leaf phenology was assessed through five repeated UAV LiDAR acquisitions conducted at three mixed broadleaf forest plots in northern Serbia between March and October 2024. Metrics examined included filled-voxel ratio, vertical plant area volume density profiles, and upper canopy rugosity index, computed at a 0.10 m voxel resolution. Leaf-off acquisitions in early spring showed filled-voxel ratios 41–58% lower than peak leaf-on values in July, with the largest relative changes observed in the understorey layer (below 8 m). Height percentile metrics (P70–P95) remained comparatively stable across seasons (coefficient of variation < 6%), suggesting utility as season-independent inputs for AGB models. Point cloud density varied from 95 to 220 points m⁻² across flights due to wind-induced platform instability. The study provides a seasonal calibration reference for researchers integrating multi-temporal LiDAR data into continuous forest monitoring workflows in continental European climates.

SYN-PUB-04473.title: Effect of Post-Weld Heat Treatment on Residual Stress Distribution in T-Joint Welds of Low-Alloy Steel
SYN-PUB-04473.text:
Effect of Post-Weld Heat Treatment on Residual Stress Distribution in T-Joint Welds of Low-Alloy Steel (2012, journal, Welding and Structural Engineering Transactions).
Authors: Bojan Erić (R0365); Miroslav Vučković (outside co-author); Andreja Sedmak (outside co-author); Nenad Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: residual stress; post-weld heat treatment; T-joint; hole-drilling; finite element.
Residual stresses in as-welded and post-weld heat-treated (PWHT) T-joint specimens of S460M low-alloy steel were measured by hole-drilling with strain-gauge rosettes and compared with sequentially coupled thermal–mechanical FE simulations. Six as-welded and six PWHT specimens (650 °C for 1 h, furnace-cooled) were examined. The FE model employed a double-ellipsoid heat source and temperature-dependent material data derived from dilatometry. Peak tensile residual stresses at the weld toe in the as-welded condition reached 312 MPa in the longitudinal direction and 187 MPa transversally. After PWHT, peak values fell to 74 MPa and 41 MPa, respectively. Agreement between hole-drilling measurements and simulation was within 15% at all measurement points. The study quantified how PWHT redistribution of residual stress affected predicted fatigue lives using a linear-elastic fracture-mechanics assessment: estimated endurance at the design stress range of 90 MPa increased from 1.2 × 10⁶ to 3.8 × 10⁶ cycles following PWHT.

SYN-PUB-04474.title: Low-Cycle Fatigue Behaviour of Cruciform Welded Joints at −40 °C: An Experimental Study
SYN-PUB-04474.text:
Low-Cycle Fatigue Behaviour of Cruciform Welded Joints at −40 °C: An Experimental Study (2014, journal, International Journal of Fatigue and Damage Mechanics).
Authors: Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Bojan Erić (R0365); Ljiljana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: low-cycle fatigue; low temperature; Coffin-Manson; cruciform weld; fractography.
The paper reports strain-controlled low-cycle fatigue (LCF) tests on cruciform fillet-welded joints machined from S355J2+N plate and tested at both room temperature (20 °C) and −40 °C. A total of 32 specimens were cycled at total strain amplitudes of 0.25%, 0.50%, 0.75%, and 1.00% using a servo-hydraulic machine equipped with a liquid-nitrogen climate chamber. Cyclic stress–strain curves, Coffin–Manson parameters, and fatigue ductility exponents were extracted from the hysteresis data. At −40 °C, the fatigue ductility coefficient εf′ decreased by 22% relative to room temperature, whereas the fatigue strength coefficient σf′ increased by 11%, resulting in a crossover in life predictions near 3 × 10³ reversals. Fractographic examination by SEM confirmed transgranular cleavage facets in low-temperature specimens at strain amplitudes above 0.75%, indicating a mixed ductile–brittle fracture mode not observed at room temperature. The Morrow mean-stress correction improved life predictions in the −40 °C dataset.

SYN-PUB-04475.title: Interaction of Mechanical Cyclic Loading and Thermal Cycling on Fatigue Life of Butt-Welded Structural Steel Plates
SYN-PUB-04475.text:
Interaction of Mechanical Cyclic Loading and Thermal Cycling on Fatigue Life of Butt-Welded Structural Steel Plates (2016, conference, Proceedings of the 14th European Conference on Structural Steel Research, Bratislava).
Authors: Bojan Erić (R0365); Miroslav Vučković (outside co-author); Tibor Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: thermo-mechanical fatigue; thermal cycling; crack initiation; butt weld; DIC.
This work examined whether superimposed thermal cycling (between −30 °C and +20 °C at 0.5 cycles per hour) during mechanical fatigue loading alters crack initiation and growth behaviour in butt-welded S275JR plates. Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF, with twelve specimens per programme. Crack initiation life, defined as a 5% stiffness drop, was shortest in the out-of-phase TMF condition, averaging 28% fewer cycles than the room-temperature baseline. Crack growth rates in both TMF programmes exceeded predictions based on simple superposition of mechanical and thermal stress intensities, suggesting a synergistic damage mechanism tentatively linked to accelerated oxidation at crack flanks during temperature excursions. FE simulations using temperature-dependent elastic–plastic material models reproduced the crack-tip opening displacement within 8% of experimental digital image correlation measurements. Design implications are discussed in the context of the IIW fatigue assessment recommendations.

SYN-PUB-04476.title: Fracture Toughness of Heat-Affected Zone Microstructures in S690QL High-Strength Steel Welds at Sub-Zero Temperatures
SYN-PUB-04476.text:
Fracture Toughness of Heat-Affected Zone Microstructures in S690QL High-Strength Steel Welds at Sub-Zero Temperatures (2017, journal, Journal of Pressure Equipment and Pipeline Integrity).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Gordana Štrbac (outside co-author); Bojan Erić (R0365); Radovan Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: fracture toughness; CTOD; high-strength steel; HAZ; sub-zero temperature; master curve.
Charpy impact and CTOD (crack-tip opening displacement) tests were performed on specimens extracted from the coarse-grained heat-affected zone (CGHAZ) of single-pass submerged-arc welds in 20 mm S690QL plate at temperatures of +20, 0, −20, −40, and −60 °C. The CGHAZ was reproduced by Gleeble thermal simulation at peak temperatures of 1350 °C and cooling times t8/5 of 8 s and 20 s to replicate low and high heat-input conditions. At −40 °C, mean CTOD values dropped from 0.18 mm (t8/5 = 8 s) to 0.07 mm (t8/5 = 20 s), confirming sensitivity of toughness to heat input. A Weibull statistical analysis of CTOD scatter, using the master-curve approach per EN ISO 27306, yielded reference temperatures T0 of −62 °C and −38 °C for the two thermal cycles. These values were incorporated into a fracture-mechanics fitness-for-service assessment of a hypothetical pressure vessel nozzle weld, defining the tolerable flaw size at operating temperature.

SYN-PUB-04477.title: Finite-Element Estimation of Stress Intensity Factors for Surface Cracks at Weld Toes Under Combined Bending and Torsion
SYN-PUB-04477.text:
Finite-Element Estimation of Stress Intensity Factors for Surface Cracks at Weld Toes Under Combined Bending and Torsion (2018, journal, Engineering Fracture Mechanics and Structural Integrity).
Authors: Bojan Erić (R0365); Ljiljana Kovačević (outside co-author); Martin Hofer (outside co-author).
Keywords: XFEM; stress intensity factor; combined loading; weld toe crack; torsion-bending.
Semi-elliptical surface cracks at the toe of transverse attachment welds were modelled in Abaqus using the extended finite element method (XFEM) to compute stress intensity factors KI and KIII under proportional and non-proportional combinations of four-point bending and torsion. Weld-toe geometry was parameterised by toe radius ρ (0.5–2.5 mm) and flank angle θ (30°–60°), yielding a factorial design of 25 configurations. Stress intensity factors normalised as geometric correction functions F(a/c, a/t) were tabulated for aspect ratios a/c from 0.2 to 1.0 and relative depths a/t from 0.05 to 0.6. Under non-proportional loading (90° phase shift between bending and torsion), effective ΔKeq computed via the Richard criterion exceeded the proportional-loading values by up to 34% at shallow crack depths, highlighting the inadequacy of simple scalar superposition. The resulting correction-factor tables are formatted to be compatible with the BS 7910:2013 Level 2 assessment procedure.

SYN-PUB-04478.title: Weld Residual Stress Relaxation Under Cyclic Loading: Measurements and Modelling for S355 Cruciform Joints
SYN-PUB-04478.text:
Weld Residual Stress Relaxation Under Cyclic Loading: Measurements and Modelling for S355 Cruciform Joints (2019, journal, Journal of Structural Integrity and Maintenance Research).
Authors: Bojan Erić (R0365); Miroslav Vučković (outside co-author); Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Petra Kowalczyk (outside co-author).
Keywords: residual stress relaxation; XRD; cyclic plasticity; Chaboche model; cruciform joint.
Residual stress relaxation in S355 cruciform fillet-welded joints was tracked over 10, 100, 1000, and 10 000 fatigue cycles at three nominal stress ranges (60, 120, and 180 MPa) using X-ray diffraction (XRD) on polished surfaces at the weld toe. Initial peak longitudinal residual stress averaged +287 MPa in the as-welded state. After 1000 cycles at 180 MPa, surface residual stresses had relaxed to +61 MPa, while deeper stresses (measured by sequential electropolishing to 1.2 mm depth) retained 40–60% of their initial values. A cyclic plasticity FE model employing a Chaboche kinematic hardening rule reproduced the surface relaxation trend within 12% across all conditions. A semi-empirical relaxation factor was derived and incorporated into a fatigue life calculation, reducing the unconservative error in life prediction from 42% to 11% compared with assuming fixed residual stresses. Practical guidance for applying the relaxation factor in design is summarised.

SYN-PUB-04479.title: Fatigue Assessment of Welded Joints in Crane Runway Girders Subjected to Operational Temperature Variations: A Case Study
SYN-PUB-04479.text:
Fatigue Assessment of Welded Joints in Crane Runway Girders Subjected to Operational Temperature Variations: A Case Study (2020, conference, Steel Structures and Bridge Engineering – Proceedings of the 11th Central European Conference, Novi Sad).
Authors: Dragoljub Tanasić (outside co-author); Bojan Erić (R0365); Emilija Marić (R0683); Tibor Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: crane girder; operational loading; rainflow counting; IIW assessment; temperature correction.
A fatigue assessment was performed for the welded runway girder of an outdoor overhead crane operating in a continental climate where ambient temperature ranges from −28 °C to +38 °C over a calendar year. Operational load spectra were recorded by a data logger over an eight-month measurement campaign using strain gauges at twelve positions on two girders at a metalworking plant in the Vojvodina region. Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment. Fatigue life estimates were computed following the IIW recommendations, both with and without temperature-dependent fracture-mechanics corrections derived from the authors' earlier low-temperature CTOD dataset. Ignoring temperature dependence overestimated fatigue life at the weld toe by factors of 1.3–1.7 depending on detail category. The study recommends that crane structures in cold continental climates should apply a temperature knock-down factor on the fatigue strength class.

SYN-PUB-04480.title: Comparative Evaluation of Fatigue Life Prediction Models for Welded S355 and S460 Steels Under Multiaxial Proportional Loading at Low Temperatures
SYN-PUB-04480.text:
Comparative Evaluation of Fatigue Life Prediction Models for Welded S355 and S460 Steels Under Multiaxial Proportional Loading at Low Temperatures (2021, journal, International Journal of Fatigue and Damage Mechanics).
Authors: Bojan Erić (R0365); Ljiljana Kovačević (outside co-author); Martin Hofer (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: multiaxial fatigue; critical plane; low temperature; S460NL; life prediction.
Five multiaxial fatigue models — Findley, Fatemi–Socie, Smith–Watson–Topper, Liu, and a critical-plane von Mises variant — were evaluated against an experimental dataset of 84 fatigue tests on tubular welded specimens of S355J2 and S460NL steels tested under combined axial–torsional proportional loading at 20 °C, 0 °C, −20 °C, and −40 °C. Specimens failed either at the weld toe or in the weld metal, and failure locations were identified post-fracture by SEM. All five models were calibrated using room-temperature fatigue data and then applied predictively at sub-zero temperatures. The Fatemi–Socie model, when modified to incorporate temperature-dependent shear modulus and yield strength, produced the lowest scatter band (factor of 2.1 on life) across the full temperature range. The Liu model was accurate at room temperature but increasingly non-conservative below −20 °C. A correction procedure for the low-temperature regime is proposed and validated against the experimental data.

SYN-PUB-04481.title: Thermal Gradient-Induced Residual Stress in Welded Box Sections: A Parametric Finite-Element Study
SYN-PUB-04481.text:
Thermal Gradient-Induced Residual Stress in Welded Box Sections: A Parametric Finite-Element Study (2022, journal, Thin-Walled Structures and Metal Construction).
Authors: Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Bojan Erić (R0365); Nikoleta Farkaš (outside co-author).
Keywords: thermal gradient; box section; residual stress; welding sequence; parametric FE.
Welded box-section columns fabricated from 10 mm S355 plate were analysed by sequentially coupled thermal–structural FE simulations in Abaqus to evaluate how diurnal and seasonal thermal gradients (ΔT = 20–60 K through the wall thickness) modify as-welded residual stress fields. The parametric study varied four weld sequences (one-sided, two-sided symmetric, and two asymmetric sequences) and three wall thicknesses (8, 12, and 16 mm). Thermal gradients were imposed as boundary conditions representing solar irradiation on one face of the section. Results showed that a steady 40 K gradient reduced peak tensile weld-toe residual stresses by 8–14% on the heated face while increasing compressive stresses on the opposite face by a comparable margin, with the effects being most pronounced in one-sided welding sequences. At 60 K, bending stresses induced by the gradient were of the same order as the fatigue-relevant residual stress range, justifying their inclusion in fitness-for-service assessments of outdoor structures. A simplified formula, calibrated against the FE results, is provided for quick engineering estimation.

SYN-PUB-04482.title: Crack Closure and Effective Stress Intensity Under Superimposed Mechanical and Thermal Cycling: Measurements by Digital Image Correlation
SYN-PUB-04482.text:
Crack Closure and Effective Stress Intensity Under Superimposed Mechanical and Thermal Cycling: Measurements by Digital Image Correlation (2023, journal, Journal of Experimental Mechanics and Structural Testing).
Authors: Bojan Erić (R0365); Miroslav Vučković (outside co-author); Martin Hofer (outside co-author); Svetlana Sabo (R0786); Petra Kowalczyk (outside co-author).
Keywords: crack closure; digital image correlation; thermo-mechanical fatigue; effective stress ratio; Paris law.
Crack closure behaviour was quantified experimentally in centre-cracked tension specimens of butt-welded S355JR plate subjected to mechanical fatigue (R = 0.05, ΔP = 18 kN) combined with slow thermal cycling between −25 °C and +15 °C. Full-field displacement maps were acquired by two-camera stereo DIC at six points within each mechanical load cycle and at five points within each thermal half-cycle. The crack opening load Pop was identified as the load at which DIC-detected displacements became linear over a 2 mm gauge length straddling the crack tip. Pop was 12–19% higher in the thermal-cycling condition than in the isothermal baseline, and the effective stress ratio Reff was reduced accordingly. Plasticity-induced closure, measured as the reversed plastic zone size from DIC strain fields, was 0.18 mm at room temperature and increased to 0.27 mm at −20 °C, consistent with reduced crack-tip plasticity at lower temperature. Incorporating the measured Reff into a modified Paris-law prediction reduced the mean life-prediction error from −31% to −7%.

SYN-PUB-04578.title: Control-Flow Coverage Criteria for Embedded C Programs: A Comparison of Branch, Decision, and MC/DC Coverage Under Resource Constraints
SYN-PUB-04578.text:
Control-Flow Coverage Criteria for Embedded C Programs: A Comparison of Branch, Decision, and MC/DC Coverage Under Resource Constraints (2013, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Control Systems).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Milica Vujanović (outside co-author); Dragan Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: MC/DC coverage; embedded C; Frama-C; mutation testing; RTOS.
This paper examines three widely used structural coverage criteria—branch, decision, and modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC)—as applied to embedded C programs running on microcontrollers with limited RAM and flash memory. We implemented a static instrumentation framework on top of Frama-C and evaluated it against a suite of 14 open-source RTOS driver modules totalling approximately 18,000 lines of code. Measurements were collected on an STM32-based hardware testbed. Results show that MC/DC achieves a 12–18% higher fault-detection rate compared to branch coverage on arithmetic faults injected using mutation testing, at a code-size overhead of 9–23% depending on loop density. Decision coverage proved most cost-effective for memory-constrained targets below 32 kB flash. The paper also identifies a class of unreachable branches produced by compiler optimisations that inflate apparent coverage scores, and proposes a correction heuristic validated on two industrial driver code samples.

SYN-PUB-04579.title: Bounded Model Checking of Timed Automata Models for Automotive Body-Control Modules
SYN-PUB-04579.text:
Bounded Model Checking of Timed Automata Models for Automotive Body-Control Modules (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Formal Methods in Embedded Systems (CEWFMES)).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Stefan Kostić (R0375); Milica Vujanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: bounded model checking; timed automata; UPPAAL; Z3 solver; automotive software.
We present a bounded model checking workflow for detecting timing violations in timed automata specifications of automotive body-control module (BCM) software. The approach translates UPPAAL timed automata into SMT-LIB 2 formulas and applies the Z3 solver to search for counterexamples within a user-specified time bound. We validated the method on four BCM specifications derived from an open automotive benchmark suite, covering window-lift, central-locking, and wiper subsystems. The tool found three previously undocumented timing violations in two specifications, all confirmed by back-simulation in UPPAAL. Average verification time was 4.2 seconds per property on a standard desktop workstation. Compared to exhaustive UPPAAL exploration, the SMT-based approach reduced peak memory consumption by 34% on the largest model while retaining full counterexample traceability. A detailed discussion of false negatives introduced by the chosen bound is included.

SYN-PUB-04580.title: Automated MISRA-C 2012 Violation Detection Using Abstract Interpretation: Scope, Precision, and False-Positive Rate
SYN-PUB-04580.text:
Automated MISRA-C 2012 Violation Detection Using Abstract Interpretation: Scope, Precision, and False-Positive Rate (2016, journal, Software Quality and Reliability Journal).
Authors: Jelena Ilić (outside co-author); Stefan Kostić (R0375); Neven Marković (outside co-author); Camille Dupont (outside co-author).
Keywords: MISRA-C; abstract interpretation; Frama-C; static analysis; false positives.
MISRA-C 2012 defines 143 rules for writing safe C code in safety-critical domains. Existing commercial checkers report high false-positive rates that burden code reviewers. This paper describes a rule-checking engine built on an abstract interpretation framework within Frama-C, targeting the 27 rules most commonly violated in embedded automotive and avionics code according to published defect datasets. We evaluated the engine on a corpus of 31 open-source embedded projects (total 94,000 lines of C). The engine achieved a false-positive rate of 8.3% and a false-negative rate of 4.1% on a manually annotated ground-truth subset of 1,200 injected violations. Runtime remained below 90 seconds for all projects. The paper discusses precision losses caused by pointer aliasing and provides a categorisation of 12 rule types where sound over-approximation is insufficient and bounded unrolling is required instead.

SYN-PUB-04581.title: A Survey of Counterexample Generation Techniques in Software Model Checking
SYN-PUB-04581.text:
A Survey of Counterexample Generation Techniques in Software Model Checking (2018, book chapter, Advances in Formal Methods for Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems, Springer).
Authors: Rok Štruc (outside co-author); Stefan Kostić (R0375); Andreja Kovačič (outside co-author).
Keywords: counterexample generation; CEGAR; software model checking; survey; concurrent programs.
This chapter reviews counterexample generation methods used in software model checking tools from 2005 to 2017, covering CEGAR-based refinement, interpolant-based approaches, and SMT-guided path enumeration. The survey organises 62 primary studies along four dimensions: the underlying logic fragment used, the class of properties addressed, scalability with respect to program size, and quality of counterexample explanation for human reviewers. We identify a gap in the literature regarding counterexample minimisation for concurrent embedded programs: only 7 of the 62 studies address concurrency, and fewer than half provide mechanically reproducible experimental setups. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, including the need for domain-specific explanation formats suited to control engineers who are not formal methods specialists, and the relationship between counterexample quality and debugging time in industrial settings.

SYN-PUB-04582.title: Verifying Stack Boundedness in Interrupt-Driven Embedded Programs Using CBMC
SYN-PUB-04582.text:
Verifying Stack Boundedness in Interrupt-Driven Embedded Programs Using CBMC (2019, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Embedded Systems Verification (ICESV)).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Rok Štruc (outside co-author).
Keywords: stack overflow; CBMC; interrupt-driven software; Cortex-M; worst-case stack usage.
Stack overflow is a leading cause of failure in interrupt-driven embedded software but is rarely addressed by standard model checkers because interrupt interleaving is difficult to model. This paper presents an analysis method that encodes interrupt preemption semantics into CBMC's C verification harness to check worst-case stack usage bounds statically. The encoding introduces a scheduler model with configurable priority levels and nondeteministic interrupt timing. We applied the method to eight firmware projects written for Cortex-M microcontrollers, ranging from 2,000 to 15,000 lines of C. CBMC found potential stack overflows in three projects; two were confirmed on hardware using JTAG stack monitoring. Analysis time ranged from 11 seconds to 8.4 minutes depending on interrupt nesting depth. We report on the trade-off between the precision of the interrupt model and solver performance, and discuss conditions under which the method produces safe over-approximations.

SYN-PUB-04583.title: Model-Based Test Suite Generation from UML State Machines Using SMT-Guided Path Selection
SYN-PUB-04583.text:
Model-Based Test Suite Generation from UML State Machines Using SMT-Guided Path Selection (2021, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Marija Ognjanov (R0817); Milica Vujanović (outside co-author); Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; UML state machines; SMT; coverage criteria; test generation.
We describe a test suite generation method for safety-critical software specified as UML state machines. The method translates state machines into transition systems and uses an SMT solver to select execution paths that satisfy user-specified coverage targets, including all-transitions, all-pairs, and a new metric we call fault-boundary coverage (FBC) designed to exercise guard conditions at their boundary values. Test cases are generated as concrete C test vectors using symbolic execution over the extracted paths. We evaluated the approach on a medical-device alarm management component (5 concurrent state machines, 78 transitions) and a railway interlocking subsystem specification (4 state machines, 112 transitions). FBC-guided selection achieved 100% mutation score on arithmetic guard faults with 23% fewer test cases than random path selection. The paper includes a formal definition of FBC and a proof that it subsumes branch coverage on guard conditions.

SYN-PUB-04584.title: Precision of Pointer Analysis Algorithms in Frama-C for Small Embedded Programs: An Empirical Study
SYN-PUB-04584.text:
Precision of Pointer Analysis Algorithms in Frama-C for Small Embedded Programs: An Empirical Study (2022, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Static Analysis and Program Verification (SAPV)).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Neven Marković (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: pointer analysis; Frama-C; static analysis precision; embedded C; aliasing.
Pointer aliasing undermines the precision of dataflow-based static analyses in embedded C code. This paper empirically compares four pointer analysis configurations available in Frama-C—Eva's default value analysis, a field-sensitive extension, a context-sensitive variant, and a hybrid combining the latter two—on a benchmark of 20 embedded programs between 500 and 4,000 lines. We measure precision as the ratio of resolved pointer targets and report analysis time and memory use. The context-sensitive variant resolves 91% of pointer accesses compared to 74% for the default, but requires 3.4× more time. For programs below 1,500 lines, the hybrid configuration matches context-sensitive precision with only 1.6× overhead. We also identify 11 program patterns where all four configurations produce identical imprecision, attributable to non-local pointer escapes through function pointers, and suggest a lightweight pre-pass to mitigate three of them.

SYN-PUB-04585.title: Integrating Formal Verification Artefacts into IEC 61508 Safety Cases: A Process Proposal and Case Study
SYN-PUB-04585.text:
Integrating Formal Verification Artefacts into IEC 61508 Safety Cases: A Process Proposal and Case Study (2023, journal, Reliability Engineering and Safety-Critical Software).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Jelena Ilić (outside co-author); Camille Dupont (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEC 61508; safety case; Goal Structuring Notation; CBMC; Frama-C.
IEC 61508 requires documented evidence of software correctness for Safety Integrity Levels 2–4 but does not specify how formal verification artefacts—property files, solver logs, coverage reports—should be structured as safety case arguments. This paper proposes a process for integrating CBMC verification runs and Frama-C analysis reports into Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) safety cases. We instantiated the process on a pressure-sensor firmware component developed by a Serbian automation equipment manufacturer under a research cooperation agreement, covering 14 safety requirements at SIL 2. The resulting safety case argument tree contains 47 nodes; 31 are supported directly by machine-generated artefacts. We report on practical difficulties encountered, including solver non-determinism affecting reproducibility of evidence and the challenge of explaining SMT solver outputs to functional-safety auditors. The process was reviewed by two independent safety assessors.

SYN-PUB-04586.title: Incremental Verification of Patched Embedded Firmware Using Change-Impact Analysis and Reuse of SMT Proofs
SYN-PUB-04586.text:
Incremental Verification of Patched Embedded Firmware Using Change-Impact Analysis and Reuse of SMT Proofs (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Formal Methods in Software Engineering (ECFMSE)).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Andreja Kovačič (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author).
Keywords: incremental verification; firmware patching; SMT proof reuse; change-impact analysis; bounded model checking.
When firmware is patched to fix a defect, re-running full formal verification from scratch is costly. This paper presents an incremental verification approach that (1) identifies which program paths are affected by a source-level patch using a lightweight static differencing tool, (2) reuses previously computed SMT unsatisfiability certificates for unaffected paths, and (3) runs bounded model checking only on affected paths and a configurable neighbourhood. We evaluated the approach on 24 patch pairs extracted from the commit history of three open-source embedded firmware projects. Incremental verification reduced total solver time by a median of 68% compared to full re-verification, with no loss in soundness on properties that remained within the original proof scope. We characterise six patch patterns for which certificate reuse is unsafe and must be suppressed, and provide a decision procedure for detecting these patterns in under 2 seconds.

SYN-PUB-04587.title: Data-Flow Coverage Adequacy for Safety-Critical PLC Programs: Adapting Software Testing Criteria to IEC 61131-3 Structured Text
SYN-PUB-04587.text:
Data-Flow Coverage Adequacy for Safety-Critical PLC Programs: Adapting Software Testing Criteria to IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (2026, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Stefan Kostić (R0375); Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author); Tibor Farkas (outside co-author).
Keywords: data-flow coverage; PLC; IEC 61131-3; Structured Text; safety-critical software.
Programmable logic controller programs written in IEC 61131-3 Structured Text are used in process-control and building-automation systems but receive less formal analysis attention than C-based firmware. This paper adapts classical data-flow coverage criteria—all-defs, all-uses, and all-du-paths—to Structured Text by defining a control-flow graph construction for ST's iteration and selection constructs and handling its typed variable model. We implemented the analysis as a standalone tool and evaluated it on 17 ST programs from the OpenPLC benchmark, ranging from 80 to 640 lines. All-uses coverage detected 83% of seeded data-flow faults; all-du-paths detected 91% at the cost of a 2.3× increase in required test cases. The paper also identifies five ST language features—function-block instantiation, retain variables, edge-detection functions, task interleaving, and direct addressing—that require extensions to the standard du-pair definition, and proposes concrete extensions for each.

SYN-PUB-04600.title: Residual stress evolution in TiAlN-coated carbide inserts measured by synchrotron XRD before and after interrupted turning tests
SYN-PUB-04600.text:
Residual stress evolution in TiAlN-coated carbide inserts measured by synchrotron XRD before and after interrupted turning tests (2024, journal, Acta Materialia).
Authors: Jana Beranová (outside co-author); Roberto Sannino (outside co-author); Tamara Vukić (outside co-author); Danilo Grujić (R0377); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: synchrotron XRD; residual stress; TiAlN; stress relaxation; cutting edge.
Residual stress in TiAlN-coated WC-Co inserts was measured by synchrotron X-ray diffraction (beamline energy 87 keV) at three states: as-deposited, after turning of AISI 52100 steel (62 HRC) for 500 m at 150 m/min, and after 1000 m at the same conditions. Measurements were taken at 12 positions along the cutting edge at each state. As-deposited compressive stress in the TiAlN coating was −3.8 ± 0.2 GPa. After 500 m, stress relaxed to −2.1 ± 0.4 GPa in the contact zone and −3.5 ± 0.2 GPa outside it. At 1000 m, the contact zone showed near-zero stress in two inserts with visible delamination and −1.4 GPa in the three without. The WC substrate showed compressive stresses of −0.4 GPa as-deposited with no statistically significant change after 500 m. Stress relaxation in the contact zone correlated with higher flank wear rate (r = 0.81, n = 15). Synchrotron measurement allowed a 30 µm spatial resolution, providing spatially resolved data unavailable from laboratory XRD.

SYN-PUB-04684.title: Prepoznavanje entiteta u srpskim sudskim odlukama: poređenje uslovnih slučajnih polja i transformerskih modela
SYN-PUB-04684.text:
Prepoznavanje entiteta u srpskim sudskim odlukama: poređenje uslovnih slučajnih polja i transformerskih modela (2021, conference, Zbornik radova međunarodne konferencije INFOTEH-Jahorina).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Tamara Blagojević (outside co-author); Strahinja Radović (R0385).
Keywords: named entity recognition; CRF; RoBERTa; Serbian; court decisions.
Rad poređuje uslovne slučajne mreže (CRF) i dva transformerska modela (multilingualni BERT i srpski RoBERTa) na zadatku prepoznavanja imenskih entiteta u korpusu od 2.100 anonimizovanih prvostepenih presuda iz oblasti krivičnog prava. Definisano je osam tipova entiteta: lice, organizacija, lokacija, datum, sudska referenca, zakonska odredba, novčani iznos i kaznena mera. CRF model dostiže F1 od 0,78, multilingualni BERT 0,84, a srpski RoBERTa 0,87, mereno kao mikro prosek po svim tipovima. Najveće relativno poboljšanje transformerskih modela beleži se za tip 'zakonska odredba' (F1 raste sa 0,61 na 0,83). Rad opisuje posebne izazove u anonimizovanim tekstovima gde su lična imena zamenjena oznakama, što otežava razrešavanje koreferencije. Priložena je detaljna analiza grešaka po tipovima entiteta.

SYN-PUB-04706.title: Sentinel-2 Red-Edge Bands as Auxiliary Variables for Spatial Interpolation of Canopy Temperature: A Case Study in Sunflower Fields of Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-04706.text:
Sentinel-2 Red-Edge Bands as Auxiliary Variables for Spatial Interpolation of Canopy Temperature: A Case Study in Sunflower Fields of Vojvodina (2019, journal, Remote Sensing of Environment and Precision Crop Science).
Authors: Nataša Brkić (outside co-author); Goran Filipović (outside co-author); Anna Turčanová (R0480); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Srđan Ognjanov (R0388).
Keywords: Sentinel-2; red-edge; canopy temperature; kriging with external drift; sunflower.
Thermal infrared sensors aboard Landsat-8 and Sentinel-3 provide land surface temperature at resolutions too coarse for field-scale crop stress assessment. This study tested whether Sentinel-2 red-edge and near-infrared reflectance bands, sampled in July–August 2017 during cloud-free overpasses over 4 200 ha of commercial sunflower in Vojvodina, could serve as auxiliary predictors in a kriging-with-external-drift model for canopy temperature. Canopy temperature was measured with 22 handheld infrared thermometers installed at 10-minute intervals across three farms. KED using a linear combination of the 705 nm and 740 nm Sentinel-2 bands reduced interpolation RMSE from 1.8 °C (OK) to 1.1 °C at 10 m resolution, a 39 % improvement. Spatial maps produced daily from the KED surface correlated with manually scouted water-stress incidence zones at r = 0.74. The method requires no additional satellite acquisitions beyond the freely available Sentinel-2 archive.

SYN-PUB-05184.title: CUSUM chart sensitivity to flank-wear progression in continuous CNC turning of low-alloy steel
SYN-PUB-05184.text:
CUSUM chart sensitivity to flank-wear progression in continuous CNC turning of low-alloy steel (2012, journal, Journal of Production and Manufacturing Research).
Authors: Katarina Malešević (R0835); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920); Petar Jokić (R0432).
Keywords: CUSUM chart; flank wear; cutting force ratio; 42CrMo4; average run length.
This paper examines the sensitivity of cumulative sum (CUSUM) control charts to progressive flank-wear in continuous dry turning of 42CrMo4 low-alloy steel with coated carbide inserts. Cutting force components (Fc, Ff, Fp) were sampled at 5 kHz over 48 turning trials at three feed-rate levels (0.10, 0.15, 0.20 mm/rev) and two cutting speeds (180 and 240 m/min). Flank-wear land (VB) was measured optically at 2 min intervals up to tool failure (VB = 0.30 mm). CUSUM charts were constructed on the mean Fc signal and on two derived ratios (Fp/Fc and Ff/Fc). The ratio Fp/Fc showed the earliest and most consistent out-of-control signal, yielding an average run length to detection of 4.1 observations against 9.7 for raw Fc. At the 0.15 mm/rev feed, detection occurred at mean VB of 0.14 mm, well before the ISO-defined limit. Results indicate that ratio-based CUSUM monitoring reduces false alarms while improving detection timeliness compared to single-component charts.

SYN-PUB-05326.title: Adaptive control of GMAW for thin-walled aluminium assemblies subject to progressive fixture compliance loss
SYN-PUB-05326.text:
Adaptive control of GMAW for thin-walled aluminium assemblies subject to progressive fixture compliance loss (2018, journal, Journal of Materials Processing Technology).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Đuro Simić (R0593); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author); Valentina Simić (R0445).
Keywords: aluminium welding; GMAW; adaptive control; thin-walled structures; fixture compliance; arc voltage.
Thin-walled aluminium structures lose clamping force progressively during welding due to thermal expansion, which alters fit-up gap and contact with the fixture heat sink. This study develops an adaptive control strategy in which arc voltage and WFS are adjusted every 0.5 s based on measured changes in pool width and arc electrical signatures. Twelve test assemblies made from 2 mm AA6082-T4 sheets were welded under controlled compliance loss simulated by calibrated spring-loaded fixtures. Under constant-parameter welding, 38 % of assemblies showed burn-through or incomplete fusion in the later portions of the seam. With the adaptive controller active, the defect rate dropped to 8 %. Electrical signal features, specifically arc voltage variance over 50 ms windows, were found to be early indicators of gap increase, with a 120 ms lead time relative to visible pool width change.

SYN-PUB-05474.title: Combining CRF Sequence Labelling with Spatial Context Features for Field Extraction in Inspection Certificates
SYN-PUB-05474.text:
Combining CRF Sequence Labelling with Spatial Context Features for Field Extraction in Inspection Certificates (2016, journal, Journal of Information Science and Engineering).
Authors: Tatjana Sremčević (outside co-author); Predrag Ljubojević (R0460); Nikola Grujičić (outside co-author); Jovan Puzović (R0484).
Keywords: conditional random fields; sequence labelling; field extraction; inspection certificates; spatial features.
Inspection certificates issued by accredited testing laboratories follow loose conventions but no single fixed template. This work treats field extraction as a sequence labelling problem over sorted text tokens, augmented with spatial features derived from each token's bounding box and its nearest neighbours. A conditional random field model is trained on 1,100 annotated inspection certificates and evaluated on a held-out set of 275 certificates from laboratories not represented in training. The feature set includes token geometry, font-size estimates from bounding-box height, relative page position, left-margin alignment, and the label of the spatially closest token. Adding spatial context features raised per-field extraction accuracy from 72.3 % to 83.7 % compared with a purely sequential baseline. Error analysis identified measurement units as the most frequently mislabelled token class. The trained model is integrated into a prototype pipeline, and processing throughput of 8.4 certificates per second is reported on a standard 2014-era server.

SYN-PUB-05526.title: Voltage fluctuation propagation from 35 kV to 110 kV: attenuation factors observed during arc furnace operation
SYN-PUB-05526.text:
Voltage fluctuation propagation from 35 kV to 110 kV: attenuation factors observed during arc furnace operation (2018, journal, Electric Power Systems Research).
Authors: Dragan Stanković (outside co-author); Vesna Malešević (R0465); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Miloš Perić (outside co-author); Radomír Fišer (outside co-author).
Keywords: flicker propagation; voltage attenuation; 35 kV; 110 kV; short-circuit power.
Flicker disturbances generated by arc furnace installations at medium voltage propagate upstream to the high-voltage transmission network, but the attenuation experienced during this propagation is seldom quantified from simultaneous measurements at both voltage levels. This paper presents synchronised measurements at the 35 kV and 110 kV busbars of two substations that supply arc furnace plants in northern Serbia, covering a combined monitoring period of 26 weeks. Simultaneous Pst and Plt indices were computed from class-A instruments with GPS time-synchronisation. The ratio Plt(110 kV)/Plt(35 kV) ranged from 0.31 to 0.68, with a median of 0.47. Attenuation was found to increase with short-circuit power at the 110 kV bus. A simple linear regression model predicts the 110 kV Plt from the 35 kV Plt and the short-circuit impedance ratio with an R² of 0.79. The model supports planning engineers in estimating upstream flicker impact without additional instrumentation.

SYN-PUB-05706.title: Class Imbalance in Serbian Administrative Court Decisions: A Baseline Study
SYN-PUB-05706.text:
Class Imbalance in Serbian Administrative Court Decisions: A Baseline Study (2014, journal, Journal of Information and Organizational Sciences).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Slobodan Krstić (outside co-author).
Keywords: class imbalance; administrative courts; Serbian legal corpus; text classification; baseline.
Administrative court rulings in Serbia exhibit a pronounced class imbalance: approximately 78% of decisions in a collected corpus of 3,400 documents belong to a single outcome category. This paper documents the construction of that corpus, covering rulings from 2005 to 2012, and evaluates five standard classifiers—naive Bayes, logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, and SVM—under original class distributions. F1-scores for minority classes fall below 0.21 across all methods when no resampling is applied. The paper analyses the linguistic and structural features most predictive of outcome, including citation patterns and procedural section length. Results serve as a reproducible baseline for subsequent resampling and augmentation experiments. All preprocessing code and anonymised metadata are released alongside the paper. The study intentionally avoids resampling or cost-sensitive learning so that future work can quantify gains relative to a clean reference point.

SYN-PUB-05707.title: Back-Translation as Data Augmentation for Low-Resource Legal Sentence Classification
SYN-PUB-05707.text:
Back-Translation as Data Augmentation for Low-Resource Legal Sentence Classification (2018, conference, Proceedings of the Language Technologies and Digital Humanities Conference).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Petra Horvat (outside co-author); Gregor Vidmar (outside co-author).
Keywords: back-translation; data augmentation; legal NLP; multilingual BERT; low-resource.
Legal sentence classification in low-resource Slavic languages is constrained by the scarcity of annotated data and the domain specificity of vocabulary. This paper investigates back-translation—translating Serbian sentences to English and back—as an augmentation strategy for a sentence-level dataset of 1,120 annotated clauses from civil procedure documents. Three translation pipelines are tested using freely available neural machine translation models, and the round-trip fidelity of legal terminology is measured against a manually curated glossary of 340 terms. Back-translation preserves legal term identity in 74% of cases for the best pipeline. Augmented training sets are used with a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model, yielding a macro F1 of 0.68 compared to 0.59 on the original data. Error analysis reveals that procedural verbs suffer the highest mistranslation rate, suggesting domain-adaptive fine-tuning of the translation component as a future direction. The dataset and annotation guidelines are publicly available.

SYN-PUB-05708.title: Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus
SYN-PUB-05708.text:
Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus (2020, journal, Informatica: An International Journal of Computing and Informatics).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Nikola Supić (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer learning; domain adaptation; labour law; intermediate pretraining; Croatian Serbian.
Transformer-based language models pretrained on large general corpora require substantial fine-tuning data to adapt to specialised legal domains. This paper examines whether intermediate pretraining on a moderately sized Croatian–Serbian legal text collection (approximately 120,000 sentences from publicly accessible legislation and court decisions) improves downstream performance on a Serbian labour-law classification task with only 640 training examples. Four model variants are compared: multilingual BERT with no intermediate pretraining, the same model with intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus, and two models pretrained on each national subset separately. Intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus achieves the best macro F1 (0.72) on a held-out test set of 160 examples, surpassing the no-pretraining baseline by 0.11. Differences between the Croatian-only and Serbian-only intermediate pretraining conditions are modest, suggesting that vocabulary overlap rather than syntactic similarity drives the gain. Computational cost and practical guidance for reproducing the pipeline on limited hardware are discussed.

SYN-PUB-05709.title: Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models
SYN-PUB-05709.text:
Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models (2021, journal, Expert Systems with Applications).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Slobodan Krstić (outside co-author); Eszter Fábián (outside co-author).
Keywords: judicial sequence prediction; LSTM; GRU; focal loss; civil litigation.
Civil litigation in Serbia often involves multiple procedural stages, and the outcome of each stage influences the distribution of subsequent outcomes. This paper frames judicial decision sequences as a temporal classification problem and evaluates three recurrent architectures—vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU—on a dataset of 2,180 complete case trajectories spanning first instance, appeal, and revision stages. Each stage is represented by a combination of extracted text features and structured metadata (case type, duration, court tier). The dataset is severely imbalanced at the revision stage, where case types eligible for revision constitute only 9% of trajectories. Weighted cross-entropy and focal loss are compared as training objectives. The GRU with focal loss achieves a macro F1 of 0.61 at the revision stage, compared to 0.43 for weighted cross-entropy. Sequence length and court tier are identified as the strongest non-textual predictors via ablation. Limitations related to data availability outside the University's legal informatics collaboration are discussed.

SYN-PUB-05710.title: A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets
SYN-PUB-05710.text:
A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets (2022, book chapter, Advances in Legal Informatics: Methods, Systems, and Applications (edited volume, Springer)).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Ruxandra Ionescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: synthetic data; data generation; legal NLP; survey; evaluation.
The application of machine learning to legal tasks is frequently limited by small annotated corpora and ethical constraints on data sharing. This chapter surveys methods for generating synthetic legal data, covering rule-based paraphrasing, conditional language model generation, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks adapted to text. For each method the chapter describes the underlying mechanism, summarises reported performance on legal benchmarks from the literature, and lists known failure modes, such as hallucinated case citations and vocabulary drift in conditional generation. Special attention is given to evaluation protocols, since standard NLP metrics such as BLEU and perplexity do not capture the legal validity of generated texts. The chapter concludes with a decision framework helping practitioners choose a generation strategy based on available corpus size, annotation type, and downstream task. Thirty-seven papers published between 2015 and 2022 are reviewed.

SYN-PUB-05711.title: Conditional GPT-2 Fine-Tuning for Minority-Class Augmentation in a Small Serbian Court Decision Dataset
SYN-PUB-05711.text:
Conditional GPT-2 Fine-Tuning for Minority-Class Augmentation in a Small Serbian Court Decision Dataset (2023, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Science).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Slobodan Krstić (outside co-author).
Keywords: GPT-2; conditional generation; augmentation; administrative courts; expert evaluation.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-05712.title: Cost-Sensitive Learning vs. Resampling: A Controlled Comparison on Four Serbian Legal Classification Tasks
SYN-PUB-05712.text:
Cost-Sensitive Learning vs. Resampling: A Controlled Comparison on Four Serbian Legal Classification Tasks (2024, journal, ACM Transactions on Information Systems).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ognjen Malešević (R0987); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Eszter Fábián (outside co-author); Ruxandra Ionescu (outside co-author); Nikola Supić (outside co-author).
Keywords: cost-sensitive learning; resampling; focal loss; imbalance ratio; benchmarking.
Practitioners addressing class imbalance must choose between modifying the training objective and modifying the training set, but systematic comparisons on legal text data are rare. This paper applies seven resampling strategies (random oversampling, random undersampling, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, and two hybrid methods) and four cost-sensitive objectives (weighted cross-entropy, focal loss, asymmetric loss, and class-balanced softmax) to four Serbian legal classification tasks drawn from administrative, civil, criminal, and labour law subdomains. Corpus sizes range from 412 to 2,180 documents and imbalance ratios from 1:4 to 1:19. Results show no single strategy dominates across tasks; cost-sensitive objectives outperform resampling on the two smallest datasets, while hybrid resampling performs better on the two larger corpora. Statistical significance is assessed with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across cross-validation folds. The paper provides a reproducible experimental framework and releases all task-specific evaluation scripts.

SYN-PUB-05713.title: Annotated corpus of Serbian electrical maintenance texts: construction methodology and baseline statistics
SYN-PUB-05713.text:
Annotated corpus of Serbian electrical maintenance texts: construction methodology and baseline statistics (2016, conference, Language Resources and Evaluation Conference for South-East European Languages (LREC-SEEL)).
Authors: Maja Ristić (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Jovan Puzović (R0484); Vukica Ognjanov (R0979); Andrei Popescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: corpus construction; named entity recognition; annotation; Serbian NLP; maintenance texts.
Reliable named entity recognition and relation extraction in the power-systems maintenance domain require annotated corpora that reflect the vocabulary and writing style of field personnel. This paper describes the construction of a 9,800-sentence corpus drawn from work orders, inspection reports, and incident summaries produced by two Serbian electricity distribution companies between 2008 and 2014. Annotation guidelines were defined to cover four entity types—equipment identifier, fault descriptor, location reference, and repair action—and two relation types: fault-equipment and action-equipment. A team of four annotators, including two electrical engineers and two computational linguists, performed the labelling using the BRAT annotation tool. Final inter-annotator kappa values ranged from 0.68 to 0.79 depending on entity type. The corpus contains 47,000 entity mentions and 31,000 labelled relation instances. Baseline results using a CRF tagger are reported, with an F1 of 0.73 for fault descriptors, which proved the most variable category. The corpus is released under a restricted-access licence pending operator approval.

SYN-PUB-05935.title: Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach
SYN-PUB-05935.text:
Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach (2017, journal, Progress in Organic Coatings).
Authors: Miroslav Vujić (outside co-author); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Ljiljana Stanković (outside co-author); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author); Sanja Lukić (R0504).
Keywords: response surface methodology; corona discharge; recycled board; process optimisation; ink adhesion variability.
Recycled packaging boards sourced from three European mills exhibited substantial variability in initial surface energy (28–37 mJ/m²) due to differing furnish compositions and coating histories. A central composite response-surface design with four factors (electrode gap 1–3 mm, line speed 50–150 m/min, power density 5–20 W·min/m², ambient humidity 30–65 % RH) was used to model total surface energy and polar component as responses. Forty-three experimental runs were performed. The quadratic model explained 88 % of variance in total surface energy; power density and electrode gap were the dominant factors, with a statistically significant interaction. A validated optimal treatment window (gap 1.5 mm, 12 W·min/m², 40–55 % RH) yielded total surface energy ≥ 50 mJ/m² across all three board grades, reducing within-batch variability in ink adhesion peel force from ± 0.9 N/cm to ± 0.3 N/cm.

SYN-PUB-05944.title: Residence time effects on fixed-bed pyrolysis of corn stover: product distribution and energy balance
SYN-PUB-05944.text:
Residence time effects on fixed-bed pyrolysis of corn stover: product distribution and energy balance (2015, journal, Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis).
Authors: Nemanja Ilić (outside co-author); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author); Péter Balogh (outside co-author); Sanja Lukić (R0504); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992).
Keywords: corn stover; residence time; fixed-bed pyrolysis; bio-oil; energy balance.
A parametric study was conducted in a bench-scale fixed-bed reactor using milled corn stover (particle size 0.5–1.0 mm, moisture 8.3 wt%) at 500 °C with residence times of 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes. Gas, liquid (bio-oil), and solid (biochar) product fractions were gravimetrically quantified. At 15 min, biochar yield was 32.4% and bio-oil 38.1%; extending residence time to 120 min reduced biochar yield marginally to 29.6% while increasing non-condensable gas fraction from 18.2 to 24.5 wt%. Bio-oil higher heating value ranged from 16.8 to 18.3 MJ kg⁻¹. An energy balance across the reactor showed that the char fraction retained 38–44% of feedstock energy regardless of residence time, whereas extended holding increased secondary cracking of bio-oil vapours. Recommendations for process optimisation targeting simultaneous biochar and syngas valorisation are presented.

SYN-PUB-06094.title: Influence of Residual Stress on the Natural Frequencies of Welded Steel Frame Members
SYN-PUB-06094.text:
Influence of Residual Stress on the Natural Frequencies of Welded Steel Frame Members (2021, journal, Journal of Constructional Steel Research and Diagnostics).
Authors: Theodora Ionescu (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Zoran Aćimović (outside co-author); Borislav Bogdanović (R0518).
Keywords: residual stress; hole-drilling; stress relief annealing; geometric stiffness; FE model.
Residual stresses induced by welding alter geometric stiffness and thereby affect natural frequencies of frame members. This study quantifies the relationship using a combined experimental and finite-element approach. Residual stress profiles in twelve S355 steel beam specimens were measured by the hole-drilling method at five cross-sections per specimen; specimens were then tested for natural frequencies using impact hammer excitation before and after stress-relief annealing at 600 °C for two hours. Frequency increases of 0.8–2.3% were observed after annealing, depending on weld sequence and heat input. A 3D FE model incorporating measured residual stress fields as initial conditions reproduced the pre-annealing frequencies with a mean error of 1.1%. Parametric sensitivity analysis showed that longitudinal compressive residual stress near the weld toe exerted the strongest influence on the first bending frequency. The results imply that residual stress state should be accounted for when establishing SHM baselines for newly fabricated or repaired steel structures.

SYN-PUB-06388.title: Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts
SYN-PUB-06388.text:
Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Vision).
Authors: Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author); Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Tamara Đurić (outside co-author).
Detecting surface defects on highly reflective metal components remains a significant challenge for automated visual inspection systems, primarily because specular reflections obscure subtle anomalies and corrupt standard feature representations. This paper presents a few-shot learning framework tailored specifically to reflective surfaces, combining a reflection-aware preprocessing pipeline with a prototypical network backbone trained on a curated set of metallic defect categories. A novel data augmentation strategy simulates varying illumination angles and reflection intensities, substantially increasing intra-class diversity without requiring large annotated datasets. The proposed method is evaluated on a newly introduced benchmark—ReflectDefect-M—comprising five metallic material types and twelve defect classes, collected in cooperation with regional SME manufacturing partners. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves a mean average precision of 87.3% using only five support examples per defect class, outperforming seven competitive baselines by margins ranging from 4.1 to 11.6 percentage points. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each pipeline stage. The work establishes a practical pathway for deploying few-shot defect detectors in small-batch production settings where collecting large labeled datasets is economically infeasible.

SYN-PUB-06389.title: Quantized detectors for real-time inspection on edge devices
SYN-PUB-06389.text:
Quantized detectors for real-time inspection on edge devices (2023, conference, Embedded AI Conference).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Rastko Petrović (outside co-author); Lena Hofmann (outside co-author); Miloš Cvejić (outside co-author).
Real-time visual inspection on embedded and edge hardware demands detectors that are simultaneously accurate and computationally lean. This paper investigates the application of post-training and quantization-aware training techniques to a family of convolutional defect detectors intended for deployment on low-power edge devices used in industrial conveyor-line inspection. We evaluate INT8 and mixed-precision INT4/INT8 quantization strategies across four detector architectures, measuring the trade-off between inference latency, memory footprint, and detection accuracy on three public industrial defect benchmarks. A structured pruning step preceding quantization is shown to recover accuracy losses for the most aggressive quantization settings. On a representative ARM Cortex-M55 target platform, the best-performing quantized detector achieves 34 frames per second with less than 2% mAP degradation relative to the full-precision baseline, satisfying the real-time constraint of most conveyor inspection scenarios. We further provide deployment guidelines and an open-source model-conversion toolkit compatible with common edge inference runtimes, lowering the barrier for practitioners in small and medium manufacturing enterprises to adopt AI-based inspection.

SYN-PUB-06390.title: Synthetic defect generation for visual quality control
SYN-PUB-06390.text:
Synthetic defect generation for visual quality control (2022, journal, Machine Vision Applications Review).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author).
The scarcity of labeled defect images is a persistent bottleneck in training robust visual quality control models, particularly for rare or newly introduced defect types. This paper explores procedural and generative approaches to synthetic defect generation, proposing a unified pipeline that combines physically based rendering (PBR) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) fine-tuned on a small set of real defect exemplars. The pipeline produces photorealistic defect images across six categories—scratches, pits, cracks, stains, delamination, and inclusion—on both metallic and polymer substrates. A systematic evaluation protocol measures the downstream impact of synthetic augmentation on detection model performance using three standard industrial datasets. Models trained with a 70% synthetic / 30% real mixture achieve accuracy within 3.2% of fully supervised baselines trained on complete real datasets, while reducing annotation effort by approximately 80%. The study also benchmarks the realism of generated images using FID and a domain-expert perceptual rating study. The findings support synthetic data generation as a cost-effective strategy for bootstrapping quality control systems in low-data manufacturing environments.

SYN-PUB-06391.title: Adaptive anomaly detection for multi-product assembly lines using one-class contrastive learning
SYN-PUB-06391.text:
Adaptive anomaly detection for multi-product assembly lines using one-class contrastive learning (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Stefan Brandt (outside co-author).
Keywords: anomaly detection; one-class learning; contrastive learning; multi-product inspection; edge inference.
Modern assembly lines frequently switch between product variants, requiring inspection systems that adapt rapidly to new normal-appearance distributions without collecting defect examples in advance. This paper presents an adaptive one-class contrastive learning framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in multi-product settings. The approach uses a momentum-updated reference encoder and an online memory bank of normal embeddings that is refreshed at product changeover events, enabling the model to track appearance shifts without full retraining. A self-supervised pretext task based on synthetic local masking strengthens the encoder's sensitivity to subtle textural and structural anomalies. The framework is evaluated on a novel multi-variant industrial benchmark—PolyAssembly-7—covering seven polymer component types across four product families. It achieves an average AUROC of 93.1% across all variants and demonstrates adaptation in fewer than 50 unlabeled normal samples per changeover, outperforming five established one-class detection baselines.
