Inference runs at 28 fps on an NVIDIA Jetson edge module. The results highlight the viability of continual anomaly detection for flexible manufacturing without persistent human annotation effort.

SYN-PUB-06392.title: Knowledge distillation for lightweight surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware
SYN-PUB-06392.text:
Knowledge distillation for lightweight surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware (2023, journal, Journal of Real-Time Image Processing).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Rastko Petrović (outside co-author); Lena Hofmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge distillation; edge computing; model compression; surface inspection; heterogeneous hardware.
Deploying high-accuracy surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware—spanning microcontrollers, FPGAs, and GPU-equipped single-board computers—requires models that balance computational cost with detection performance across very different hardware profiles. This paper proposes a hardware-aware knowledge distillation pipeline in which a large teacher network transfers representational knowledge to a suite of student architectures of varying capacities, each targeting a specific hardware tier. A novel attention-alignment distillation loss aligns intermediate feature maps at multiple scales, preserving fine-grained defect discriminability in the student networks. Experiments on three industrial surface inspection datasets show that the distilled lightweight students retain 95–98% of teacher mAP while reducing multiply-accumulate operations by 4× to 11× depending on the target hardware. We further present a hardware profiling methodology that automates student architecture selection given user-defined latency and accuracy constraints. The complete pipeline is released as an open-source toolkit, enabling non-expert practitioners to generate inspection-ready models for their specific edge deployment targets.

SYN-PUB-06393.title: Domain randomization strategies for cross-industry transfer in visual defect detection
SYN-PUB-06393.text:
Domain randomization strategies for cross-industry transfer in visual defect detection (2022, journal, Computer Vision and Image Understanding).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Marc Delacroix (outside co-author).
Keywords: domain randomization; transfer learning; defect detection; synthetic data; industrial inspection.
Visual defect detection models trained on one industrial domain often fail to generalize when transferred to a different material type, surface finish, or manufacturing process. This paper systematically investigates domain randomization as a transfer-enabling strategy, examining how randomization of texture, illumination, background clutter, and camera parameters during synthetic training data generation affects cross-domain transferability. A large-scale factorial experiment is conducted across six source-target domain pairs spanning metallic, ceramic, and textile substrates. Results show that targeted randomization of illumination direction and surface reflectance parameters yields the largest gains in target-domain detection accuracy, while excessive geometric randomization can degrade performance. Building on these findings, we propose an adaptive randomization curriculum that progressively increases domain diversity during training, guided by a domain-gap estimator computed from unlabeled target samples. The curriculum approach achieves a 6.8% average mAP improvement over static randomization across all transfer pairs, demonstrating a principled path toward generalizable industrial vision systems that require minimal target-domain labeling.

SYN-PUB-06394.title: Temporal consistency regularization for video-based industrial anomaly detection
SYN-PUB-06394.text:
Temporal consistency regularization for video-based industrial anomaly detection (2021, conference, International Conference on Machine Vision and Applications (ICMVA)).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Tamara Đurić (outside co-author); Ivana Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: anomaly detection; video inspection; temporal consistency; industrial vision; recurrent networks.
Frame-level anomaly detectors applied to industrial video streams often produce temporally inconsistent predictions, flagging and clearing the same defect region across successive frames due to minor illumination or motion changes. This paper introduces a temporal consistency regularization scheme that enforces smooth anomaly score trajectories across video frames without requiring ground-truth temporal annotations. A recurrent scoring head aggregates frame-level embeddings over a short sliding window, and a consistency loss penalizes abrupt score oscillations that are inconsistent with the physical persistence of genuine defects. The approach is evaluated on a new video inspection dataset—ConveyorVID—capturing three product types under realistic factory floor conditions including vibration, partial occlusion, and varying conveyor speed. The regularized model reduces the false-positive rate by 31% and improves temporal F1 score by 8.4 points compared to a strong frame-level baseline, with a negligible increase in computational overhead. Qualitative results confirm that the detector maintains stable anomaly localization across frames, a property that is critical for downstream alarm-triggering logic in automated quality control systems.

SYN-PUB-06395.title: Federated learning for privacy-preserving collaborative defect model training across SME factories
SYN-PUB-06395.text:
Federated learning for privacy-preserving collaborative defect model training across SME factories (2023, conference, Workshop on AI for Smart Manufacturing, ECML PKDD).
Authors: Miloš Cvejić (outside co-author); Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Katarina Bjelić (outside co-author).
Keywords: federated learning; defect detection; privacy-preserving AI; SME manufacturing; collaborative learning.
Small and medium enterprises in manufacturing are often reluctant to share proprietary defect imagery due to intellectual property and competitive concerns, yet individually they lack the data volume needed to train robust inspection models. This paper presents a federated learning framework designed specifically for collaborative defect detection across multiple SME factories, where each factory trains a local model on its own data and only gradient updates are communicated to a central aggregation server. A defect-class-aware aggregation strategy weights participant contributions proportionally to their class coverage, mitigating the class imbalance that arises when different factories produce different defect types. Communication efficiency is improved through structured gradient sparsification tailored to convolutional inspection model architectures. The framework is validated in a simulated federation of six virtual factories instantiated from three public industrial datasets partitioned to mimic realistic cross-factory data heterogeneity. Federated models match the accuracy of centrally trained counterparts within 4% mAP while transmitting less than 12% of the raw gradient volume, demonstrating practical feasibility for bandwidth-constrained industrial networks.

SYN-PUB-06396.title: Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines
SYN-PUB-06396.text:
Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines (2021, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author).
Keywords: active learning; annotation efficiency; defect detection; model uncertainty; industrial inspection.
Labeling defect images in industrial settings is expensive and requires domain expertise, making the efficient allocation of annotation effort a critical practical concern. This paper proposes an active learning framework for industrial defect detection that uses ensemble-based model uncertainty to prioritize the most informative unlabeled samples for expert annotation. A Monte Carlo dropout ensemble estimates epistemic uncertainty at the instance and region levels, and a diversity-aware sampling strategy prevents the selection of redundant near-duplicate crops from the same production batch. The framework is integrated into a realistic annotation pipeline validated with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-molded plastic components. Across both domains, the active learning approach achieves 90% of fully supervised baseline performance using only 35% of the total available labeled data, reducing annotation cost by an estimated 58% in practitioner time. A user study with three quality control engineers confirms that the uncertainty-guided sample ordering significantly reduces the cognitive load of the labeling process compared to random sample presentation.

SYN-PUB-06424.title: Automatska klasifikacija sudskih odluka korišćenjem SVM klasifikatora i TF-IDF reprezentacije
SYN-PUB-06424.text:
Automatska klasifikacija sudskih odluka korišćenjem SVM klasifikatora i TF-IDF reprezentacije (2010, journal, Journal of Information and Organizational Sciences).
Authors: Branislav Popović (outside co-author); Mirela Ostojić (outside co-author); Ksenija Mitrović (R0552).
Keywords: SVM; text classification; legal documents; Serbian; TF-IDF.
Rad predstavlja sistem za automatsku klasifikaciju sudskih odluka Vrhovnog kasacionog suda Republike Srbije u 12 pravnih oblasti. Korpus se sastoji od 4.200 anonimizovanih odluka prikupljenih između 2003. i 2008. godine. Primenjen je SVM klasifikator sa linearnim jezgrom na TF-IDF vektorizovanim tekstovima, uz eksperimentisanje sa različitim veličinama n-grama (unigrami, bigrami i trigrami). Evaluacija je sprovedena petostukim unakrsnim validiranjem. Najbolji rezultat postignut je kombinacijom unigrama i bigrama: makro F1 mera iznosila je 0,81. Analiza grešaka pokazuje da su kategorije sa malim brojem primera i dvosmislenom terminologijom (npr. radno pravo u odnosu na privredno pravo) najtežie za razlikovanje. Rad takođe opisuje postupak anotacije i metriku inter-anotatorne saglasnosti (Koen kapa = 0,79).

SYN-PUB-06425.title: Building a Manually Annotated Corpus of Serbian Legal Texts for NLP Benchmarking
SYN-PUB-06425.text:
Building a Manually Annotated Corpus of Serbian Legal Texts for NLP Benchmarking (2012, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation for South-East European Languages (LRESEL)).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Branislav Popović (outside co-author); Tibor Vámos (outside co-author).
Keywords: corpus annotation; Serbian NLP; legal corpus; named entity recognition; benchmarking.
This paper describes the construction and release of SerbLex-1.0, a manually annotated corpus of 8,500 Serbian legal documents spanning legislation, court rulings, and administrative decisions from 1995 to 2010. Annotation covers sentence boundaries, named entities (persons, organisations, locations, dates), and thematic categories across 18 legal domains. Inter-annotator agreement was measured on a 1,200-document subset, yielding a Cohen's kappa of 0.76 for named entity spans and 0.83 for thematic labels. The paper reports baseline performance figures for three established classifiers—Naive Bayes, maximum entropy, and SVM—alongside a rule-based tokeniser adapted for Serbian legal orthography. Corpus statistics reveal significant class imbalance, with commercial law and civil procedure accounting for over 40% of documents. The corpus is made available under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence.

SYN-PUB-06426.title: Polu-nadgledano učenje za kategorizaciju zakonodavnih izmena u srpskom pravnom sistemu
SYN-PUB-06426.text:
Polu-nadgledano učenje za kategorizaciju zakonodavnih izmena u srpskom pravnom sistemu (2014, journal, Računarstvo i informatika – časopis za teoriju i primenu računarskih nauka).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Nemanja Ćosić (outside co-author).
Keywords: semi-supervised learning; co-training; legislative text; Serbian; label propagation.
Ovaj rad istražuje primenu polu-nadgledanih metoda klasifikacije na problem automatskog prepoznavanja vrsta izmena u zakonodavnim tekstovima (dopune, brisanja, supstitucije i terminološke promene). Polazni skup označenih primera obuhvata 620 ručno obeleženih paragrafa iz Službenog glasnika RS za period 2008–2012, dok se polu-nadgledana komponenta oslanja na 14.000 neobeleženih paragrafa. Testirana su tri pristupa: samo-učenje (self-training), ko-učenje (co-training) sa dva pogleda (leksički i sintaksički) i grafovski zasnovano širenje oznaka (label propagation). Ko-učenje postiže makro F1 od 0,74 u odnosu na 0,68 kod čisto nadgledanog modela pri istoj količini označenih podataka. Rad analizira uticaj veličine inicijalnog labeled skupa (50, 200 i 620 primera) na stabilnost rezultata i predlaže heuristiku za odabir pouzdanih samoobeleženih primera.

SYN-PUB-06427.title: Semantic Similarity Measures for Matching Legal Clauses Across Jurisdictions
SYN-PUB-06427.text:
Semantic Similarity Measures for Matching Legal Clauses Across Jurisdictions (2016, journal, International Journal of Legal Information Technology).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Johann Steinhauer (outside co-author).
Keywords: semantic similarity; legal clauses; cross-lingual; word embeddings; contract law.
Identifying equivalent or near-equivalent clauses in contract law documents from different national jurisdictions is an important task for comparative legal research and cross-border compliance. This study evaluates six semantic similarity measures—cosine similarity over TF-IDF vectors, BM25, word mover's distance, averaged word2vec embeddings, Doc2Vec, and a fine-tuned multilingual sentence encoder—on a manually constructed parallel dataset of 1,840 clause pairs drawn from Serbian, Croatian, and Austrian commercial contracts. Each pair was labelled by two legal experts as equivalent, partially equivalent, or non-equivalent. Spearman correlation between model scores and expert ratings is reported for each method. The fine-tuned sentence encoder achieves ρ = 0.71, substantially outperforming the TF-IDF baseline (ρ = 0.48). Error analysis shows that domain-specific terminology and negation patterns are the main sources of failure across all methods.

SYN-PUB-06428.title: Detekcija anomalija u javnim nabavkama primenom metoda obrade teksta i statističkog modeliranja
SYN-PUB-06428.text:
Detekcija anomalija u javnim nabavkama primenom metoda obrade teksta i statističkog modeliranja (2017, journal, Zbornik radova FTN – Elektrotehnika i računarstvo).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Aleksandra Radovanović (outside co-author); Miloš Jovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: anomaly detection; public procurement; one-class SVM; MinHash; Serbian.
Rad opisuje sistem za automatsku detekciju potencijalno neregularnih tender dokumenata u bazi javnih nabavki Republike Srbije. Korišćen je skup od 23.400 tenderskih specifikacija objavljenih između 2013. i 2016. godine. Anomalije su definisane u tri kategorije: neuobičajeni tehnički uslovi koji ograničavaju konkurenciju, nekonzistentna upotreba merne jedinice i vrednosti, i kopiranje teksta između naizgled nepovezanih ponuda. Za detekciju prve kategorije primenjen je one-class SVM na TF-IDF vektorima; za drugu je korišćena statistička kontrolna karta zasnovana na z-skoru numerički ekstrahovanih vrednosti; za treću fuzzy heširanje (MinHash LSH). Sistem je validiran na 200 ručno pregledanih primera od strane revizora Državne revizorske institucije, pri čemu je postignut recall od 0,83 i precision od 0,61. Rad diskutuje ograničenja uzrokovana kvalitetom izvornih OCR dokumenata.

SYN-PUB-06429.title: Domain Adaptation of Pre-trained Word Embeddings for South Slavic Legal Text
SYN-PUB-06429.text:
Domain Adaptation of Pre-trained Word Embeddings for South Slavic Legal Text (2018, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on NLP for Legal and Governmental Documents (LegGov-NLP) at LREC).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Tamara Blagojević (outside co-author); Mirko Stanić (outside co-author); Renata Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: domain adaptation; word embeddings; South Slavic languages; legal NLP; fastText.
General-purpose word embedding models trained on news and web corpora perform poorly on legal text due to the divergent distribution of technical and archaic terminology. This paper investigates three domain adaptation strategies—continued training, vocabulary extension, and retrofitting with a legal synonym lexicon—applied to publicly available fastText models for Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian. Adaptation uses a 120-million-token corpus assembled from national gazettes and court databases. Intrinsic evaluation uses a newly constructed legal word analogy set (3,200 quadruples) and a legal similarity judgement set (480 pairs). The retrofitting approach yields the largest gains on similarity judgements, improving Spearman correlation from 0.38 to 0.57 for Serbian. Downstream evaluation on two classification tasks (document type and legal domain) shows improvements of 2–4 F1 points over unadapted embeddings. All adapted models and evaluation sets are released publicly.

SYN-PUB-06430.title: Fine-Tuning BERT for Regulatory Compliance Classification in the Energy Sector
SYN-PUB-06430.text:
Fine-Tuning BERT for Regulatory Compliance Classification in the Energy Sector (2020, journal, Journal of Intelligent Information Systems).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Stefan Marković (outside co-author); Claudia Neumann (outside co-author).
Keywords: BERT; regulatory compliance; energy sector; fine-tuning; text classification.
This study examines the performance of fine-tuned BERT-based models for classifying technical regulatory documents from the Serbian and European energy sector according to a compliance taxonomy with 24 leaf categories. A domain-specific corpus of 9,800 labelled documents was constructed from the regulatory archive of the Energy Agency of the Republic of Serbia and publicly available EU energy directives, with labels assigned by two certified compliance officers. Four model variants were compared: multilingual BERT, Serbian-only BERT, a legal-domain BERT pre-trained on EU legislative text (LegalBERT-EU), and a baseline TF-IDF+SVM pipeline. LegalBERT-EU achieved the highest macro F1 of 0.86, followed by Serbian BERT at 0.83. The SVM baseline reached 0.74. Attention analysis reveals that the transformer models rely heavily on modal verbs and obligation phrases as classification signals. Training and inference times are reported for a mid-range GPU server.

SYN-PUB-06431.title: Detecting Contradictory Obligations in Contract Drafts Using Sentence-Level Entailment Models
SYN-PUB-06431.text:
Detecting Contradictory Obligations in Contract Drafts Using Sentence-Level Entailment Models (2022, journal, Artificial Intelligence and Law).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Stefan Marković (outside co-author); Renata Horvat (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: natural language inference; contradiction detection; contract analysis; deontic logic; cross-lingual.
Contracts drafted by multiple parties over successive revisions sometimes contain clauses that create contradictory obligations. This paper addresses automated detection of such contradictions using natural language inference (NLI) models adapted to contractual text. A dataset of 2,640 clause pairs was annotated by contract lawyers as entailment, neutral, or contradiction, drawn from 480 service-level agreements and supply contracts in Serbian and English. Cross-lingual zero-shot transfer from an English-trained NLI model achieves an F1 of 0.61 on the Serbian subset, while a fine-tuned multilingual model reaches 0.78. A rule-augmented hybrid system combining the NLI model with a hand-crafted deontic logic pattern library achieves 0.82 F1. Ablation experiments show the pattern library contributes most to recall on negation-based contradictions. The annotated dataset will be released upon acceptance.

SYN-PUB-06432.title: Merenje semantičke sličnosti između srpskih zakonskih normi i korporativnih politika: pristup zasnovan na kontrastivnom učenju
SYN-PUB-06432.text:
Merenje semantičke sličnosti između srpskih zakonskih normi i korporativnih politika: pristup zasnovan na kontrastivnom učenju (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Central European Conference on Information and Intelligent Systems (CECIIS)).
Authors: Jelena Đurić (outside co-author); Nikola Tomović (outside co-author); Ksenija Mitrović (R0552).
Keywords: contrastive learning; semantic similarity; compliance; Serbian; sentence encoders.
Ovaj rad razmatra problem automatskog uparivanja zakonskih normi iz domaćeg zakonodavstva sa internim korporativnim politikama radi provere usklađenosti. Predložen je pristup zasnovan na kontrastivnom učenju gde su pozitivni parovi ručno definisani od strane compliance konsultanata, a negativni parovi uzorkovani iz različitih zakonskih oblasti. Model koristi dvotokový enkoder sa srpskim RoBERTa inicijalizacijom, finajtuiran na 3.200 anotiranih parova. Evaluacija obuhvata i standardnu preciznost na test skupu (mAP = 0,79) i praktičnu metriku odbranjenu pred poslovnim korisnicima: udeo slučajeva gde je tačan zakon rangiran unutar prvih tri rezultata (Recall@3 = 0,88). Poređenje sa BM25 i standardnim kosinus similaritetom na SBERT vektorima ukazuje na napredak od 9, odnosno 5 procentnih poena za Recall@3. Model je integrisan u prototip alata za compliance koji je testiran u dve kompanije iz finansijskog sektora.

SYN-PUB-06433.title: Evaluacija velikih jezičkih modela na zadacima pravnog rezonovanja u srpskom jeziku
SYN-PUB-06433.text:
Evaluacija velikih jezičkih modela na zadacima pravnog rezonovanja u srpskom jeziku (2025, conference, Jezik, tehnologija i pravo – zbornik radova Druge konferencije o računarskoj lingvistici za srpski jezik).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Tamara Blagojević (outside co-author); Milica Nešić (outside co-author); Stefan Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: large language models; legal reasoning; Serbian; LLM evaluation; NLP benchmarks.
Rad sistematski procenjuje sposobnost četiri velika jezička modela (LLM) – GPT-4o, Llama 3 70B, Mistral Large i srpski prilagođen model SrbGPT-7B – na skupu zadataka pravnog rezonovanja u srpskom jeziku. Definisano je pet zadataka: identifikacija relevantnog zakonskog osnova, detekcija kršenja proceduralnih normi, ekstrakcija strana u sporu, summarizacija presude u propisanom formatu i klasifikacija u pravnu oblast. Svaki zadatak pokriva 200 primera, ručno proverenih od strane pravnih stručnjaka. GPT-4o postiže najvišu tačnost u četiri od pet zadataka (73–89%), dok SrbGPT-7B, uprkos mnogo manjem broju parametara, postiže konkurentne rezultate na morfološki zahtevnijim zadacima ekstrakcije. Rad identifikuje sistematske greške u razumevanju negacije i upućivanja na prethodne stavove (anaphora resolution) kao zajednički problem svih modela. Zaključci su relevantni za procenu praktične primenljivosti LLM-ova u pravosudnom kontekstu.

SYN-PUB-06434.title: Continual Learning for Evolving Legal Taxonomies: Preventing Catastrophic Forgetting in Serbian Statutory Classification
SYN-PUB-06434.text:
Continual Learning for Evolving Legal Taxonomies: Preventing Catastrophic Forgetting in Serbian Statutory Classification (2026, journal, Information Processing and Management).
Authors: Ksenija Mitrović (R0552); Jelena Đurić (outside co-author); Aron Fehér (outside co-author).
Keywords: continual learning; catastrophic forgetting; legal taxonomy; elastic weight consolidation; statutory classification.
Legal classification systems face a practical challenge: national legislatures periodically restructure statutory categories, requiring models to learn new classes without forgetting old ones. This paper applies five continual learning strategies—fine-tuning, elastic weight consolidation (EWC), progressive neural networks, experience replay, and a generative replay variant using a lightweight language model—to a Serbian statutory classification task spanning three taxonomy versions issued between 2018 and 2024. Each taxonomy update introduces between two and seven new categories and retires one to three existing ones. Performance is measured using backward transfer, forward transfer, and average accuracy across all versions. EWC and generative replay show the smallest backward transfer (0.04 and 0.03 average F1 drop respectively) while maintaining competitive forward transfer. Naive fine-tuning exhibits catastrophic forgetting with a backward transfer of −0.19. The study provides practical guidance on update schedules and replay buffer sizing for operational legal NLP systems.

SYN-PUB-06500.title: Quantisation Effects on Recall and Storage in Billion-Scale ANN Search
SYN-PUB-06500.text:
Quantisation Effects on Recall and Storage in Billion-Scale ANN Search (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Database and Information Systems (ICDIS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author); Sara Despotović (R0559); Nikola Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: product quantisation; ANN search; HNSW; billion-scale; vector compression.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-06501.title: Index Routing Policies for Multi-Tenant Search Services: A Simulation Study
SYN-PUB-06501.text:
Index Routing Policies for Multi-Tenant Search Services: A Simulation Study (2023, journal, Journal of Distributed Computing Systems (JDCS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Sara Despotović (R0559); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: multi-tenant search; index routing; cluster simulation; load balancing.
Multi-tenant search services host thousands of independent indexes on shared infrastructure. Routing decisions—which node handles each index shard—affect both query latency and hardware utilisation. We simulate a 20-node cluster hosting 3,200 index shards with heterogeneous sizes and query-rate profiles drawn from anonymised access logs of a mid-sized document management platform. Four routing policies are compared: random placement, size-balanced bin packing, query-rate-aware placement, and a combined policy that jointly optimises for size and rate. The combined policy reduces 99th-percentile latency by 27% and lowers peak CPU utilisation by 19% relative to random placement under realistic diurnal load patterns. Simulation is implemented in a purpose-built discrete-event framework to allow reproducible experimentation without requiring access to production hardware. Sensitivity analyses show the gains hold across a range of shard-size distributions.

SYN-PUB-06563.title: Comparing generalised extreme value and log-normal tail models for Serbian flood damage records, 1980–2014
SYN-PUB-06563.text:
Comparing generalised extreme value and log-normal tail models for Serbian flood damage records, 1980–2014 (2017, journal, Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment).
Authors: Dragana Stjepanović (outside co-author); Ildikó Virág (outside co-author); Péter Szabó (R0842); Andrej Kokol Bukovšek (outside co-author); Nenad Fejsa (R0565).
Keywords: GEV distribution; flood losses; block maxima; return levels; L-moments.
Annual maximum insured flood losses from 14 Serbian counties over 35 years are modelled with the block maxima generalised extreme value (GEV) distribution and, as a benchmark, a log-normal upper tail. Maximum likelihood, L-moment, and Bayesian (non-informative Jeffreys prior) parameter estimates are compared for the GEV shape, location, and scale. In ten of the 14 counties the posterior shape parameter credible interval includes zero, suggesting Gumbel behaviour; three counties show positive shape consistent with heavy-tail Fréchet behaviour. Return-level estimates for 50- and 100-year events differ substantially between GEV and log-normal models when the shape is positive. The practical implication for regional reinsurance pricing is discussed. Data were obtained from the Serbian Flood Insurance Pool archive.

SYN-PUB-06614.title: A Rule-Based Framework for Detecting Structural Inconsistencies in REST API Responses
SYN-PUB-06614.text:
A Rule-Based Framework for Detecting Structural Inconsistencies in REST API Responses (2015, journal, Journal of Information and Software Engineering (JISE)).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Jelena Stojčić (outside co-author); Mirjana Malešević (R0571).
Keywords: REST API; schema validation; rule-based monitoring; JSON; data quality.
Web service APIs frequently change their response schemas without formal versioning, causing downstream data consumers to silently ingest malformed or incomplete records. This paper presents a lightweight rule-based framework that continuously inspects JSON payloads returned by REST endpoints and flags deviations from a registered baseline schema. The framework encodes expected field types, cardinality constraints, and value-range rules in a declarative specification file. Violations are classified into four severity tiers and surfaced through an alerting interface. The approach was evaluated against a corpus of 14 publicly accessible APIs monitored over six months, capturing 38 distinct schema-change events. Detection latency averaged 1.4 seconds from the first non-conforming response. False-positive rates remained below 2.1% across all monitored endpoints. The paper also discusses how rule sets can be partially auto-generated from historical response samples using frequency-based field inference. The implementation is provided as a self-contained Java library with a configuration-file interface.

SYN-PUB-06616.title: Cross-Source Consistency Validation for Event-Triggered Business Logic in Distributed Retail Systems
SYN-PUB-06616.text:
Cross-Source Consistency Validation for Event-Triggered Business Logic in Distributed Retail Systems (2018, journal, International Journal of Distributed and Parallel Systems (IJDPS)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Nikola Lazić (outside co-author); Cornelia Munteanu (outside co-author).
Keywords: cross-source consistency; event-driven systems; distributed retail; conflict detection; business logic.
When a single business event—such as a purchase confirmation—must be reflected consistently across inventory, billing, and logistics APIs, inconsistencies arising from partial failures or race conditions can corrupt downstream decision logic. This paper formalises a consistency validation model that reconciles event records from multiple independent API sources by aligning them on a shared transaction identifier and a configurable time window. A conflict detection module compares field-level values across sources and produces a structured discrepancy report. The approach was tested on a synthetic dataset of 500,000 simulated purchase events with injected inconsistencies at rates of 0.5%, 2%, and 5%. Precision exceeded 97% in all three scenarios; recall dropped to 91% at 0.5% injection rate due to borderline timestamp ambiguities. The paper proposes a tie-breaking heuristic based on source-reliability weights that partially recovers recall in low-rate conditions. Runtime overhead on a four-core commodity server was under 8% of total pipeline throughput.

SYN-PUB-06617.title: Schema Drift in Production API Pipelines: A Classification and Empirical Frequency Study
SYN-PUB-06617.text:
Schema Drift in Production API Pipelines: A Classification and Empirical Frequency Study (2020, journal, Journal of Data and Information Quality (JDIQ Supplement)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Bojana Đurić (outside co-author); Nenad Dimitrijević (R0592); Miroslav Kratochvíl (outside co-author); Stefan Ognjanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: schema drift; API monitoring; taxonomy; empirical study; pipeline reliability.
Schema drift—the unannounced alteration of data structures returned by APIs—is a recurring but poorly documented source of pipeline failures in practice. This paper presents a taxonomy of drift types encountered in production environments, distinguishing field addition, field removal, type coercion, key renaming, and structural nesting changes. An automated monitoring agent was deployed against 31 internal API endpoints operated by four partner organisations over 12 months, logging all response payloads in a versioned data store. Analysis of 9.7 million captured responses identified 74 drift events. Field addition was the most frequent type (41%), followed by type coercion (27%). Drift events clustered around software release dates, with 68% occurring within 48 hours of a detected version tag change in response headers. The paper derives practical design guidelines for pipeline engineers and discusses the feasibility of proactive drift prediction using release-calendar metadata.

SYN-PUB-06618.title: Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry
SYN-PUB-06618.text:
Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Data Quality in Engineering Systems (DQES 2021)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Todorović (outside co-author); Péter Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: Isolation Forest; multivariate anomaly detection; IoT telemetry; streaming data; unsupervised learning.
High-frequency telemetry streams produced by IoT gateways and industrial APIs exhibit multivariate numeric patterns that rule-based detectors handle poorly when anomalies involve correlated deviations across several fields simultaneously. This paper investigates the use of the Isolation Forest algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection in such streams, focusing on tuning the contamination parameter and the number of estimators under streaming constraints. Experiments used telemetry data from a factory automation pilot comprising six sensor channels sampled at 10 Hz over 30 days, yielding approximately 15.5 million records. Isolation Forest outperformed a univariate z-score baseline by 18 percentage points in F1 score on held-out labelled anomaly windows. The paper also reports the effect of sub-sampling strategies on detection quality when full-stream processing is not feasible, and provides a reference configuration table for practitioners operating within defined memory budgets. No labelled training data was required beyond the held-out evaluation set.

SYN-PUB-06619.title: Data Quality Monitoring in Apache Kafka Pipelines: Design Patterns and Operational Trade-offs
SYN-PUB-06619.text:
Data Quality Monitoring in Apache Kafka Pipelines: Design Patterns and Operational Trade-offs (2022, book chapter, Advances in Distributed Data Engineering (Springer LNCS volume, invented)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Dragana Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Apache Kafka; design patterns; data quality; stream processing; schema registry.
Apache Kafka has become a standard backbone for real-time data integration, yet integrating data quality checks directly into Kafka-based pipelines introduces non-trivial design decisions around consumer group placement, serialisation overhead, and back-pressure handling. This book chapter surveys and categorises design patterns for embedding schema validation, completeness checks, and anomaly scoring into Kafka consumer and Kafka Streams topologies. Four patterns are described in detail: inline validator consumers, side-car quality topics, quality-aware stream processors, and batch reconciliation jobs reading from compacted topics. Each pattern is evaluated against five criteria: latency impact, fault isolation, replayability, operational complexity, and suitability for schema drift detection. The chapter draws on deployment experience from three pilot integrations and provides worked configuration examples for each pattern using the Confluent Schema Registry and custom Avro schemas. Intended audience is data engineers and architects with working Kafka experience.

SYN-PUB-06620.title: Detecting Silent Data Corruption Caused by API Middleware Caching in Event-Driven Microservices
SYN-PUB-06620.text:
Detecting Silent Data Corruption Caused by API Middleware Caching in Event-Driven Microservices (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Services Computing (fictional sub-venue: Special Issue on Data Integrity in Microservices)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Ivan Marković (outside co-author); Hana Blažević (outside co-author); Stefan Ognjanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: caching; stale data; microservices; consistency audit; event-driven architecture.
Middleware caching layers in microservice architectures can serve stale data to downstream consumers long after the source record has been updated, producing a form of silent data corruption that is difficult to detect because individual responses remain schema-valid. This paper describes a consistency audit mechanism that periodically issues cache-bypass probe requests and compares their payloads against the most recently cached versions stored in a pipeline audit log. Discrepancies are scored by field-level severity weights reflecting business criticality. The mechanism was deployed in a logistics integration scenario comprising 11 microservices and approximately 200,000 event transactions per day. Over a four-week observation window, 312 stale-cache discrepancy instances were identified, of which 29 affected fields classified as high-criticality. The paper analyses the relationship between cache TTL settings and discrepancy frequency and proposes an adaptive TTL reduction policy triggered by elevated discrepancy scores. End-to-end detection latency averaged 3.1 seconds.

SYN-PUB-06621.title: Benchmarking Schema-Drift Detectors Under Controlled Injection: A Reproducible Evaluation Protocol
SYN-PUB-06621.text:
Benchmarking Schema-Drift Detectors Under Controlled Injection: A Reproducible Evaluation Protocol (2025, journal, Journal of Systems and Software — Data Engineering Track (fictional sub-venue)).
Authors: Emőke Varga (outside co-author); Radovan Jovanović (outside co-author); Luisa Ferreira (outside co-author); Mirjana Malešević (R0571).
Keywords: benchmarking; schema drift; reproducibility; evaluation protocol; JSON streams.
Comparing schema-drift detection methods across published papers is hampered by incompatible datasets, inconsistent drift injection procedures, and unreported hyperparameter choices. This paper proposes a reproducible benchmarking protocol for schema-drift detectors operating on JSON API streams. The protocol defines six canonical drift injection categories, each with three severity levels, applied to a synthetic baseline dataset generated by a configurable data generator released alongside the paper. Five existing detection approaches—including two rule-based and three statistical methods—were re-implemented and evaluated under the protocol. Results show that rule-based methods achieve higher precision on structural drift (type coercion, key removal) but fail entirely on distributional value drift, whereas statistical detectors show the inverse pattern. No single evaluated method scored above 0.80 F1 across all six categories simultaneously. The paper concludes with a discussion of hybrid architectures and releases all code and datasets under an open licence to facilitate future comparisons.

SYN-PUB-06622.title: Incremental Schema Inference for Long-Running API Integrations Using Probabilistic Field Tracking
SYN-PUB-06622.text:
Incremental Schema Inference for Long-Running API Integrations Using Probabilistic Field Tracking (2026, conference, Proceedings of the 18th European Conference on Data Engineering Practices (ECDEP 2026)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Todorović (outside co-author); Anita Schwarz (outside co-author).
Keywords: schema inference; probabilistic models; API integration; incremental learning; data governance.
Maintaining accurate schema documentation for APIs that evolve continuously over years is impractical when done manually. This paper presents an incremental schema inference engine that updates a probabilistic field model after each observed API response, tracking field presence probability, dominant type, value entropy, and co-occurrence correlations with other fields. The engine distinguishes transient field appearances (sparse presence below a configurable threshold) from stable schema additions, reducing noise in drift alerts. It was evaluated on a 26-month archive of responses from seven APIs in a supply chain integration platform, comprising 31 million records. The inferred schemas at month 26 matched manually audited ground-truth schemas with 94.2% field-level precision and 96.8% recall. Incremental update cost per response averaged 0.9 milliseconds on a mid-range server. The paper discusses integration with existing Kafka-based pipeline monitoring and provides configuration guidance for organisations with limited schema governance resources.

SYN-PUB-06623.title: One-Class SVM for Detection of Scripted Clients in a Massively Multiplayer Online Environment
SYN-PUB-06623.text:
One-Class SVM for Detection of Scripted Clients in a Massively Multiplayer Online Environment (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information and Intelligent Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948); Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Dragana Tadić (R0856); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: one-class SVM; scripted clients; bot detection; anomaly detection; online games.
Scripted clients—programs that automate repetitive in-game actions—undermine economy balance in online games and are difficult to identify using rule-based filters alone. This paper applies one-class support vector machines (OC-SVM) to a labelled telemetry dataset of 48,000 sessions drawn from a game server log archive, of which 3,200 sessions were confirmed scripted via ban records. Training used only the majority legitimate-player class. Feature vectors were constructed from 22 behavioural metrics including action entropy, movement path straightness, click interval coefficient of variation, and resource acquisition rate. Radial basis function kernel parameters were tuned via cross-validation on a held-out clean subset. The resulting model achieved an F1 score of 0.81 on the contaminated test split, with a false-positive rate of 4.3%. Results were compared against isolation forest and local outlier factor baselines. The paper also discusses the effect of class contamination levels during training on downstream detection performance.

SYN-PUB-06789.title: Supraharmonic emissions (2–150 kHz) from grid-connected photovoltaic inverters: field measurements and spectral characterisation
SYN-PUB-06789.text:
Supraharmonic emissions (2–150 kHz) from grid-connected photovoltaic inverters: field measurements and spectral characterisation (2017, journal, Renewable Energy and Power Quality Journal).
Authors: Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Rossella Fantozzi (outside co-author); Martin Bartoš (R0587); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: supraharmonics; photovoltaic inverter; grid-connected; spectral characterisation; 2–150 kHz.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-06790.title: Penetration Loss of Agricultural Greenhouse Structures at Sub-GHz Frequencies
SYN-PUB-06790.text:
Penetration Loss of Agricultural Greenhouse Structures at Sub-GHz Frequencies (2025, journal, IET Microwaves, Antennas and Propagation).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Biljana Pešić (outside co-author); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author); Martin Bartoš (R0587); Sonja Mišković (outside co-author).
Keywords: greenhouse propagation; penetration loss; precision agriculture; sub-GHz; IoT; polycarbonate.
Precision agriculture IoT systems often require radio links to pass through greenhouse structures whose aluminium frames, polycarbonate panels, and elevated humidity create attenuation conditions not well characterised in existing standards. Penetration loss was measured at 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz for three representative greenhouse wall and roof construction types: single-wall polycarbonate, double-wall polycarbonate, and glass with aluminium framing. Measurements were taken at 30 incidence angles between 0° and 70° in dry and wet surface conditions. Single-wall polycarbonate showed low penetration loss (2–4 dB) largely independent of frequency, while aluminium-framed glass panels exhibited 9–14 dB depending on frame density and incidence angle. Wet surfaces added 0.5–2.5 dB across all materials. A simple table of incidence-angle-dependent correction factors is derived for use in existing path-loss models, and its accuracy is validated against measurements from a commercial greenhouse IoT installation with 12 sensor nodes.

SYN-PUB-06837.title: Residual Oil Film Thickness on Cold-Rolled Steel Strip and Its Influence on MIG Weld Pool Stability
SYN-PUB-06837.text:
Residual Oil Film Thickness on Cold-Rolled Steel Strip and Its Influence on MIG Weld Pool Stability (2017, journal, Journal of Manufacturing and Surface Engineering).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Branislav Krstić (outside co-author); Sonja Đurić (outside co-author); Tamara Novković (outside co-author).
Keywords: pre-weld cleanliness; oil film; arc stability; porosity; cold-rolled steel.
Stamped automotive-grade cold-rolled mild-steel blanks typically carry residual drawing oil films in the range of 0.3–2.5 g/m². This study quantifies the relationship between oil film thickness, measured gravimetrically after solvent extraction, and arc stability indicators during MIG welding. Twenty-four coupons with controlled oil loads (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.5 g/m², applied by roller coating with a SAE 10W reference oil) were welded under a fixed parameter set optimised for zero-oil conditions. Arc voltage and current waveforms were sampled at 50 kHz and analysed for short-circuit frequency, arc-on time fraction, and standard deviation of voltage. At 1.5 g/m² and above, arc-on time fraction dropped from 0.81 to 0.67 and short-circuit frequency increased by 34 %, accompanied by a 51 % rise in spatter mass. Bead porosity, assessed by X-ray radiography per EN ISO 5817, remained within level C limits up to 1.0 g/m² but exceeded them at higher loads. The results suggest a practical cleanliness threshold of ≤ 1.0 g/m² for production lines without degreasing pre-treatment.

SYN-PUB-06838.title: Weld Process Parameter Optimisation for Low-Spatter MIG/MAG Joining of Thin Mild-Steel Sheet
SYN-PUB-06838.text:
Weld Process Parameter Optimisation for Low-Spatter MIG/MAG Joining of Thin Mild-Steel Sheet (2017, book chapter, PhD Thesis, University of Novi Sad).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593).
Keywords: MIG/MAG; spatter; response surface methodology; thin sheet; shielding gas.
This doctoral thesis presents a systematic investigation of process variable interactions governing spatter formation in short-arc and globular-to-spray-transition MIG/MAG welding of S235JR and DC01 sheet in thicknesses of 1.0–2.5 mm. Response surface methodology with a central composite design covering five factors — arc voltage, wire feed speed, travel speed, contact-tip-to-work distance, and shielding gas composition (Ar/CO₂ ratio 75/25 to 92/8) — was used to build regression models for spatter mass rate, bead width deviation, and tensile efficiency. Optimised conditions were validated on 120 weld specimens; spatter mass rates below 0.08 g/m were achieved on 1.2 mm sheet with a mixed gas of Ar/CO₂ 82/18 at 17.8 V, 5.8 m/min, and 45 cm/min travel speed. Mechanical testing confirmed all welds met EN ISO 15614-1 requirements. A simplified decision chart translating sheet thickness and joint configuration into parameter windows is provided as a practical outcome for production engineers.

SYN-PUB-06839.title: Alkaline Degreasing Bath Concentration and Temperature Effects on Residual Carbon and Wettability of Mild-Steel Sheet Before Powder Coating
SYN-PUB-06839.text:
Alkaline Degreasing Bath Concentration and Temperature Effects on Residual Carbon and Wettability of Mild-Steel Sheet Before Powder Coating (2019, journal, Surface Treatment and Finishing — European Journal).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Mirjana Vukčević (outside co-author); Nikola Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: alkaline degreasing; surface cleanliness; wettability; powder coating; pre-treatment.
Alkaline spray degreasing is the first stage in most powder coating pre-treatment lines. This study investigates how bath concentration (10–40 g/L of a commercial alkaline degreaser, Alkoclean 720) and temperature (45–70 °C) affect the residual total organic carbon (TOC) on the sheet surface and the resulting water contact angle. A 3² factorial design was applied to DC01 cold-rolled panels (100 × 150 mm) at a fixed spray pressure of 1.2 bar and 60 s exposure. Residual TOC was measured by combustion analysis of surface swabs. Contact angle was measured by sessile drop with deionised water. Bath concentration was the more influential factor: raising concentration from 10 to 40 g/L reduced median TOC from 48 to 9 µg/dm² and contact angle from 62° to 14°. Temperature above 60 °C provided marginal additional improvement. Cross-cut adhesion testing (EN ISO 2409) of subsequently phosphated and powder-coated panels showed a direct correlation between contact angle after degreasing and final coating adhesion class, with all panels degreased at ≥ 20 g/L achieving class 0.

SYN-PUB-06840.title: Measurement Uncertainty in Contact Angle Determination as a Process Control Indicator in Powder Coating Pre-Treatment
SYN-PUB-06840.text:
Measurement Uncertainty in Contact Angle Determination as a Process Control Indicator in Powder Coating Pre-Treatment (2020, journal, Measurement Science and Quality Assurance).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: contact angle; measurement uncertainty; GUM; powder coating; quality control.
Contact angle measurement by the sessile drop method is increasingly used as an inline or near-line indicator of surface cleanliness in powder coating pre-treatment lines. However, its measurement uncertainty under industrial conditions has not been systematically characterised. This study applies the GUM framework to quantify uncertainty contributions from drop volume (1–5 µL), image acquisition angle, baseline detection algorithm, and surface roughness for DC01 panels at various stages of a five-stage pre-treatment line (degrease, rinse, zinc phosphate, rinse, passivation). Expanded uncertainty (k = 2) ranged from ±1.8° on smooth panels after rinsing to ±6.4° on phosphated panels with Ra ≈ 1.8 µm. Operator-to-operator reproducibility, evaluated across four operators on identical panels, contributed 18–31 % of total variance depending on stage. Practical control limits accounting for these uncertainties are proposed for each pre-treatment stage, offering a statistically defensible accept/reject criterion for production quality control.

SYN-PUB-06841.title: Phosphate Coat Weight Uniformity Across a Conveyor-Fed Spray Phosphating Line: A Multi-Point Sampling Study
SYN-PUB-06841.text:
Phosphate Coat Weight Uniformity Across a Conveyor-Fed Spray Phosphating Line: A Multi-Point Sampling Study (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Central European Conference on Surface Engineering, Graz).
Authors: Nikola Radovanović (outside co-author); Đuro Simić (R0593); Katarina Mađarević (outside co-author); Péter Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: zinc phosphating; coat weight; process control; spray line; powder coating.
Zinc phosphate pre-treatment is critical to adhesion and corrosion resistance in electrostatic powder coating. This paper reports a multi-point sampling campaign at a medium-sized contract coating shop operating a seven-stage spray line with a throughput of 1800 m²/day. Coat weight was determined gravimetrically (strip-and-weigh per EN ISO 9717) at nine positions across the conveyor width and three longitudinal positions per batch, over 14 production days. Mean coat weight was 2.4 g/m² with a within-batch coefficient of variation of 11–19 % and a between-day coefficient of variation of 8 %. Edge zones (within 80 mm of conveyor rail) showed systematically 22 % lower coat weights, attributable to spray shadow effects characterised by flow visualisation with tracer dye. Bath chemistry (Zn²⁺, total acid, free acid, accelerator concentration) was logged concurrently; free acid point emerged as the strongest predictor of coat weight in a multiple regression model (R² = 0.71). Adjusting free acid set-point from 0.8 to 1.1 points reduced between-position variance by 31 % over a two-week trial.

SYN-PUB-06842.title: Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input
SYN-PUB-06842.text:
Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input (2023, journal, International Journal of Welding Science and Practice).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Tamara Novković (outside co-author); Uroš Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: shielding gas; Ar/CO₂; thin sheet; heat input; bead geometry.
Very thin mild-steel sheet (1.0 mm DC01) presents a narrow operating window in MIG welding because heat input must be minimised to avoid burn-through while maintaining fusion. This paper reports the effect of Ar/CO₂ mixture ratios (75/25, 82/18, 90/10, and 97/3 vol%) on spatter mass, bead width, dilution, and distortion in bead-on-plate welds at a fixed heat input of 85 J/mm. Forty-eight specimens were welded and measured. Ar/CO₂ 90/10 produced the lowest spatter mass (0.06 g/m) and the most consistent bead width (coefficient of variation 4.2 %), while 75/25 produced 0.21 g/m spatter. Hardness traverses across the heat-affected zone showed a maximum of 198 HV1 for all gas compositions, indicating no detrimental microstructural change. Distortion, measured by three-point deflection, was lowest at 97/3 but accompanied by an irregular bead profile with 14 % of runs showing incomplete fusion. The 90/10 ratio is recommended as the practical optimum for this thickness.

SYN-PUB-06843.title: Statistical Process Control Implementation for a Four-Stage Pre-Treatment Line Feeding an Electrostatic Powder Coating Operation
SYN-PUB-06843.text:
Statistical Process Control Implementation for a Four-Stage Pre-Treatment Line Feeding an Electrostatic Powder Coating Operation (2025, journal, Quality Engineering and Industrial Metrology).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Dragana Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPC; control charts; powder coating; pre-treatment; process capability.
This paper describes the design and pilot implementation of a statistical process control (SPC) scheme for a four-stage pre-treatment line (alkaline degrease, rinse, iron phosphate, rinse) at a small powder coating contractor in Novi Sad. Control variables selected for Shewhart chart monitoring were degreaser bath concentration, bath temperature, phosphate bath conductivity, and rinse-water conductivity at the final rinse stage. A three-month baseline data collection phase (n = 312 shift-level observations) established control limits. Capability indices (Cpk) were computed for each variable against supplier-specified bath chemistry windows; initial Cpk values ranged from 0.71 to 1.18. After operator training and the introduction of twice-daily titration checks replacing the previous once-daily practice, Cpk for degreaser concentration improved to 1.41 and phosphate conductivity to 1.29 over the subsequent three months. Coating adhesion cross-cut failures dropped from 4.1 % to 1.2 % of panels in the same period. The paper discusses the practical barriers to SPC adoption in small coating shops and proposes a minimal-instrument monitoring protocol.

SYN-PUB-06844.title: Pulsed MIG Welding of 1.2 mm Mild-Steel Sheet: Parameter Window Mapping for Spatter-Free Operation at 150–300 A Mean Current
SYN-PUB-06844.text:
Pulsed MIG Welding of 1.2 mm Mild-Steel Sheet: Parameter Window Mapping for Spatter-Free Operation at 150–300 A Mean Current (2026, journal, Welding in Production Engineering).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Tamara Novković (outside co-author); Ladislav Horváth (outside co-author); Milica Jovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: pulsed MIG; parameter optimisation; spatter-free; D-optimal design; response surface.
Pulsed MIG welding offers the potential for spatter-free operation across a wider thickness range than conventional short-arc transfer, but the interaction between peak current, pulse duration, background current, and frequency creates a large parameter space. This study applies a D-optimal design with 41 experimental runs to map the spatter-free operating window for 1.2 mm S235JR sheet using an inverter source with independent pulse parameter control (Varkon PulseMaster 400). Spatter was classified as zero, low (< 0.03 g/m), or unacceptable (≥ 0.03 g/m) based on production-line cleanliness targets. The response surface model identified a feasible zero-spatter region centred on peak current 320 A, pulse duration 2.1 ms, background current 42 A, and frequency 95 Hz for Ar/CO₂ 90/10 shielding gas. Travel speed and contact-tip-to-work distance were fixed at 48 cm/min and 14 mm respectively. Bead-on-plate and T-fillet specimens welded at the optimum point showed tensile shear strengths of 390–408 MPa and no radiographic indications above EN ISO 5817 level B. The mapped window boundaries are presented as a contour chart suitable for direct use in parameter card preparation.

SYN-PUB-06872.title: Competency Outcome Modelling in Mathematics Education: A Mixed-Effects Survival Analysis of Time-to-Mastery
SYN-PUB-06872.text:
Competency Outcome Modelling in Mathematics Education: A Mixed-Effects Survival Analysis of Time-to-Mastery (2019, journal, Statistics and Education Review).
Authors: Jelena Bosnić (outside co-author); Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author); Zuzana Kmeťová (R0595).
Keywords: survival analysis; time-to-mastery; mixed-effects models; competency; mathematics education.
This paper frames competency attainment in undergraduate mathematics as a time-to-event outcome and applies mixed-effects parametric survival models to longitudinal assessment data. Records from 2,240 students completing a multi-module calculus sequence over five academic years were analysed. The outcome was defined as the week in which a student first demonstrated sustained mastery on adaptive quizzes, operationalised as three consecutive passing scores above 80 %. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model with random student and instructor intercepts provided the best fit (log-likelihood ratio test against Weibull, p < 0.001). Time-to-mastery was significantly shortened by higher prior achievement scores and by weekly formative quiz completion, and was lengthened by patterns of concentrated last-minute access. The paper contributes a reusable feature engineering pipeline for Moodle log data and provides worked R code as a supplementary appendix.

SYN-PUB-07001.title: Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks
SYN-PUB-07001.text:
Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks (2010, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Đorđe Petrović (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: conducted emissions; time-domain simulation; single-phase rectifier; LISN; low-voltage network.
A time-domain simulation framework is developed to predict conducted emissions from single-phase uncontrolled rectifiers connected to a simplified residential low-voltage network. The network is represented by a ladder model with frequency-dependent line parameters derived from measurements on a 230 V, 50 Hz test feeder of approximately 120 m length. Rectifier loads ranging from 100 W to 2 kW are modelled as nonlinear voltage-dependent current sources parameterised from laboratory measurements. Simulated disturbance voltages at the mains terminal are compared against LISN-based measurements following CISPR 16-1-1 procedures over the 9 kHz to 30 MHz range. Agreement within 4 dB is achieved across the 150 kHz to 2 MHz sub-band, with larger deviations at higher frequencies attributed to parasitic capacitances not included in the ladder model. The study identifies the 450 kHz to 600 kHz interval as the most sensitive to load power level, with peak quasi-peak levels increasing by up to 11 dB when aggregate load increases from 500 W to 2 kW. The results suggest that existing CISPR limits may be approached under dense residential loading conditions.

SYN-PUB-07002.title: Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks
SYN-PUB-07002.text:
Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks (2011, conference, Proceedings of the 8th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology (EMCEE), Belgrade).
Authors: Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Luca Marchetti (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: cable impedance; frequency-dependent parameters; transmission-line model; SPICE; conducted emission.
The per-unit-length impedance and admittance parameters of four cable types commonly deployed in Serbian urban low-voltage distribution networks are characterised over the 10 kHz to 30 MHz frequency range using a two-port vector network analyser. Cable lengths between 10 m and 80 m are measured in open-circuit and short-circuit configurations, and results are fitted to a standard transmission-line model augmented with a skin-effect correction term. Measured propagation constants are compared to values predicted by IEC 60228-based geometric calculations, revealing deviations of up to 18% in the attenuation constant above 1 MHz for flat-conductor aluminium cables. The characterised parameters are incorporated into a SPICE-compatible model library intended for conducted emission simulations. Sensitivity analysis shows that uncertainty in conductor geometry translates to a maximum 6 dB uncertainty in predicted disturbance voltage at a 30 m cable termination at 10 MHz. The data set covers NYY, NAYY, NYM and NYFGbY cable types in cross-sections from 1.5 mm² to 25 mm².

SYN-PUB-07003.title: Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars
SYN-PUB-07003.text:
Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars (2013, journal, Electrical Power Systems Research).
Authors: Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Bojan Ristić (outside co-author).
Keywords: harmonic distortion; variable-speed drives; power quality; harmonic load flow; EN 50160.
Harmonic voltage measurements are carried out on three low-voltage industrial busbars (400 V, 50 Hz) in a metalworking facility over a seven-day continuous recording period using a class A power quality analyser. Variable-speed drives of 5.5 kW to 90 kW nameplate ratings account for between 40% and 70% of connected load depending on the shift schedule. Total harmonic distortion of voltage (THDV) consistently exceeds the EN 50160 indicative limit of 8% during peak production hours, reaching up to 12.3%. The fifth and seventh voltage harmonics dominate, with average magnitudes of 4.1% and 3.6% of fundamental respectively. Measured current spectra from individual drives are used to construct aggregated injection models following IEC 61000-3-6 guidelines, and harmonic load flow calculations are performed on a network model validated against field measurements. Simulations reproduce measured THDV values within 1.5 percentage points. Mitigation options including passive fifth-harmonic filters and increased feeder conductor cross-section are evaluated, with the former reducing THDV to below 6% under peak load.

SYN-PUB-07004.title: Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation
SYN-PUB-07004.text:
Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation (2014, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Klaus Hoffmeister (outside co-author); Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: LISN; CISPR 32; switch-mode power supply; test reproducibility; mains impedance.
Switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) are tested for conducted emissions according to CISPR 32 using three commercially available line impedance stabilisation networks (LISNs) of nominally identical 50 Ω/50 µH topology but from different manufacturers. Tests are performed on five SMPS samples with rated power between 30 W and 250 W. Measured quasi-peak levels at the same SMPS unit differ by up to 7.2 dB across LISNs in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band, exceeding the 3 dB reproducibility figure often cited in the literature. The observed discrepancies are traced to differences in the LISN high-frequency impedance characteristic, particularly a self-resonance near 1.4 MHz in one unit. An additional test campaign varies the mains source impedance from 0.05 Ω to 0.8 Ω at 50 Hz by inserting series inductors, demonstrating that SMPS peak emission levels shift by up to 5 dB due to changes in rectifier operating point. These findings have implications for compliance margins and for the interpretation of borderline-pass test results.

SYN-PUB-07005.title: Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study
SYN-PUB-07005.text:
Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study (2018, journal, International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: ripple control; supraharmonics; interference; time-domain model; distribution network.
Ripple control systems operating at 316.7 Hz and 750 Hz are widely used by distribution system operators in central Europe for remote load switching. This study investigates the extent to which supraharmonic emissions from switch-mode loads corrupt ripple control telegram reception in a 400 V test feeder modelled from parameters measured in a suburban distribution area near Novi Sad. A full time-domain model is built in MATLAB/Simulink incorporating a ripple control transmitter, feeder impedance, and four classes of switching loads: SMPS, LED drivers, PV micro-inverters, and EV on-board chargers. At 15% feeder loading with mixed loads, signal-to-interference ratio at the receiver input drops below the 20 dB design threshold assumed in EN 61000-5-1 for ripple control. Worst-case degradation of 28 dB is observed when multiple PV micro-inverters synchronise their switching near the ripple control frequency. Temporal correlation between load power cycles and interference bursts is demonstrated. The model is validated against a 4-hour measurement record from the test feeder with 4.5% mean absolute error in receiver input voltage.

SYN-PUB-07006.title: Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis
SYN-PUB-07006.text:
Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis (2019, journal, Metrology and Measurement Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Ida Lerch (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: common mode; differential mode; conducted emissions; measurement uncertainty; LISN.
Four methods for separating common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) conducted emissions from single-phase equipment are compared: a commercial CM/DM separator, a home-built balun-based separator, a two-LISN simultaneous measurement approach, and a post-processing technique applied to standard LISN recordings. Measurements are performed on five reference loads including a 100 W SMPS, a 40 W LED driver array, and a 1.5 kW motor controller in the 150 kHz to 30 MHz band. Separator insertion loss and balance-to-unbalance conversion ratio are characterised by network analyser, revealing that the commercial unit maintains 40 dB mode separation only below 5 MHz. Uncertainty budgets are constructed according to JCGM 100:2008 for each method. Total standard uncertainty ranges from 1.1 dB to 3.8 dB depending on method and frequency, with the two-LISN method providing the lowest uncertainty above 10 MHz. Practical guidance is provided on method selection depending on available equipment and required accuracy.

SYN-PUB-07008.title: Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling
SYN-PUB-07008.text:
Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Jasmina Jokić (R0769); Marta Johansson (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: EV charger; conducted emissions; three-phase feeder; phase coupling; charging infrastructure.
Three-phase low-voltage feeders serving residential parking areas with electric vehicle charging infrastructure are studied using a combination of laboratory measurements and network simulation. On-board chargers of 3.3 kW, 7.4 kW and 11 kW rated power are characterised individually on a LISN test bench, and their emission spectra exported as Norton equivalent sources. A three-phase feeder model of 60 m length is parameterised from field impedance measurements and loaded with up to 12 simultaneous charger connections distributed across phases. Phase-to-phase coupling via the neutral conductor and earth return path is analysed and shown to introduce cross-phase disturbance voltages up to 8 dB below the directly driven phase in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band. Feeder impedance variation due to the connection of reactive compensation capacitors shifts dominant emission peaks by up to 40 kHz. Compliance margins relative to EN 61000-3-11 group emission limits shrink by 6 dB when six or more chargers of the same type operate simultaneously. Results are discussed in the context of planned charging hub deployments.

SYN-PUB-07010.title: Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign
SYN-PUB-07010.text:
Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign (2023, journal, Electric Power Systems Research).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Rossella Fantozzi (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: supraharmonics; long-term monitoring; statistical characterisation; low-voltage feeder; lognormal distribution.
Continuous monitoring of supraharmonic current and voltage emissions at the 400 V low-voltage busbar of a suburban distribution substation near Novi Sad is carried out over twelve consecutive months using a purpose-built acquisition system with 1 MS/s sampling and 90 dB dynamic range. The feeder supplies a mixture of residential and small commercial loads. Emission spectra are computed in 200 Hz bins from 2 kHz to 150 kHz on a ten-minute aggregation basis in accordance with the draft measurement protocol of IEC/TR 61000-2-1-2 Ed.2. Statistical distributions of emission levels are fitted to lognormal models at selected spectral bins; the 95th percentile levels at 16 kHz and 40 kHz are 12.1% and 6.3% of the fundamental current respectively. Clear diurnal and weekly patterns are observed, with evening peaks 4 to 9 dB above overnight minima. Seasonal variation is modest (less than 2 dB) except at 16 kHz, where a 5 dB increase in winter is attributed to increased LED and SMPS loading. The data set is made available as a supplementary repository and is intended for validation of aggregation models.

SYN-PUB-07011.title: Aggregated conducted emission modelling of heterogeneous smart meter populations: a stochastic approach
SYN-PUB-07011.text:
Aggregated conducted emission modelling of heterogeneous smart meter populations: a stochastic approach (2025, journal, IET Generation, Transmission and Distribution).
Authors: Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Pieter van den Berghe (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: smart meter; PLC; conducted emissions; stochastic aggregation; Monte Carlo.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07201.title: Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh
SYN-PUB-07201.text:
Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh (2012, conference, Proceedings of the 4th European Conference on Sensor Networks in Transport and Logistics).
Authors: Miroslav Pejić (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Dragana Tomić (outside co-author); Žarko Ivanović (R0630); Ivan Zec (R0903).
Keywords: refrigerated trailer; spatial temperature mapping; ZigBee mesh; ATP regulations; cold chain.
Spatial temperature heterogeneity inside refrigerated semi-trailers was characterised using a 16-node ZigBee mesh network mounted at three heights and four longitudinal positions. Measurements were conducted over 22 journeys between Novi Sad and Vienna covering a total of 14,300 km under summer and winter conditions. Nodes sampled at 1-minute intervals, producing approximately 1.1 million temperature records. Analysis identified a persistent warm zone near the rear doors, averaging 2.1 °C above the set-point of +4 °C during door-open events lasting more than 90 seconds. A principal component decomposition of the spatial profiles revealed that the first two components explain 81% of within-trailer variance. These findings were used to propose three alternative sensor placement strategies that reduce the probability of undetected warm zones by a factor of 2.4 compared to the single-probe standard practice currently mandated by ATP regulations.

SYN-PUB-07503.title: Estimating bivariate return periods for compound drought–heat events using an elliptical copula approach
SYN-PUB-07503.text:
Estimating bivariate return periods for compound drought–heat events using an elliptical copula approach (2012, journal, International Journal of Climatology and Risk).
Authors: Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Konstantin Balog (outside co-author); Rolf Seeberg (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: compound events; SPI; Student-t copula; bivariate return period; Pannonian Plain.
Compound drought–heat events cause disproportionate impacts on agriculture and human health relative to either hazard individually. Using monthly standardised precipitation index (SPI-3) and maximum temperature anomaly data from 1960 to 2009 for 14 stations across the Pannonian Plain, this study fits Gaussian and Student-t copulas to model the dependence between drought severity and concurrent heat intensity. The Student-t copula with estimated degrees-of-freedom parameter ν̂ = 4.1 fits better than the Gaussian copula at the majority of stations, indicating heavier joint tail behaviour. Bivariate return periods in the Kendall sense and in the survival copula sense are computed and compared. Results indicate that Kendall return periods exceed univariate return periods by a factor of 1.3 to 2.1 for moderate events but converge toward univariate values for very rare events. A regionalisation using hierarchical clustering identifies three coherent zones across the domain.

SYN-PUB-07504.title: Vine copula models for multivariate dependence in a network of Danube basin river gauges
SYN-PUB-07504.text:
Vine copula models for multivariate dependence in a network of Danube basin river gauges (2014, journal, Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Bojan Đurić (outside co-author); Ingrid Håkon (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: vine copulas; R-vine; river discharge; multivariate flood risk; Danube.
Multivariate flood risk assessment requires joint models for discharge at several gauging stations simultaneously. Regular vine copulae (R-vines) decompose a multivariate distribution into a cascade of bivariate pair copulae and offer flexibility that no single parametric family can match. Discharge records from nine stations along the Danube corridor and its main tributaries within Serbia (1970–2010) were standardised to unit Fréchet margins. An R-vine structure was selected using the minimum spanning tree algorithm applied to pairwise empirical Kendall τ values. Each pair copula family was chosen from a candidate set of twelve families by the Akaike information criterion. Out-of-sample predictive performance was evaluated using a conditional probability scoring rule on withheld data from 2000–2010. The fitted vine model assigned non-negligible probability to simultaneous high-discharge events across all nine stations, whereas a meta-Gaussian model underestimated this probability by a factor of approximately three. Simulated 10 000-year realisations from the fitted vine are provided for use in hydraulic engineering design.

SYN-PUB-07505.title: Extreme value copulas
SYN-PUB-07505.text:
Extreme value copulas (2016, book chapter, Handbook of Statistical Methods in Environmental Sciences, Chapter 8, Edited by T. Bartha and K. Szabó, Pécs University Press).
Authors: Miroslav Jevtić (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: extreme value copulas; Pickands representation; max-stable processes; parametric estimation; spatial extremes.
This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of the class of extreme value copulas arising as the limiting dependence structures of componentwise block maxima. The Pickands representation theorem is stated and proved, and its implications for the parametric subfamilies — logistic, asymmetric logistic, Galambos and Hüsler–Reiss — are derived. Estimation methods including maximum likelihood, the method of moments via Kendall's tau, and nonparametric estimators of the Pickands function are compared with respect to bias and variance in a comprehensive simulation study. The chapter includes a treatment of the connection between extreme value copulas and max-stable random fields, which is relevant for spatial modelling of environmental extremes. Three worked examples using Balkan precipitation and temperature data illustrate the methods. The chapter is intended for graduate students and researchers with a background in mathematical statistics.
