SYN-PUB-07506.title: Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of compound flood–wind events at the Serbian Danube reach
SYN-PUB-07506.text:
Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of compound flood–wind events at the Serbian Danube reach (2017, journal, Extremes: Statistical Theory and Applications in Science, Engineering and Economics).
Authors: Nataša Todorović (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Carlo Ventura (outside co-author).
Keywords: peaks-over-threshold; generalised Pareto distribution; bivariate extremes; threshold selection; Galambos copula.
The peaks-over-threshold (POT) method requires selection of a threshold above which observations are modelled by the generalised Pareto distribution. In the bivariate context, both variables must exceed respective thresholds simultaneously or separately depending on the risk definition. This paper evaluates five threshold selection diagnostics — mean residual life plots, parameter stability plots, and three automated criteria based on goodness-of-fit — applied to concurrent records of river discharge and mean daily wind speed at five stations on the Serbian Danube reach (1980–2015). The copula of the bivariate exceedances is modelled with a censored-likelihood approach that accounts for observations exceeding only one threshold. Results show that the Galambos copula fits the bivariate extremes well (upper tail dependence coefficient 0.22–0.35) and that threshold choice materially affects estimated joint return levels: a 10 percent increase in threshold reduces the estimated 200-year joint quantile by up to 18 percent. Guidance for practitioners is provided.

SYN-PUB-07507.title: Comparing parametric and nonparametric multivariate quantile contour estimation under copula misspecification
SYN-PUB-07507.text:
Comparing parametric and nonparametric multivariate quantile contour estimation under copula misspecification (2021, journal, Statistical Papers).
Authors: Miroslav Jevtić (outside co-author); Ondřej Hlávka (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: multivariate quantile contours; return period analysis; depth functions; copula misspecification; nonparametric estimation.
Multivariate quantile contours — level sets of a joint distribution at a given probability level — are central to multivariate return period analysis but sensitive to model misspecification. This simulation study compares five estimators: the Kendall quantile contour under three parametric copula families (Gaussian, Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard), the geometric quantile estimator of Chaudhuri and the depth-based Tukey median contour estimated by the Donoho–Gasko algorithm. Data are generated from six dependence structures at sample sizes n = 100, 300, 500, 1000, with standard Gumbel margins. Performance is measured by the integrated squared Hausdorff distance between estimated and true contours. Parametric estimators outperform nonparametric competitors when the model is correctly specified, but nonparametric depth-based contours exhibit substantially lower worst-case error across misspecified scenarios. A data-driven selection rule combining a copula goodness-of-fit test with a nonparametric fallback is proposed and evaluated on a subset of Serbian environmental monitoring data.

SYN-PUB-07508.title: Modelling the joint distribution of extreme wildfire weather indices in Serbia using time-varying copulas
SYN-PUB-07508.text:
Modelling the joint distribution of extreme wildfire weather indices in Serbia using time-varying copulas (2022, journal, International Journal of Wildland Fire).
Authors: Milena Radović (outside co-author); Sanja Konjević (outside co-author); Hanna Lehtonen (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: wildfire weather indices; non-stationary copulas; time-varying dependence; GEV; climate change.
Climate change is shifting the distributional properties of wildfire weather indices, so static copula models fitted over long historical periods may be inadequate for current risk assessments. Daily records of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) components — Fine Fuel Moisture Code and Drought Code — from 18 stations in Serbia for 1961–2020 were used to investigate non-stationarity in both marginal distributions and dependence structure. Marginal parameters of the fitted GEV distributions were allowed to vary as smooth functions of a global temperature covariate using penalised spline regression. The copula dependence parameter was then estimated conditional on the same covariate using a local-likelihood approach with a Gaussian kernel. Estimated Kendall τ increased from approximately 0.31 in the 1960s to 0.48 in the 2010s, indicating strengthening co-occurrence of the two fire risk indicators. This trend implies that joint exceedance probabilities have roughly doubled over the observational record.

SYN-PUB-07509.title: Sensitivity of infrastructure failure probability to tail dependence assumptions: a case study for bridge foundations on the Sava River
SYN-PUB-07509.text:
Sensitivity of infrastructure failure probability to tail dependence assumptions: a case study for bridge foundations on the Sava River (2023, journal, Reliability Engineering and System Safety).
Authors: Predrag Nikolić (outside co-author); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: structural reliability; tail dependence sensitivity; bridge foundations; Sava River; limit-state function.
The structural reliability of bridge foundations in alluvial reaches depends jointly on peak discharge, scour depth and ice loading, three variables whose dependence in the extreme tails is poorly constrained by available data. This paper quantifies the sensitivity of estimated annual failure probability to the choice of tail dependence structure. A structural limit-state function for a simplified foundation model is combined with a joint hazard model in which the copula family is varied across six candidates spanning tail independence to strong upper tail dependence. The difference between the failure probability under the independence copula and under the upper-tail-dependent Gumbel–Hougaard copula with τ = 0.4 is approximately one order of magnitude at annual exceedance probability 10⁻⁴, a difference that is practically significant for design. A robust upper bound is obtained by taking the maximum over a class of copulas with matching Kendall τ.

SYN-PUB-07510.title: Bayesian estimation of C-vine copula parameters for high-dimensional environmental hazard vectors
SYN-PUB-07510.text:
Bayesian estimation of C-vine copula parameters for high-dimensional environmental hazard vectors (2024, preprint, arXiv preprint (submitted to Computational Statistics and Data Analysis)).
Authors: Vesna Stanković (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Pieter Van den Berg (outside co-author).
Keywords: C-vine copula; Bayesian inference; reversible-jump MCMC; high-dimensional dependence; Vojvodina.
C-vine copulas reduce the dimensionality problem in multivariate dependence modelling by expressing the joint density as a product of bivariate pair copulas arranged in a tree structure. When the dimension is moderate to high (here d = 8), maximum likelihood estimation of the full parameter vector becomes computationally burdensome and confidence intervals are poorly calibrated. This preprint proposes a blocked Gibbs sampler for posterior inference over C-vine structures and bivariate copula family indicators jointly, using a reversible-jump extension. Experiments on simulated data with n = 500 show that credible intervals for tail dependence coefficients have nominal coverage 3 to 8 percentage points closer to 95 percent than profile likelihood intervals. The method is applied to an eight-dimensional vector of hydrometeorological hazard indicators — discharge, precipitation intensity, wind speed, temperature anomaly, and four soil moisture metrics — observed simultaneously at a single representative site in the Bačka subregion of Vojvodina.

SYN-PUB-07511.title: A regional frequency analysis framework for multivariate compound events using spatial pooling and copula aggregation
SYN-PUB-07511.text:
A regional frequency analysis framework for multivariate compound events using spatial pooling and copula aggregation (2025, journal, Water Resources Research).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Éva Molnár (outside co-author); Radu Cojocaru (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: regional frequency analysis; compound events; Wasserstein barycenter; Danube basin; L-moments.
Regional frequency analysis (RFA) extends the information base for rare event estimation by pooling data from hydrologically homogeneous stations. Classical RFA applies to univariate distributions; this paper extends the L-moments approach to multivariate compound events by fitting station-specific copulas and aggregating them into a regional dependence structure using a weighted Wasserstein barycenter. Sixty-three stations in the middle Danube basin (Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia) contribute 40 to 95 years of simultaneous discharge and precipitation records. Homogeneity is assessed using a multivariate extension of the Hosking–Wallis H statistic. The regional copula reduces estimation uncertainty for joint return levels at ungauged locations compared to at-site estimation; the reduction in root-mean-square error for the 100-year bivariate quantile ranges from 23 to 41 percent depending on the region. The method is implemented in an open-source R package deposited at the University of Novi Sad data repository.

SYN-PUB-07512.title: Quantile regression forests for marginal standardisation in nonparametric multivariate extreme value analysis
SYN-PUB-07512.text:
Quantile regression forests for marginal standardisation in nonparametric multivariate extreme value analysis (2026, journal, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society — Series C (Applied Statistics)).
Authors: Sanja Konjević (outside co-author); Ondřej Hlávka (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: quantile regression forests; marginal standardisation; max-stable processes; discharge modelling; machine learning in extremes.
Transforming raw observations to uniform or Fréchet margins is a necessary preprocessing step in most copula-based extreme value analyses, and the quality of this transformation influences downstream inference. Standard empirical probability integral transforms perform poorly in sparse tails. This paper proposes using quantile regression forests to estimate marginal conditional distribution functions that adapt to covariate information — elevation, land use, catchment area — thereby improving tail standardisation at environmental monitoring stations. The approach is evaluated in a leave-one-out cross-validation on 44 discharge stations in Serbia and Croatia. After forest-based standardisation, the residual dependence structure is more stable across stations and seasons than after empirical-transform standardisation: the interquartile range of estimated pairwise Kendall τ values shrinks by 19 percent. The standardised residuals are then used as input to a Brown–Resnick max-stable model fitted by pairwise composite likelihood, which yields a 12 percent reduction in the composite likelihood information criterion relative to the baseline approach.

SYN-PUB-07520.title: Modal Parameter Extraction from Welded Steel Portal Frames Under Ambient Excitation
SYN-PUB-07520.text:
Modal Parameter Extraction from Welded Steel Portal Frames Under Ambient Excitation (2012, journal, Journal of Mechanical Engineering Research and Applications).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: operational modal analysis; SSI; weld defect; ambient vibration; portal frame.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07522.title: Comparison of Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Stochastic Subspace Identification for Damage Localization in Multi-Bay Steel Frames
SYN-PUB-07522.text:
Comparison of Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Stochastic Subspace Identification for Damage Localization in Multi-Bay Steel Frames (2015, journal, Journal of Vibration Diagnostics and Structural Integrity).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Attila Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: FDD; SSI-COV; damage index; multi-bay frame; damage localization.
Two widely used OMA algorithms—frequency-domain decomposition (FDD) and stochastic subspace identification (SSI-COV)—are compared for their ability to localize damage in a three-bay, two-storey welded steel frame model. Damage was simulated by progressively cutting a weld in the lower right column-beam connection in three stages, reducing net throat area by 20%, 40%, and 60%. Ambient excitation was provided by pedestrian-like loading applied at the floor levels. Both algorithms identified natural frequencies within 0.15 Hz of each other for the first six modes. Damage localization was assessed via the modal strain energy damage index (MSEDI). SSI-COV achieved correct panel identification at 20% damage in 7 of 10 repeated trials, while FDD achieved correct localization in only 4 of 10 at the same damage level. At 40% and 60% damage, both methods localized correctly in all trials. The study recommends SSI-COV for early-stage damage detection when signal-to-noise conditions are moderate.

SYN-PUB-07523.title: Temperature Effects on Modal Parameters of Welded Steel Frame Structures: A Seasonal Monitoring Study
SYN-PUB-07523.text:
Temperature Effects on Modal Parameters of Welded Steel Frame Structures: A Seasonal Monitoring Study (2017, journal, Structural Monitoring and Maintenance).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Branislav Nikolić (outside co-author); Theodora Ionescu (outside co-author); Svetlana Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: temperature compensation; continuous monitoring; industrial rack structure; environmental variability; OMA.
Environmental temperature variation is a known source of false alarms in vibration-based structural health monitoring systems. This paper reports a 14-month continuous monitoring campaign on a full-scale welded steel storage rack structure at an industrial facility in Zrenjanin, during which ambient temperature ranged from −14 °C to +38 °C. Twelve accelerometers and four temperature sensors were installed. OMA was performed on 30-minute data windows using SSI-COV. The first natural frequency varied by up to 4.3% over the monitoring period, primarily correlated with temperature (Pearson r = −0.81). A linear regression model was fitted to remove temperature effects from frequency trends; residuals were examined for anomalies. No structural damage occurred during the campaign, confirming the temperature model captured the dominant environmental influence. The study provides a temperature-compensation baseline that can support future damage detection in similar industrial steel structures in the Pannonian climate zone.

SYN-PUB-07524.title: Laser Vibrometry Measurements of Weld-Zone Mode Shapes in Thin-Walled Steel Box Sections
SYN-PUB-07524.text:
Laser Vibrometry Measurements of Weld-Zone Mode Shapes in Thin-Walled Steel Box Sections (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 14th European Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation, Prague).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Radovan Stupar (outside co-author).
Keywords: laser Doppler vibrometry; thin-walled box section; lack of fusion; operational deflection shape; wavelet energy.
Conventional accelerometer grids cannot resolve high-spatial-resolution mode shapes in thin-walled welded box sections without adding significant mass. This paper uses a scanning laser Doppler vibrometer (SLDV) to measure operational deflection shapes at 320 scan points on three box-section specimens (wall thickness 4 mm, 6 mm, and 8 mm) under harmonic excitation at frequencies corresponding to the first five bending and torsional modes. Specimens were fabricated with identical nominal welds; one specimen per thickness group contained an artificial internal lack-of-fusion defect of 12 mm length introduced by inserting a 0.3 mm Teflon insert during fabrication. The SLDV measurements revealed localized amplitude anomalies of 8–23% at the defect location for the 4 mm and 6 mm specimens at modes 3 and 4, while the 8 mm specimen showed no detectable anomaly. Mass loading from a hypothetical 4-accelerometer grid would have shifted frequencies by up to 2.1%, justifying the non-contact approach. Fractional wavelet energy maps derived from the velocity fields improved defect contrast over raw mode shape images.

SYN-PUB-07525.title: Vibration-Based Structural Health Monitoring of Steel Structures: Methods and Practical Considerations
SYN-PUB-07525.text:
Vibration-Based Structural Health Monitoring of Steel Structures: Methods and Practical Considerations (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Structural Integrity Assessment for Industrial Facilities, TechPress Bratislava).
Authors: Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author); Attila Varga (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Petra Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: SHM review; steel structures; sensor placement; damage index; long-term monitoring.
This book chapter reviews the application of vibration-based SHM to steel civil and industrial structures, with emphasis on welded connections. The chapter covers the theoretical basis of modal analysis, sensor placement strategies, algorithm selection criteria, and the practical challenges of long-term monitoring including power supply, data transmission, and environmental compensation. Case studies drawn from laboratory and field experience in the Western Balkans region illustrate typical damage scenarios (weld cracking, corrosion-induced stiffness loss, fatigue-related loosening) and the sensitivity of common damage indices to each. Particular attention is given to structures with irregular geometry or asymmetric boundary conditions, where standard damage localization indices can give misleading results. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, including the scarcity of labeled field damage datasets and the difficulty of transferring laboratory-calibrated models to field conditions.

SYN-PUB-07526.title: Detection of Fatigue Crack Initiation in Fillet-Welded T-Joints Using Damping Ratio Tracking
SYN-PUB-07526.text:
Detection of Fatigue Crack Initiation in Fillet-Welded T-Joints Using Damping Ratio Tracking (2020, journal, International Journal of Fatigue and Structural Diagnostics).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Branislav Nikolić (outside co-author); Svetlana Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: damping ratio; fatigue crack; T-joint; fillet weld; half-power bandwidth.
Changes in damping ratio are hypothesized to be more sensitive to early-stage crack initiation than frequency shifts, but damping estimation is highly variable. This paper investigates the feasibility of tracking damping ratios as a damage indicator in fillet-welded T-joint specimens subjected to cyclic three-point bending fatigue loading. Eight specimens of S275 steel were cycled at 60% and 75% of their static failure load. OMA data were collected at intervals of 5,000 load cycles. Damping ratios for the first bending mode, estimated by the half-power bandwidth method and by SSI-COV, were compared. SSI-COV estimates showed standard deviations approximately 40% lower than half-power bandwidth estimates. Damping ratios increased detectably (>2σ above baseline) at approximately 35–40% of total fatigue life at 75% load, preceding a measurable frequency drop by roughly 8,000 cycles. At 60% load, no consistent damping increase was detected prior to visible crack formation. Results suggest that damping tracking may provide early warning in moderate-to-high stress fatigue scenarios.

SYN-PUB-07527.title: Baseline-Free Damage Detection in Welded Steel Trusses Using Transmissibility Functions
SYN-PUB-07527.text:
Baseline-Free Damage Detection in Welded Steel Trusses Using Transmissibility Functions (2022, journal, Mechanical Systems and Structural Diagnostics).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Radovan Stupar (outside co-author); Marko Fehér (outside co-author).
Keywords: transmissibility function; baseline-free; Pratt truss; damage localization; transmissibility damage index.
Transmissibility-based methods do not require a pristine baseline measurement, making them attractive for structures where an undamaged reference state was never recorded. This paper evaluates a transmissibility-function damage indicator on three laboratory-scale welded Pratt-type steel truss specimens. Each truss had 11 joints; damage was introduced at single joints by partially cutting the weld of one diagonal member to depths of 1, 2, and 3 mm. Transmissibility functions were computed between all sensor-pair combinations (15 pairs from 6 accelerometers) under broadband random excitation. A transmissibility damage index (TDI) based on the Euclidean norm of transmissibility differences between two arbitrary operating conditions was computed. Correct damage localization was achieved in 18 of 21 test cases (86%) across all damage levels and joint positions. Failed cases were concentrated at joints near the support conditions. Comparison with the modal strain energy method showed similar localization accuracy but lower computational demand for TDI. The approach requires no FE model and no undamaged reference.

SYN-PUB-07528.title: Low-Cost Wireless Sensor Network for Continuous Vibration Monitoring of a Welded Steel Overhead Crane Girder
SYN-PUB-07528.text:
Low-Cost Wireless Sensor Network for Continuous Vibration Monitoring of a Welded Steel Overhead Crane Girder (2023, journal, Sensors and Structural Monitoring Letters).
Authors: Nemanja Tešić (outside co-author); Branislav Nikolić (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Maja Ristić (R0939); Petra Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: wireless sensor network; MEMS accelerometer; crane girder; weld fatigue crack; automated OMA.
Overhead crane girders in production halls undergo repetitive dynamic loading from hoisting operations and are susceptible to weld fatigue at rail attachment points. This paper describes the design, installation, and 18-month operation of a low-cost wireless accelerometer network (8 nodes, MEMS sensors, 1 kHz sampling) installed on a 22-metre span welded box-girder crane at a metalworking company in Zrenjanin. Data were transmitted to a local edge device and processed using automated SSI-COV at each hoisting event. Over 3,400 events were recorded. The first bending frequency showed a gradual decrease of 0.9% over the monitoring period; post-campaign visual inspection revealed a 28 mm weld fatigue crack at one rail attachment. Frequency changes tracked the estimated crack length progression using a fracture mechanics model calibrated to the geometry. System power consumption averaged 220 mW per node. The study demonstrates that MEMS-based wireless networks can detect slow-growing weld fatigue cracks in crane girders under purely operational loading.

SYN-PUB-07529.title: Principal Component Analysis of Long-Term Modal Data for Anomaly Detection in an Industrial Steel Frame: Influence of Operational Load Patterns
SYN-PUB-07529.text:
Principal Component Analysis of Long-Term Modal Data for Anomaly Detection in an Industrial Steel Frame: Influence of Operational Load Patterns (2024, journal, Journal of Structural Health Monitoring and Condition Assessment).
Authors: Radovan Stupar (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Attila Varga (outside co-author); Nemanja Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: PCA; statistical process control; long-term monitoring; mezzanine frame; anomaly detection.
Statistical process control methods applied to long-term SHM data must account not only for environmental variability but also for systematic changes in operational loads such as storage fill levels or production-line traffic. This paper applies principal component analysis (PCA) to a 22-month dataset of modal parameters (12 frequency and 8 damping estimates per measurement epoch) collected from a welded steel mezzanine frame in a logistics warehouse in the Novi Sad industrial zone. Ambient excitation was provided by forklift traffic. Temperature, humidity, and floor load (estimated from a weigh-bridge log) were recorded simultaneously. A PCA model trained on the first 6 months of data reduced the feature vector to 3 principal components explaining 87% of variance. Control charts on the residuals flagged three anomalous periods; two corresponded to planned maintenance (bolt retightening), and one corresponded to a previously unreported localized weld crack found during the subsequent annual inspection. False alarm rate over the remaining 16 months was 3.1%, comparable to the 5% control limit set.

SYN-PUB-07530.title: Modal Testing Protocol for Welded Steel Frame Structures in Active Industrial Environments: Repeatability and Interference Assessment
SYN-PUB-07530.text:
Modal Testing Protocol for Welded Steel Frame Structures in Active Industrial Environments: Repeatability and Interference Assessment (2026, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Structural Health Monitoring and Integrity Assessment, Ljubljana).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Siniša Petrov (outside co-author); Theodora Ionescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: testing protocol; repeatability; effective independence; industrial environment; standardization.
Performing modal tests in operating industrial environments introduces variability from background machinery noise, temperature gradients, and measurement interruptions. This paper proposes and evaluates a standardized testing protocol designed to maximize repeatability under such conditions. The protocol specifies sensor placement rules based on effective independence (EFI) criteria, a minimum recording duration formula as a function of the target frequency resolution and lowest expected natural frequency, and a quality-control step using automated pole stabilization diagrams with human-review triggers. The protocol was validated on five distinct welded steel frame types at three industrial sites in Vojvodina over a period of two years, with two operators per site performing independent tests within 48 hours of each other. Inter-operator repeatability of estimated natural frequencies was within 0.4% for all structures and all modes up to the sixth. Damping ratio repeatability was within 12% of the mean value for 89% of identified modes. The protocol is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible without specialized training beyond standard OMA software familiarity.

SYN-PUB-07783.title: Partition-Aware Inverted Index Construction for Heterogeneous Document Streams
SYN-PUB-07783.text:
Partition-Aware Inverted Index Construction for Heterogeneous Document Streams (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information Retrieval (CECIR)).
Authors: Miroslav Bjelogrlić (outside co-author); Darko Vukelić (outside co-author); Radovan Radulović (R0694); Snežana Todorović (R0741).
Keywords: inverted index; stream indexing; index partitioning; multilingual.
This paper addresses the challenge of building inverted indexes over document streams that vary widely in language, length, and encoding. We propose a partition-aware construction algorithm that assigns incoming documents to index shards based on a lightweight language-and-length feature hash, reducing cross-shard query fan-out by approximately 34% compared to round-robin partitioning on a corpus of 12 million news articles drawn from four Balkan-language feeds. Index build time on a six-node cluster decreased by 18% while median query latency fell from 47 ms to 31 ms at the 50th percentile. The approach requires no prior knowledge of the full corpus distribution and adapts incrementally as stream statistics shift. Experiments use Apache Lucene as the underlying segment engine, with a custom coordinator layer implemented in Java. Recall at rank 10 remains within 0.4% of a monolithic baseline.

SYN-PUB-07802.title: Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity
SYN-PUB-07802.text:
Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity (2021, journal, Microelectronics Journal).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696).
Keywords: wake-up receiver; asynchronous MAC; envelope detector; 868 MHz; event-driven sensing.
Polling-based duty cycling requires a node to activate its main radio at fixed intervals regardless of whether data are ready, wasting energy between physiological events. A wake-up receiver (WuRx) circuit that remains continuously active at very low power can replace this periodic wakeup. This paper presents a WuRx designed in 130 nm CMOS consuming 4.2 µW from a 1.0 V supply. The circuit uses an envelope detector followed by a three-stage comparator with hysteresis to decode an amplitude-shift-keyed wake-up beacon at 868 MHz. Measured sensitivity was −62 dBm at a target false-alarm rate of one per hour. Selectivity to adjacent channels was verified in a shielded box with an interferer 3 MHz offset at levels up to −20 dBm. Die area was 0.19 mm². When integrated into a complete sensor node alongside a CC1310 main radio, the WuRx reduced mean idle-state current from 18.4 µA (timer-based duty cycle at 1% duty) to 6.7 µA under a traffic model representative of a cardiac event monitor with bursts averaging twice per hour.

SYN-PUB-07846.title: Estimating Soil Surface Temperature at 10 m Resolution Over Agricultural Fields by Fusing Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices with Landsat-9 Thermal Band
SYN-PUB-07846.text:
Estimating Soil Surface Temperature at 10 m Resolution Over Agricultural Fields by Fusing Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices with Landsat-9 Thermal Band (2024, journal, IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations).
Authors: Nataša Brkić (outside co-author); Petra Varga (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Дарко Тошић (R0700).
Keywords: Landsat-9; Sentinel-2; data fusion; soil surface temperature; thermal sharpening.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08093.title: Downscaling Monthly Air Temperature Over the Vojvodina Plain Using MODIS Land Surface Temperature and Regression-Kriging
SYN-PUB-08093.text:
Downscaling Monthly Air Temperature Over the Vojvodina Plain Using MODIS Land Surface Temperature and Regression-Kriging (2011, journal, Journal of Applied Geoinformatics and Earth Observation).
Authors: Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Zsolt Horváth (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: MODIS LST; regression-kriging; air temperature; Vojvodina; downscaling.
Monthly mean air temperature fields at 1 km resolution were produced for the Vojvodina plain by combining MODIS Terra LST composites (MOD11A2, 2003–2008) with ground observations from 34 meteorological stations operated by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. A regression-kriging framework was adopted in which daytime and night-time LST, elevation, and distance to water bodies served as covariates in an ordinary least-squares pre-regression step, with residuals subsequently interpolated by ordinary kriging. Leave-one-out cross-validation yielded a mean absolute error of 0.62 °C averaged across all months, improving on straight inverse-distance weighting by 31 %. Spatial patterns of cold air pooling in topographic depressions and urban heat islands around Novi Sad and Subotica were captured more faithfully than in the national 10 km gridded product. Seasonal decomposition showed the strongest LST-to-air-temperature coupling in July and weakest in December, a result attributed to soil moisture and snow cover masking effects.

SYN-PUB-08094.title: Mapping Growing Degree Days at Sub-Kilometre Scale Across the Middle Danube Basin
SYN-PUB-08094.text:
Mapping Growing Degree Days at Sub-Kilometre Scale Across the Middle Danube Basin (2013, journal, International Journal of Biometeorology and Spatial Sciences).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Mirela Ostojić (outside co-author); Anca Păun (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: growing degree days; ERA-Interim; geographically weighted regression; Danube basin; agroclimatic indices.
Growing degree days (GDD, base 10 °C) were computed at 500 m resolution for the 2005–2010 growing seasons across a 180 000 km² domain spanning Hungary, Serbia, Croatia and Romania. Temperature surfaces were produced by spatially downscaling ERA-Interim reanalysis fields using a statistical transfer function fitted to surface station data and MODIS LST anomalies. The transfer function was a geographically weighted regression model, separately calibrated for spring and summer sub-periods to account for differing advection regimes. Validation against 51 held-out stations showed RMSE in cumulative GDD below 120 GDD-days for the April–September period. The resulting maps revealed consistent positive anomalies along the Fruška Gora slopes relative to flat Vojvodina, with implications for early-harvest crop variety selection. The dataset was made available as a 12-band GeoTIFF archive through a regional agrometeorological data portal.

SYN-PUB-08095.title: Estimating Reference Evapotranspiration in Data-Sparse Regions by Fusing SEVIRI and MODIS Thermal Imagery
SYN-PUB-08095.text:
Estimating Reference Evapotranspiration in Data-Sparse Regions by Fusing SEVIRI and MODIS Thermal Imagery (2015, journal, Agricultural and Forest Meteorology Letters).
Authors: Jovana Tešanović (outside co-author); Fabrizio Moretti (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: reference evapotranspiration; MSG SEVIRI; Penman-Monteith; data fusion; Serbia.
Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀, Penman–Monteith FAO-56) requires net radiation and humidity inputs that are often measured only at sparse synoptic stations. This study fused instantaneous surface radiation estimates from the MSG/SEVIRI satellite (3 km, 15-minute) with daytime MODIS LST (1 km, daily) to reconstruct diurnal temperature and radiation cycles at 1 km resolution over Serbia for 2008–2011. A temporal interpolation scheme based on sinusoidal fitting between two daily MODIS overpasses was applied to fill the radiometric gap left by SEVIRI's coarser spatial detail. Daily ET₀ estimated from the downscaled inputs agreed with FAO Penman–Monteith computed from station data to within 0.38 mm day⁻¹ (RMSE, n = 28 stations). Spatial maps revealed a systematic ET₀ gradient from the Pannonian lowland to the Šar Mountains exceeding 1.1 mm day⁻¹ in July, consistent with independent eddy covariance records at two sites.

SYN-PUB-08096.title: Kriging Interpolation Variants for Daily Precipitation in Complex Terrain: A Comparative Assessment Over the Dinaric Alps Fringe
SYN-PUB-08096.text:
Kriging Interpolation Variants for Daily Precipitation in Complex Terrain: A Comparative Assessment Over the Dinaric Alps Fringe (2015, conference, Proceedings of the 4th Balkan Conference on Geomatics and Geoinformatics).
Authors: Dragan Vujović (outside co-author); Marija Lazić (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: kriging; daily precipitation; Dinaric Alps; variogram; geostatistics.
Four kriging variants — ordinary kriging (OK), kriging with external drift (KED), co-kriging with elevation, and indicator kriging of wet-day occurrence — were evaluated for daily precipitation interpolation using a 62-station network across a 55 000 km² domain covering the Dinaric fringe of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro. The 2009–2013 wet-season record was used, with 15 % of stations withheld for validation in each of 200 bootstrap iterations. KED using terrain-exposed elevation as the external drift variable outperformed OK in 73 % of daily cases, with mean RMSE reductions of 12 % in autumn and 8 % in spring. Indicator kriging proved most accurate for binary wet-day mapping, reducing false wet-cell fractions by 18 percentage points compared with deterministic methods. Variogram range parameters varied seasonally between 28 km in convective summer and 110 km in frontal winter regimes.

SYN-PUB-08097.title: Spatiotemporal Drought Monitoring Over the Pannonian Basin Using the SPEI at Multiple Time Scales Derived from Downscaled Gridded Climate Data
SYN-PUB-08097.text:
Spatiotemporal Drought Monitoring Over the Pannonian Basin Using the SPEI at Multiple Time Scales Derived from Downscaled Gridded Climate Data (2018, journal, International Journal of Climatology and Remote Sensing Applications).
Authors: Tamás Bodnár (outside co-author); Jovana Tešanović (outside co-author); Loredana Constantin (outside co-author); Milena Nedić (R1023); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: SPEI; drought monitoring; Pannonian Basin; NDVI; trend analysis.
The Standardised Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month accumulation periods was computed at 1 km resolution over the Pannonian Basin for 1991–2015 using monthly precipitation and ET₀ grids produced by the author's regression-kriging pipeline. The resulting 25-year, 288-layer dataset allowed continuous spatial tracking of drought onset, intensity and recovery without relying on station interpolation alone. Trend analysis using the Mann–Kendall test identified statistically significant (p < 0.05) drying trends in 34 % of the study area at the 12-month SPEI, concentrated in the eastern Hungarian and western Romanian sectors. Correlation of 3-month SPEI with satellite NDVI composites (MODIS MOD13Q1) reached 0.71 for rainfed maize areas, confirming utility for near-real-time agricultural drought early warning. Comparison with the European Drought Observatory CCI SM product showed spatial agreement of 78 % for severe drought flags.

SYN-PUB-08098.title: Comparison of Machine Learning Regressors and Geostatistical Models for 1 km Daily Minimum Temperature Mapping Over Serbia
SYN-PUB-08098.text:
Comparison of Machine Learning Regressors and Geostatistical Models for 1 km Daily Minimum Temperature Mapping Over Serbia (2020, journal, Computers and Geosciences – Environmental Applications).
Authors: Marija Lazić (outside co-author); Bojan Đorđević (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: random forest; regression-kriging; minimum temperature; machine learning; ensemble.
Random forest (RF), gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost), and artificial neural networks were compared against regression-kriging and co-kriging for the task of producing daily minimum temperature grids at 1 km over Serbia. Inputs common to all methods included MODIS LST, DEM-derived topographic variables, distance to major water bodies, and calendar-day encoding. Training used station data from 67 automatic weather stations for 2013–2017; testing was performed on 2018–2019 withheld data. Random forest achieved the lowest test RMSE (0.88 °C) compared with regression-kriging (0.97 °C), XGBoost (0.91 °C), and co-kriging (1.03 °C). However, regression-kriging produced better-calibrated prediction intervals and smoother spatial fields in data-sparse mountain regions. An ensemble blending RF predictions with kriging residuals achieved RMSE of 0.81 °C while retaining spatial coherence. Computational cost for the ensemble was approximately 4× that of standalone RF.

SYN-PUB-08099.title: Reconstructing Pre-Satellite Agroclimatic Grids for the Carpathian–Pannonian Region Using Historical Station Records and Spatial Reanalysis
SYN-PUB-08099.text:
Reconstructing Pre-Satellite Agroclimatic Grids for the Carpathian–Pannonian Region Using Historical Station Records and Spatial Reanalysis (2021, journal, Climate Dynamics – Regional Studies).
Authors: Tamás Bodnár (outside co-author); Anca Păun (outside co-author); Srđan Krstić (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: historical climate reconstruction; ERA-20C; growing season; Carpathian-Pannonian; bias correction.
High-resolution gridded records of growing season length, heat accumulation, and aridity index were reconstructed for the 1961–2000 period over the Carpathian–Pannonian region by downscaling the ERA-20C centennial reanalysis to 2 km using transfer functions calibrated on the 2001–2015 overlap period with MODIS LST data. Station data from 148 surface synoptic stations in five countries were used to bias-correct the ERA-20C baseline. Trend testing showed a 14-day advance in start-of-growing-season dates between 1961 and 2000 in the lowland zone, consistent with independent phenological records for winter wheat. The reconstruction fills a critical gap for long-term impact assessments that require spatial data prior to the MODIS era. Uncertainty was quantified by propagating station observation errors and ERA-20C ensemble spread through the downscaling chain, yielding 90 % confidence intervals of ±3 days for growing season start.

SYN-PUB-08100.title: Agroclimatic Zoning of Soybean Cultivation Potential in the Western Balkans Under Present and Near-Term (2030–2040) Climate Projections
SYN-PUB-08100.text:
Agroclimatic Zoning of Soybean Cultivation Potential in the Western Balkans Under Present and Near-Term (2030–2040) Climate Projections (2022, journal, Field Crops Research and Spatial Modelling).
Authors: Snežana Branković (outside co-author); Claudiu Nistor (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: soybean; agroclimatic zoning; EURO-CORDEX; Western Balkans; RCP scenarios.
Soybean cultivation in the Western Balkans is expanding but spatially under-characterised. This study applied a set of agroclimatic indices — growing season length, sum of active temperatures above 10 °C, number of dry spells exceeding 10 days in July–August, and mean diurnal temperature range during pod fill — computed from high-resolution (1 km) historical grids and from dynamically downscaled EURO-CORDEX RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 projections for 2030–2040. Under RCP4.5, the area classified as highly suitable for soybean is projected to increase by 11 % relative to the 1991–2020 baseline, driven primarily by warming in the mountainous interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro. Under RCP8.5, suitability decreases in the Vojvodina core zone due to increased drought stress frequency. Results were delivered as Web Map Service layers and as 1 km GeoTIFF products.

SYN-PUB-08101.title: A Benchmark Dataset for Sub-Kilometre Agroclimatic Index Mapping in the Pannonian Zone
SYN-PUB-08101.text:
A Benchmark Dataset for Sub-Kilometre Agroclimatic Index Mapping in the Pannonian Zone (2023, journal, Earth System Science Data – Regional Contributions).
Authors: Jovana Tešanović (outside co-author); Goran Filipović (outside co-author); Mirela Ostojić (outside co-author); Darko Mirković (R0877); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Sara Šijački (R0828).
Keywords: benchmark dataset; agroclimatic indices; Pannonian zone; GDD; Huglin index.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08102.title: Sensitivity of Spatial Downscaling Performance to Variogram Estimation Sample Size in Sparse Station Networks
SYN-PUB-08102.text:
Sensitivity of Spatial Downscaling Performance to Variogram Estimation Sample Size in Sparse Station Networks (2026, journal, Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment).
Authors: Bojan Đorđević (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: variogram estimation; REML; kriging; sparse networks; Monte Carlo simulation.
Variogram estimation is a fundamental step in geostatistical downscaling, but its reliability degrades when fewer than 30–40 stations are available — a common situation in developing countries. Using a sub-sampling simulation study on the 72-station Serbian agrometeorological network, this work examined how kriging interpolation error grows as the estimation sample is reduced from 72 to 8 stations for monthly mean temperature, total precipitation, and reference ET₀. Variograms were estimated by the method-of-moments and by restricted maximum likelihood (REML). REML maintained acceptable nugget-to-sill ratios down to 15 stations where the method-of-moments failed, yielding 18 % lower RMSE on average. Below 12 stations, both estimators produced unreliable range parameters. The study provides practical guidance for selecting estimation method and minimum station density thresholds for each variable type, expressed as a function of spatial autocorrelation range.

SYN-PUB-08103.title: Detecting inter-annual change in softwood floodplain forest extent using dense Sentinel-2 time-series and a change vector approach
SYN-PUB-08103.text:
Detecting inter-annual change in softwood floodplain forest extent using dense Sentinel-2 time-series and a change vector approach (2020, journal, Remote Sensing of Riparian and Wetland Environments).
Authors: Aleksandra Đorđević (outside co-author); Predrag Vuković (outside co-author); Marina Malešević (R0730); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Jasmina Jakovljević (R0898); Helena Novak (outside co-author).
Keywords: Sentinel-2; change vector analysis; softwood forest; Sava River; phenological composites.
Softwood gallery forests dominated by Salix alba and Populus nigra are among the most flood-disturbance-adapted habitats in Pannonian river floodplains, but their spatial extent can fluctuate substantially between years in response to flood frequency and timber harvesting. This study applied a change vector analysis framework to annual phenological composites derived from Sentinel-2 MSI 10 m imagery for the period 2016–2021 across a 210 km reach of the Sava River floodplain in Serbia. Annual composites were constructed using the 20th percentile NIR and the maximum NDRE over a 60-day spring window. Change magnitudes exceeding one standard deviation above the multi-year mean were flagged and attributed to four process categories (flood disturbance, harvest clearance, natural regeneration, encroachment) using auxiliary topographic wetness index and forest management registry data. Over the six-year period, 2,140 ha of softwood forest underwent detectable canopy-layer change, with flood-related losses concentrated in the 2019 and 2021 high-water years. Accuracy of change attribution reached 82% against independent field verification of 160 change patches. The approach requires no training data beyond the composite stack and is applicable at the scale of an entire national river network.

SYN-PUB-08138.title: Sensitivity of Solvency II SCR estimates to extreme-value model choice for motor third-party liability tail risk
SYN-PUB-08138.text:
Sensitivity of Solvency II SCR estimates to extreme-value model choice for motor third-party liability tail risk (2025, journal, Journal of Risk and Insurance Modelling).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Tijana Vučković (outside co-author); Andrej Kokol Bukovšek (outside co-author); Nada Dobanovački (R0732); Gordana Todorović-Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Solvency II; SCR; MTPL; tail risk; model uncertainty.
Under Solvency II, the solvency capital requirement (SCR) for reserve risk in motor third-party liability (MTPL) lines depends on assumptions about the tail of the claim severity distribution. Regulators permit internal models if adequately validated. We analyse a synthetic MTPL portfolio calibrated to match aggregate statistics from the Serbian Insurance Supervision Agency's public reports: 4,200 closed claims over eight years, of which 38 exceed the 95th percentile. Five severity tail models (GPD, log-normal tail, Burr, Weibull, and a spliced log-normal–GPD) are fitted by maximum likelihood and by MCMC with weakly informative priors. The resulting one-year 99.5th-percentile VaR estimates—the SCR basis—range from 1.41 to 1.87 times the mean reserve. Bayes factors weakly favour the spliced model but the SCR uncertainty from model choice dwarfs parameter uncertainty in all cases.

SYN-PUB-08203.title: Evaluating Compression Schemes for Posting Lists in Low-Resource Server Environments
SYN-PUB-08203.text:
Evaluating Compression Schemes for Posting Lists in Low-Resource Server Environments (2015, journal, Journal of Data and Information Engineering (JDIE)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Miroslav Bjelogrlić (outside co-author).
Keywords: posting list compression; codec comparison; full-text search; low-resource deployment.
Posting-list compression directly affects both the memory footprint and decode throughput of full-text search engines. We systematically compare seven integer-compression codecs—including FOR-delta, PForDelta, Simple-8b, and a bitpacking variant—across three corpora of 1 million, 10 million, and 50 million documents sourced from Serbian, Croatian, and Hungarian web crawls. Experiments are conducted on commodity hardware with 16 GB RAM to reflect the constraints typical of small research or company deployments. PForDelta achieves the best decode throughput at 1.1 billion integers per second on the largest corpus, while a tuned FOR-delta variant yields the smallest on-disk footprint at 2.3 bits per integer. We also report how codec choice interacts with query selectivity: high-frequency terms favour block-oriented codecs, whereas rare-term queries are insensitive to codec selection. Practical guidance is provided for operators choosing codecs without exhaustive tuning budgets.

SYN-PUB-08204.title: A Sharded Query Broker for Sub-100 ms Retrieval over Fifty Index Partitions
SYN-PUB-08204.text:
A Sharded Query Broker for Sub-100 ms Retrieval over Fifty Index Partitions (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Scalable Data Management Systems (SSDMS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Tomáš Hradil (outside co-author); Darko Vukelić (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: query brokering; scatter-gather; distributed search; latency.
Scaling a search service beyond a single machine introduces coordinator overhead that can dominate end-to-end latency when shard count is large. We design and evaluate a sharded query broker that uses a two-phase scatter–gather protocol with early termination: in the first phase, each shard returns only top-k document identifiers and their scores; in the second phase, only shards holding documents that could affect the global top-k are asked for full postings. Tested on a 50-shard cluster indexing 200 million documents (a synthetic web corpus generated from Common Crawl metadata), the broker keeps 95th-percentile latency below 94 ms for single-term queries and below 140 ms for three-term Boolean conjunctions at 500 queries per second. A comparison with a naïve full-scatter baseline shows a 41% latency reduction with less than 0.1% loss in NDCG@10.

SYN-PUB-08205.title: Distributed Full-Text Indexing for Heterogeneous Document Collections: Architectures and Trade-offs
SYN-PUB-08205.text:
Distributed Full-Text Indexing for Heterogeneous Document Collections: Architectures and Trade-offs (2018, book chapter, Advances in Large-Scale Text Processing, edited volume, IOS Press Academic).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Jelena Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: distributed indexing; survey; document partitioning; index architecture.
This book chapter surveys architectures for distributed full-text indexing, focusing on the trade-offs between document-partitioned and term-partitioned layouts when collections are heterogeneous in language, format, and update frequency. We categorise existing systems along four axes: partitioning strategy, merge policy, fault tolerance mechanism, and query routing logic. For each axis we review the academic literature from 2005 to 2016 and relate design choices to measurable outcomes: index freshness, query latency distribution, and hardware utilisation. A recurring finding is that document-partitioned layouts tolerate heterogeneous update rates better, while term-partitioned layouts reduce per-query network traffic for vocabulary-rich corpora. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems, including the integration of real-time segment merging with batch reindexing and the impact of multilingual tokenisation on partition balance.

SYN-PUB-08206.title: Incremental HNSW Index Updates Under Concurrent Write Load
SYN-PUB-08206.text:
Incremental HNSW Index Updates Under Concurrent Write Load (2020, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Vector and Similarity Search (EVSS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Rade Milošević (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: HNSW; ANN search; index updates; vector search; compaction.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs provide high recall and low query latency for approximate nearest-neighbour search but were originally designed for static datasets. We study how concurrent insertions and deletions affect graph connectivity and search quality when updates arrive at rates between 500 and 10,000 vectors per second. Using a 768-dimensional sentence-embedding corpus of 8 million documents (generated with an open encoder trained on multilingual Wikipedia), we measure recall@10 degradation as a function of the fraction of deleted nodes not yet compacted. At 15% uncompacted deletions, recall falls by 3.1 percentage points. We propose a lightweight background compaction scheduler that monitors the deleted-node ratio and triggers partial graph reconstruction during low-traffic windows, recovering recall to within 0.6 points of the static baseline without pausing query serving. Experiments run on a single 40-core server with 256 GB RAM.

SYN-PUB-08207.title: Hybrid Sparse–Dense Retrieval: Combining BM25 and Vector Indexes Without Score Normalisation Heuristics
SYN-PUB-08207.text:
Hybrid Sparse–Dense Retrieval: Combining BM25 and Vector Indexes Without Score Normalisation Heuristics (2021, journal, Journal of Information Retrieval Research (JIRR)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Rade Milošević (outside co-author); Marco Dellarocca (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: hybrid retrieval; BM25; dense retrieval; reciprocal rank fusion; multilingual.
Combining a lexical BM25 index with a dense vector index requires merging scores from incompatible distributions. Most practical systems rely on hand-tuned linear interpolation weights or min–max normalisation, both of which are sensitive to corpus and query distribution shifts. We propose a rank-based fusion approach grounded in reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) that requires no score normalisation and is calibrated using a small set of 500 labelled query–document pairs. Evaluation on two corpora—a 3-million-document Serbian legal archive and a 7-million-document multilingual news collection—shows that the proposed method matches or exceeds the best normalisation baseline on NDCG@10 (gains of 1.8 and 2.4 points respectively) while being robust to out-of-distribution query sets. Latency overhead compared to BM25 alone is 22 ms at the 95th percentile on the larger corpus when vector retrieval runs on GPU.

SYN-PUB-08208.title: Learned Sparse Retrieval for Low-Resource South Slavic Languages
SYN-PUB-08208.text:
Learned Sparse Retrieval for Low-Resource South Slavic Languages (2025, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Language Technologies and Information Access (BALTIA)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Milica Savić (outside co-author); Marco Dellarocca (outside co-author).
Keywords: learned sparse retrieval; SPLADE; South Slavic languages; low-resource NLP; multilingual IR.
Learned sparse retrieval models such as SPLADE expand query and document terms using transformer-derived weights, producing sparse vectors that are indexed in a standard inverted index. Their effectiveness on languages other than English is less studied. We fine-tune a multilingual base transformer on Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian document–query pairs assembled from publicly available court decisions and parliamentary records, producing a total of 280,000 training triples. The resulting model is evaluated on three held-out test sets. MRR@10 improves by 6.1, 4.8, and 5.3 points over BM25 on the Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian sets respectively. Index size is 2.1× that of BM25, and query latency at the 95th percentile is 38 ms on a CPU-only server. We also report the effect of training set size, showing useful gains above approximately 40,000 triples.

SYN-PUB-08209.title: Tiered Vector Storage: Exploiting NVMe and DRAM Hierarchies for ANN Index Serving
SYN-PUB-08209.text:
Tiered Vector Storage: Exploiting NVMe and DRAM Hierarchies for ANN Index Serving (2026, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Data Storage and Retrieval Systems (DATSYS)).
Authors: Milica Savić (outside co-author); Nikola Stanković (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Jürgen Albrecht (outside co-author).
Keywords: tiered storage; NVMe; ANN search; HNSW; memory hierarchy.
Dense vector indexes for ANN search are memory-intensive; billion-scale deployments frequently exceed available DRAM. We design a tiered storage manager that partitions HNSW graph layers across DRAM and NVMe, keeping upper graph layers and frequently accessed vectors in DRAM while spilling lower layers to NVMe. Access patterns are tracked with a lightweight frequency counter and a decay factor that deprioritises temporally stale vectors. On a 1.5-billion-vector index (768 dimensions, float16) requiring 2.2 TB uncompressed, the tiered system achieves 89.1% recall@10 using 128 GB DRAM plus 2 TB NVMe, compared to 94.3% recall with full DRAM loading. Query throughput at this recall level is 1,340 queries per second, a 4.2× improvement over a pure NVMe baseline. The implementation builds on an open-source ANN library with a custom I/O scheduler.

SYN-PUB-08210.title: Distributed Stream Processing: Architectures, Algorithms, and Deployment
SYN-PUB-08210.text:
Distributed Stream Processing: Architectures, Algorithms, and Deployment (2022, book chapter, Handbook of Big Data Systems Engineering, Springer).
Authors: Miroslav Tošić (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Balázs Fekete (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: stream processing survey; operator graph; exactly-once semantics; fault tolerance; textbook.
This book chapter surveys the architectural space of distributed stream processing systems, covering foundational data models (data streams, continuous queries, operator graphs), core algorithmic challenges (join algorithms, windowing, state management, fault tolerance), and deployment considerations on both on-premises clusters and cloud-native infrastructure. The chapter is structured in three parts. The first part establishes formal definitions and a taxonomy of processing guarantees (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once). The second part surveys algorithms for the main operator classes—filters, aggregations, joins, and enrichments—with emphasis on complexity trade-offs under varying data distributions. The third part addresses operational concerns: resource allocation, monitoring, schema management, and integration with batch systems. Representative open-source and commercial systems are discussed as illustrative examples without prescriptive endorsement. Annotated references guide readers toward primary literature for each subtopic. The chapter is intended for graduate students and practitioners with prior exposure to database systems and parallel computing.

SYN-PUB-08314.title: A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments
SYN-PUB-08314.text:
A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments (2013, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Sensor Systems).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: watchdog timer; fault recovery; wireless sensor node; soil monitoring; ATmega.
Unattended wireless sensor nodes in field deployments frequently enter irrecoverable software states due to memory corruption, peripheral lockup, or stack overflow caused by transient power events. This paper presents a layered watchdog architecture implemented on an ATmega128RFA1 platform in which three independent timers supervise the operating system scheduler, the radio driver, and the analog front-end sequencer separately. When any tier detects a violation of its expected heartbeat window, a graduated recovery procedure is executed that avoids full device reset in roughly 74 percent of observed fault cases, thereby preserving the sensor's runtime context. The scheme was evaluated over a 90-day outdoor deployment of 18 nodes sampling soil moisture at 10-minute intervals. Mean time between unrecoverable resets increased from 11.3 days in the baseline configuration to 61.7 days with the proposed architecture. Current overhead introduced by the additional supervision circuitry was measured at 38 µA in active mode, representing less than 2 percent of total node consumption. The design is described in sufficient detail to be reproduced on comparable 8-bit and 16-bit microcontroller families.

SYN-PUB-08315.title: On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring
SYN-PUB-08315.text:
On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring (2018, journal, Sensors and Actuators: Methods and Applications).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Ivan Zec (R0903); Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author).
Keywords: sensor drift; humidity sensor; recursive least squares; edge diagnostics; anomaly detection.
Capacitive and resistive humidity sensors used in long-term field deployments exhibit systematic drift attributable to membrane contamination, mechanical stress, and UV degradation of the sensing polymer. This study examines drift detection using a recursive least-squares estimator running on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller with 64 kB RAM. The estimator maintains a sliding 72-hour model of sensor behaviour and raises a diagnostic flag when the standardised prediction residual exceeds a threshold calibrated to yield a 5 percent false-alarm rate under clean operating conditions. The method was validated against a controlled ageing experiment in which 24 SHT31-compatible sensors were exposed to accelerated UV and humidity cycling; 21 of 22 drift events exceeding 3 percent RH offset were detected within 8 hours of onset. Computational cost was benchmarked at 1.2 ms per update cycle at 48 MHz, consuming negligible battery capacity relative to the radio subsystem. The paper includes a discussion of threshold sensitivity as a function of sampling interval and recommends a minimum of 15-minute sampling for reliable operation.

SYN-PUB-08316.title: Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions
SYN-PUB-08316.text:
Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions (2020, book chapter, Handbook of Low-Power Sensing Systems for Environmental Applications (TechPress Academic, Vienna)).
Authors: Gordana Simić (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Ralf Brünner (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy harvesting; solar power; transmission scheduling; supercapacitor; duty cycle control.
Solar energy harvesting for IoT nodes in temperate climates is complicated by persistent partial shading from vegetation, cloud cover, and seasonal sun angle variation. This chapter reviews energy buffering and transmission scheduling strategies applicable to nodes where the harvester output drops to 10–40 percent of rated capacity for multi-hour periods. A discrete-time predictive controller is presented that adjusts the uplink reporting interval and transmission power based on a rolling 24-hour energy budget estimated from a small supercapacitor voltage sensor. Simulations using one-year solar irradiance data from three sites in the Pannonian Plain show that the controller maintains the reporting duty cycle above 85 percent of the target rate throughout the year compared with 61 percent for a fixed-interval baseline. The chapter also covers hardware design guidelines for solar panel placement and MPPT circuit selection, and discusses the trade-off between supercapacitor capacity, leakage current, and cold-start reliability in sub-zero conditions.

SYN-PUB-08317.title: Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments
SYN-PUB-08317.text:
Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments (2021, conference, IEEE International Conference on Agricultural IoT and Precision Farming (AIPF)).
Authors: Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Marija Đurić (outside co-author); Konstantinos Papadimitriou (outside co-author).
Keywords: data quality; gateway processing; agricultural IoT; anomaly flagging; heterogeneous networks.
Aggregation gateways in agricultural IoT networks receive streams from sensors operating under different power regimes, communication protocols, and environmental exposures. This paper proposes a gateway-side data quality scoring framework that assigns each incoming measurement a composite score based on four sub-metrics: timeliness (elapsed time since last message relative to expected interval), signal plausibility (z-score against a rolling peer-group distribution), battery state estimate, and historical reliability index derived from 30-day uptime statistics. The framework was implemented in Python 3.9 on a Raspberry Pi 4 gateway serving 61 nodes in a test vineyard in Fruška Gora, processing approximately 8,700 messages per day. Over a 5-month evaluation period, the composite score correctly flagged 93 of 97 manually confirmed measurement anomalies and produced 11 false positives. Score computation added a mean latency of 4.1 ms per message at gateway level. The scoring metadata is forwarded alongside raw measurements to a central time-series database, enabling downstream analytics to weight observations accordingly. Integration steps for two commercial farm management platforms are documented.

SYN-PUB-08318.title: Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study
SYN-PUB-08318.text:
Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study (2022, journal, Embedded Systems and Wireless Communications Letters).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Aleksandra Ninković (outside co-author); Tibor Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: FOTA; firmware update; NB-IoT; rural deployment; link quality.
Over-the-air firmware updates (FOTA) are essential for maintaining security and functionality of deployed IoT nodes but are poorly characterised in weak-signal rural cellular conditions. This study documents 1,840 FOTA sessions conducted across 46 NB-IoT nodes installed at distances of 8–22 km from the nearest base station in the southern Bačka region of Serbia. Update payloads ranged from 48 to 192 kB and were delivered using a block-based transfer protocol with configurable block size and retry budget. Session success rate was 81.4 percent without adaptive configuration and rose to 94.6 percent when block size was reduced from 512 to 128 bytes and the retry budget was tripled. Failed sessions were traced primarily to receive-window mismatches during peak network load periods. Energy cost per successful update was measured between 0.9 and 3.4 mAh depending on retry overhead. The paper quantifies the dependency of success rate on RSRP and presents a simple heuristic for selecting block size based on a short link probe transmitted before each update session.

SYN-PUB-08319.title: Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study
SYN-PUB-08319.text:
Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.NI)).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Florian Kersting (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT congestion; duty cycle; dense IoT; network simulation; transmission scheduling.
When hundreds of IoT nodes sharing a single NB-IoT cell simultaneously enter their reporting window, uplink congestion increases packet delay and loss in ways that interact nonlinearly with node-level duty-cycle power management. This preprint reports a combined simulation and measurement study: a system-level LTE-M/NB-IoT simulator was configured to match the topology of a 312-node crop monitoring network in Srem, and its congestion behaviour was cross-validated against 8 weeks of gateway-side timestamps showing mean delay growth from 1.2 s to 14.7 s during morning reporting peaks. The simulator was then used to evaluate four transmission-window randomisation strategies across node densities from 50 to 500 nodes per cell. A jitter-and-backoff strategy combining a randomised initial delay drawn from a 0–300 s uniform window with an exponential backoff on contention reduced 99th-percentile delay from 41 s to 8 s and cut failed transmissions by 63 percent at 400 nodes per cell. Interaction effects with solar harvesting schedules are discussed and a recommended configuration table is provided for deployment engineers.

SYN-PUB-08739.title: Empirical Path-Loss Measurements at 868 MHz in a Multi-Floor Office Building
SYN-PUB-08739.text:
Empirical Path-Loss Measurements at 868 MHz in a Multi-Floor Office Building (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 21st Telecommunications Forum TELFOR, Belgrade).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Dragan Vučić (outside co-author); Miroslav Stevanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: 868 MHz; path-loss; indoor measurement; floor attenuation; LoRaWAN planning.
This paper presents a path-loss measurement campaign conducted across six floors of a reinforced-concrete office building in Novi Sad. A continuous-wave transmitter operating at 868 MHz was placed at three fixed positions on the ground floor, and received power was logged at 214 measurement points using a calibrated spectrum analyser mounted on a wheeled trolley. The collected data were compared against the ITU-R P.1238 indoor model and a dual-slope log-distance fit. The dual-slope model with breakpoint at 15 m showed a root-mean-square error of 4.1 dB, outperforming the ITU-R model by 2.3 dB on upper floors where inter-floor attenuation dominates. Floor attenuation factors extracted from the data ranged from 11 dB to 17 dB depending on floor construction type. The dataset and derived model coefficients are provided for direct use in LoRaWAN network planning tools.

SYN-PUB-08740.title: Delay Spread Statistics in Warehouse Environments at 433 MHz and 868 MHz
SYN-PUB-08740.text:
Delay Spread Statistics in Warehouse Environments at 433 MHz and 868 MHz (2015, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Dragan Vučić (outside co-author); Katalin Fodor (outside co-author).
Keywords: delay spread; wideband channel; warehouse; 433 MHz; 868 MHz; channel sounding.
Wideband channel impulse responses were measured in two logistics warehouses with steel shelving, concrete floors, and metallic roofing, using a vector network analyser with 801 frequency points spanning a 200 MHz band centred on each carrier frequency. Measurements were taken along 18 linear tracks of 20 m each under loaded and unloaded shelf conditions. RMS delay spread at 433 MHz ranged from 38 ns to 124 ns, while at 868 MHz values were 29 ns to 98 ns. Loaded shelves consistently reduced delay spread by 10–25 % compared to empty conditions, attributed to increased absorption. A lognormal fit adequately described the delay spread distribution at both frequencies with similar shape parameters. The results indicate that standard LoRa spreading factors provide sufficient guard intervals for these environments without additional equalisation, but gateway placement relative to shelf aisles significantly affects coverage uniformity.

SYN-PUB-08741.title: Small Planar Inverted-F Antenna for 868 MHz LoRa End-Node Integration
SYN-PUB-08741.text:
Small Planar Inverted-F Antenna for 868 MHz LoRa End-Node Integration (2016, journal, Microwave and Optical Technology Letters (European Edition)).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: PIFA; LoRa antenna; 868 MHz; PCB antenna; radiation efficiency.
A compact planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) was designed and fabricated for integration onto a 50 mm × 30 mm PCB intended for battery-powered LoRa sensor nodes. The antenna occupies a 25 mm × 8 mm footprint on an FR-4 substrate with 1.6 mm thickness. Matching was achieved through a shorting strip and a tuning slot, yielding a measured −10 dB bandwidth of 28 MHz centred at 868 MHz, covering the full European LoRa band. Measured gain was −0.8 dBi in free space and dropped by 1.4 dB when the PCB was placed inside an ABS plastic enclosure of 2 mm wall thickness. Radiation efficiency was 61 %. The sensitivity of the resonant frequency to hand proximity was characterised using a phantom limb fixture; detuning of up to 14 MHz was observed, which remains within the matched bandwidth. The design is compared against a monopole reference and a commercially available chip antenna.

SYN-PUB-08742.title: Reverberation Chamber Characterisation of Antenna Radiation Efficiency for Sub-GHz IoT Devices
SYN-PUB-08742.text:
Reverberation Chamber Characterisation of Antenna Radiation Efficiency for Sub-GHz IoT Devices (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 26th International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM), Split).
Authors: Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Jens Hoffmann (outside co-author); Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Miroslav Stevanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: reverberation chamber; radiation efficiency; IoT antennas; sub-GHz; measurement uncertainty.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08743.title: Link Budget Tool for LoRaWAN Deployments in Mixed Indoor–Outdoor Industrial Sites
SYN-PUB-08743.text:
Link Budget Tool for LoRaWAN Deployments in Mixed Indoor–Outdoor Industrial Sites (2020, journal, Journal of Communications Software and Systems).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Dragan Vučić (outside co-author); Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: LoRaWAN; link budget; industrial IoT; coverage prediction; RSSI; spreading factor.
A deterministic link-budget calculation tool was developed to assist network planners in estimating coverage for LoRaWAN deployments that span both indoor factory halls and adjacent outdoor yard areas. The tool combines empirical path-loss exponents derived from dedicated measurement campaigns at three industrial sites in the Vojvodina region with a material-dependent wall-transmission loss database compiled from waveguide measurement data. Users specify building geometry, gateway positions, and target reliability thresholds; the tool outputs a coverage probability map and recommends spreading-factor assignments per zone. Validation was performed by comparing predicted received-signal strength indicator (RSSI) values with drive-test data from a 23-gateway pilot deployment; median prediction error was 3.8 dB with a standard deviation of 6.2 dB across 1 840 logged packets. The tool is implemented in Python and the source code is publicly available under a BSD licence.

SYN-PUB-08744.title: Spatial Correlation of Received Signal Strength in LoRa Networks Inside Hospital Buildings
SYN-PUB-08744.text:
Spatial Correlation of Received Signal Strength in LoRa Networks Inside Hospital Buildings (2021, journal, Wireless Personal Communications).
Authors: Biljana Pešić (outside co-author); Katalin Fodor (outside co-author); Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Zoltán Nemes (outside co-author).
Keywords: hospital propagation; LoRaWAN; RSSI; spatial correlation; semivariogram; healthcare IoT.
Hospital buildings present specific propagation challenges owing to a heterogeneous mix of construction materials, frequent metallic obstacles, and strict electromagnetic compatibility requirements. This paper analyses the spatial correlation structure of RSSI measurements from a static LoRaWAN testbed installed in a four-wing hospital building in Novi Sad, comprising three gateways and 47 fixed end-nodes over a monitoring period of four weeks. Semivariogram analysis was used to quantify spatial correlation lengths, which ranged from 6 m in densely furnished patient wards to 22 m in long straight corridors. Temporal variation of RSSI at fixed nodes showed a diurnal pattern with peak-to-peak variation of up to 4 dB, correlating with occupancy levels. The findings suggest that gateway placement optimisation based on static measurements may overestimate coverage reliability during peak occupancy, and a safety margin of at least 5 dB is recommended for healthcare IoT system planning.

SYN-PUB-08745.title: Angle-of-Arrival Estimation Accuracy for Indoor Localisation at 868 MHz Using a Four-Element Switched Beam Array
SYN-PUB-08745.text:
Angle-of-Arrival Estimation Accuracy for Indoor Localisation at 868 MHz Using a Four-Element Switched Beam Array (2023, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (regional invited session, Zagreb)).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Marco Bertoni (outside co-author).
Keywords: angle of arrival; switched beam array; indoor localisation; 868 MHz; LoRa; asset tracking.
A switched-beam array consisting of four printed Yagi elements arranged in a cross configuration was constructed and evaluated for angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation in indoor environments. The array aperture was 220 mm and operated at 868 MHz with a measured half-power beamwidth of 72° per sector. AoA estimation was performed using a maximum-likelihood algorithm applied to received signal strength differences between sectors. Laboratory tests in an anechoic enclosure yielded a mean absolute angular error of 4.2°. In a furnished office environment with rich multipath, the error increased to 11.7° for line-of-sight paths and 19.4° for non-line-of-sight paths at distances between 5 m and 30 m. The effect of antenna placement height (1 m vs. 2.5 m) on estimation accuracy was also evaluated; the higher placement reduced non-line-of-sight error by approximately 3°. Results are discussed in the context of asset-tracking accuracy requirements.

SYN-PUB-08820.title: Empirical Path-Loss Characterisation for 868 MHz Signals in a Mixed Residential and Commercial District
SYN-PUB-08820.text:
Empirical Path-Loss Characterisation for 868 MHz Signals in a Mixed Residential and Commercial District (2010, journal, Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computing – Serbia).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: path-loss model; 868 MHz; measurement campaign; COST 231 Hata; shadowing.
This paper presents a measurement-based path-loss study conducted in the Liman district of Novi Sad at 868 MHz during autumn 2009. A total of 4 800 received signal strength indicator samples were collected along 22 transects using a calibrated test transmitter and a portable receiver mounted on a bicycle. The log-distance model with a dual-slope breakpoint at 120 m was fitted to the data, yielding path-loss exponents of 2.1 and 3.6 for the near and far zones, respectively.
